Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 1:

Allah the Exalted says:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Sad. (1)﴾ In this verse there is a separation between each letter, so we read it: "Alif," then we pause to read "Lam," then we pause to read "Mim," then we pause to read "Sad." Here are letters that break the rule for a wisdom, because these letters are disjointed, like "Alif Lam Mim," "Ha Mim," "Ta Ha," "Ya Sin," "Sad," "Qaf," and all of them are built on sukun (the vowelless state), which indicates that these letters, even if it seems to you that they are one word, each letter has an independent meaning with Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah, he has a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied tenfold. I do not say that Alif Lam Mim is one letter; rather, Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter." [1] The Messenger (ﷺ) indicated that these letters have independent matters, and they are not so unless they have a benefit that makes it good to pause and stop upon them. Whoever understood them understood, and whoever worshipped by them worshipped by them. Every reader of the Qur'an takes his reward for each letter. So if a reader says, "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," and then pronounces after that one letter or more, he has received a good deed for each letter. When we read some of the opening letters of the surahs, we find that Surat al-Baqarah begins with the saying of the Truth: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. (1)﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

And we read here at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Sad. (1)﴾ (Surat al-A'raf):

These are disjointed letters. They were pronounced with sukun and with separation between each letter and another. It is also noticed in them that they were not read as musammayat (the named letters/sounds), but were read as asma' (names). What is the meaning of musammayat and what is the meaning of asma'? When you say "kataba" (he wrote), you do not say "kaf," "ta," "ba," but you pronounce the musammclass of kaf as "ka," and its ism (name) is "kaf" with a fatha; as for its musamma (referent sound) it is "ka." So every letter has a musamma, namely the sound that a person utters, and it has an ism, and the unlettered person pronounces the musammayat even if he does not know their asma'. As for the learner, he alone understands that when he says "kataba," it is composed of a kaf with a fatha, a ta with a fatha, and a ba with a fatha; as for the unlettered person, he does not know this detail.

If the Messenger of Allah received that and said "Alif Lam Mim," while he was unlettered and had not been taught, then who taught him to pronounce the musammayat of the letters with these names? He must have been taught and received them, and the Truth is the One who says: ﴿So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation (18)﴾ [Surat al-Qiyamah].

So what you will hear, O Muhammad, you will recite; therefore you find wonders. You find "Alif Lam Mim" at the beginning of al-Baqarah and at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran, but you read the first verse of Surat al-Fil: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (1)﴾ [Surat al-Fil].

What is the difference between Alif, Lam and Mim at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, and Surat Al 'Imran and others, and the same letters at the beginning of Surat al-Fil and others such as Surat al-Sharh? You read them at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran as asma', and you read them at the beginning of Surat al-Fil as musammayat. What made you distinguish between these and those is that you heard them read at the beginning of al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran in this way, and you heard them read at the beginning of Surat al-Fil in that way. So recitation is tawqif (divinely fixed transmission), and no one may dare to recite the Qur'an without hearing it from a teacher. No; he must hear it first so that he knows how to recite it.

We read "﴿Mim. Sad.﴾" at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf, and these are disjointed letters, and we know that the disjointed letters are twenty-eight letters, and we find half of them, fourteen letters, in the openings of the surahs. One of them may occur at the beginning of a surah as a single letter, such as: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an (1)﴾ [Surat Qaf], and likewise the saying of the Truth: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, possessor of reminder (1)﴾ [Surat Sad], and likewise the saying of the Truth: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe (1)﴾ [Surat al-Qalam]. Sometimes two disjointed letters occur, such as the saying of the Truth: ﴿Ha Mim (1)﴾ [Surat al-Ahqaf]. Sometimes three disjointed letters occur, such as: ﴿Alif Lam Mim (1)﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah]. Sometimes Allah brings four disjointed letters, such as the saying of the Truth: ﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad (1)﴾ [Surat al-A'raf]. Sometimes He brings five disjointed letters, such as the saying of the Truth: ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad (1)﴾ [Surat Maryam].

When you look at the fourteen letters, you find that they represent half of the alphabet letters, and this half contains half of the rules of the letters: some of them are munsharah (spread out in articulation), or mahmus (whispered), or mukhfa (concealed), or mustaliyah (raised). And from each type you find half, which indicates that they are placed with precise calculation. Although the description of the letters, as mustali (raised), mufakhkham (heavy), murraqaq (light), munshar (spread), or mahmus (whispered), came later than the revelation of the Qur'an, the One who said it knows what His creation will arrive at regarding these disjointed letters, and He has wisdom in that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was unlettered and did not sit with a teacher, so how could he pronounce the names of the letters, when the names of the letters are known only to one who has learned? So he had indeed been taught them. We know that the Qur'an came challenging the Arabs, so that it would be a miracle for the Master of creation, and one is not challenged except one who excels in this craft. The Arabs were famous for eloquence, oratory, poetry, rhymed prose, and proverbs; they were a people of speech, eloquence and rhetoric. The Qur'an came to them of the kind of their excellence. When Allah challenges the Arabs by sending down a Qur'an they cannot bring its like, the raw material, which is language, is one, and it is from the very letters of the language in which the Arabs excelled, and with the very words they use; yet they were unable to bring its like, because it came from a powerful Lord, whereas the speech of the Arabs and their eloquence are the work of created human beings who are powerless.

Thus we know the secret of the disjointed letters, which came to establish that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received the Qur'an from the Exalted Assembly, because he was unlettered and had learned nothing; yet he knew the names of the letters, and knowledge of the names of the letters, as I said, is known only to the learner. "He Who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know" [Surat al-Alaq]. The human mind may circle around the verses, and in these letters there are many meanings. We find that many thinkers and reflectors on the words of Allah have found much in the field of the majesty and beauty of the Qur'an. You find a Sufi who says that ﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad﴾ came here for a wisdom: you pronounce the first word "alif," which is the hamzah from the throat; the lam you pronounce from the tongue; and the mim you pronounce from the lips; and thereby you cover the places of articulation of the letters from the throat, tongue and lips.

The Sufi said that to show you that this surah speaks about matters of life, beginning with the creation of mankind from Adam, an indication of the primacy of human creation; and a middle, which is livelihood; and an end, which is death and reckoning, then life in the Hereafter. The "Sad" came because in this surah are the stories of most of the prophets. Thus this Sufi made his circuit and came out of it. Shall we reject it? No, we do not reject it by nature, but we say to him: Is that all of Allah's knowledge in it? No, because it is incumbent upon us to become acquainted with the meanings in it and to take them according to our human capacity. We have read them according to the measure of Allah's intent, but we will never grasp all the horizons of Allah's intents, because our understandings are limited.

We humans set words that have no meaning so that they indicate things that serve life. For example, in armies you find one who sets a "password" for each camp, so that no one enters except one who knows the word. Whoever knows the "password" can enter. Every password has a meaning for the one who set it, and its price may be life for one who approaches the army camp without knowing it.

﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad (1)﴾ [Surat al-A'raf]: We find these disjointed letters are a discourse about the Book.

1 Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Darimi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 2:

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿A Book revealed to you, so let there be no constriction in your breast because of it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers.﴾

When you hear "revealed" (unzila), understand that it came from a direction above, meaning that the legislation is from on high. Some scholars said: Is there any constriction (haraj) in the breast of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? Let us be attentive: whenever a command comes from our Lord and clarifies, "so let there be no constriction in your breast," the prohibition is not directed at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself; rather, the prohibition is aimed at constriction or narrowness, that it should not enter the Messenger of Allah. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying: "O constriction, do not descend upon the heart of Muhammad."

But other scholars said: The Truth has come with His words, glory be to Him, "so let there be no constriction in your breast," because the Truth knows that Muhammad may feel his chest tighten by virtue of his humanity, and grieve, because they say of him that he is a sorcerer, a liar, and a madman. When your opponent comes and attributes to you qualities that you know are not in you, then he is the liar, for you have not lied and have not practiced sorcery, and you desire the guidance of the people. His words, glory be to Him, "so let there be no constriction in your breast," came for one of two purposes: either the command is directed at the constriction, that it not settle in the breast of the Messenger of Allah, or the command is directed at the Messenger himself, as reassurance and calming for him, meaning: do not be distressed, for it was sent down to you from God. Would God send down to you a Qur'an to become the method of His creation and a straight path for them, and then abandon you to the foolishness of these people? No, it is not possible. So be completely at ease.

﴿So let there be no constriction in your breast because of it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf]: Warning (indhar) occurs only toward one who opposes, for warning is an informing of evil that the one addressed should expect. It is also a reminder for the believers, just as He said earlier in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾.

Here we note that messages (risalat) require a sender above, who is God; a sent one, who is the Messenger; and a recipient, who is the community (ummah). The recipient either listens and is guided, or does not. The verse came to say: ﴿A Book revealed﴾ from God, who is the Sender, and "to you" because you are the Messenger, and those to whom it is sent are the community. Either you warn them if they oppose, or you remind them, guide them and help them, or you give them good news if they are believers.

The Almighty then says:

﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow, besides Him, any protectors. Little do you take heed.﴾ (7:3)

Since the servants are to be divided, before the bearer of the message and the Book that came with him, into those who accept guidance and those who need warning, He says to them: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ (part of verse 3 of Surat al-A'raf).

He forbids them from polytheism and from not seeking guidance, meaning seeking guidance (al-istihda', i.e. asking to be guided), so He says: ﴿and do not follow, besides Him, any protectors. Little do you take heed﴾ (part of verse 3 of Surat al-A'raf).

When the Almighty comes in verses such as these and says "wa-dhikra" (and a reminder) or "wa-dhakkir" (and remind), He is only drawing our attention to the fact that the innate nature (al-fitra) with which man is created is a believing one, and that all the messages did not come to create a new faith, but came to remind (of the covenant that was taken from us in the days when we were in the world of the atoms, before we had the capacity of choice):

﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified…"﴾ (7:172).

This is the affirmation in the world of the atoms. So when the Almighty says ﴿Little do you take heed﴾, we are drawing attention to what the fathers forgot to convey to the sons. The fathers teach the sons the requirements of their lives, and it was incumbent upon them to teach them also the values of life which they themselves received, because when Adam and Eve first descended to earth, the Almighty said to them:

﴿Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance…﴾ (20:123).

Thus we know that there was a "guidance" that descended upon Adam, and it was incumbent upon Adam to teach it to the children, and the children to teach it to the grandchildren, and this "guidance" should have remained transmitted along the chain of life just as all the provisions of life have arrived. Then He brings to us the grounds for following:

﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord…﴾ (7:3). The method that comes from the Supreme Lord is the one that sets life right, and there is no shame upon any of you in following what has been sent down to him from the God who nurtures, the Capable, who nurtured and created from nothing, and supplied from nothing, and who is the one who undertakes the nurturing. He cannot nurture our bodies with food, drink and air and not nurture our values with morals. ﴿And do not follow, besides Him, any protectors﴾.

Since He has made clear: follow what has been sent down to you from above, it is not right for you to go to someone other than Him and take from him, just as the world does now when it takes its laws from other than God and from human desires. This one loves capitalism and imposes it by the sword, and another loves socialism and imposes it by the sword. Each one imposes by his sword the laws that suit him. All of them fall short of God's method, because they are the ideas of men, and they clash with the ideas of men; and the better course than this and that is that we take from Him, whom we do not disdain to be slaves to.

﴿...And do not follow, besides Him, any protectors. Little do you take heed﴾ (7:3). And remember, O believer, that your honour lies in following God's method, which is manifest in your not submitting to one who is your equal. This is the distinctive feature of the religion that makes a person live in dignity in the universe, with his dignity preserved. If a matter beyond his means comes to him, he meets it with the means available to him, believing that the Lord of the means will provide help, and God indeed provides him help, so he prostrates to God in gratitude. As for one who has no lord, when a matter beyond his means comes to him, his life becomes constricted for him, and he may commit suicide.

Then the Almighty explains that the procession of messages has continued since Adam, and whenever heedlessness comes over mankind, God sends a messenger to alert them, and to awaken the values and the religious immunity that exist within the self, such that when the self inclines toward something deviant, the self itself becomes alert and says: "Why did you do this?" This is the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama). If the self-reproaching soul falls silent, and man grows accustomed to error, and his soul becomes one that commands evil at all times, then the society around him corrects him.

This is the benefit of mutual exhortation to truth and patience (al-tawasi bi'l-haqq wa'l-sabr). Each one is advised in one situation and advises in another situation; when he weakens before a desire, another person who has not weakened in that desire comes and advises him, and a person exchanges advice with others. This is the meaning of mutual exhortation. Advice does not come from a group that professionally advises people; rather, each person advises in what he is strong in, and advises in what he is weak in. If society becomes corrupt, heaven intervenes with a new messenger, a new miracle, and a new method. But God has secured the community of Muhammad in this matter, so no messenger came after him, because we are the best community brought forth for mankind. And the excellence manifests in that we enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. So mutual exhortation remains until the Hour is established. ﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ (3:110).

This is a characteristic that will never end. If you see a wrong, there must be a cell of goodness that denounces it and says: No. And since the Almighty made Muhammad the seal of the messengers, that is a testimony for his community that it has become trustworthy, and that its self-immunity will never be lacking or cease, and likewise social immunity will never be lacking from it. No messenger will come after the lord of creation, our master Muhammad (ﷺ).

And the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿How many a town have We destroyed! Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were resting at midday.﴾

When you hear "kam" (how many), know that the matter has gone beyond counting, so that it requires you to ask about it. This indicates something great beyond number. When the number is small, however, it is not asked about but is known. The "qarya" (town) is a name for the place prepared specially for people to live in. Is it the towns that are destroyed, or the people in them? The Truth made clear that the word comes once to mean the place and its inhabitants, or it may mean its people. An example is His saying in Surat Yusuf: ﴿And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan...﴾ [Yusuf 82]. Naturally, a person would not ask a place or buildings, but rather the people of the town. The Truth did not say "ask the people of the town," because what is being asked about is a matter of such truth that the place itself bears witness along with the two angels. Once again, the Truth makes clear that He destroys the town with its inhabitants and its buildings: ﴿How many a town have We destroyed! Our punishment came upon it...﴾.

Which comes first: the destruction, or does the punishment come first and then destroy? What comes first is the punishment, which then destroys. The manifestations of cosmic events do not come impromptu; their matter was decreed from eternity. It is as if the Truth is saying here: "How many a town We decreed to destroy, and Our punishment came upon it, so that what We had said from eternity would be fulfilled." That is, events come in accordance with what is willed, even if the one spoken of by the Truth has a choice.

We know that the town is a place, and accordingly it has no choice. If the one spoken of has the right of choice, He (glory be to Him) knows from eternity that he will do what He speaks of. He brings it in a Qur'an that is recited, so that conduct conforms to what Allah has informed of. ﴿How many a town have We destroyed! Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were resting at midday.﴾ [Al-A'raf 4]. "Al-ba's" (punishment, might) is the force that cannot be repelled or overcome. "Bayatan" means by night, and ﴿or while they were resting at midday﴾ means during the qaylula (midday rest). Why does the punishment come at night or during the midday rest? We find in the account of those who were destroyed, such as the people of Lut, that their destruction happened at night, and the people of Shu'ayb had their destruction during the midday rest. Night and midday rest are times of relaxation and repose, and events surprise them so that they cannot prepare. ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned.﴾ [As-Saffat 177]: that is, destruction comes to them at a time when they are asleep, and they have no strength to face the punishment. ﴿Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were resting at midday﴾ [Al-A'raf 4].

When He (glory be to Him) says ﴿by night, or while they were resting at midday﴾, it may be that this town has extensions. The time of midday rest for one group differs from the time for those who live in the extension of the town, so for them the time is night, and the midday rest is the time when they sleep for relaxation and repose.

How did they receive the hour when the punishment that would destroy them came? The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And their plea was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

With this statement the matter becomes clear. From His words ﴿their plea﴾ we understand that the matter is a claim (ida'). We say: "So-and-so made a claim (da'wa) against so-and-so," and then either he establishes evidence (bayyina) to prove his claim, or he does not. The word da'wa is also used for supplication (du'a'): ﴿And the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (Qur'an 10:10). Here the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And their plea was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

Our Lord explains this matter in many verses. It is their acknowledgment of committing wrongdoing and of persisting in it. So He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." So they will admit their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ (Surah al-Mulk).

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾.

Al-Haqq asks the messengers, after gathering them, about the extent to which their peoples believed them. The question comes for the purpose of affirmation (al-iqrar). The matter of questioning appears in the Qur'an in forms whose outward meaning seems contradictory, but in reality their aspects are distinct, and this is what led the opponents of the Qur'an to claim that the Qur'an contains contradiction. Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that day, nor will they ask one another﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun), and He also says: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about his intimate friend﴾ (Surah al-Ma'arij, 10). He, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿Nor will the criminals be asked about their sins﴾ (part of verse 78, Surah al-Qasas). He, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿So on that Day, no man or jinn will be asked about his sin﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 39). Then He says here: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

This is what leads some orientalists to rush into trying to show that the Qur'an, God forbid, contains contradictions. We say to each of them: you are taking the Qur'an without the faculty of eloquence in the language. If you considered that the Qur'an was received by a people whose tongue is Arabic, and who remained upon their disbelief, it cannot be said that they were flattering (the Prophet). And if they had found this contradiction, would they not have been able to refute the claim of Muhammad by saying: "How could the Qur'an be a miracle while it is contradictory?!" But the disbelievers did not say it, which indicates that their faculties received the Qur'an in accordance with what the Speaker of the Qur'an intended. In our customs, we pose a question in two ways: sometimes a student asks his teacher in order to learn, and sometimes a teacher asks his student in order to establish (a point).

So the question comes for two things: either you ask in order to learn, and this is the (ordinary) inquiry (istifham), or you ask in order to establish, so that the proof becomes more binding upon the one questioned. So if God will question him, that is, question him with a question of affirmation, so that the argument against him is more forceful. After that they say: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." So they will acknowledge their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 10–11). This is their acknowledgment and affirmation, and both are the strongest of proofs, because the speech of one who is being questioned is (merely) testimony, but the speech of one who affirms is acknowledgment and confession.

So when the questioning is affirmed, it is a question of establishment from God, so that they become witnesses against themselves, and this is a more eloquent proof and a cutting off of the paths of denial. Either a person affirms, and if he does not affirm, his limbs will testify, because the will has been separated from them and the person no longer has power over them, in confirmation of the words of the Truth: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has given us speech, He who gives speech to all things"﴾ (part of verse 21, Surah Fussilat). And the Truth here says: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾, and it is a question for affirmation. Allah says of it: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ (part of verse 109, Surah al-Ma'idah).

And when the Truth questions the messengers, who have already delivered their message, that will be a rebuke to those to whom they were sent.

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿So We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾.

That is, He will inform them of everything they did at the moment of reckoning, because He, glorified is He, has never been absent for a single day from any of His creation. For this reason He said: ﴿and We were not absent﴾. We know that creation is multiple in its essences, multiple in its events, and multiple in its locations. They are many beings, every being has an event, and every being has a place. So when the Truth says to all of them: ﴿and We were not absent﴾, it means that He is with all of them, since He is not absent from any event, and these events are many. Therefore He is in every time and in every place.

If you ask, "How can He be here and there?" I say: take that within the framework of His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. Meanings of this kind in the unseen (al-ghaybiyyat) cannot be governed by these images. We have already said this when we spoke about the coming of God: He possesses the freedom of power, ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾, and He was never absent in any event or place.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth. So those whose scales are heavy – those are the successful.﴾

In these verses we find discussion of the weighing of deeds. All of this serves to affirm the proof against them, for Allah does not wrong anyone. In the weighing of deeds there is also the nullifying of the argument of those who fear the Fire yet did not fulfil Allah's rights in the world. All of this confirms the proof, makes justice manifest, and cuts off every excuse. Here is a noble statement in which the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya' 21:47]. These scales are the very essence of justice, not merely just scales. The precision of the scales of the Hereafter reaches the point that they are themselves justice in their very nature. Here the Truth says: ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth.﴾ Yes, the scale on that Day is truth and exactness. Let us recall that He said earlier:

﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:160]

The true scale is that upon which the justice of the whole universe rests. Everything in it is weighed, and glory be to Him, it is He who assigns measures according to the wisdom, perfection and precision by which every being performs what is required of it. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And the heaven He raised up, and He set the balance [in place]﴾ [Surah al-Rahman 55:7].

We have not seen the heaven hurl down upon us unexpected events from it; the universe has a precise system. The weighing on the Day of Resurrection is absolute truth. On that Day the scales of the earth, which suffered either from a defect in the instrument with which they were weighed, or a defect in the weighing itself, or being affected by the events of the universe and the interactions occurring within it, will be nullified. As for the scale of heaven, no one has any part in it, and it is affected only by the value of what the human being has done. At that moment He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth.﴾

So it is that the scale in this world may suffer some defect, and likewise ownership (al-mulk); for He, glory be to Him, gave means of possession suited to each person: this one owns such-and-such, another owns such-and-such, and a third owns such-and-such. Then each person disposes of this possession, whether justly or unjustly, according to his choice. But when the Last Day comes, there is no ownership for anyone: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Surah Ghafir 40:16, part of verse]. The matter on that day belongs to Allah alone. If dominion in this world was entrusted by the Truth to His servants, that trusteeship ends on the Last Day: ﴿So whoever's scales are heavy – those are the successful.﴾

And He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿As for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life. And as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss. And what can make you know what that is? It is a fire, intensely hot.﴾ [Surah al-Qari'ah 101:6–11].

Thus the scale makes good deeds heavy and is lightened by evil deeds. We note that the rational division for establishing a scale, a weigher and a thing weighed requires three possibilities: that one pan be heavy and the other light, or that they be equal. But this state does not exist here.

Al-Sha'rawi says: The Truth (al-Haqq) speaks of those whose scales are light, and He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls, for they used to wrong Our signs.﴾

The previous surah also mentioned both cases, and in this surah too He mentioned both cases. It is remarkable that this discourse about heaviness and lightness, without any mention of a third case, namely the case where the two pans are equal, comes at the beginning of Surah al-A'raf. But He, glorified be He, says afterward in Surah al-A'raf:

﴿And upon the heights there are men who recognize each by his mark.﴾ These are the ones whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. Our Lord has made for them a place resembling the mane (urf) of a horse, and the mane of a horse is considered the highest part of it. Sometimes the horse's hair falls to the right, and sometimes it falls to the left, and there is no direction that has more claim to the hair than the other. The Truth has prepared for the People of the Heights a place from which they hear the people of the Fire calling out to the people of the Garden, and the people of the Garden calling out to the people of the Fire, while the People of the Heights sit, neither in the Garden nor in the Fire. They are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, and by this the rational division is confirmed in the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿And upon the heights there are men who recognize each by his mark.﴾ (part of verse 46, Surah al-A'raf).

So their good deeds are not heavy enough to enter them into the Garden, and their bad deeds are not light enough to enter them into the Fire; their scale has its two pans balanced. Some scholars said regarding the scale: there is indeed an actual scale. Others said that what is meant by the scale is the absolute justice established by the Supreme Just. What is more astonishing is that the Truth said there are scales: is there one scale for each person, or for each category of obligations a scale: a scale for creeds and a scale for rulings, and so on? Will our Lord reckon with us in succession, or are there multiple scales? The evidence is that our master Imam Ali, when he was asked: "Will God reckon with all His creation at one time?" replied: "And what is strange about this? Is He not providing for them all at one time?" Thus, regarding God, the matter of the scale is very easy, and He, glorified be He, is not hindered by anything.

﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls, for they used to wrong Our signs.﴾ (part of verse 9, Surah al-A'raf): Yes, they have lost their souls, for each of them used to take up desires and commit sins by which he indulged himself, and on the Last Day he finds that he has lost everything. As the common proverb says: "He lost the skin and the carcass" (khasira al-jild wa al-saqt). Why? The answer comes from the Truth:

﴿for they used to wrong Our signs.﴾

Al-Sha'rawi, in his commentary on Surah 7, verse 10:

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We have certainly established you on the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood. Little are you grateful.﴾

The mumakkin (one who is established) is the one who occupies a place without being displaced; thus it is said: "I have established you in such-and-such," meaning: I have given you the place and no one disputes it with you. God, glory be to Him, has established us on the earth and made for us in it means of sustaining life, the luxuries of life, the adornments of life, and the finery of life. The earth did not withhold when we tilled it; rather, it brought forth crops for us. The sun has not withdrawn from us with its light, its radiance and its heat. Everything in this world performs its task. We were not established on the earth by our own capabilities, but by the power of God. This should never have been absent from our sight. None of us has control over the sun, the moon, the wind or the earth; rather, the One who created them and subjected them is your Lord and their Lord. You are established, and everything responds to you by God's subjugation of it to you.

﴿And We have certainly established you on the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood. Little are you grateful.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). The word "ma'ayish" is the plural of ma'ishah, and ma'ishah means life; al-'aysh is the essentials of life. That is why, in the villages, they called bread 'aysh, because they have an extremely high regard for it, since they knew it to be a fundamental element of life.

The word of the Truth: ﴿little are you grateful﴾ indicates that there are those who give thanks. Among people, some thank God for His blessings in a general way, for the totality of blessings, or thank Him in a specific way for each blessing, down to the individual parts of a single blessing. When he begins to eat, he says: "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and after eating he says: "Praise be to God." And there are those who, when taking a single morsel, say "In the name of God," and when they chew and swallow it, they say "Praise be to God," because it stuck in their throat. Likewise, when we drink, we should drink in three gulps: at the first gulp we say "In the name of God," and when we finish it we say "Praise be to God," and likewise for the second and third. Whoever does this will not be able to commit disobedience for as long as the effects of this sip of water remain in his body, because all of it is "In the name of God." It guards him from sin, because if you were to count a single blessing, you would find in it many blessings.

When you do not give thanks, you are only narrowing for yourselves the doors of God's blessings, for if you thanked Him for the blessings, the blessings would increase upon you: ﴿If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾. And it is folly not to give thanks.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 11:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿And We did create you and then give you shape; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.﴾

The matter of creation has already been addressed in Surat al-Baqarah: the creation of Adam and of Satan. The story is spread over seven surahs, in seven places found in Surat al-Baqarah, Surat al-A'raf, Surat al-Hajj, Surat al-Isra', Surat al-Kahf, Surat Ta-Ha, and Surat Sad. However, the story in each place has multiple snapshots: here is one snapshot, there is a second, and that one is a third, and so on. This is because this is a blessing that God must repeat, so that it settles in the minds of His servants. Had He mentioned it only once, it might be forgotten; therefore God repeats the reminder of it more than once. When God wishes to bring blessings to mind and draw attention to them in various things, He repeats them, as He repeated the bringing to mind of blessings in a single surah in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

He mentions these blessings from their beginning, saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? He let loose the two seas, meeting side by side; between them is a barrier which they do not transgress. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? From them emerge the pearl and the coral.﴾ [Surat al-Rahman]

﴿And His are the ships rising high on the sea like landmarks. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? Everyone upon it is passing away. And there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ [Surat al-Rahman]. After every blessing He says: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

By this, glorified is He, He intends to multiply and repeat their mention upon the ears, so that they settle in the hearts, even in deaf ears. Sometimes He brings it in a matter whose outward appearance is not a blessing, such as His saying: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ [Surat al-Rahman]. The Truth has mentioned all of this because, at the moment when He makes matters clear to us as they really are while we are in the house of obligation (dar al-taklif), this is a mercy and a blessing from Him upon us, because it calls us to guard against what is forbidden and to keep away and withdraw from transgressions.

To God belongs the highest likeness, before and after. When a son enters school, we say to him: "If you fall short in such-and-such, you will fail." By this saying you show him mercy through counsel; you have not left him without making him see the consequences of matters. Likewise, when you see evil befalling the disbelievers, this pleases you, because if the disbelievers were equal to the believers there would be no virtue or distinction for faith. Punishment is a vengeance upon the disbeliever and a blessing upon its counterpart, the believer.

The story of the creation of Adam has come in the Qur'an in all its aspects seven times, because it is the story of the beginning of creation, and it is what answers the question that man seeks an answer to, for he looked around and found himself in a cosmos prepared for him in the best possible way. The universe did not come into being after man; rather, man appeared upon the universe, and the question has continued to arise about how creation came about. The question is as important as the existence of man in the universe. You survey kinds in the cosmos, and each kind has a function. Its function is related to you: a mineral has a function, a plant has a function, an animal has a function, and all of them flow into your service, because the mineral benefits the plant, and draws nourishment from it in order to nourish the animal, and the animal benefits you and nourishes you. Thus all kinds flow into your service. But you, O human, what is your work in this cosmos? Therefore it was necessary for man to learn his function. The Truth, glorified is He, wished to make man aware of his function, because He, may He be exalted, is the Maker, and when man seeks his Maker, the power of God becomes manifest to him in everything He has made. It was also necessary for man to receive news from the Creator.

Glorified is He sends down to us the method from heaven, and this method is accompanied by a miracle at the hand of a messenger. The Truth sent down the method to him and entrusted him with the task of conveying it. The messenger informs, and then we infer from the miracle the truth of his report. It was therefore necessary that we believe the messenger, because he comes with a sign and a miracle from God.

The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought the message at the age of forty, with the miraculous method, and informed us that he was a messenger from God. It was necessary that we investigate, in order to verify the truth of the conveyance from God, by reasoning about his claim. This messenger came forty years after his birth, with a miracle of the kind in which his people excelled, and not of the kind in which he himself excelled. His miracle is not from himself, but from God; because the Messenger brought the miracle after forty years of his birth, and it is not reasonable that genius should burst forth after forty years of birth, for we know that genius appears in the late second decade and early third decade of a person's life. Then we look and find him speaking all the miraculously eloquent speech. Nor is it reasonable that he should bring news of the cosmos, he who was an unlettered man whose father died while he was in his mother's womb, then his mother died when he was six, and likewise his grandfather died. He saw people falling away around him; so who then made him aware that he would be granted respite and his life prolonged until he reached forty, so that he might convey to us his miracle? Therefore we find the Qur'an argue for this, saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ [Surat Yunus, 15]. Thus the strong proof becomes manifest that he, peace and blessings be upon him, is commanded to convey what is revealed to him; and this is confirmed a second time in the Truth's saying: ﴿Say, "If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?"﴾ [Surat Yunus, 16].

Here we find that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, received the command from God to make clear to them: Have you known of me, during my lifetime, that I composed poetry or wisdom, or brought you the like of it? Thus, if we reason the matter, and reflect and contemplate his claim, we shall affirm that he is the Messenger of God, and that the miracle was sent down to him from heaven.

﴿And We did create you and then give you shape; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.﴾ [Surat al-A'raf].

Thus we see that the matter of creation and origination is something the human intellect must investigate, in order to know its function in existence. And when it investigates in order to know its function in existence, it must abandon every guess and conjecture; for this matter cannot be approached with premises present to show us how we were created, nor for what purpose we were created! The manner of creation is an unseen matter, and there is nothing before us from which we can extrapolate to reach it. God has decided the matter of creation, whether concerning the heavens and the earth and what lies between them, or concerning man. He, glorified is He, has decided these two matters, and there is no source of knowledge of the matter in them except from God, glorified is He. He has closed the door of independent reasoning (ijtihad) concerning them, and likewise the door of conjecture, and He named those who undertake every human inquiry in this field as misguided misleaders. Therefore He said, to settle this matter and put an end to it, and to relieve minds from investigating it: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one who would take misleaders as helpers.﴾ [Surat al-Kahf, 51]. It is as if one who says, "How were the heavens and the earth created, and how was man created?" is misguided, because God did not make him witness it, and this speaker was not a helper, nor a support, nor a partner to God.

God, glorified is He, has related to us the story of the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of man, and this verse deals with the creation of man. Whoever investigates inductively and goes back into the past will surely find the matter to be logical, for the world multiplies, and its multiplication is a visible matter; and it is not only among humans, but among those who serve humans from other kinds, we find in them the phenomenon of reproduction, in plants and animals. And if we look at the census from one century and find the number less than the present census, which is five thousand million, and whenever we return to the past the census decreases until we reach two; for creation comes only from two, and God solved the riddle for us, saying: ﴿He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate﴾ [Surat al-Nisa', 1, part of the verse]. This is a sound statement, confirmed by statistics and made certain by them, for the world multiplies with the passage of time into the future. ﴿And from both of them He spread many men and women﴾ [Surat al-Nisa', 1, part of the verse]. This is a true statement. And He, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿And of everything We created two mates﴾ [Surat al-Dhariyat, 49, part of the verse].

He, glorified is He, informed us of the story of Adam and how Eve was created. Did He take a part of Adam and create Eve from it? That may be correct; or did He create from him his mate, meaning that He created her from the same kind and in the same manner? That too is correct. God has been content to mention the creation of Adam rather than the creation of Eve, and gave us the model in one, and said: ﴿and created from it its mate﴾. The word "minha" (from it) in this verse may be partitive, like His saying, the Truth: ﴿a messenger from yourselves﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran, 164, part of the verse]. He, glorified is He, did not take a piece of the Arabs and say that it is "Muhammad"; rather He made Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, of the same kind in creation and origination. And when He speaks here, He says to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place a khalifa (successor) upon the earth﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah, 30, part of the verse], and this is the first announcement; then He followed that with: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾ [Surat al-Hijr, 29]. So before the breathing of the spirit there is shaping; but to whom does the shaping refer, and who is the one "shaped from"? The shaping refers to Adam. It has been said that he was made of clay (salsal), of black mud altered (hama' masnun), of dust, and of mud; these are multiple stages. If He, glorified is He, says of Adam that he was made of dust, we say yes; if He says "of water," we say yes; if He says "of mud," this is a true statement, for water when mixed with dust becomes mud. If He says ﴿of black mud altered﴾, this is permissible, for hama' is mud that has fermented, its smell changed, then dried and became clay (salsal). Thus these are multiple stages of creation. Then the Truth said: ﴿and I breathed into him of My spirit﴾. Thus the chapters of creation are completed. Then He said: ﴿fall down in prostration to him﴾.

The scholars say: the intended meaning of prostration is submission and veneration, not prostration as we know it. Others said: the intended meaning of prostration is the prostration we know, and that Adam was like a qibla, like the Ka'bah toward which we turn in prayer. But we have a remark here, and we say: we prostrate only to God, and since our Lord has said "prostrate," then prostration is compliance with the command of the Creator of Adam. The intention, then, was not worship of Adam, but obedience to the primary command of God. The command to prostrate to Adam was willed by God, because He, glorified is He, subjected the whole cosmos to serve Adam; among the angels are those who manage affairs, among them are guardians, and among them are those who stand in His presence. So the prostration of the angels to Adam was not a submission by the angels to Adam, but

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, as the Noble Qur'an relates:

﴿He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ (7:12)

Then He said, as the Noble Qur'an relates: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ (17:61). Thus the stance was one of arrogance and self-exaltation. And His saying, the Truth: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ (38:75). When we analyse this text, we find His saying ﴿What prevented you﴾, meaning: what held you back. The Qur'an has presented this matter in two styles. The Truth said once: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating?﴾ and said once more: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾. This means that the first style came with the negating "lā" (lā, "not"), while the second style came without the negating "lā". His saying ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ is sound and clear, meaning: what held you back from prostrating. But ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating?﴾ requires a pause. For this reason the scholars said: the "lā" here is superfluous (zā'idah), and among those who were most courteous in their manners, they said: the "lā" is a connective particle (ṣilah). But neither view is satisfactory or appropriate, because whoever said that did not perceive the root *m-n-ʿ* (manaʿa, "to prevent") and the various purposes for which it is used. You say: "I prevented so-and-so from doing such-and-such," as though he was about to do it and you prevented him.

So ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ is as though he had an inclination to prostrate, and then a force stronger than him came, prevented him, held him back and came between him and prostrating. But that did not happen. The verb *manaʿa* is also used for abstention (imtināʿ), where a person refrains from an action because another has persuaded him to abandon prostration, so he is convinced and refrains. There is a difference between *mamnūʿ* (one who is prevented) and *mumtaniʿ* (one who abstains): *mamnūʿ* is what is in ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾, while *mumtaniʿ* means that he refrained of his own accord, and no one prevented him, but he was persuaded. And if prevention is from abstention, the style has come to affirm the actual meaning, which is prevention from prostration. This is the reason for the repetition in the Qur'an. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿He said, "What prevented you from not prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾ (7:12).

He, glory be to Him, had commanded the angels, and Iblis was present with them, either in the way of height, since he surpassed the angels in obeying God while being free to choose, so his rank was high; or in the way of proximity, since the angels are higher than Iblis in their original creation and nature. In whatever state of height or proximity he was, it was incumbent on Iblis to prostrate. But he said in replying to his Lord: ﴿I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.﴾ (7:12).

He, glory be to Him, did not ask Iblis about a comparison between himself and Adam, but asked him while He already knew from eternity that Iblis had refrained by conviction, not by compulsion. For this reason Iblis said: "I am better than him," so the matter revolved in his mind to find a justification for not prostrating. In his Iblisian understanding, it is not proper for the superior to prostrate to the inferior, so as long as Iblis believed that he was better than Adam and thought he was higher than him, it was not proper for him to prostrate to him. And higher than him why? Because he said: ﴿You created me from fire and created him from clay.﴾ So it was as though fire has an elevation, and in this he was completely mistaken, because when kinds differ, it is because each kind has its role. No kind is superior to another: fire has a function, clay has a function, and fire cannot perform the function of clay; one cannot plant in fire.

So excellence is realised in both together, as long as each performs its function. For this reason do not say: "This is better than that," but say: "This one's work is finer than that one's work." Everything in existence, when placed in the station intended for it, is good. For this reason I say: do not say of an iron rod that it is a straight rod, and say of the swallow's bent stick that this stick is crooked, because the function of the swallow requires it to be crooked, and its crookedness is what enables it to perform its function, since excellence is realised among things of equal function. But Iblis said: ﴿I am better than him..﴾ (7:12). He said it out of obstinacy, out of pride, out of disbelief, when he turned away from the command of God and wished to alter the will of God in His command, as though he were finding fault with the Truth in His command and returning the order to the one who gave it. So the recompense of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted be He, to Iblis was only that He said to him: ﴿He said, "Then get down from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so go out; you are indeed among the debased."﴾ (7:13).

Descent (al-hubut) requires moving from a high station to a lower one, and this is what led the scholars to say that the Garden which Allah described as "high" is in the sky. We say: No. Descent does not necessarily have to be a spatial descent; it may be a descent of rank (hubut makanah), and there is a difference between descent of place (hubut al-makan) and descent of rank (hubut al-makanah). The Truth said to Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿It was said, "O Nuh, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations [descended] from those who are with you…"﴾ [Surah Hud, 48].

That is, "Descend from the ship." Therefore, the root h-b-t does not signify descent from a higher place to a lower place; rather, we say it is from a place or from a rank: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it"﴾. This is a demotion from rank, because he was no longer fit to be in the presence of the angels. He had been in the presence of the angels because he had bound himself to obedience, and he was created to be free to obey or to disobey. When this quality left him, he was no longer fit to remain in this station, for the angels do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded. ﴿He said, "Then descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein…"﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 13]: that is, it is not befitting for you to be arrogant in it.

Your refusing a command from the One worshipped, when He has directed it to you while you are the worshipper, is a kind of arrogance toward the one who commands. The angels are a group who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded. So as long as you are one who is proud and exalts himself over this station, you are not fit for it. It is as if the work was what qualified him to be in the height, and when it departed from him and left him, he became fit to be in the lowness. Thus the matter was not tied to essence (al-dhatiyyah). In this there is a lowering of the value of his statement that he is from fire and Adam is from clay, because the measure by which matters are weighed is the measure of performing the work. And among the wisdom of the Truth is that the jinn take on the capacity for things which humans cannot do, such as speed, piercing barriers, and overcoming some causes. The jinn may pass through a wall or a body, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed the devil runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs (through him)"(1). That is like a [hidden] illness, because this is the nature of fire, the element from which he was created, and it transgresses barriers. The jinn have attained such subtlety and transparency that they can pass through anything. But Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, wished to show the jinn: do not think that your element is what gave you this distinction; rather, it is the will of the One who gave the element, as evidence that He made you lower in rank than man. He, glory be to Him, makes a human, such as our master Sulayman, one whom you serve, O jinni; He subjects you and makes you serve him. And in the assembly of Sulayman, He made the one who had knowledge of the Book bring a power greater than the power of an "ifrit" of the jinn. The Truth is the One who says: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said…﴾ [Surah al-Naml, 39]: and this indicates that there are also clever and foolish ones in the world of the jinn. The one who had knowledge of the Book surpassed the ifrit of the jinn in time, for this ifrit had said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place…﴾ [Surah al-Naml, 39].

The maqam is the span of time in which Sulayman may sit in his assembly. So what did the one who had knowledge of the Book say, and he was a human?

﴿He said, "The one who had knowledge of the Book said, 'I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you…"﴾ [Surah al-Naml, 40]: as if he would bring the throne of Bilqis before Sulayman finished returning his glance, which he had sent to look at something. Sulayman saw the throne before him, and for this reason the Qur'anic expression is eloquent: ﴿So when he saw it settled beside him﴾ [Surah al-Naml, 40]: as if the matter did not bear delay, but was executed immediately. Thus the Truth makes clear to created beings of the elements: beware that you understand your distinction by your elements; I am able, by the freedom of My power, to make the lower control the higher, because it is the will of the Element of elements. ﴿He said, "Then descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so go out; indeed you are among the debased"﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 13]. The word ﴿fahbit﴾ indicates and shows that descent is a matter of meaning, that is, you are not fit for this rank or that station. This is what the word ﴿fahbit﴾ indicates; then the command to leave the place came afterward.

Al-saghar is humiliation and abasement; because he met the command with arrogance, he must be recompensed with humiliation. Thus he was treated in the opposite of his aim, and treatment in the opposite of one's aim is a kind of discipline, refinement and instruction, just as the Law establishes that one who kills a victim is deprived of his inheritance from him, because he killed him to hasten the inheritance; therefore Allah willed to deprive him of the inheritance, and by committing the killing he became barred from inheritance.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, Muslim in al-Salam, Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, Ibn Majah in al-Sawm, and Ahmad 3/156, 285, 337.

Then the Truth (may He be exalted) says after that: ﴿He said, "Give me respite until the day they are raised."﴾

The meaning of ﴿anzirni﴾ ("give me respite") is "grant me a delay," i.e., do not hasten to punish me, and do not make my term close at hand. This is shown by His words, glorified is He: ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those given respite."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 15:

Al-inzar (respite) is the request for a postponement and for death not to be hastened. Iblis requested it so that he could satisfy his rancor against the children of Adam and Adam himself, because he had brought upon him humiliation (al-sigar), abasement (al-dhillah), expulsion (al-tard) and descent (al-hubut). For this reason he insisted on striving to lead the children of Adam astray so that they too would become disobedient.

It is as if Iblis, in this request, wanted to escape death and to remain alive until the Day of Resurrection (yawm al-ba'th), on which everyone who has died will be raised. It is as if he wanted to leap over the word of the Truth: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ (Qur'an 3:185). So God made clear that your postponement extends to the appointed time (yawm al-waqt al-ma'lum), known to Us and unknown to you. For if the term were known, one who knew it might disobey for a long period and then perform righteous deeds just before the appointed term. But God, by keeping the time of death hidden, intended that its time be expected at every moment.

In another verse the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Until the appointed day﴾ (Qur'an 15:38). The appointed time (al-waqt al-ma'lum) is the first blast:

﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾ (Qur'an 39:68).

It is as if Iblis wanted to flee from death in order to reach the second blast, but our Lord made clear that he remains until a known time, and the end of this known time must be before the first blast.

Then the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.﴾ (7:16)

Al-Ighwa': enticement to disobedience. From ighwa' is al-ghayy, which is destruction. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿...so they will meet with ghayy (destruction)﴾ [Maryam: 59].

When we read ﴿fa-bima aghwaytani﴾ it means: "Then by Your enticing me, O Allah, I will do such-and-such." In this way he attributes the enticement to Allah. But does our Lord lead astray or guide? Allah guides with guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala) and guidance of enablement (hidayat al-tamkin). We have previously spoken at length about hidayat al-dalala and dalalat al-tamkin. Allah, glorified is He, created Satan with choice, and did not create him compelled and subjugated like the angels. Because he was created with choice, He gave him the opportunity to obey and to disobey. It is as if Satan, by this statement, wishes that he had been created compelled. He says that Allah is the one who gave him the cause of disobedience. He did not consider that choice is an opportunity not only for misguidance, but also an opportunity for guidance. And you, O Satan, are the one who chose misguidance.

So Satan's statement ﴿fa-bima aghwaytani﴾ intends by it that he, through his disobedience, cast doubt upon Allah. We say to him: No, our Lord did not lead astray, because the Truth, glorified and exalted, does not lead astray but guides. For if Allah had created him compelled and subjugated, He would not have given him the opportunity to choose this or that. He created him in the form of "do" and "do not do," and he chose to do nothing but disobedience. ﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path."﴾ (7:16). What is understood from the phrase is that "them" are the children of Adam. Al-qu'ud (sitting) is a kind of the active body's movement, because the one who moves is either standing, or sitting, or lying down asleep. The most restful state is lying down asleep, because the body in this state is at rest by the force of earth's gravity. When a person is sitting, gravity presses on him a little; when standing, he carries the weight of his body on his feet. That is why we say to someone who has stood a long time on his feet: "Sit until you rest," and if he sat and was tired, it is said to him: "Lie down a little to rest."

Why did Satan choose to say ﴿la-aq'udanna (I will surely sit)﴾? So that he would be at ease, since he had tired of standing. Also, while in the sitting position he remains alert and watchful. The Truth says: ﴿and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush...﴾ [al-Tawba: 5]. He did not say "stand," so that people would not exhaust themselves with long standing; rather, at the moment they face the matter, they must rise. Sitting is closer to standing, because lying down is closer to slackness and sleep. Satan chose the position that preserves his strength and keeps his attention: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.﴾ Since Satan will lead astray, and will misguide others, he will choose for misguidance those who are on the path of guidance. As for one who goes astray by his own choice and is lost by his own nature, Satan has been relieved of him and does not want him. This is a phenomenon that happens to people when they strive and exert themselves in obedience. The young man who is obedient and committed finds that Satan tries to tempt him to turn him away from prayer and obedience, because Satan spies on a person's religion. He is like a thief, and a thief does not circle around a ruined house; the thief circles around a house full of good.

We notice this matter in everyone who comes to prayer. One of them says: "When I pray, the whisperings come to me and make me doubt the prayer." We say to him: Yes, this is true. When this whispering comes to you, consider it a healthy sign in faith, because it means that Satan knows your deed is accepted, and therefore he tries to spoil your obedience for you. For if you were corrupt from the beginning, and you stood for prayer without wudu', the whispering would not have come to you. But Satan wants to spoil your obedience, and therefore Allah says: ﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should touch you, seek refuge in Allah...﴾ (7:200).

Why? Because Allah created you and created him. Although you cannot repel him, since he flows in you like blood in the veins and penetrates you with thoughts and sensations that you cannot control; he brings you the most important matters at the time of prayer, so you remember things you did not remember, and he brings you the most complex problems while you are praying. All of that is because he said: ﴿la-aq'udanna lahum sirataka al-mustaqim (I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path)﴾, and he did not say that he would sit on the crooked path. Satan will not sit in a wine gathering, but he sits at the doors of mosques or inside mosques to spoil people's righteous deeds. So what do we do in this situation? The Truth, glorified is He, directs us to seek refuge: ﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah.﴾ The meaning of ﴿fa-ista'idh﴾ is: then take refuge from him with Allah. For Allah, who gave him the capacity to penetrate you, into your blood, and into your thoughts, is the One able to prevent him. When you say "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan" with alarm and turning to Him, glorified is He, He, majestic in His glory, rescues you from him. If you are reciting the Qur'an and a thought from Satan comes to you, say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." When you say this, it is as if you have alerted him that you have realized where this prompting came from: once, twice, and thrice. Then Satan says to himself: "This believer is shrewd, alert, and wary; I cannot mislead him. Let me search for someone else."

That is why we saw Imam Abu Hanifa, who was famous for giving fatwas, when a questioner came to him saying: "I lost money that I had buried in a piece of land, and I do not know its place now. Guide me to it, O Shaykh." Naturally this question was outside the realm of knowledge. Abu Hanifa said: "My son, there is nothing of knowledge in that, but I will devise a way for you: when night comes, stand before your Lord praying this night, perhaps Allah, glorified and exalted, will send you one of His soldiers who will tell you the place of your money."

While Abu Hanifa was performing the dawn prayer, behold, the man came, smiling and laughing, saying: "O Imam, I have found the money!" Abu Hanifa laughed and said: "By Allah, I knew that Satan would not let you complete your night with your Lord, and he would come to tell you. Would that you had completed it in gratitude to Allah. Come, stand for the prayer." Thus Satan knows how to sit in wait and how to swear oaths, for in another verse he says: ﴿He said: "Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all."﴾ (38:82). He was able to bring the oath that helps him in his mission; he said: ﴿fa-bi-'izzatika la-ughwiyannahum (then by Your might I will surely mislead them)﴾, meaning: by Your independence from Your creation and Your lack of need for them, for You are the Victor who is not overpowered; for if You willed them, I could not have taken them. But You willed that each person choose: ﴿Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (18:29).

So he swore, and through this door Satan enters upon man: ﴿fa-bi-'izzatika la-ughwiyannahum ajma'in (then by Your might I will surely mislead them all)﴾. Then he made an exception to himself and said: ﴿except Your chosen servants among them﴾ (38:83), because the one whom Allah wills to be guided, Satan cannot mislead, for he does not contend with our Lord or oppose Him; rather he contends with the creatures of Allah, and does not enter into battle with our Lord, but enters into battle with His creatures, in a battle in which he has neither argument nor strength. For the one who prevails in battles either compels you to act, or persuades you to act without compulsion. Does Iblis possess either of these? No. Therefore in the Hereafter he will say: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me﴾ (14:22). Authority is of two kinds: authority that overpowers, and authority that persuades. Satan enters upon man through these doors.

Al-Sha'rawi says: The Truth then says, on the tongue of Iblis (Satan):

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left. And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾

That which is "before them" is what lies ahead, and "from behind them" means from the back; "from their right" means from the right side, and "from their left" means from the left side. The thing that lies ahead of the whole world, toward which we are all moving, is ﴿the Hereafter﴾. When Satan comes from the front, he casts doubt upon them regarding the reality of the Hereafter and casts doubt upon the Resurrection. He tries to make the human being not turn toward the way of God, so that he becomes one of those who do not believe in meeting God and who doubt the existence of another abode in which the good-doer will be recompensed for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. This has indeed happened, and we have found those who say, with the tongue of their state, the Qur'an's words: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? Or our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ (Surat al-Saffat). Therefore the Truth presents the matter of the Resurrection in a way that leaves Satan no opening in it. He makes clear to us that He, glory be to Him, was not unable to create us at first; so He will not be unable to restore us, and restoration is surely easier than initiation, because He will restore them from something existing, whereas initiation was from nothing. When He, glory be to Him, makes clear to people that restoration is easier than initiation, He is addressing them in terms they cannot find a way to deny. Otherwise, before the perfect power of God, all works are equal: nothing is easy and minor for Him and another thing difficult and arduous. He, glory be to Him, informs us of the completeness of His knowledge, saying: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Book﴾ (Surat Qaf). That is, every single thing has a written record containing all its elements and parts.

Satan also comes from behind, and behind each of us are our descendants, whom we fear to leave in want. So Satan whispers to some people to commit theft, plunder or bribery for the sake of the future of their children, and the corruption of many people comes from this direction. Such corruption also comes when some people reach a high position and their age has grown great, and they turn to God with evil, thinking they are leaving their dependants in good condition. But if you truly fear for them, then entrust them into the hand of their Lord, and do not secure their lives in another direction.

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear God and speak words of rectitude.﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', 9)

As for why Satan does not come to the human being from above and from below: the above is the direction to which one turns seeking aid and refuge with his Lord, and the below is the direction of particular servitude, for the servant is closest to his Lord when he is prostrating. In these two states he is protected from Satan's domination over him, because God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority.﴾ And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left. And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

Satan comes from the right to make people disinclined toward good deeds and obedience and to turn them away from doing good. The right is the symbol of good deeds, because the recorder of good deeds is on the right and the recorder of evil deeds is on the left. He comes from their left to tempt them with the desires of disobedience.

We notice that the Truth used the expression ﴿from their right﴾ and ﴿from their left﴾ and did not use "ʿalā" (on), because "ʿalā" implies dominance, and Satan has no dominance at all, since he possesses neither the power of compulsion that prevents, nor the power of argument that convinces. And because most people do not remember to thank those who have bestowed blessings upon them, Satan skillfully misguides them. Therefore the Truth, as a concluding appendage to the verse, says: ﴿... And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿He said, "Get out of it, disgraced and banished. Whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with all of you."﴾

Pride has so deluded Satan that he imagines himself clever. He explained to us his plan and method, and thereby showed us that Allah's judgment against him has taken effect, by making his scheming weak. Glorified is He who said: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak.﴾ (Surah an-Nisa, 4:76)

The Truth has alerted us to Satan's scheming and deception, and the sincere advisor is the one who takes precautions and builds immunity against Satan's whisperings. Here the Truth says: ﴿He said, "Get out of it, disgraced and banished..."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:18). The Truth had said to him earlier: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the debased."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:13). So there is a descent and a departure in humiliation, and a leaving of the place. Then here there is also an affirmation that, upon his departure, he will be accompanied by blame, humiliation, expulsion and curse.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...Whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with all of you.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:18). In this is a declaration to those who follow Satan that they are people of Hell. Allah did not prepare Hell merely to hold the disbelievers. Rather, He prepared it on the basis that all creation might disbelieve in Him, just as He prepared Paradise on the basis that all creation would believe in Him. He has no lack of space: if all creation believes, He has prepared Paradise to receive them all, and if they all disbelieve, He has prepared the Fire for them all. This confirms the Truth's words: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 23:10-11), and His words: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship other than Allah are firewood for Hell; you will be its entrants.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya, 21:98).

With this, we have explained the matter of Iblis, who refused to obey the command of the Supreme Commander to prostrate to Adam.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 19:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (19)

The Qur'an returns to the subject of Adam after dealing with the matter of Iblis, saying: ﴿And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden.﴾ Many scholars have transmitted the knowledge, through widespread transmission, that the Garden is the Garden of the Hereafter and of eternity. Some have objected, asking: How does Iblis enter the Garden of eternity? And how does he leave it? And does one who enters the Garden leave it?

Those scholars who said that the Garden is the Garden of the Hereafter did not pay attention to the meaning of the word "jannah" (garden). When the word "jannah" is uttered, it takes what is called in the language "dominance of usage" (ghalabat al-isti'mal), that is, the word is taken from its many meanings to a single meaning that stands alone by convention, such that when it is heard the mind turns to it. So, O believer, when you hear the word "jannah," your mind turns to the Garden of the Hereafter, because it is the one that is truly regarded as a garden.
