But when the word comes in the Qur'an and the speaker is God, we must first study the word and its uses in the language, because the Qur'an came in a clear Arabic tongue, and it is permissible for a word to exist in the language with several meanings. When the matter concerns religion and jurisprudence, we take the word from its linguistic meaning and cause it to refer to its technical legal meaning.

An example of this is the word "hajj." When you hear the word "hajj," you say: it is the intention to the Sacred House of God for rites and worship in specified months, although "hajj" in the language means "intention": if you intend anything you say, "I have hajjed to it" (hajjtu ilayhi). When Islam came, it took this word from the language and used it for the hajj in its legal sense, namely the intention to the Sacred House for the rites. Likewise the word "salah": in the language it means supplication. God's saying, ﴿And pray for them (wa salli 'alayhim)﴾, means: supplicate for them. When Islam came, it took the word from the language and made it apply to a new technical meaning, such that when it is uttered it refers to that meaning: the specific sayings and actions, begun with the takbir and concluded with the taslim, with their particular conditions.

But does our taking the word from the language, and the Law giving it a technical meaning, mean abandoning its original meaning? No. For if you wish to use it in its original meaning, you may do so, but you will need an indicator (qarinah) showing that you do not mean the legal prayer, since the word "salah" has come to denote the five well-known daily prayers, although its original meaning was supplication. This is what led the scholars to hold that the word "jannah," when uttered, turns the mind to the eternal Garden. We say: the linguistic meaning of "jannah" is a place in which there are dense and varied trees; their density and height screen a person and shield him from everything around him, and as for the fruits, necessities and luxuries in it, that is because it screens a person from what is outside it, and he is content simply to be within it. The Qur'an has not used "jannah" in the sense of the Garden of eternity only, but also says: ﴿Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines?﴾ (Qur'an 2:266), and likewise the Exalted says: ﴿And present to them a parable of two men: for one of them We made two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with palm trees, and between them We placed fields of crops﴾ (Qur'an 18:32), and the Truth's saying: ﴿There was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left. "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him: a good land and a forgiving Lord."﴾ (Qur'an 34:15).

And I say: we must investigate the horizons of God's intended meanings when He teaches us from Himself and makes us stand on the meaning intended. We know that the first message that came from God concerning Adam informed us that He created Adam as a khalifah on earth: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah﴾ (Qur'an 2:30). So Adam was created for the earth, and let us not wrong Adam by saying he was created for the Garden, and that we would have lived in it, but he disobeyed and we were sent down to earth. Therefore we say: No. We must remember that the first message from God about Adam is that He placed him on earth as a khalifah. What we should have asked is: since God made him a khalifah on earth, what then brought about this story of the Garden?

God created Adam to be a khalifah on earth, and he was to receive from God obligations confined to "do" and "do not do," for if you do not comply, corruption will appear in society. As for what gives rise to no corruption, He, glorified be He, leaves it permissible; therefore, whatever does not involve "do" and "do not do" does not corrupt society. So "do" and "do not do" are the measure of guaranteeing righteousness on earth.

And did God create man like this, without disturbances that spoil for him the way of God? No. Since Satan took this stance toward Adam and said, "I will mislead them," he will beautify for you the "do" and the "do not do": when the command to pray comes to you, Satan will prod you so that you do not pray; when the command not to drink wine comes to you, Satan will beautify for you drinking it, and he will try to shift the domain of "do" into the domain of "do not do," and likewise he will try to beautify for you "doing" what is in the domain of "do not do," so that your movement is thrown into confusion.

The Truth, glorified be He, wants a method that governs the movement of life and guarantees that the khilafah on earth performs its mission in a way that makes man happy in this world and blessed in the Hereafter. Therefore the Truth had to train His khalifah on earth in the method, so that he does not receive the method only theoretically. Hence He, glorified and exalted be He, willed not to let Adam undertake the mission of khilafah until He had given him training in the mission in "do" and "do not do." He warned him of the obstacles that stand in the way of "do," so that they do not come into the domain of "do not do," and likewise of the obstacles in the domain of "do not do," so that they do not come into the domain of "do." He chose for him a place containing every requisite of life and its luxury, so that he would not tire at all in anything during the training, and He made clear to him that this Garden, a beautiful orchard containing every requisite of life and its luxury, and He commanded him: eat from everything in it, and do not approach this tree.

"Eat" is the command, and "do not approach" is the prohibition. God made clear to Adam that the one who would disturb his application of God's method is the enemy whose enmity is established, namely Iblis, for when he refused to prostrate to Adam he received expulsion and curse, so he swore and said: ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all"﴾ (Qur'an 38:82).

It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, made the Garden as a place containing every requisite of life for Adam, by God's making and preparation, and gave him of it the measure that supplies the requisite without excess that would weary him, nor bloating, nor suffering hardships of health, etc.; for He, glorified be He, gives Adam the sufficient measure. And He is capable of all things, as evidenced by His nurturing the fetus in its mother's womb: the fetus grows, and growth means that it receives nourishment and does not expel waste, because the nourishment that God causes to enter it is only according to its growth. And since our Lord is the One who supplies the training garden with nourishment, He is capable of complete preparation.

Thus the Garden in which Adam was initially placed is not the Garden of recompense, because the Garden of recompense must come after obligation; there can be no obligation in it, and whoever dwells in it does not leave it. And Adam, as we know, was created for the earth; so the presence of the Garden here means that it is a place of training for the mission of khilafah, a matter embodied in "so eat" and a prohibition embodied in "do not approach." He did not say to them, "Do not eat," but said, "do not approach," because approaching is a likely path to seduction and leads to it. And he ate from it because he came toward it and drew near to it; had he listened and not drawn near, he would not have eaten from it.

So God established for Adam in the Garden of training and drill two symbols: the first symbol for "do," and the second symbol for "do not do." We find that what God forbade is few compared with what He permitted and commanded. This is from God's mercy to the servants: the believer does what he is commanded and does not hover around what God has forbidden, because when he sees what God forbade he is not safe from his soul inclining toward it. That is why He said: ﴿And do not approach﴾, for had they not approached, the tree would not have tempted them with any sight. For this reason, in many matters that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, forbids, and at the top of which are those that protect and preserve the basic creed, He says "do not approach" or "avoid." He, glorified be He, is the One who says: ﴿So avoid the filth of idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾ (Qur'an 22:30); He did not say "do not worship idols" but said: ﴿so avoid﴾. And regarding wine too He came with avoidance. But some superficial people say: no prohibition of wine was revealed, rather it says "avoid." We say to them: avoidance is stronger than mere prohibition, because the ultimate aim of prohibition is that it prevents you from drinking wine; but avoidance requires that you not go toward it, nor sit in the place where it is found, nor press it, nor carry it. {.. And do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers (19)} [Surah al-A'raf]: wrongdoing (zulm) is transgressing the limit or giving a person what is not his right. God makes clear: I did not give you a right to approach the side of this tree; whoever of you approaches it has violated what I legislated for you. {Lest you be among the wrongdoers}, that is, you enter into the category of those who wrong themselves, because God does not wrong anyone, while you wrong yourself, since you give a small desire for a short time and afterward receive its punishment, a painful torment for a long time and in a more severe form. This is wronging yourself, and it is also proof that you cannot be trusted with yourself.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 7, verse 20:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Then Satan whispered to them both, to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts, and said: "Your Lord has forbidden you this tree only lest you become angels or become among the immortals."﴾

The word "waswasa" (whispered) indicates murmuring and seduction. We know that one who speaks of good does not mind that people hear him, but one who speaks of evil whispers for fear that someone will expose him. It is as if every evil must come in a whisper, and its doer knows that this speech should not be happening, feels ashamed of it, and does not want society to know about it. "Waswasa" is derived from an enticing sound, because the waswasa is the sound of the ringing of gold and jewelry. Thus what Satan said to Adam and his wife was an enticing speech meant to divert them from the commands of a wise Lord.

His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾ gives us the grounds for Eve's innocence, because it is commonly believed that Eve was the one who insisted that Adam eat from the tree, and many of us wrong Eve, although the Qur'an affirms that the whispering was directed at Adam and Eve together. ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both, to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾ (part of verse 20 of Surah al-A'raf). Did Satan whisper to them in order to reveal to them what was concealed of their private parts, or did he whisper so that they would disobey God? He whispered so that they would disobey God, and he knew that there was a punishment for disobedience, and he knew that when they ate of what our Lord had forbidden, their private parts would become visible. "Al-sau'a" (the awrah, private part) is that which is displeasing to look at, and we use it for the 'awra (the parts of the body that must be covered), and human nature shrinks from seeing the fully human being's awrah. It is as if, at the beginning, neither of them had seen the other's awrah or their own, because the Truth says: ﴿to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾.

The private parts are four: two for the man and two for the woman. So it is as if each of them could not see their own two, and likewise could not see the other's two, because all the private parts have something that hides them from sight, and this is very reasonable speech. Did not our lady, the Mother of the Believers 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), say: "I have never seen, nor do I see, of myself [anything]"? In this statement is the peak of modesty, because she did not even come to the expression, since the organ, as long as it is an awrah, is built upon concealment. This was when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke and said: ("O people, you will be gathered before Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, 'as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise upon Us; indeed We will be doing it'"). 'A'isha was amazed, and he said to her: "The matter is too serious for anyone to look at anyone."

﴿to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾ (part of verse 20 of Surah al-A'raf). With what had it been concealed? There must have been a garment on each of them, and the scholars have said much about this garment. Some say: the fingernails of a human being are the remnant of the garment that existed with Adam and Eve, which used to conceal the private parts. And it is said: any person who is in a state of extreme laughter and expansiveness, and wants to restrain himself, and prevent himself and stop himself from laughing, will find that this happens to him if he looks at his fingernails; then he cannot laugh, because it is a remnant of the moment of regret over the exposure of the private part. Try it on yourself, and you will find yourself prevented from laughing, and this is a work of the work of the God.

Or the veil that concealed the private part was the divine light that enveloped them, and very intense light, when it envelops, does not reveal. It is true that by light you see things, but if it intensifies it blinds you to things and hides them so that you do not see them, because any matter that exceeds its limit turns into its opposite. So either the garment was the fingernails, or it was the divine light that covered them and concealed the private part. The private part has been called "sau'a" and "'awra" because it is displeasing (tasu'u); so why is it displeasing? And what is the difference between two openings: an opening in the mouth and an opening in the 'awra?

The opening of the 'awra is "sau'a" in terms of what comes out of it. When they were eating from the provision of our Lord, they did not, as we have said, need to expel waste, because God's provision gives each of them sufficiently for movement and action, and the matter was merely openings resembling one another. But when they departed from God's intentions regarding food, and ate other than what God had commanded, and practiced choosing food, the waste began to come out, with its unacceptable smell. So is the appearance of the private part to them a symbol that there is a violation of God's methodology, whether in values and moral matters or in material matters?

Yes; because everything in which God's methodology is violated must reveal an 'awra, and if you see any 'awra in society, know that one of God's methodologies has been disabled. The Qur'an conveys what Satan said to them as whispering: ﴿And he said: "Your Lord has forbidden you this tree only lest you become angels or become among the immortals."﴾ (part of verse 20 of Surah al-A'raf). He whispered and inspired them that the Truth wanted them not to approach this tree, because whoever eats from it becomes an angel or immortal. Neither of them examined Satan's words to know that his scheming was weak, flimsy and stupid; for if he knew that whoever eats from this tree becomes an angel or remains among the immortals, why did he not snatch from it what would make him an angel or immortal? In this is a lesson showing us that whoever is made to look attractive and is confronted by someone with seduction must examine carefully which seduction he is following, and scrutinize the consequences of what he is about to do.

And if Satan said: ﴿He said: "Give me respite until the day they are raised."﴾ (part of verse 20 of Surah al-A'raf) — then why did he not save himself entirely by eating from this tree and end the matter? Therefore, what Satan was saying was a lie.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says: ﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors."﴾

"Qasama" is a verb of the mufa'ala pattern, which generally denotes participation: there are two parties, each of whom is an agent in one respect and an object in another, like "shaarak Zaid 'Amran" (Zaid made 'Amr a partner), which also means that 'Amr made Zaid a partner. Thus the pattern fa'ala and tafa'ala works so that each is an agent from one aspect and an object from another. In meaning, we find both as agent and object, so "qasama" requires two actions. Did Iblis then sit and swear to Adam and his wife while they swore back? We say no, because this pattern sometimes comes without the sense of mutuality, or in the sense of mufa'ala lazima (intransitive reciprocity). The intransitive mufa'ala is evident in the Truth's saying: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾ (part of verse 142, Surat al-A'raf). "Wa'adna" (We appointed) is like a form of fa'ala: who made the appointment? It is Allah who promised Moses (peace be upon him), and Moses entered into the promise by accepting it and fulfilling it.

So "qasamahuma" means they accepted the oath and entered into it.

﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf): "Qasama" means "aqsama" (he swore). Therefore, when our Lord reproached our master Adam, He made clear (glorified is He): "I said that he is an enemy to you and to your wife, and he will surely expel you both from the Garden so that you will toil and suffer." Adam said: "My Lord, I did not believe that any of Your creatures would swear by You to falsehood." It did not occur to the mind that a creature would swear by Allah to falsehood. This was the first deception in creation. Hence Qatada (may Allah be pleased with him) says: "The believer in Allah is deceived." The Prophet (ﷺ) married a woman who entered upon him, and from the cunning of women, his wives, who feared that he would become overly enamoured of her, said to her: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loves this word, so when he comes to you, say it! Say: 'I seek refuge in Allah from you.'" When the Messenger of Allah entered upon her, she said to him: "I seek refuge in Allah from you." He said to her: "You have sought refuge in One who grants refuge." And the Messenger did not approach her. This explains to us how the believer in Allah is deceived. Likewise, our master Abdullah ibn Umar used to free those slaves who performed the prayer well, perfected it, observed its times, and stood in it humbly. When the slaves learned of this, they made a practice of performing prayer in front of the place where he sat, and they would perform it with humility. He (may Allah be pleased with him) would free them. Someone came to him and said: "The slaves are deceiving you," and he said: "Whoever deceives us by Allah, we allow ourselves to be deceived by him."

The advice here is an incitement to oppose the command of Allah. Adam should not have been heedless, and he should have weighed the two matters: Satan's seduction to eat, against the command of the Truth (glorified is He), who said to him and to his wife: "Do not approach this tree." But he did not comply.

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿So He caused them to fall by deception. And when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to join over themselves from the leaves of the Garden. And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?"﴾ (7:22).

﴿فَدَلَّاهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ﴾ means: He brought them down from the rank of obedience to the depth of disobedience and sin, by the deception with which He (Satan) deceived them and tricked them with the oath. "Dalla" is derived from "dallā rijlayhi fi al-bi'r" (he lowered his legs into the well) to see whether there is water in it or not, or "dalla habl al-dalw" (he lowered the bucket rope) to let it down into the well. Its meaning: he does the thing once and then again. "Bi-ghurur" means "by enticement" so as to bring them into disobedience: he showed them sincere advice and concealed deceit.

Here is a pause that indicates the struggle between truth and falsehood within the soul. ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ﴾ This indicates that by the mere tasting, they both recalled that the incitement came from Iblis, which had led them to go to the tree, and that what they had taken was only a taste; so both of them became aware of the gravity of the matter.

﴿فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآَتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ [part of verse 22, surah al-A'raf]: "Al-khasf" (joining, patching) means you bring something and stick it onto something to cover another thing. In the past, when the sole of a shoe wore out and a tear appeared, the cobbler would place over it a patch of leather wider than the tear so that it would hold.

Thus Adam and Eve did: they took from the leaves of the Garden and placed one leaf upon another to cover their private parts. The Truth's words ﴿وَطَفِقَا﴾ mean that they made from the leaves of the tree a covering for their private parts.

Here the Truth says: ﴿And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?"﴾ [part of verse 22, surah al-A'raf]: The obligation here was in one matter, while permission was in many matters, and He, glory be to Him, obligated them only with one matter, namely not approaching the tree, while what was permitted was abundant; therefore it was not fitting that they should forget the obligation. This command was not delivered through an intermediary but directly, and for this reason this situation will help us understand a scene of the story in another surah, namely the Truth's words ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray﴾ [part of verse 121, surah Ta-Ha]. Here the Truth did not mention the account of the disobedience, and said to them: ﴿Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?﴾ [part of verse 22, surah al-A'raf].

He, glory be to Him, does not declare something sinful except by explicit text, and He had already said: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾, and clarified that there is a seductive element, namely Iblis, whose enmity was established earlier when he refused to prostrate, for which reason the Truth expelled him. So if He seized them and punished them for this sin, then He is the Just, and they are the ones who wronged themselves. And the answer had to be: "Yes, our Lord, You did forbid us, and You told us that." This is presenting the ruling with the strongest of proofs, because a ruling may come by informing, and it may come by a question in affirmative form, and it is stronger if it comes as a question in negative form.

﴿إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ [part of verse 22, surah al-A'raf]: We know that "al-'aduw" (enemy) is the adversary who wishes to inflict harm and injury upon you, and "mubin" means "encompassing," and this is evidence showing Satan's enmity and its encompassing nature, because it has already been made clear that he will come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left. Or it means: it clarifies the enmity and is a fierce adversary.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 23:

The confession of sin comes from Adam and Hawwa' (Eve): ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾

These are the words of which Allah said in another context: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah]. So it is as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, decreed the heedlessness of His creation regarding the method (manhaj), and so He legislated for them the means of repentance to Him. The means of repentance have three stages: its legislation is a mercy; then the sinner turns to it, with acknowledgment and return (inabah), and its acceptance from Him, glorified is He, is a mercy. The legislation asks you to act, and when you repent, Allah turns to you. The legislation of repentance is therefore a mercy, not only for the sinner but for others as well, because if Allah had not legislated repentance, the one who commits a disobedience and finds no forgiveness would spread in sins, and when he spreads in sins, the whole society suffers.

﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf). This is the stance after sin of Adam and his wife, and it differs from the stance of Iblis after sin. Iblis wanted to justify the transgression: ﴿He said: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 61). So what did Adam and Hawwa' say? ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 23).

Therefore, the recompense of Iblis, who refused the commands of Allah and His judgment, was to be expelled from His mercy, while the recompense of one who acknowledges that he has sinned and that he has wronged himself is that his repentance is accepted. Thus it is not correct for people who persist in disobedience to say, "These are my circumstances," justifying and rationalizing the sins they commit. Rather, each of them should not expel himself from the realm of mercy, and he should say: "What I do is forbidden, but I cannot control myself." By this he has not rejected the ruling; rather, he has charged himself with shortcoming and acknowledged the sin, and thus he becomes worthy of forgiveness and worthy of repentance.

Here we ask: what is the difference between the disobedience of Iblis and the disobedience of Adam? We say: Iblis disobeyed and came with the stance of rejecting the command, but Adam disobeyed and acknowledged the sin and sought forgiveness.

When Adam and his wife Hawwa' said, ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾ together, in one breath and with a sorrowful tone, does that not indicate that they had learned it? If each of them had apologized to Allah alone, they would have differed in the manner of apology. This is evidence that it was taught to them, and for this reason our Lord said: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 37). They both said ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾, and "anfusana" is the plural of "nafs" (self); they did not say "nafsayna" (the dual), but said "anfusana", meaning that their hearts too had been purified and cleansed of the effect of that sin, and that this remains buried and embedded in the souls of their offspring.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others. On earth you will have a dwelling-place and provision for a time."﴾

We turn and find that there was already a command to Iblis to descend, and here is another command to descend. By God, if the Garden of eternity were their place of residence, and Adam had been created for it, then sinned, then repented, they would never have been taken out of it. But He, glory be to Him, commanded Adam to descend to the earth in which He made him a khalifah (vicegerent), so that he might undertake the task of vicegerency within the framework of the trial that befell him. He must respect God's command in every obligation, and respect God's prohibition in every obligation, and beware of the enmity of Satan, for he will whisper to him. He has already tested this himself, so let him descend equipped with the experience, and he has no excuse after that. ﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others."﴾ The address here is in the plural, and He did not say "go down" (dual) to the two of them. In another verse He said: ﴿"Go down, both of you, from it, all together."﴾ (Part of verse 123, Surat Ta-Ha).

This is so that we know that the narration of the story in several places came to give many snapshots. The command here came with His saying ﴿"Go down"﴾ because the descent was shared by the three: Adam, Eve, and Iblis. The enmity is pre-existing and we do not claim it. Enmity is between two sides: two in one side, Adam and Eve, and one on the other side, Iblis. The Truth wants to clarify realities for us, and that the Speaker is God. Every letter is weighed with Him; therefore we find Him, glory be to Him, saying to us: ﴿"Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?"﴾ (Part of verse 82, Surat an-Nisa).

That is, beware of taking the surface of the text, but search the background of the text, and do not take the surface of the wording; rather, look at what lies behind the words.

﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others. On earth you will have a dwelling-place and provision for a time."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf): The word "enemy" means the existence of conflict and battles that will take place among the children of Adam with one another, or enmity will occur between them and their enemies among the inhabitants of the earth, from jinn and others, but it is for a limited duration. Therefore He said: ﴿"On earth you will have a dwelling-place and provision for a time."﴾ That is, you have settlement on earth and enjoyment for a time. The struggle of the one who holds the truth in the truth must be taken as a provision in this world, and he must not take it as a battle without reward. No, you strive and receive a great reward for the striving, and this is provision.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says after that: ﴿He said: In it you will live, and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth﴾ (7:25).

It is as if He had said: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾ (7:24). So He wished to give us the image of life's journey and to draw for us our relationship with the earth, concerning which He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ (part of 2:30). Thus He has linked us to the earth: we were created from its clay, and we enjoy what is in it of features, goods and fruits. Then we die so that we may return to it, and after that we will be resurrected. So each of us is from the earth; from it he lives, in it he dies, and he goes back to his origin and his source, to the mother earth. It wraps him, embraces him, and takes him into its bosom, and it is tender toward him especially in the time of his weakness. When a person is in good health, while a brother of his is in the opposite condition, the mother's heart is with the weak, with the sick, and with the young.

The earth is what receives all of mankind. It takes the human being and draws out his harm, and conceals his smell. As for his loved ones in this world and his brothers, they hasten to cover him with dust, to avoid the process of decomposition. As soon as a person dies, or his name is forgotten, they say: "Where is the corpse?" and they do not say: "Where is so-and-so?" After the shroud, the body is placed in the coffin, so that it may be covered with dust, and the grave-digger stamps upon it with his feet.

Next, the Truth (al-Haqq) turns to address the children of Adam, saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness — that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that they may remember.﴾

The phrase ﴿O children of Adam﴾ draws attention to remembering your father's past with your clear enemy, Iblis. You are the offspring of Adam, and Satan exists, so be alert. The Truth has sent down to you clothing that covers your private parts, because the first disobedience that occurred exposed the private parts. Sending down (inzal) implies a direction of height, so that we understand that every good on earth has its supply descending from the heavens. He, glory be to Him, is the One who sent down clothing, because He is the One who sent down rain, and rain nourished the seeds of plants, so the plants came out, which we spun and which became garments. It is as though, if you were to attribute every good to its source, you would find it descending from the sky. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, bestows favour upon His servants, saying: ﴿And He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock...﴾ [Surah al-Zumar, 6]. Yes, He is the One who sent down livestock too, because causation in plants is a first stage, and causation in animals is a second stage; He is the One who made plants grow out of the earth so that animals might feed on them. He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people...﴾ [Surah al-Hadid, 25]. Yes, He, glory be to Him, is the One who sent down iron too, because we take it from the earth which Allah created; and this is evidence that the (various) sendings-down are, in fact, what Allah intends to protect every method (manhaj) by.

﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you clothing that covers your private parts...﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 26]. So if We have sent down clothing that covers the shame of the senses and the shame of matter, likewise We have sent down clothing that covers the shame of values. Just as you sense and perceive that material clothing conceals and covers the physical, sensory shame, you must also know that the clothing which Allah sends down of values is that by which He conceals and covers your moral shame. The clothing of material life did not stop at merely covering shame, but extended beyond that to the luxury of life as well.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿...We have certainly sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness — that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that they may remember.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 26]. Al-riash is the covering of birds, and in former times people would take bird feathers to decorate garments. They would place feathers on crowns. The common people took up this word and said: "So-and-so is murayyash" — meaning he possesses not only the necessities of life, but also the luxury of life. Thus this noble statement brings the legitimacy of luxury, on condition that it be lawful (halal). It has been said that after drawing our attention to the necessities of life, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, draws our attention to beauty in life, and He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And horses, mules, and donkeys, for you to ride and as an adornment...﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 8]. Riding is to avoid hardship, and adornment is for beauty. Likewise the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ (part of verse 32, Surah al-A'raf).

Indeed, He, glory be to Him, asked for our adornment when we come before Him in His house, saying: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship﴾ (part of verse 31, Surah al-A'raf). So this is a command to adornment. And here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness — that is best﴾ (part of verse 26, Surah al-A'raf). Yes, the clothing of righteousness is better than all of that, because material clothing covers material nakedness, and at its best it provides concealment from the disgrace of this world, but the clothing of righteousness conceals from us the disgrace of the Hereafter.

Or, the clothing of righteousness is that by which you guard yourselves against the terrors of wars; it is better than the clothing of adornment and finery because by it you protect yourselves from being killed. Or, that clothing, the clothing of righteousness, is better than material clothing, and it is among the signs of Allah, that is, among His wonders, and it is among the striking things. Man among you is composed of matter that has material needs and material nakedness, and there are value-based matters without which life is not ordered; the Truth has given you the means of material life, the adornment of material life, and given you that by which you live in peace and in war, and the method of righteousness achieves for you all these advantages. So take the signs from what you know and what you sense, so that you may deduce from them what is hidden from you that you do not sense.

Then Allah, exalted is He, says after that:

﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan seduce you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping off from them their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.﴾ (7:27)

Before He asks us not to be seduced by Satan, He explains that He has arranged for us all the necessities of life, and we must remember Satan's stance toward our father Adam and his seduction of him.

Fitnah (trial, test) is originally a test, and it is sometimes applied to the harmful effect, where it is worse than killing. But does a person fall into every fitnah? No, because fitnah is a test, and in a test a person either passes or fails. If he passes, the fitnah gives him good; if he fails, it gives him evil.

After Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the story of the creation of Adam, and informed us that He created him for the khilafah (vicegerency) on earth, and that the matter of the Garden is a preliminary stage for receiving the khilafah, because when he becomes a khalifah on earth, Allah has a method (manhaj) governing all his movements; and since he has a method governing all his movements, out of mercy toward him Allah did not send him down to the earth at the outset to receive the method without practical training in it. So He made the Garden a stage of the stages before the khilafah on earth, and warned him against Satan, who refused to prostrate to him, and wanted him to take the experience of obligation (taklif). Every obligation is confined to "do such-and-such" and "do not do such-and-such." Therefore Allah willed to make for him in the Garden a period of training for the task, so that he would descend to earth directly entrusted with the task of khilafah after being provided with the actual, practical experience. He explained to him: eat from everything in the Garden, but do not approach this tree. "Eat" is a command, and "do not approach" is a prohibition. Every legal obligation lies between "do not do" and "do."

After that He warned him against Satan, who places and sets up obstacles for him in carrying out Allah's method. When Adam and Eve approached the tree and ate from it, they opposed Allah's command in "and do not approach," and Allah wanted to show them through practical experience that opposing Allah's command must result in a nakedness (awrah) that appears in life. So their private parts became apparent to him and to his wife. When their private parts became apparent to them, each of them knew that opposing Allah's command reveals the nakedness of the earth and the nakedness of society. So Allah commanded him: "Go down to the earth, equipped with this experience."

When Adam and his wife descended to the earth, the method of heaven was sent to him after the experience, and He wanted to show us that he disobeyed his Lord's command in His saying "and do not approach," and he received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance. And Allah, exalted is He, wanted to show us that Adam embodies that he is a human who errs and makes mistakes, is overtaken by heedlessness, and may oppose Allah's method in something, then awakens from his heedlessness and repents. And after He charged him with conveying Allah's message and he became a prophet, infallibility (ʿiṣmah) came to him, so he is not heedless or forgetful in conveying the message.

Therefore we must take note of the Qur'anic text: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾ (part of 20:121). This is the nature of mankind: that he disobeys and then repents when he wishes to repent. We must also take note of His saying, the Truth: ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾. So selection came after the disobedience, because his disobedience was a natural matter, since he was human, who errs and is right, and forgets and is heedless. But after he went out of the Garden, Allah chose him to be a prophet and messenger, and since he became a prophet and messenger, infallibility came to him: ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾ (20:122).

Therefore it is not right for us to say: "How could Adam disobey while he was a prophet?!" We say: note that prophethood did not come to him until after he disobeyed and repented; he represents the stage of humanity, because he is the father of all humanity, and humanity is divided into two parts: humans who convey from God, and prophets who convey from God. He has in humanity that he disobeyed, and in prophethood that his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance and guided him. As for those who say that Adam was created for the Garden, we say to them: No. Understand from God, for He says: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah﴾.

The matter of the Garden was one of the stages that preceded the khilafah on earth. It was a training for the task he would carry out on earth. Otherwise, if Allah had created Adam for the Garden and disobedience had removed him from it, yet Allah had accepted his repentance, then since He accepted his repentance He should have kept him in the Garden. From here we say and affirm that the Garden was one of the stages that preceded the khilafah on earth. After that, the Truth, exalted is He, wants to bestow upon us the experience of Adam so that we may take admonition from it, know Satan's enmity toward us, and not fall into the fitnah as Adam fell.

﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan seduce you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping off from them their clothing to show them their private parts..﴾ (7:27): This is a prohibition addressed to the children of Adam, not a prohibition addressed to Satan. This is within man's capacity to do or not do; He, glory be to Him, does not forbid man from something not within his capacity, but forbids him from what is within his capacity. Satan has sworn that he will seduce him, and he will do so, because he swore and said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely seduce them all﴾ (38:82). So beware that you be deceived by Satan's seduction, for his matter with your father is clear, and his experience with your father must be applied to you, so that he does not seduce you as he removed your parents from the Garden. Some ask: why did Allah not say, "Let not Satan seduce you as he seduced your parents," but said: ﴿let not Satan seduce you as he removed your parents from the Garden﴾? We say: this is the height and the refined seduction (or charm) of the Qur'an's eloquent expression.

This is a warning against Satan's seduction, lest he remove us from the Garden of obligation, just as he seduced our parents and removed them from the Garden of trial. This style is called iḥtibāk (interlocking ellipsis), which is making the speech into two halves and deleting from each of them the counterpart of what is affirmed in the other, for the sake of brevity. This is the style that conveys the meaning with utmost concision, to alert the listener's mind to the words of Allah, so that he grasps from the expression the wisdom of the expression, its conciseness, and the absence of superfluity in its styles.

﴿let not Satan seduce you as he removed your parents from the Garden..﴾ (7:27): As we have learned, fitnah is originally a test, in order to purify a thing from the impurities mixed with it. When there are impurities in something, we know that gold is mixed with copper or another metal, and when we want to take the pure gold, we subject it to fire until it shakes off and removes what has adhered to it. Likewise, fitnah with respect to people comes as a test for the human being, to purify himself from the impurities of this matter, and to remember what Iblis did to Adam and Eve. So when he comes to seduce you, beware of being seduced, for the fitnah will harm you just as it previously harmed your father and mother Eve. Satan is the one who rebels against Allah's method among the jinn, and the jinn are a kind among whom are believers and disbelievers. The Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And among us are the righteous, and among us are other than that..﴾ (72:11).

The rebellious Satan from this kind against Allah's method is not one only. Read the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me, while they are an enemy to you..﴾ (18:50). Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them..﴾ (7:27): "his tribe" (qabīl) is his army and his offspring, whom he spreads throughout the universe to fulfill his oath: ﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely seduce them all﴾ (38:82). So the seduction of Satan came only to take the creatures of Allah out of the method of Allah. When Iblis disobeyed his Lord, that grieved him: after he had been at the peak of obedience, he became one who disobeys Allah's command with a disobedience that led him to disbelief, because he rejected the judgment of Allah. This angered his breast and enraged him, and made him go to excess and extravagance in enmity toward man, because he knew that his expulsion and cursing were because of Adam and his offspring.

﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them﴾ (part of 7:27): This indicates that the intended meaning is the offspring of Satan. If the intended meaning were the human satans along with them, He would not have said: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them﴾. Accordingly this verse concerns the offspring, and the Truth, exalted is He, teaches us to be attentive that Satan will not be satisfied with himself nor with the offspring, but will make it appear attractive to a group of people to become human satans just as jinn satans exist. These are the ones of whom He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And thus We made for every prophet an enemy: satans of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with ornate speech as deception﴾ (6:112). The phrase "ornate speech" means the enticement that makes a person commit disobedience and be moved by it, and be influenced by decorated speech. Every act of disobedience in the universe begins in this way, from ornate speech. Falsehood has its callers, its promoters, and its announcers; they make attractive to people some of their desires that divert them from Allah's method. We notice that the enemies of Allah and the enemies of His method lie in wait for the seasons of faith among people. When the season of faith comes, the enemies of Allah fear that the season will pass leaving a gift of faith in people's souls, so they try to unite their efforts to deprive people of the season's breath of grace. If they deprive people of the season's grace, they have achieved their aim of enmity toward Islam. ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe﴾.

Indeed Satan sees you, O responsible ones, he and his tribe. The qabīl denotes a group, the least of which is three of different kinds, or a group who are descended from one father and one mother. The scholars differed concerning the intended meaning of this noble saying. Some people said: ﴿because they are his armies and offspring﴾, meaning his armies from among mankind, and they did not heed the saying of the Truth: ﴿from where you do not see them﴾. So the intended meaning of "qabīl" here must be the offspring, because we see humans. In the Truth's saying there is an intensification of the need for caution and vigilance, because an enemy you see you can repel his harm, but an enemy who sees you while you do not see him, his enmity is severe and his scheming is worse. The jinn see us while we do not see them. Some scholars explained this by saying that we are created from clay, which is dense, while they are created from fire, which is subtle.

So the subtle can affect the dense, as evidenced by the fact that we feel the heat of fire even though there is a wall between us and it, but the dense cannot affect the subtle nor penetrate it. Thus the jinn's penetrating power and subtlety are greater than human subtlety, and that is why they have lightness of movement. And we do not see them.

This means that Satan is not seen. However, it is established in authentic reports that Satan has been seen, and he is of fire, and the angels are of light; both are hidden, concealed kinds. The angel has appeared in human form, and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "This is Jibril, who came to teach the people their religion" (1). On this basis, those contemporary with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibril not in his angelic form, but in a form consistent with the human kind, so he appeared to them materially.

It is also established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Satan and said: "Indeed a ifrit of the jinn kept attacking me last night to cut off my prayer, but Allah enabled me over him, so I choked him, and I almost tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque until you all would look at him in the morning" (2). That was from the courtesy of prophethood. So Satan takes forms, and you do not see him in his reality; if he wants you to see him, he appears in a material form. The scholars discussed this matter in a discussion that shows their eagerness to understand the Book of Allah, and shows their eagerness to clarify its intended meanings.

1. Related by Muslim in Faith (al-Iman).
2. Related by Muslim in Mosques (al-Masajid), and al-Bukhari in Prayer, and Ahmad. "Fa-dha'attahu" means: I choked him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 28:

The Truthful (Allah, glorified is He) then says: ﴿When they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾

Al-fāḥisha (indecency) is derived from al-tafaḥhush, meaning excessive increase in ugliness. For this reason some scholars restricted it to a specific type of sin, namely adultery (zina), because it is an excessive increase in ugliness. Every sin a person commits ends with its own effect, but adultery leaves behind consequences. Either the child is buried alive (yu'add), or the woman has an abortion, or she gives birth to her child and casts it away, and it lives as an outcast in society, finding no one responsible for it. Thus the matter extends far more than any other sin. And this sin produces doubt within society. We can imagine a man doubting whether those who are attributed to him and bear his name are not of his loins, and this is an extremely great affliction.

Those who said that al-fāḥisha intended by the verse is adultery looked at the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an indecency and an evil way﴾ [Surat al-Isrā' 32].

Or al-fāḥisha is that which carries a prescribed penalty (ḥadd), or al-fāḥisha is the major sins (al-kabā'ir). We take it to mean an excessive increase in ugliness of any kind.

So what is the indecency intended here? It is the indecencies that preceded in His words: ﴿Allah did not institute any baḥīra or sā'iba...﴾ [Surat al-Mā'ida 103]. Likewise what came in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children...﴾ [Surat al-An'ām 137], and likewise in His words, the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And they assign to Allah a portion of what He has created of produce and livestock, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners..."﴾ [Surat al-An'ām 136]. Or the intended meaning is that they used to circumambulate the House naked: the men circumambulated by day and the women circumambulated by night. Why? Because they claimed piety. They said, "We wish to circumambulate the House of our Lord as our mothers bore us, and to strip ourselves of the goods of this world, and not circumambulate the House of Allah in garments in which we have disobeyed Allah."

Their saying, "We found our fathers doing it," is imitation (taqlīd), and imitation does not confer a legal ruling (ḥukm taklīfī), although it may confer a training knowledge (ʿilm tadrībī), by training children in what Allah requires of the responsible person, so that when they reach the age of obligation they will be able to and become accustomed to what they are charged with. And what shows that imitation does not yield truth is that you find the contradictory doctrines of communism and capitalism, for example, both having imitators: for this doctrine there are imitators, and for that doctrine there are imitators. If imitation were acknowledged as truth, then two opposing imitations would both be true, and two opposites cannot both be true, because, as they say, opposites do not coincide. This is the rational proof for refuting imitation. Hence we observe in the style of Qur'anic expression that it is extremely precise, for the One who speaks is God.

﴿When they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it"﴾ (part of verse 28, Surat al-A'rāf): God's response to them regarding the matter of imitation is that He, glorified is He, did not give a rebuttal, because it is self-evident that it does not lead to truth. Rather He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾ (part of verse 28, Surat al-A'rāf). This is a rebuttal of their saying, "and Allah has commanded us to do it." Where is the rebuttal of their saying, "We found our fathers doing it"?

We say: it is a matter that needs no rebuttal, because it is a matter rejected by the innate reason (al-ʿaql al-fiṭrī), and therefore Allah left out a reply to it, since its falsehood is clear to innate reason. He instead responded to their claim that Allah commands indecency, and Allah does not command indecency. Then how was Allah's command to you? Is it a direct command, meaning that He commanded each one of you to commit an indecency? Have you not arrived at the words of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or that He send a messenger﴾ (part of verse 51, Surat al-Shūrā).

Or does the command to indecency reach you through a prophet? How could that be, when you deny the coming of the Messenger? Thus your saying is refuted from two directions. The first direction: there is no way to know the command of Allah except that He address you directly or address you through messengers, because you are not fit for direct address. The second direction: you deny the matter of the prophets and messengers. Since Allah has neither addressed you directly nor through messengers, there remains only to be said to you: ﴿Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?﴾ (part of verse 28, Surat al-A'rāf). There is no answer to the question except by one of two matters: either they say "No," and they have then contradicted themselves; or they say "Yes," and then we say that they speak about Allah what they do not know, and they have exposed themselves and acknowledged that Allah did not command indecency, but that Allah commanded justice. Therefore He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Say, "My Lord has commanded justice. And set your faces [toward Him] at every place of prostration, and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. As He originated you, you will return"﴾ [Surat al-A'rāf 29].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 29:

Al-qist is justice ('adl), from qasata qist (qistan). As for qasit, it is the active participle of qasata qast and qasut, meaning one who deviates and departs from the truth. Al-qasitun are those who swerve, incline away from the truth, and do wrong. The word 'adl means equalization (al-taswiyah). If you incline toward the truth, that is the beloved justice; but if you incline toward falsehood, that is a detested matter. ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice.﴾ This is a declarative sentence (jumlah khabariyyah).

﴿And set your faces upright at every place of worship﴾ (part of verse 29 of Surat al-A'raf): This is an imperative verb (fi'l amr). It may occur to the mind that this is the conjunction of an imperative to a declarative, but let us note that the truth (al-Haqq) connects it to "Say," so that the intended meaning is: "Say: My Lord has commanded justice," and "Say: Set your faces upright at every place of worship." The wajh (face) is the specific mark of a person, for if a person hides his face from one who knows him, he is only recognized if he has a distinctive garment that no one but he wears. The face is the most noble thing in the bodily creation, and therefore prostration (sujud) is placing the face upon the earth, and this is the utmost submission to God's command to prostrate, because prostration from the free agent, who is the human being, occurs by placing the forehead on the ground. Everything subject to God's judgment we describe as prostrating: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures... (18)﴾ [Surat al-Hajj]. The trees prostrate, and they are plants; the creatures prostrate, and they are of the animal kind; and the sun, the moon, the stars, and the mountains are of the inanimate, and they too are prostrating. But when the discourse came to humanity, He, glorified be He, divided them and said: ﴿And many among mankind, and many deserve the punishment...(18)﴾ [Surat al-Hajj], because the human being has the distinctive quality of choice, while the rest of creation has no choice. Thus prostration may be for one without a face, and what is meant by it is merely submission; but as for the human being, prostration is with the face, to make known that he is a vicegerent (mustakhlaf), and that all creation is subjected to his service, obedient, and all glorifying our Lord. So if the master whom all these kinds serve—animal, plant, and inanimate—has placed his face upon the earth, then he is submissive from the very beginning, when we say of him that he is prostrating.

﴿And set your faces upright at every place of worship...(29)﴾ [Surat al-A'raf]: iqamah means that you place a thing where it is fitted and created and where it is required of it. If you turn it toward another direction, you have bent it, inclined it, curved it, and made it crooked. Thus the setting upright of the face occurs through prostration, because the One who subjected this existence to you and governed you by the method of responsibility is the One for whose sake you placed your face on the earth. If you do not do so, you are choosing crookedness for your face. Know that this humility, submissiveness, and prostration to God will not only give you lordship over the other kinds, which give you the goods of this world, but placing your forehead and face on the earth also gives you blessing in work and gives you the good of the Hereafter too. The intelligent person is one who knows that he has taken lordship over the kinds, so he perfects servitude to God, and thus takes the two goods of this world and the Hereafter, in which no bliss escapes him and he does not escape bliss. As for this world, you approach it with vicegerency, and you know that bliss may escape you or you may cause bliss to escape; and when you remember God and are submissive to God, you attain blessing in the movement of vicegerency.

﴿And set your faces upright at every place of worship...(29)﴾ [Surat al-A'raf]: masjid is the place of prostration. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I have been favored over the prophets in six ways: I have been given concise comprehensive speech (jawami' al-kalim), I have been aided with awe, spoils have been made lawful for me, the earth has been made for me a purifier and a place of prostration (masjid), I have been sent to all creation, and the prophets have been sealed with me." [Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah.]

Therefore every place on earth is a masjid; if you enter a house of worship to pray, that is a masjid. The whole earth is a masjid for you; it is valid for you to prostrate and pray in it, and to carry on your work in it as well. In the factory you practise your craft, and when the time of prayer comes you pray; likewise you pray in the field. But the technical masjid is the place endowed and restricted to being a masjid, where nothing else is practised. If you take masjid to mean that the whole earth is a masjid, then ﴿set your faces upright﴾ applies throughout all regions of the earth. If you take it to mean the mosque, then the intended meaning is establishing prayer in the specified place, and it has a direction, which is the Ka'bah. Likewise your direction is the same whenever you pray in any place. We call mosques the houses of God, but by the choice of God's creatures: some of us build a mosque here or there, and they turn toward a house chosen by God, which is the Ka'bah. That is why it is the Ka'bah and the direction for all the houses of God.

The summary of the matter is that we make the qiblah of the mosque face the Ka'bah and set our faces upon it, that is, upon the direction in which worship is made upright: that you turn in your prayers toward the Ka'bah, for it is the house of God by God's choosing.

Whenever prayer overtakes you, pray in any mosque. Or ﴿and set your faces upright at every place of worship﴾ is intended to mean turning toward prayer in a mosque. Here the scholars differed: is performing and establishing prayer in the mosque recommended (mandub) or obligatory (hatm)? The majority said recommended, and a minority said obligatory. We say: obligation (al-hatmiyyah) has no proof.

Those who held that prayer in the mosque is obligatory cited the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I have resolved to order firewood to be gathered, then order the prayer to be called, then order a man to lead the people, then go to men and burn their houses over them." [Agreed upon.]

We say: did the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do that or did he not? The Messenger of God did not do that; he intended by the command severity, to encourage us to pray in the mosques at every call to prayer.

The True One, glorified be He, says: ﴿And call upon Him, making the religion sincerely His﴾ (part of verse 29 of Surat al-A'raf). Supplication (du'a') is a request from one who is powerless directed to one who is capable, concerning an act the supplicant loves. When you call upon your Lord, call upon Him sincerely devoted to Him in religion, such that causes are not in your mind; for if causes are in your mind, you have not made the religion sincere, because the meaning of ikhlas is purifying anything of the impurities in it, and impurities in beliefs and in deeds corrupt perfection and sincerity. Beware of thinking that this matter does not come to anyone, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my heart is veiled (layughan), and indeed I seek God's forgiveness every day a hundred times." [Narrated by Muslim in the book of remembrance and supplication, chapter on the recommendation of seeking forgiveness, and by Abu Dawud in the prayer, and by al-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm, and by Imam Ahmad 4/211. The word (layughan) means that which covers the heart; it is said to mean lapses and heedlessness from remembrance, or his concern for his community, so he seeks forgiveness for it. Al-Manawi said: it is a veiling of lights, not a veiling of obstructions, nor any heedlessness.]

Therefore sincerity is a process of the heart. When you call upon God, call upon Him always out of necessity (idtirar). Necessity means that your hope and expectation in all causes is cut off, so you turn to the Causer. As long as you are in necessity, our Lord will answer your supplication, because you have exhausted the causes. Some people call upon God out of luxury: a person may possess his day's food and say, "Grant me provision," and have a good dwelling and say, "I want a house that I own." Thus some of us ask God for things for which causes exist, and we must take them; and most of our supplications are not made with insistence. I challenge anyone whose affair has reached necessity and whom God does not answer.

The True One concludes the noble verse with: ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ (part of verse 29 of Surat al-A'raf). God, glorified be He, addresses the human being and shows tenderness to him, reminding him with "do this," "do this," "do this." He, glorified be He, is capable of creating him compelled to act, but He, may He be exalted, willed to make the human being a master and made him one who chooses; and He subdued all kinds to be subjected and to act as He wills. He affirmed for Himself the attribute of power, and nothing escapes His power. So you, O servant, are able to disobey God, yet you obey; and this is the greatness of faith, for it establishes the attribute of being beloved to God. When a person is deceived by causes, by the service of the whole cosmos, by the health in him, by the strength in him, by the wealth in him, you find the Truth drawing his attention: "Note that you will not escape Me. I gave you choice in this world, but you will return to Me in the Hereafter, and there will be no causes, and you will find only the Causer." Therefore read: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (part of verse 16 of Surat Ghafir). It is as if dominion before that, that is in this world, had some share for humans through their handling of causes: this one owns, that one owns, another employs. For you in the Hereafter there is no owner and no king except God. So beware of being deceived by causes, thinking they have submitted to you and that you have managed to control them, for your return is to God.

1 Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah.
2 Agreed upon.
3 Narrated by Muslim in the book of remembrance and supplication, chapter on the recommendation of seeking forgiveness; by Abu Dawud in the prayer; by al-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm; and by Imam Ahmad 4/211. The word (layughan) means that which covers the heart; it is said to mean lapses and heedlessness from remembrance, or his concern for his community, so he seeks forgiveness for it. Al-Manawi said: it is a veiling of lights, not a veiling of obstructions, nor any heedlessness.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 30:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that: ﴿A party He guided, and a party upon whom error was justly decreed. Indeed, they took the devils as protectors instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾

Recall that we said before: Allah guided everyone, meaning that He conveyed His method to them through the procession of the messengers. When He, glory be to Him, says ﴿a party He guided, and a party upon whom error was justly decreed﴾, the intended meaning here is not the guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala), but rather the guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'una). We have distinguished between the guidance of indication and the guidance of assistance.

The Truth's words ﴿a party He guided﴾ mean the guidance of assistance, because this party turned to Allah in faith, so Allah eased for them the burden of obedience, made them hate disobedience, and helped them in their task. As for the one who refused Allah and did not respond to the guidance of indication, would Allah assist him? No. He leaves him in his misguidance and lets him be between himself and error, and had He willed him to be guided, no one could have changed that. He, glory be to Him, is exalted above wronging any of His creatures, but those upon whom error was justly decreed had that happen to them because of what they did.

﴿Indeed, they took the devils as protectors instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided﴾ (part of verse 30, surah al-A'raf): Whoever commits a sin and acknowledges his sin, this remains a sin. But whoever says it is guidance, this is arrogance and disbelief, because he rejects the ruling of Allah. It is better for those who commit sins to say: the ruling of Allah is correct, but we were unable to control ourselves. But for the sinner to reject the ruling of Allah and say: it is guidance, his matter is grave, because he moves from the rank of a sinner to the rank of a disbeliever, and we seek refuge in Allah.

﴿And they think that they are guided﴾ (part of verse 30, surah al-A'raf): Because they do what Allah has forbidden, and would that they did it while recognizing it as forbidden and that they were unable to control themselves. Rather, they did it and assumed that guidance lies in the act. This matter is widespread in many sins, such as usury (riba). We find someone who says: it is permissible, and we say: say it is forbidden, and if you could not control yourself, then you enter the category of sin, and do not enter the category of disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah. You may seek forgiveness and our Lord will forgive you and accept your repentance. But to reject the ruling of Allah and say it is permissible! This is the danger, because you distance yourself and leave the circle of sin, decline and fall into disbelief. Guard yourself against being like that, and know that every son of Adam is a sinner, and Allah only prescribed repentance for His servants because He decreed that His servants would err and be correct. Among His mercy is that He prescribed repentance, and among His mercy also is that He accepts this repentance. So why would you leave a space in which you can get out to a space that constricts you, from which you cannot get out?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 31:

The Truthful One (Allah), glorified is He, says after that: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.﴾

When you hear "zina" (adornment, zīnah), it is understood as beautification that goes beyond the basic form of a thing. And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿take your adornment at every place of worship﴾ (part of verse 31 of Surat al-A'raf): this means that the Muslim goes to the mosque in the finest clothing he has. Likewise, what is meant by ﴿take your adornment at every place of worship﴾ may be a response to a particular situation, namely that they used to circumambulate the House naked, and that the adornment meant here is covering the private parts. Or, what is meant by adornment is what goes beyond the necessities of covering. Or, if what is meant by it is clean, beautiful, good clothing, then we know that the mosque is a place where the servants of Allah gather, and they are diverse in the affairs of their lives, and every occupation in life has its own dress and its own attire. The one who sits at a desk to receive people has his clothes, and the one who works in "blacksmithing" has a special uniform suited to the work. But when you go to the mosque to gather together in the meeting with Allah, should each one come in the clothes of his trade to enter the mosque? No. Let there be for the mosque a garment that does not offend others. If the work clothes of a factory or otherwise are not fitting, then make for the mosque clean clothes, so that no one is harmed by being beside you; for we go to the mosque for a common purpose that unites everyone, which is meeting Allah in the House of Allah, so you must honour this meeting.

﴿And eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive﴾ (part of verse 31 of Surat al-A'raf): Food and drink are among the permissible matters, because in them are the foundations of life. So eat and drink according to what sustains life, and do not be excessive. Allah has permitted you the greater part and forbidden you the lesser, so do not go beyond the greater part that He has permitted you to what Allah has forbidden, for this is excess against the self. The evidence is that if you find nothing but carrion, it is lawful for you on condition that you do not exceed. It is not correct to shift things from permissibility to prohibition, because Allah has placed in the lawful what suffices you from the unlawful. So if there is nothing that suffices you, then the Truth permits you to take what preserves your life. Those who are excessive are those who transgress the limits. There is no excess in what is lawful; excess occurs only in what is forbidden. For this reason it is reported in a narration: "If you spent the weight of Uhud in gold on something lawful, you would not be considered excessive; but if you spent a single dirham on something forbidden, you would be considered excessive." And for this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asks you to give every blessing its due, on condition that this does not lead to arrogance (bataraḥ). When Sayyiduna Uthman ibn Maz'un came to him, having wished to become a monk (tarahhub), to devote himself to worship (tanassuk) and to wander the earth, and said to the Messenger of Allah: "O Messenger of Allah, I wished to have myself castrated (ukhtasi), that is, to cut off his testicles, so that he would have no sexual desire," the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Uthman, the castration of my community is fasting." Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning one who cannot marry: "O assembly of youth, whoever among you is able to marry (al-ba'ah), let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the private parts; and whoever cannot, let him fast, for it is a shield for him" (1).

It is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the people and warned them, and ten of the Companions gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un, namely: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Dharr, Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, al-Miqdad, Sulayman, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, and Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin. They agreed to fast by day, stand in prayer by night, not sleep on beds, not eat meat, not approach women, and to castrate themselves (2). So the Prophetic guidance was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praised his Lord and extolled Him, and said: "What is the matter with people who say such and such? But I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break my fast, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me" (3).

1 Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim.
2 Tahqiq al-Bari (Fath al-Bari).
3 Reported by Muslim.

Al-Sha'rawi then continues, with the Truth (may He be glorified):

﴿Say: "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?" Say: "They are for those who believe in the life of this world, purely for them on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the signs for a people who know.﴾ [7:32]

Since He brought it forth for His servants, He has willed it for them. What is beneficial for females, the Sunnah has made lawful for females; and what is suitable for males, the Sunnah has made lawful for males. Likewise, the good provision is lawful for the believing men and the believing women. Let us note the precision of expression here in His saying: ﴿Say: "They are for those who believe in the life of this world"﴾ (part of 7:32), then He continues:

﴿purely for them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (part of 7:32). It is as if we are facing two states: a state in this world and another on the Day of Resurrection. This means that adornment in the life of this world is not purely for the believers, because the disbelievers share it with them. It is from the bounty of Lordship (rubübiyyah), and the bounty of Lordship is for the believer and the disbeliever alike. Perhaps the disbeliever has a greater share in this world than the believer, but in the Hereafter the adornment will be exclusively for the believers, with no disbeliever sharing it with them.

Likewise, the Truth (glorified and exalted be He) grants the believer wakefulness of faith through the presence of changing circumstances (aghyar) within him. The meaning of the presence of changing circumstances is that a person may be subjected to fluctuations between health and sickness, wealth and poverty, strength and weakness. Thus is man in this world; it is the abode of changing circumstances, and man encounters in it things he may dislike. Therefore, the world is not purely bliss, because of the changing circumstances that come to you and grieve you. They grieve you when the charge of faith is absent from you, for if you keep the charge of faith with you at every event that Allah brings upon you, it would turn you toward His wisdom.

﴿Say: "They are for those who believe in the life of this world, purely for them on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ (part of 7:32). It is possible to read the word "khālisah" in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and it may be read in another reading in the nominative as a predicate after a predicate (khabar ba'd khabar). The meaning is: it is not purely for the believers in this world, because the disbelievers share it with them; and it is also not free from the impurities of changing circumstances. But in the Hereafter it is purely for the believers, so the disbelievers do not share it with them, and changing circumstances do not come to them therein.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who know﴾ (part of 7:32). The meaning of ﴿We detail the signs﴾ is: We do not bring the signs in summary, but We detail the signs for every believer, leaving no gap, and bring in them everything that the judgments of life require, with a detail that makes our affairs understood to us with no ambiguity.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says after that: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin, and transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾

Allah (exalted is He) began the verse with "innama" (only), which is restrictive: that is, my Lord has forbidden only these things: indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, sin, transgression without right, associating partners with Allah, and saying about Allah what you do not know. So do not bring in other things and make them forbidden, for they do not fall under these. Allah's words in the previous verse, ﴿Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah?﴾, are in the form of a question, so that they would answer it themselves.
