They will find no reason for forbidding the adornment of Allah, because the Truth has made clear and explained what is forbidden, saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin, and transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

We reflect on the five prohibitions mentioned in the verse. When we look at the foundations of life in the earth, so that man may remain a khalifah (vicegerent) in it, we see that it is necessary to safeguard certain things essential to the soundness of lineage (purity of descent), that is, procreation and offspring, which are essential to society. For when a man is confident that this son is from him, he cares for him, because he is attributed to him, and he nurtures and raises him. But if he doubts this matter, he neglects and casts him off, and likewise society neglects him, and no one raises him, pays attention to him, or cares for him.

Thus the soundness of lineage is an important matter, so that society may be a sound society, in which no individual exists except that he is reckoned to his father, so that he bears for him all the consequences of his life. Therefore you must know that street children despite the presence of their fathers result from a doubt that arose in the father that this is not his son. Hence the instinct of tenderness has died in him, so he does not care whether he sees him or does not see him, whether he is at home or has wandered off, whether he eats or goes hungry, whether he is naked or not.

Thus the purity of lineage is a guarantee of the soundness of society, for society will be between a nurturer who attends to a small one being raised, the nurturer being able to work, and the one being raised being a child who needs upbringing. Therefore Allah forbade indecencies (al-fawahish) and al-fahsh, as we said, is that whose ugliness increases, and they explained it as zina (fornication), for its effect does not stop at the sin and the enjoyment, but extends to offspring. And what extends to offspring is an encroachment upon society, and it becomes a neglected society with no guardian.

As for sin (al-ithm): is it every major sin, or that for which the prescribed penalty (hadd) is imposed on its perpetrator? The scholars have agreed that sin (ithm) is wine and gambling (maysir), for Allah said explicitly: ﴿And their sin is greater than their benefit﴾ (part of verse 219 of Surat al-Baqarah).

Allah intended by this to safeguard the faculty that organizes the movement of life in man, which is the intellect ('aql), and that wine obscures the intellect. Man is obliged to preserve his intellect so that he may confront the affairs of life with it, in a confrontation that keeps the good in its goodness or increases it and does not transgress against the human being. When the intellect is covered by wine, it becomes corrupt and disordered, and thereby the planning of life's movement is disrupted. As for those who drink and say: "We want to forget our worries," we say to them: it is not the intention of the Lawgiver that each one forget what concerns him, for if each one forgot what concerns him, no one would take precaution, and no one would undertake the estimation of affairs that guarantee safety.

Indeed the Lawgiver asks you to confront the worries you suffer from, in order to remove them. As for covering the intellect, you have fled from the problem. Therefore you must confront life's problems with your intellect and thinking. If the problem arose from your neglect of a causal duty, that is, one that has causes and you fell short in taking those causes, then you are to blame. But if the problem came to you from a matter beyond your capacity, that is, it descended upon you as a decree and destiny, then know that the one who sends it upon you has wisdom in it.

Perhaps the trial is so that Allah may protect you from people's eyes, so that they envy you for it, because every possessor of a blessing is envied, and so that the blessing is not completed for you, for the completion of a blessing upon a person heralds its departure. You are a son of changing circumstances in a world of changing circumstances, and if it is completed for you, the blessing may change into a decrease.

Thus thinking about encountering harmful causes and avoiding them comes from complete intellect, and thinking about things that have no cause comes from faith, and faith asks you to refer everything to the wisdom of the All-Wise. So you need the intellect, so do not cover it by drinking wine, for the intellect directs the movement of life.

Baghy (transgression) we know to be exceeding the limit by wrongdoing, or greater, or stinginess. Wrongdoing is that you take the right of another and deprive him of the fruit of his labour, so he becomes disinclined to work. Therefore the Truth forbids that anyone transgress against anyone, whether in his honour, his person, or his wealth. We must safeguard honour from indecencies, for every indecency may bring forth children from unlawful union, and if it does not, it squanders honour, which is what must be preserved. Likewise no one may transgress against the sanctities (mahārim) of another, and likewise no one may transgress against a person's life by destroying it by killing.

The Truth protects wealth, so that transgression against it is prevented, and no one takes another's fruit of labour and struggle by aggression and injustice. The manifestations of transgression are many. Among transgression is that you seize authority by force without right, but there is one who seizes authority by force and compulsion with right. For example, if you are riding a ship, then winds and storms arise, and you are more skilled at steering it: would you leave the captain to steer it, though it may sink with those on board, or would you take his hand and grasp the helm and steer it to save it and those on it? In this case you have taken command by right, to preserve people's lives, and this is transgression with right, which differs from transgression without right. And so that you may distinguish between transgression with right and transgression without right, we say: this becomes apparent and clear when we take the ship's property from him to preserve and safeguard it and make it grow for him, so we have taken from its owner out of care for this right. Although in its outward appearance it is a transgression against the owner of the right, it was in his interest and in the public interest, so this is transgression with right, or it is named transgression because it came in the form of stripping the right from its owner unjustly. This is called in the science of rhetoric *mushākalah* (figurative correspondence), which is mentioning a thing by the word of another because it occurs in the company of that other. We also read Allah's words: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ 42:40. Is the recompense of an evil an evil? No, rather it is an evil for the one upon whom it falls, for when he committed an evil and embezzled, say, money, and you struck his hand and took the money from him, you have distressed him. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ 16:126.

Whoever transgresses against us without right, we must remind him that there is one stronger than he, so that he expects that transgression may reach him from one more capable than he.

The Truth draws our attention to the act that has no forgiveness: ﴿and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority.﴾ It is impossible that the Truth should send down a partner to the One we worship and support it with proof, authority and argument that it is a partner to Him—exalted is Allah far above that, high above all. For among the characteristics of faith is that He (exalted is He) negates this shirk by His rational proofs and His transmitted proofs.

And since the Truth has said to us in this verse: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and sin, and transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

Some other verses have gathered these things, in a concise frame and with their opposites as well. The Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to kindred, and forbids immorality and bad conduct and transgression﴾ (part of verse 90, Surat al-Nahl). He mentioned indecency (al-fahshā') in this verse to affirm the purity of lineages, and also mentioned the prohibition of the munkar (what is rejected) and transgression, and in the verse we are contemplating he added only sin. As if sin in the verse of ordering justice and good conduct and forbidding indecency, munkar and transgression is buried within "munkar," and munkar is not forbidden by the Shari'ah alone, but is what a sound nature rejects. Also, one whose nature is not sound describes it as munkar when sins bring harm upon him; here he says: "I seek refuge in Allah from them." But if he commits them against others, he believes they are not munkar. For example, we find a man who permits himself to open his eyes on people's nakedness and takes pleasure in this matter, yet when he sees another person opening his eyes on his own nakedness or on his daughter, for instance, he sees in that the most hideous of evils. Therefore you must set a limit for munkar that encompasses you and encompasses others, and do not look only at the duty imposed on you alone, but look at the duty imposed on others. And beware of saying: "He restricted my sight from enjoying a body passing before me." Just as He (exalted is He) forbade your gaze upon that, He forbade the gazes of all people from looking upon your sanctities (maḥārim); and in this is your protection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 34:

Having made lawful these good things and adornments, and forbidden indecencies, wrongdoing, transgression and sin, He (glory be to Him) says: ﴿For every nation there is an appointed term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they hasten it.﴾

We are here before a Qur'anic text that is confirmed by the realities of existence. Those who shed blood, oppressed, violated honour and seized property, that state did not endure for them. Rather, God granted them respite in their transgression, and then seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. Even if their adversaries had wished to avenge themselves upon them, they would not have reached even the lowest degree of the vengeance of heaven. The Truth brings about this retribution against tyrants to preserve the safety of society. So if you see corruption or tyranny, beware of despairing, for the Truth (glory be to Him) has made clear that every nation has a term, a beginning and an end. In our short lives we have seen more than one nation whose term has come. Therefore every tyrant ought to take this verse to heart: ﴿For every nation there is an appointed term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they hasten it.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). The term of every nation is known to God, because falsehood and injustice, if they do not bite people with a bite that makes them cry out, then they do not look longingly towards the truth nor aspire to it, and pain is a means of wellbeing, for it confirms to you that your condition is not natural. On this basis, the matters that occur in the universe, and these nations that oppress, persecute, and possess tyranny and arrogance, only act in this way until a known term. So beware of despairing, but you must look longingly towards the truth, and towards the presence of God, so that you take refuge in Him alone. For this reason we find that most of the people who experienced these events found nothing but the oasis of faith in God; they fled to His House as pilgrims, to His mosques as those who maintain them, and to the recitation of His Qur'an in remembrance. We look at these matters and say: the wicked tyrant, whatever he does, will surely be made by God to serve His religion. And there are people who, had the age not bitten them and afflicted them, as if a tyrant had been set over them, would never have fled to God seeking deliverance, nor turned to our Lord in worship.

In the reality of our lives, each of us knows people who did not worship their Lord: they did not pray, did not fast, and did not remember their Lord. Then an injury from an oppressor befell them, and the wronged person turns to God, seeking refuge in Him and taking refuge with Him. For this reason we say to the oppressor: by God, if you knew what you have done for the religion of God, and did not take a reward for it, you would regret it. You have brought to the religion of God a band of people who were not religious. And if you knew what your tyranny, your injustice and your arrogance bring about in the way of supporting the religion of God, you would not have done what you did. Indeed, for every nation there is a term; so if you are a tyrant at the head of a tyrannical group, then for that there is an end.

Look at history and you will find that some states, at the height of their vigour and harshness, took sovereignty over peoples, and then after a period of time disappointment befalls them, and domination over them comes from the weak. This is because this is the term. The Truth blinds their insight in their conduct; they think it guarantees them superiority, and then it makes the weak overcome them and dominate them. When the term comes, no one can delay it, because the timing is in the hand of the universe, and they also cannot hasten this term. Here we notice the word "sa'a" (hour). The word "sa'a" now has a modern technical sense, in that it is a measure of time for regulating schedules. We know that the day is divided into twenty-four hours, and smaller than the hour is the minute, and smaller than the minute is the second, and larger than the hour is the day. Who knows, perhaps mankind will invent instruments to regulate a fraction of a second.

Likewise, the word "sa'a" is also applied to the Hour of the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 35:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves, relating to you My signs, then whoever is mindful of God and does right, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾

Here the Truth addresses the children of Adam, after mentioning that He made the good things and adornments lawful for them and forbade them the five matters: indecency (al-fawahish), wrongdoing (al-munkar), oppression (al-baghy), sin (al-ithm), and associating partners with God (al-shirk). He set for them a system that guarantees the safety of society, and He reassured them that He will take vengeance on any unjust nation by setting for injustice an end and a term. So, O children of Adam, you must conduct the affairs of your lives within the framework of these premises.

﴿O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves, relating to you My signs..﴾ [Surah al-A'raf]: You must receive the messengers of God with the attentiveness of one who is distressed, looking forward and longing for that which will protect him and benefit him, because the Messenger is the one who announces to each of you what God has made lawful of the good things and pleasures of life, and who makes clear to you what God has forbidden so that society may live in soundness.

It was expected that, the moment a messenger comes, we would find society eager to cling to him and to receive the message from him, not that the messenger should keep calling gently while society refuses him. It is a mercy from God for you that society refuses and the messenger persists, making clear the signs and proofs of God, so that every person may take what helps him in the affairs of his life and be guided to the straight path. When you are healthy, you insist on the doctor and seek him out; so the demand of reason is that when a messenger comes to convey to us the method of God for managing the movement of life, we should long for him and look forward to him, not oppose him. People of sound nature (ahl al-fitrah al-salimah) usually rejoice in the Messenger as soon as he says that he is a messenger and that his sign of truthfulness is with him. People of sound nature measure the Messenger's words by his past with them, so they know that he is sincere and has not committed sin. This is the benefit of His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is solicitous over you; for the believers he is kind and merciful.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah]. No stranger whom you do not know has come to you; rather, you have with him a clear and manifest history. Therefore we find that those who first believed in the Messenger of God did not wait until the Qur'an was recited to them, but believed in him on account of their prior knowledge of him, because they lived with him and knew every detail of his character. An example of this: when Muhammad (ﷺ) informed our lady Khadijah, may God be pleased with her, of the news of his prophethood and confided to her his fear that what had descended upon him might be from the jinn or their touch, she hastened to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, because he had knowledge of the Book; and before that she had said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Indeed you keep the ties of kinship, bear the burdens of others, help the destitute, honour guests and aid in the calamities of truth." All these premises indicate that you, O Messenger of God, are under God's protection and care, because you were upright in conduct before you were made a prophet and before you came into being as a messenger from God. Is it reasonable that one who abandons lying to people would lie about God?! Likewise, we find our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, the moment the Messenger of God said, "I am a messenger," said to him: "You have spoken the truth." If this indicates anything, it indicates the truthfulness of natural disposition. This is the benefit of ﴿a messenger from among yourselves﴾, or from your human kind, so that in him you find a good example. Had a messenger come to us from the angels and said, "This is the method, and you have an example in me," we would have answered him with a convincing, easy and simple reply: "Could we do as you do, when you are an angel created upon goodness?"

But when a messenger comes to us from our human kind, who is capable of doing good and capable of doing evil, he is the existing example. That is why it was from the folly of the disbelievers that they said what the Qur'an recounts of them: ﴿Nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has God sent a mere human as a messenger?"﴾ [Surah al-Isra']. It is folly, shortsightedness and anger; for God sent Muhammad, and he is a human being. Did they want an angel? And if he were an angel, how could he be an example, when his nature differs from the natures of humans? Therefore the Truth gives the logical answer: ﴿Say: Had there been angels walking calmly in the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ That is so that the example in him may be realised for us; He, glory be to Him, did not force His presence upon you artificially, nor did He bring you into a matter that is hard and burdensome for you, but He came to you with one of you whose history you know, and He did not bring him from another kind.

﴿O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves, relating to you My signs..﴾ [part of verse 35, Surah al-A'raf]. Note His saying ﴿relating to you My signs﴾: He used the word "yaqussuna" (relate), because qisas (narrative) is derived from the root "qaf" and the doubled "sad"; this is taken from "qass al-athar" (tracing the trail), for a man whose camels or sheep had been stolen would go to see the traces of the footprints. So ﴿relating to you My signs﴾ means that they are committed to what has come to them, not deviating from it, just as you do not deviate from tracing the trail when you want the one who left the trace.

﴿Then whoever is mindful of God and does right, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾ [part of verse 35, Surah al-A'raf]: "Taqwa" (mindfulness of God) means that you place between yourself and something that harms you a shield. Therefore the Truth says, ﴿Guard yourselves against the Fire﴾, so that by righteous deeds we ward off from ourselves the flame of the Fire. When it is said, ﴿Be mindful of God﴾, it means: be mindful of the requirements of the attributes of majesty (al-jabarut) of God, because you will not be able to bear the majesty of our Lord; and you must commit yourselves to performing the commands and also to abstaining from the prohibitions. The command to taqwa here means that we should not deny or reject the messages of the messengers, for they came to rescue mankind; so when society falls ill, it must hasten and turn to the physician who comes with the method of God to care for it, who is the Messenger. Therefore it is not right to reject a message that has evidence and a miracle.

﴿Then whoever is mindful of God and does right, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾: "Aslaha" (does right) indicates that there is something not sound which he made sound, or that he preserved the soundness of what is sound and raised its soundness higher. Like a well from which we drink: if the well performs its function, we do not fill it in, nor throw filth into it, and thus the sound remains sound; and we may increase the well's soundness by building a wall around its mouth, or by installing a pump that draws water from the well to pump it to the houses. In this way we increase the sound in soundness. The calamity in this world is those who claim to be reforming while they are corrupters; God says of them: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who are greatest in loss as to their deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work.﴾ [Surah al-Kahf]. So when you undertake any work, you must know its premises, what those premises will give it, and what you will take from it. Keep what is sound in the universe sound or increase its soundness; and then there is no fear for you, and you will not grieve over anything that escaped you, so that the saying of the Truth is fulfilled: ﴿So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you.﴾ [part of verse 23, Surah al-Hadid]. And what is the counterpart of those upon whom there is no fear, nor do they grieve; that is, those who have done right and been mindful of God? The counterpart is what comes in His saying: ﴿But those who denied Our signs and waxed proud against them, those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide.﴾

Why should the fate of those who deny Our signs and act arrogantly toward them be that they become the companions of the Fire and abide therein forever? Because, although the means of life were made easy for them, they did not take into account that they would have a share in the Hereafter, nor did they turn their attention to the ultimate end. The belief in the word of the Truth was absent from them: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ (Surah ash-Shura, 42:20). Suppose one of them has taken what he has taken in this world: why did he forget that its lifespan is limited? And why did he not give heed to time in the Hereafter? You must know that you, in this world, are a khalifah (vicegerent) on the earth. Since we are all children of one kind and created in it, and mastery over the other kinds belongs to us, we must have a unified ultimate goal, because whatever we differ over cannot be considered an ultimate goal. The final goal is meeting Allah, for the equal end in the universe is death, which delivers us to a second life. So the one who is arrogant toward the signs of Allah has entered into a losing transaction, because whoever compares this world with the other life will find that the time of man in this world is short, while the time of the Hereafter has no end. The lifespan of man in this world is uncertain and not assured, and enjoyment in it is in proportion to the individual's means and capabilities, whereas the Hereafter is certain, and the bliss of the believer in it is in proportion to the expansiveness of Allah's power.

﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; therein they abide forever﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah al-A'raf, 7:36). And "companions of the Fire" means that the sinner is accompanied and constantly joined by the Fire, just as a person is accompanied and joined by his companion among us; for the Fire is familiar with the disobedient, and it is the one that says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾.

Almighty Allah says after that: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of the Scripture until, when Our messengers come to them to take their souls, they say, "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have departed from us," and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.﴾ (7:37).

And ﴿Who is more unjust﴾ comes in the form of a question whose answer can only be an affirmation. No one is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah, because first he wrongs himself, and wrongs his community. The first wrong to the self is that he is content with a transient life and forsakes an eternal life. As for his wronging of people, it is because he will bear the burdens of what they do, since he has fabricated lies against Allah ﴿or denied His signs﴾. That is, he attributes to Allah what He did not say, or denies what Allah has said, and both matters are equivalent to one another. The "āyah" (sign, a wondrous matter), as we know, is a remarkable matter, and "āyāt" has been applied in the Qur'an to multiple meanings. Allah says: ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed﴾ (41:3).

Likewise, it has been applied to the miracles that Allah sends as confirmation of His messengers. ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (17:59). Here, "āyāt" means miracles, i.e., extraordinary matters.

The Qur'an has informed us about the cosmic signs, and He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon﴾ (41:37). Thus, "āyah" is then a wondrous thing, and it includes the Qur'an, because when you look at the arrangement of the Qur'anic verses, and at their comprehensiveness of the realities of existence, and at their fulfilment of the issues of the entire universe, you say to yourself: this is a marvellous thing, because the one upon whose tongue these verses came is an unlettered prophet, who was not known to have pursued learning, and they never tested him as one who composes poetry or prose, nor was he practised in speech, and after that he did not experience the rule of nations, nor did he study the history of nations so as to derive the laws that have baffled the contemporary civilisations from matching them.

When the Bedouin nation carried its methodology to Persia, and Persia had the whole civilisation of the East, nevertheless Persia took its laws from this Bedouin nation. The entire system of this nomadic nation before the arrival of the message with our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was summed up in the system of the tribe, and each tribe had a chief. After his message (ﷺ) came, he brought a system that unites all the nations of the world, then succeeds in administering the entire world. This is a remarkable matter, and every one of these signs was a miracle and marvellous.

Likewise, the cosmic signs, which we find characterised by tremendous precision: the sun and the moon are by reckoning, and each in an orbit they swim. It is a marvellous system.

Thus, the marvels in the signs are the verses of the Qur'an, the miracles and the cosmic signs. And how then do they deny the signs? Do they not look at the universe and at the precision of its making and the structure of its formation, which has no contradiction in it? These are signs that speak of the precision of the Creator; He is the Knowing, the Capable, the Wise, the Reckoner. Likewise, how do they deny the Messenger who came with the miracles, saying that he is a sorcerer, and when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to them, they deny them? Thus they did not reflect on the signs of the universe to derive from them the greatness of the Maker, His wisdom and His precision, and they did not turn to belief in Him as the summit of doctrine. Likewise, they denied the miraculous signs that the messengers brought, so they did not believe the messengers, and the last of them and its summit is the signs of the Mighty Qur'an.

When Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, presented this issue, He questioned: how do you say, "He has bewitched the people, so they believed in him; why then did he not bewitch you?" And when they said: ﴿It is only a human who teaches him﴾ (16:103),

the Truth said: ﴿...the tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ (16:103).

And they said: ﴿They are fables of the ancients which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening﴾ (25:5).

So Allah teaches His messengers to say: ﴿...I dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?﴾ (10:16). Here Allah commands His messenger to remind them that he lived among them for forty years; was it known of him that he said or spoke anything of this?

So would Allah leave those who denied the signs? They are creatures of Allah, and Allah summoned them into existence; therefore He guarantees for them the necessities of life, and He ordered the causes of the universe to serve these deniers and disbelievers just as they serve the obedient believers. Whoever among them takes the causes well, takes their results; and if believers neglect taking the causes, they will not take their results. All of this is because it is a gift of lordship, and because He created them, so they must be provided for; the cosmic laws serve the obedient and serve the disobedient, because that is the sunnah of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the sunnah of Allah.

Thus their disbelief will not prevent from them their portion of the Scripture that was decreed for them, of provision and life, which is inscribed in the Book that was sent down to them. Therefore Allah says: ﴿Those will receive their portion of the Scripture﴾ (7:37). Or it will reach them, that is, there will befall them punishment from what is made clear in the Book which We sent to show that the obedient has reward and the disobedient has punishment. So the Truth says here: ﴿until, when Our messengers come to them to take their souls, they say, "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have departed from us," and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾ (7:37). And when you hear ﴿yatawaffawnahum﴾ you understand that life ends and the soul separates from the body; this is "tawaffī." Sometimes it is attributed to the Supreme Truth, glory be to Him and exalted; sometimes it is attributed to the angel; and sometimes what is meant is the angel's followers, i.e., his soldiers. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿until, when death comes to one of them, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect﴾. The three modes converge, because the Angel of Death did not bring death from himself, but received it from Allah; so the highest command is from Allah, the mediating command is for the angel, and the executing command is for the messengers.

"Tawaffī," in its unrestricted sense, is the completion of the term. If it is the term of life, it is a fulfilment by death; and if the term is the barzakh, which is the period between the grave and the reckoning, until the appointed time of their entry into the Fire arrives, then this is the fulfilment of their second term, because every person has two terms: a term that ends this life, and the term he takes in the barzakh until the reckoning arrives.

This does not prevent saying that the resurrection of every person comes with his death, because the resurrection has stages, beginning at the grave and ending with eternal abiding in Paradise or in the Fire. And when the angels ask them: ﴿Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?﴾ They say: ﴿They have departed from us, and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾ (7:37). They thus acknowledge that those whom they used to invoke besides Allah have vanished and disappeared, and no trace of them appears to them.

﴿And they said: "When we are lost in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (32:10). They thus affirm the absence of those they used to invoke besides Allah, and what is meant is that they have no existence; and by this they have testified against themselves to their disbelief. But this testimony will not avail, because the time of obligation has ended, and they are now in an abode of compulsion over everything Allah wills; in the abode of obligation a person was free to act or not to act, but in the Hereafter this testimony does not benefit. This is to make clear the justice of the recompense that befalls them, and they will not be able to resist the recompense; therefore the Truth says: ﴿He will say, "Enter among nations that have passed away before you, of jinn and mankind, into the Fire." Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister, until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾ (7:38).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary also makes clear to us that, by the command "Be" (﴿kun﴾), they will enter the Fire just as nations that passed away before them entered it, so they are not unprecedented. They will go in together with them to the destination to which they are heading; they are a mixed multitude, because disbelief will all be gathered together in the requital.

Indeed, imitating the nations that came before is what led them to disbelief. The nations that preceded were an example of misguidance for the nation that followed, so when they enter [the Fire] they curse them.

Suppose a man once entered prison for a crime he committed, and afterwards there entered upon him someone who had incited him to the crime, who had made it seem attractive to him, and whom he had imitated. By God, at the hour when the two meet in prison, will the first not curse the second? ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister, until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them: "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say: "For each there is double, but you do not know."﴾ [Surah al-A'raf].

After they overtake one another and gather together, this strange dialogue takes place between them: ﴿The last of them will say of the first of them: "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire..."﴾ [Surah al-A'raf]. If you say: the "last" (al-ukhra), meaning the one who entered the Fire later, was the one who followed the first in misguidance, and the first had gone ahead of them into the Fire, then ﴿the last of them says to the first of them﴾, meaning that the first are the leaders who misled, and the other group are the followers who imitated. ﴿The last of them says to the first of them: "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us."﴾ And they address their speech to our Lord: ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us."﴾ How can this be? The expected form would have been: "The last of them says to the first of them: 'You misled us.'" But this statement came in this form because those who misled others are too lowly to be addressed directly, since the whole situation is in God's hand. When they say "God" in addressing all, ﴿these are the ones who misled us﴾: "these" is a pointing to them, so it is as if the speech is directed to God as a testimony from them against those who were the means of their misguidance, and they say this to our Lord so that they may receive the double punishment of the Fire, in confirmation of His saying, the Truth: ﴿So give them a double punishment of the Fire..." [38]﴾ [Surah al-A'raf].

Then God said to them all: ﴿For each there is double, but you do not know﴾: so each nation among them receives double punishment for having gone astray and led astray. We understand that "ḍiʿf" (double) means "a thing equal to its like." You, O followers, have also misled others through example, because you increased their number, strengthened their power, and incited people to follow them, so for you there is double punishment on account of your also having misled. But you do not know that the One who reckons with you is precise in reckoning, and gives every person his due in full.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 39:

And what does the first of them say to the last of them? The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾

That is: since you are going to receive double the punishment as we do, then the heads are equal. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾ It is as if the criminal, at the moment he meets and encounters a criminal like himself, says to him: "Drink of this very punishment." This is not an injustice from God, nor an exercise of domination over His servants, but the justice of the judgment; for that only happened because of what you earned.

It is known that "tasting" belongs to flavours, so do they eat the punishment? No. The Truth has made every limb in them taste the punishment, and when the Truth wills that the punishment encompass the body, He makes every organ of the body possess the sensitivity of taste like that of the tongue.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Allah presents a parable: a town that was secure and at rest, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place; but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ [Surah al-Nahl] This is the "making to taste"; it is as if it became a garment of hunger encompassing the whole body. And "making to taste" is the most intense of perceptions in its effect, while the garment is more all-encompassing for the body. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾ The Truth did not say "for what you used to earn" in the sense of deliberate effort, because their earning of evil deeds no longer involved contrivance; rather it became a natural matter for them. Although the natural course in creation is that a person does good without strain or artifice, and in evil deeds he struggles against his soul, because that happens contrary to what he was disposed to; but these people, from their excessive addiction to evil deeds, had their natural disposition corrupted, and their faculties no longer resisted when committing evil deeds; rather they came to commit sin as a natural thing. This is the danger that befalls those who are wasteful against their own souls, since one of them rejoices in doing evil deeds.

The Almighty then says: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and acted arrogantly towards them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾ (7:40)

Al-Haqq wants to give a new ruling and to identify who is subject to it, so that he may be known by his crime, a crime not linked to any previous one, and so that every person knows that this is a crime and that whoever commits it will meet a judgement and a punishment. ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and acted arrogantly towards them﴾. We have already learned the meaning of "signs" (āyāt): they are the miraculous verses of the Qur'an or the cosmic signs. Any person who considers himself too great to follow a method brought by a messenger known among his people for his trustworthiness deserves severe punishment. It is true that Muhammad (ﷺ) did not have the rank and authority that could rival the leaders and nobles of Quraysh, and for this reason we find those who say: ﴿They said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?"﴾ [Surat al-Zukhruf] (43:31). They acknowledge the exalted status of the Qur'an, but they wished that it had been sent down to someone other than him, provided he was among the great by their material standards and measures.

Whoever denies the signs and is arrogant toward following the Messenger, the gates of heaven will not be opened for him. ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and acted arrogantly towards them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾ [Surat al-A'raf] (7:40). Thereby we know who are the ones for whom the gates of heaven will not be opened, and naturally we know that their counterparts are those for whom the gates of heaven are opened. They are the believers, and when their souls ascend to the Highest Assembly, their righteous deeds ascend with them and raise them higher. As for the deniers, they do not rise but descend, and they do not enter Paradise. He, glory be to Him, has made entry into Paradise dependent on something impossible by reason, custom and nature: ﴿nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. "The eye of the needle" (samm al-khayyāt) is the hole of the needle, into which the twisted strand of thread enters. A twisted strand of thread can enter the hole only if the diameter of the strand is less than the diameter of the hole, if the strand is stiff enough to pass through, and if the end of the strand is uneven; for if it is cut and its ends are even, it will not enter the hole. Therefore we find the tailor makes a point on the strand so that he can insert it into the eye of the needle.

When we bring a camel and say to it, "Enter the eye of the needle," can it do so? Of course not. Therefore we find that the Almighty has made the entry of these people into Paradise dependent on something impossible.

Some people have said: What is the connection between the camel and the eye of the needle? We say: "al-jamal" is also applied to a thick, twisted rope, such as the ropes of a ship, which we find thick and plaited. The poets took up this matter; one of them describes his preoccupation with the beloved, his longing for her and his passion for her, to the point that he wastes away and weakness overcomes him, and he says:
"Even if what I suffer of anguish and passion
Were upon a camel, no unbelieving disbeliever would enter the Fire."

Because the anguish and passion that this poet suffers from, if they afflicted a camel, it would grow thin and emaciated until it could pass through the eye of the needle. Here our Lord clarifies: if the camel enters the eye of the needle, then I will admit them to Paradise.

﴿until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals﴾ [from verse 40, Surat al-A'raf]: and they deserve this recompense for what they committed.

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hellfire beneath them, and over them coverings (of Fire). Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ (7:41)

Al-mihad is the bedding, from which comes mihad al-tifl (the infant's cradle/bed), and al-ghashiyah is the covering. That is, the spread beneath these wrongdoers is Jahannam (Hell), and its covering is also Jahannam. In another verse, Almighty Allah says: ﴿For them there will be layers of Fire above them, and beneath them layers (of Fire)﴾ (from 39:16). So the zulal (layers) and the ghawashi (coverings) envelop two directions in the post-creation structure of the human being. The dimensions are six: front and back, right and left, above and below. Al-mihad points to the downward direction, and al-ghawashi point to the upward direction, and likewise the zulal of Fire. But Allah willed to make Jahannam encompass the six dimensions of the disbeliever, as He says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure will surround them﴾ (from 18:29). This means that the punishment includes all directions of the wrongdoers.

Jahannam is derived from al-juhumah, which is that which is frightening, stern, and of repulsive countenance. Then He brings the contrast, to charge the soul with aversion to that situation and to make endearing to the soul the counterpart of such a situation, so He says: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We do not burden any soul except [within] its capacity; those are the companions of Paradise, they therein will abide eternally.﴾ (7:42)

And thus does the Truth inform us that those who believed and did righteous deeds are the companions of Paradise, and they will abide therein forever. And the Truth places a reminder between the introduction of the verse and its conclusion: ﴿We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity﴾; so that we understand that those who have been extravagant against themselves through disbelief and denial of the signs have not grasped the reality of faith, and that restraining the soul from many of its desires is within the soul's capacity and not beyond its power. Therefore He, glory be to Him, made clear to us that He imposes obligations with "do" and "do not," and that is within the limits of the one who is obligated.

And when we survey the picture as a whole, for the sake of comparison and contrast between the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise, we find that the Truth said concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them — the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals﴾ (7:40): so they will not enter Paradise, and by that a benefit has been taken from them. The matter does not stop there; rather, they will enter the Fire. So here there are two matters: the withholding of benefit, which is their not entering Paradise — He, glory be to Him, deprived them of that bliss, and that is the recompense for their criminality. After that came their entry into the Fire, and this is another recompense. So the Truth said: ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hellfire, and above them coverings. And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ (7:41). In the first, He said, glory be to Him, "And thus do We recompense the criminals," and in the second He said, "And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers." It is as if criminality was the cause of their not entering Paradise, and wrongdoing was the cause of there being coverings above them, and a bed of Hellfire for them, and they, in the Fire, are encompassed by its enclosure.

After that charge which makes us loathe the people of the Fire and their misconduct regarding what they were first charged with, and the reason for the monstrousness of their recompense second, it is fitting that we long for the opposite. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds — We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity — those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ [al-A'raf 7:42]. The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ came between the subject and the predicate, as a parenthetical statement; because the style requires us to be informed that those who believed and did righteous deeds have eternal abiding in Paradise. And ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ came between the two pillars of the sentence, namely the subject and the predicate; because when we hear ﴿And those who believed﴾, this is an act of the heart, and then we hear ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, which is an act of the limbs; and thereby, that is, by the act of the heart joined with the act of the limbs, there is realized from conduct what accords with belief. Belief always facilitates faithful conduct and makes the hardships of the obligations in righteous deeds acceptable and light. Therefore He, glory be to Him, made clear: beware lest you think that I have burdened you beyond your capacity — no; I do not burden except within capacity. And beware lest you understand my saying ﴿and those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ to be a desire to exhaust your souls; rather, that is within your power, because I am the Legislator, and the Legislator only places obligation within the capacity of the one obligated.

And in our practical life we do the same: we find the engineer who designs a machine informs us of the extent of its capabilities, so he does not load it beyond its capacity, or else it breaks. And if a human craftsman does not burden the deaf machine beyond what it can bear, would He who created mankind burden them beyond what they can bear? It is impossible that this should be so.

Therefore it is necessary to close the door on those who try to escape from their obligations. Do not attach the ruling to your faltering, unjust capacity; rather, fix the capacity to God's obligation. If He has imposed it, then be certain that it is within capacity. The proof of the liar who wants to escape the ruling is his attempt to subject the ruling to his own capacity, while others do not wish to do what he does. So when the Truth forbids wine-drinking, you find others not drinking wine in compliance with God's command; likewise you find those who abstain from fornication or from consuming usury. If your like, who is an individual of your own kind, is able to do this deed, then the one who does not refrain from such prohibited things is the sinner, not because the obligation is difficult. Obligation is the command of the Wise Legislator, "do" and "do not," and He, glory be to Him, does not obligate a human except when he is able to fulfil the demands of the Law; for God does not obligate except according to capacity. Preserving capacity requires sustenance: food, drink, clothing, and whatever else life requires. Therefore He, glory be to Him, made clear that He provides for a person all the basic material necessities of life. Beware lest you think that when God obligates a person, He obligates him with hardship; rather, it is the person who places himself in hardship. He said: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted — [7] [al-Talaq 65:7]: "restricted his provision" means He narrowed it slightly.

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Let him who has abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted — let him spend from what God has given him. God does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ [al-Talaq 65:7]. So do not presume and estimate your living expenses and then try to force your income to conform to that notion; rather, look at what comes to you and live within the scope and frame of that income. If your income is one hundred pounds, arrange your life so that your expenditure equals your income, for God does not burden you except with what He has given you. Let us consider what God has given us. Therefore do not include in your reckoning of provision except what God has legislated: do not steal, do not plunder, do not embezzle, and do not take bribes and then say, "This is what God gave me." No; you must not take or benefit except by what God has made lawful for you. If you live within the bounds of what God has made lawful, God will help you in every matter and every need, because you live by God's method. Then the Truth will remove from you the affairs of life that would require you to exceed what God has given you, and they will not occur to your mind or the minds of your children. You may find yourself, for example, entering the market with a limited amount of money given to you by God, and seeing many goods; but the Truth makes you look only within the bounds of what is within your capacity. Likewise God makes beautiful for you what is within your capacity and keeps far from you what is beyond your capacity, because God does not burden a soul except with what He has given it, and He does not stir the desires of the soul except within these limits.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds — We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity — those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ [al-A'raf 7:42]: The companions of Paradise are those who never part from it, just as a companion loves his companion; Paradise seeks them, and they seek Paradise, and life there is everlasting. Whatever pleasures of this world you missed did not have permanence. You do not take or benefit except by what God has made lawful for you; and if you live within the bounds of what God has made lawful, He will help you in this world. You fear that you will die and lose the blessing, and if you do not die you fear the blessing will leave you, because the world is change. In that is a drawing of attention to the laws of God in His creation: you find the healthy one has become sick, and the rich has become poor; nothing is permanent in human nature. Thereby God balances the scale of people: He turns to the economic condition and distributes it among creation, and you find that the one who does not rebel against God's decree in his provision and his work, God makes for him ease after hardship. And in Paradise God empties its people of such changes.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; rivers will flow beneath them; and they will say, "Praise be to God who guided us to this; we would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth." And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do"﴾ [al-A'raf 7:43].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 43:

His Exalted saying: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾ also applies to the people of ijtihad (independent reasoning, personal effort to reach a judgment) who each exerted ijtihad in this world and differed. These will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with no resentment or spite in the breast of any of them. Therefore, you find that our master Imam 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, when he recited this verse, would say: "O Allah, make me, 'Uthman, Talhah and al-Zubayr among these." This is because these are the ones among whom disagreement occurred over the matter of the caliphate, and each of them was a Companion and was given the glad tidings of Paradise. So if the souls have been entered by extraneous things, beware lest you think that these extraneous things will accompany you in the abode of recompense in the Hereafter, for Allah says: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾.

The disagreement was an ijtihadi disagreement among believers, and they had done righteous deeds, and each of them wanted the good among the deeds. Some of the worldly extraneous matters that arose from that were something of the work of the heart. So He, glory be to Him, made clear: beware lest you understand that this will continue with them in the Hereafter, for when they differed they were all living by the ijtihadat of Allah, and in the Hereafter there is no ijtihad for anyone. The Truth wishes to make this matter a universal principle. An example of that: you find a man who married a woman by measures other than Allah's measures in marriage; he married her because she is beautiful, for example, or because her father has standing or wealth. After the marriage her wealthy father did not give him any of his money, so he says: "He deceived me and married me to his daughter," or "she was beautiful," and then he encountered in her many ugly traits and came to hate her. We say to such a man: since you did not choose her by Allah's measures, you must receive the recompense of your choice.

But whoever marries a woman according to the religion of Allah and finds in her some ugliness, that ugliness will not accompany him in the Hereafter. Therefore you find that the Truth has brought this very principle, and did not bring it concerning sons or daughters, but concerning husband and wife, because they are the pillars of the family. So He makes clear to the man: beware lest you imagine that the woman angered you, or wearied you, or troubled you with a bad trait in her; beware lest you think this bad trait will accompany her in the Hereafter. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and purified spouses﴾ (part of verse 15, Surat Al 'Imran): and purified spouses, purified of the things over which you were angry, and they will be purified by Allah's purifying of them.

﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; beneath them rivers will flow﴾ (part of verse 43, Surat al-A'raf): You find the Truth says once: ﴿beneath it rivers flow﴾ and once says: ﴿beneath them rivers flow﴾, and we find "min" (from) makes a distinction between the two statements. We see someone who settles in a palace, and water flowing around and beneath it, pleasing the eyes. The water of the Hereafter is water unspoiled, and it does not contain the turbidity of this world. Just as we rejoice in water in this world, we will rejoice in it many times over in the Hereafter. Water may flow beneath a palace while its source is far away, so the owner of the palace fears that another will cut it off from him. The Truth reassures His righteous servants: rivers will flow beneath your gardens, and all waters will have their own essence from the position of each being you are in; no one will control you, no one will block the source of water from you, and you will see the rivers of the Hereafter without banks, because everything is held as in this world, but by "Be" which belongs to Allah. Therefore the servants will say in the Garden of the Hereafter: ﴿Praise be to Allah who guided us to this; we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾ (part of verse 43, Surat al-A'raf). They say "Praise be to Allah" because He, may He be exalted, has gathered them, guided them and directed them to the reward and bliss without disturbances. Praising Allah is an act of worship that believers say in the Hereafter, because they discharged Allah's right in His obligations in this world, and Allah gives them beyond what they expect in the Hereafter. The bliss of the Hereafter has no restriction on it, and no human, however advanced in innovation, will be able to reach what is in Paradise, because the thing is realized for you as soon as it occurs to your mind. ﴿And they say, Praise be to Allah﴾: this praise of Allah was in this world an act of worship under obligation, whereas in the Hereafter it is "joy, delight and enjoyment." ﴿And they say, Praise be to Allah who guided us to this; we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾.

The believer says it, because if Allah had not sent down a heavenly method that defines the movement of his life in uprightness, warning him and frightening him away from sins, he would not have reached Paradise. Guidance, as we have said, is indicating the path that leads to the goal, so you must first know the goal and then lay down the path that leads to it, such that it is not crooked and nothing obstructs you on it that lengthens the distance. The saying of the Truth: ﴿We would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾ prevents humans from laying down laws for humans that guide them to the goal, because humans themselves do not know the goal; therefore their Creator makes it clear to them through His method sent down upon His Messenger.

Since guidance is from Allah, He, glory be to Him, will not address every human directly, but He sends Messengers who recite to us the verses of Allah and explain the method to us. Therefore the Truth in the same verse says with His wise words: ﴿Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. And it will be called out to them: This is the Garden, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ (part of verse 43, Surat al-A'raf). You, in the life of this world, when you find someone who says to you: if you want to rest, I advise you to go to such-and-such a place by such-and-such a route, and you will find yourself happy and at ease; then you believe him and carry out what he said, and you find the man truthful. Do you not feel happiness? If the Truth has sent Messengers with clear proofs, signs and the correct method, and believers walked upon it and then found Paradise and bliss, then they had to thank Allah and say: ﴿The messengers of our Lord came with the truth﴾. And because the Messengers did not deceive them but brought them good. ﴿And it will be called out to them: This is the Garden, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾.

It is as if the Truth is clarifying for us, while we are in the abode of obligation, that we should receive the method on this basis, and each one must determine his place in the Garden by his nearness to Allah's method or his distance from it, because entering Paradise is the reward of work according to the method of the Truth. Here the scholars paused, may Allah reward them with good, and said: how do we reconcile this verse: ﴿This is the Garden, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ (part of verse 43, Surat al-A'raf)?

And with the saying of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His grace and mercy"(1).

I say: there is no contradiction between the saying of Allah, the Exalted, and the saying of the Truthful and Believed One, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who conveyed from Allah, glory be to Him; rather, between them there is confirmation. For the Truth, when He legislated, made clear that whoever does righteous deeds will enter Paradise, and this legislation was not compelled upon Allah by anyone; rather, it is He who gives it to us out of His bounty. So no one has a right over Allah, because there is no work that returns benefit to Allah; following the method returns to the servant benefit and good. So if you enter Paradise, this too is by Allah's bounty. The Qur'an alerts us to combining these verses and that there is no conflict between a hadith text and a Qur'anic text. He says: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ (58) [Surat Yunus].

So the recompense of every deed returns to the human, because he receives his reward for his action; if the reward is greater than the worth of the action, it is from bounty. For the Truth is the One who says: ﴿...every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ (21) [Surat al-Tur], and He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿And that man has not but what he strives for﴾ (39) [Surat al-Najm]. If you understand the language and have a mature linguistic sense, you say: this "lam" is for possession, and it indicates that you have no claim upon Allah except through your striving according to Allah's method, and that this verse has defined justice and did not define bounty.

﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice...﴾ (58) [Surat Yunus]: An example of that is that we as Muslims pray over a deceased Muslim, and the legislation has commanded us to do so, and to ask Allah to overlook his misdeeds. Does this prayer add anything extra to the deceased beyond his deeds? If it were not a prayer that adds something, the legislation would not have commanded it. It is a prayer over a deceased Muslim, and his Islam is from his own deeds. And we find the Truth says: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith...﴾ (21) [Surat al-Tur]: meaning that fathers and sons share together in faith and in deeds. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will join them with their descendants...﴾ (21) [Surat al-Tur]: this joining indicates that the rank of the descendants was less than the rank of the fathers, but the Truth raises their rank in honour of the fathers. This joining is a reward for the descendants, and it may also be a reward for the fathers; so their children are brought to them while they are together, since all have shared in faith, and the fathers were careful to seek lawful provision in feeding the children and raised them only upon Allah's method. A father may see the children of a neighbour wearing luxurious clothing and eating good food, while his children bear hardship and live a life of subsistence with this father who is committed to righteous deeds and lawful earnings; and the children attain Paradise with the father because they bore with him the hardships of adhering to what is lawful.

Thus we find every believer has received the result of his deed and more. ﴿...And it will be called out to them: This is the Garden, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do (43)﴾ [Surat al-A'raf]: "Uriltumuha" (you have been made to inherit it) derives from "al-irth" (inheritance), and indicates that something has passed to another. We know that Allah, from eternity, knew how every creature would proceed and what it would do of disbelief, faith and disobedience, and despite that, He, glory be to Him, prepared for each of His creatures a place in the Garden on the basis that he would be a believer, and prepared for each of His creatures a place in the Fire on the basis that he would disbelieve.

So He, glory be to Him, prepared gardens according to the number of His creatures, and prepared places in Hell according to their number. So there is no shortage of places with a capable, powerful God. If we all believe, the vast Garden will not be too narrow for us, and, Allah forbid, if all creatures disbelieve, the Fire will not be too narrow for them. If a group of creatures are to enter Paradise by their deeds, where do the places of the people of the Fire go? The Truth, by His bounty, grants them to the believers. Thus they inherit those who did not deserve Paradise because of disbelief.

After speaking of the Garden and recompense, and of the praise of delight, joy and enjoyment, and of the covenant of the Garden, it was fitting for the Exalted Truth to speak of the position of the people of Paradise regarding the people of the Fire; so He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true; have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes." Then a crier will announce between them: "The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"﴾ (44).

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq and al-Marda, Muslim in Sifat al-Munafiqin, al-Tirmidhi in al-Janaiz, Abu Dawud in al-Janaiz, al-Nasa'i in al-Janaiz, Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, and Ahmad in his Musnad 6/125.

And so we see the rebuke. The verse portrays for us how the people of Paradise look upon the people of the Fire. This mutual seeing is part of the bliss and part of the painful punishment. When the believer who held to God's method sees those who opposed him, oppressed him and harmed him in the Fire, this is part of the complete delight. And the other, when he sees his opponent in Paradise, this too is part of the complete torment. Therefore they must see one another, and for this reason a dialogue takes place: the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire, acknowledging that they have found what their Lord promised them to be true and real, and that the Truth has granted them this Paradise. So: "Have you, O people of the Fire, found what your Lord promised to be true?"

We note that there is a difference between the two expressions although the logical context is one. The people of Paradise say: ﴿Indeed we have found what our Lord promised us to be true﴾, using "what our Lord promised us" (ما وعدنا ربنا). But in the second occurrence of "what He promised" (ما وعد), the particle of the pronoun for "you" (الكاف) is not attached; rather it says: "Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"

He, glory be to Him, said "what He promised" (ما وعد) alone and did not say "what He promised you" (ما وعدكم) as He said "what He promised us" (ما وعدنا). This is because the intent is to draw their attention to the absolute promise, not only the promise specific to them, but also the specific promise to the opposite party. Thus the absolute promise of God is realized: the people of Paradise, by their faith and their deeds, are in Paradise by God's grace, and the people of the Fire, by their disbelief and disobedience, are in the Fire as a punishment from God.

Here the people of the Fire answer: ("They said: Yes"). This is an acknowledgment by them of the visible reality they have lived, a reality that after having been a threat has now come to pass. They did not deny it, because denial occurs only between two disputants when they are not in the same scene. In the world, before the scene appeared, they used to deny the message from God, but the Hereafter has become a reality and their presence in the Fire has been realized.

﴿Then a caller called out between them: the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers﴾ (part of verse 44, Surah al-A'raf): That is, a caller from among the angels calls out, audible to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, that expulsion from the mercy of God is upon the wrongdoers, who wronged themselves by not believing and by denying the Last Day.

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾ (45)

The one who bars (others) from the way of Allah is the one who holds back from the way of Allah and also bars others from it; that is, he strays in himself and then leads others astray. These are the ones who seek to make the methodology (manhaj) of Allah crooked, who disparage it and do not believe in it, so they object to the establishing of the prescribed punishments (hudud) and retaliation (qisas), and they repel people from the methodology of Allah, so that people turn away from the religion. Thus they have barred themselves from the way of Allah and sought crookedness in what Allah has legislated, in order to repel people from what Allah has legislated. The matter does not stop at that; rather, they are disbelievers in the Hereafter. Had any one of them truly believed in the Hereafter and known that he has a return and a resort to Allah, he would not have done that.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 46:

He, glory be to Him, says after that: ﴿And between them is a barrier, and upon the heights (al-A'raf) are men who recognise each by his mark. And they call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, though they long (to).﴾

The barrier exists between the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire, and they see one another through it. Allah, the Truthful, has explained it when He says: ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Return you behind you and seek light." So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; inside it is mercy, and outside it, facing them, is torment.﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 57:13). The inner side of this barrier is mercy on the side of the people of the Garden, and its outer side, facing the people of the Fire, contains torment. God is capable of all things. Therefore nothing of the wretchedness of the people of the Fire reaches the people of the Garden, and nothing of the bliss of the people of the Garden reaches the people of the Fire. The people of the Fire hear a reply to their hope that some of the light of the people of the Garden might reach them: you are seeking guidance in a place other than the place of guidance. The time of obligation has ended, and whoever wished for the light of the Hereafter should have worked for it in the world. This light is not a gift from a creature to a creature, but a gift from the Creator to a created being who believed in Him. You say, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light," but it is not within the power of the people of the Garden to give any of their light; giving on that day belongs to God alone.

﴿And between them is a barrier, and upon the heights are men who recognise each by his mark﴾ (part of verse 46, Surah al-A'raf). The "each" (kullan) refers to the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. Already two groups have preceded: the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire, and there is a third group who are upon the A'raf. The "A'raf" (heights) is the plural of "'urf" (crest), taken from the crest of a rooster, which is its highest part, and likewise the mane of a horse. It is as if between the Garden and the Fire there is an elevated place like a crest, on which stand people who recognise the people of the Fire by their marks and recognise the people of the Garden by their marks; it is as if among the features and signs there is that which distinguishes the people of the Fire from the people of the Garden.

How do these features come to exist? It is said that at the moment a person believes he becomes fit to receive the features of faith, and whenever he enters the way of God through obedience and submission, God gives him a beautiful feature that becomes established in him, accompanying him and never leaving him. Conversely, for the people of the Fire, the features of majesty and beauty depart from them, and in their place come the features of ugliness, foulness and hideousness.

When the people of the A'raf see the people of the Garden, they say, "Peace be upon you," because the people of the A'raf, being lower in rank, say to the higher, the people of the Garden, "Peace be upon you."

The people of the A'raf are those whose evil deeds equal their good deeds in the balance of divine justice, which does not wrong anyone the weight of an atom. ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. But as for him whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss.﴾ (Surah al-Qari'ah, 101:6-9). And O Lord, You have mentioned the balance, and when You described what is weighed for them, You mentioned only two groups: a group whose scales are heavy and a group whose scales are light. The ultimate logic in measuring by the balance requires that a third group exist, those whose evil deeds equal their good deeds, so their scales are not heavy that they enter the Garden, nor light that they enter the Fire. These are the ones whose deeds are presented to ﴿the Garden of mercy﴾, and so they sit upon the A'raf. Strangely, when they see the people of the Garden, they say to them, "Peace be upon you," although they have not entered, yet they long to enter, because God's mercy precedes His wrath. ﴿...And they call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, though they long (to).﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:46). Naturally, in this place there is no deceit or trickery.

And when they look toward the people of the Fire?

﴿When their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say: "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾

Observe the Qur'anic expression "their eyes were turned" (ṣuriffat abṣāruhum): it does not mean they turned their eyes themselves, because the matter is not one of choice; they dislike looking at them because they are cursed. And there is a kind of rebuke to the people of the Fire in the phrase "their eyes were turned."

His word, the Truth: ﴿When their eyes are turned toward﴾, meaning toward the direction of the companions of the Fire, ﴿they say: "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people"﴾. Here the people of al-A'raf are calling out: "O Lord, keep us far from being with them." When they see the horror of the punishment, they ask Allah and seek refuge with Him that He not admit them among them.

Al-Sha'rawi, commentary on Surah al-A'raf (7), verse 48:

The Exalted says: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, saying: "Your gathering (of wealth and men) did not avail you, nor did your arrogance."﴾

It is as if the companions of the Heights have turned their gaze toward the companions of the Fire, and they see among them categories of those being punished. There is Abu Jahl, and there is al-Walid, along with Umayya ibn Khalaf and others who used to think that their leadership of their society and their dominance over others would grant them every authority and standing. They used to mock the early converts to Islam, such as Ammar, Bilal, Suhayb and Khabbab, and others who lived for the truth and with the truth. So the people of the Heights say to these: ﴿Your gathering did not avail you, nor did your arrogance.﴾

It is as if they are saying to them: your gathering together in misguidance in the world did not benefit you in anything. Your devils, your idols, your statues and your authority did not benefit you, and likewise your arrogance toward the call to faith: did that avail you anything? No. It did not avail you anything.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that:
﴿Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not grant them any mercy? "Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve."﴾

The people of al-A'raf point to the sincere believers, such as Bilal and Khabbab, and say to the people of the Fire, such as Abu Jahl and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: "Are these the righteous among the people of the Garden, of whom you said that they would never attain Allah's mercy?" Thus the people of al-A'raf have drawn a comparison and a weighing between the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire, as though they had forgotten their own condition of standing and awaiting relief. They rejoiced at the companions of the Garden and rebuked the people of the Fire, and their own condition did not keep them from standing in the position of decision on this matter. Here Allah, glory be to Him, admits the companions of al-A'raf into His Garden, because of their joy at the companions of the Garden and their rebuke of the people of the Fire, and He says to them:
﴿"Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve."﴾ [Surat al-A'raf].
