These, as we have said, are those whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal; they are the group who sat upon al-A'raf, so their good deeds were not heavy enough to admit them to the Garden, and their bad deeds were not heavy enough for them to enter the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 50:

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of the Garden: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided you." They will say: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers."﴾

The companions of the Fire call out to the companions of the Garden, seeking help and asking that they give them, and pour upon them, some water or some of the provision Allah has granted them in the Garden. The people of the Garden will say: "We are now bound by 'Be' (kun), and we no longer have choice. Allah has forbidden you anything of the Garden and withheld it from you; so you, O people of the Fire, are prevented, or these delights are prohibited to you." When the people of the Fire ask for water, they are asking the friends of existence, [while they are] in a Fire whose enclosure has surrounded them; and ﴿if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces﴾.

Therefore the Truth (Allah) then says, concerning the disbelievers who were forbidden the good of the Garden: ﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life deceived. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their Day, and as they used to deny Our signs.﴾

Thus the Truthful Lord (al-Haqq subhanahu wa ta'ala) clarifies for us in this verse who the disbelievers are whom He has forbidden Paradise: they are those who took their religion as amusement and play. The first stage a person passes through is play, and then comes the stage of diversion (lahw). We know that every action is directed by an active energy, and before that energy is directed at it, the action passes through the mind in order to determine the aim of the effort. This aim has limits: either it brings a benefit to him, or it averts a harm from him. Every aim that neither brings a benefit nor averts a harm is play (la'ib).

So the definition of play (la'ib) is: an action for which its doer did not intend a correct purpose to avert a harm or bring a benefit. Just as children play with their toys, when a child holds a toy cannon or a toy car, does he have a correct purpose to which he directs his energy? No; for if the purpose were correct, the child would not break his toys. And the child often breaks his toy shortly after, and this is evidence that he directs energy toward no correct purpose and brings himself neither benefit nor averts from himself any harm.

But when energy is directed toward what is less important than what matters, this is diversion (lahw), as when what is required of you is one thing and you direct your energy to another. What God punishes for is diversion, while play is not. Therefore we find the Prophet (ﷺ) asking families to train their children in things that may benefit the nation, such as swimming, archery, and horse riding. But the misfortune of mankind in our time is that they have made play an end in itself. Strangely, play has acquired the law of seriousness, and no one can violate it without being punished, because the referee watches the match, and if the referee forgets a matter or makes a mistake, the crowd erupts. And I ask: you have transferred the law of seriousness to play, so why have you left seriousness without a law?

Likewise, the misfortune of diversion is heavy, because the diverted person leaves the important matter and goes to the unimportant matter. He sits down to the game of backgammon (nard), which is the board game, and leaves the work that produces his livelihood. And would that this diversion were confined to the diverted person, but it attracts the attention of those who are not diverted and takes their time, time that should have been spent on beneficial energy. The corruption of all societies arises only from some of their members using their energies in what returns to themselves and not to their nation with good. Thus diversion is idle energy. ﴿They took their religion as amusement and play, and the worldly life deceived them﴾: their deception by the worldly life comes only from the means that were created to be responsive to them, so each of them thought he was the master in control. When the worldly life deceived them, they forgot the seriousness that leads them to the beneficial, eternal end, and their punishment will be God's saying, glory be to Him: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day, and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ (part of verse 51, surah al-A'raf). Does His saying, mighty and majestic, "We will forget them," mean that He leaves them to what they do? No; rather, Hell takes them to scorch them, and their forgetting here means that He, glory be to Him, does not include them in the manifestations of His grace, kindness and mercy, and leaves them to the Fire, which scorches their faces and roasts their skins.

Thus it is confirmed anew that this world is the place where a person prepares his place in the Hereafter. If he wants a place in the highest levels (illiyyun), then he must perform the duty that gives him his place there. And if he wants a place lower than that, then he must perform the lesser work. As if a person by his deeds determines his place in the Hereafter, because the Truth does not recompense creation arbitrarily, presumptuously, or unjustly, but recompenses a person according to his work. Therefore there are the people of Paradise, the people of the Fire, and the people of the Heights (A'raf). This knowledge that the Truth reveals to us as a Qur'an, warning and giving good news, is a proof for every Muslim, so that we compete to have our positions in the Hereafter be honorable positions.

﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and the worldly life deceived them. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day, and as they used to deny Our signs (51)﴾ (surah al-A'raf). And when the Truthful Lord says: ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs﴾, the signs (ayat) are either cosmic: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾ (part of verse 37, surah Fussilat); or Qur'anic verses, as in His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses are made distinct﴾ (part of verse 3, surah Fussilat); or they are signs of miracles to establish prophethood, as in His saying: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (part of verse 59, surah al-Isra'). So they denied all the signs. The first denial was the denial of the cosmic signs that they witnessed before the duty came. They lived through the night and the day, they breathed the air, they enjoyed the warmth of the sun, the rain watered their lands, and they found the universe arranged and ordered, providing for man before man had awareness or power. These signs should have drawn their attention to the fact that they have a Creator, the Supreme Truth. And when the prophetic procession came to them, they denied the signs of miracles that indicate the truthfulness of the messengers. And when the Qur'an came as a miracle, they denied the detailed verses that carry the method. So they have no excuse in any of that, because the Truth says: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We had detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ (52).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 52:

That is, they have no excuse for any part of this denial, because the Book is detailed (mufassal). They might say: the Book is something new that has come upon us, and likewise the Messenger who brought it. So what is their position regarding the fixed cosmic signs? They have denied those too. ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge﴾.

"And We detailed it": that is, He, glory be to Him, did not send down speech that is general (mujmal) or ambiguous. No, rather in it is the detail of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. He detailed its rulings, its meanings, its admonitions and its narratives, until it came as an upright book, without any crookedness. And He, glory be to Him, is able to send down the method suited to the capacity and station of every human being.

When someone comes to us asking for a legal opinion (fatwa) on some matter, trying to twist the words so that we will issue him a ruling that justifies what he is doing, we say to him: We do not have a detailed fatwa for you, because the fatwas we have are all ready-made, and you may bring your question under whichever fatwa you wish.

﴿We detailed it with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ (52). There are people who heard the Qur'an, saw the signs, and were guided. Why were these guided and those went astray? Whoever believes in the Supreme Existence (al-Wujud al-A'la) has believed, as we said in surah al-Baqarah: ﴿This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-conscious (muttaqun)﴾ [al-Baqarah 2]. So whoever was guided to the truth believed in the Qur'an. Among them are those whose eyes overflow with tears when they hear the Qur'an, and among them is the one whose heart the faith does not touch when he hears the Qur'an.

﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those given knowledge: "What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad 47:16]. These are the ones whose hearts have become hardened, so that the light of the Qur'an does not penetrate them, enter them, or mix with them. Therefore you find the truth responding to them with His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Those are the ones whom God has sealed upon their hearts, and they follow their own desires﴾ [Muhammad 47:16].

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; and as for those who do not believe, there is heaviness in their ears, and it is blindness for them﴾ (41:44).

We have previously offered the example that the action is in some cases one, but the receiving subject differs, so the result differs. For instance, if you are in winter, go out and find the air cold, and feel that the tips of your fingers are nearly freezing from the cold, you join your two fists together and blow into them, perhaps doing so without intending to, in order to warm your hands. Likewise, when a cup of very hot tea is brought to you and you want to drink from it, you blow on it to cool it. The breath from your mouth is one; it brings warmth to your hands and coolness to the cup of tea. Thus the action is one, but the recipient is different. Likewise the Qur'an: whoever has the readiness for faith is guided by it, and whoever lacks the readiness, his heart is veiled (ghulf) from faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 53:

The stance of those who are incapable of receiving mercy is an unnatural stance. What do they expect after this disbelief, after their presumption, after their arrogance, after their refusal, and after taking religion as a diversion and a game? What do they expect? Behold, the True One, glory be to Him, makes the outcome clear to them:

﴿Do they await anything but its final outcome? On the day its final outcome comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth. Do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us? Or could we be sent back so that we might do other than what we used to do?" They have certainly lost their own selves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them.﴾ (7:53)

What is the meaning of ta'wil (interpretation, here meaning ultimate outcome)? Ta'wil is that to which a thing returns. It is the outcome which the Truth has prepared: mercy and Paradise for whoever believes, and the Fire for whoever disbelieves. The Truth is the One who speaks and who possesses His word, because the whole universe is in His hand.

Here the Exalted and Glorious says: ﴿Do they await anything but its final outcome?﴾ That is: do they await anything but the return to which their deeds lead? Indeed their final destination is punishment after reckoning, on the day when the ta'wil, the end and outcome of what they did, comes.

When the Day of Resurrection comes, the truth becomes manifest and the truthfulness of what the Messenger brought of promise and threat becomes clear, what will their words be? They will say what Allah, glory be to Him, has put on their tongues: ﴿Those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth"﴾. That is: they will declare their belief at a time when that belief will not benefit them, because they will no longer be in the abode of obligation; they will acknowledge faith at a moment when it will not profit them.

﴿Those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth. Do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us?"﴾ (part of 7:53): So they acknowledge that the messengers brought the true method, and they ask about an intercessor. We know that an intercessor must be beloved to the one with whom he intercedes. In this world we find that a person seeks someone to intercede for him with a person who is dear and esteemed to that person, or who has a word and a favour over him, so that his word is not rejected. Who, then, will come on the Day of Resurrection to intercede for these people? No one. They will find that they take as intercessors those whom they had taken as rivals to Allah. And these will also declare their aversion to them. Even if Allah had enabled them to intercede, they would not give it to the disbelieving polytheists; for in this world these were people who were directed by the commands of men and their misguidance. But on the Day of Reckoning no one is subject to another's will; even the limbs are not subject to the will of their owner, but are subject to the Supreme Truth. In the Hereafter there are no wills for anyone.

We have already offered an example and said: suppose a platoon in an army has a small leader of the rank of an officer, and the soldiers of the platoon are obliged to carry out his words. Then they went to a battle, and the junior officer gave them wrong orders, imposing his will upon them, and they carried out what they were ordered. When they return and the supreme commander calls them to account, they will say: "We did what the officer charged with our command ordered us to do." Likewise, in the Hereafter the limbs will come: their hands, their feet, their tongues and their skins will bear witness against them.

Thus the parts will raise their complaint to Allah on a day when no one will have dominion except Him, and on that day the deniers will speak the truth that will not benefit them.

﴿The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth﴾ (part of 7:53): They will search for intercession, but they will not find it. Indeed, the first to mock those who worshipped other than Allah will be the very objects of worship themselves. This is why we find the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be its bound-for-entry﴾ (21:98). And what is the fault of the worshipped? The idols have no fault; rather each of them wishes to satisfy itself by being an instrument of punishment for those who gave it what was not its due. Hence we find that the stones that were worshipped say: "You worshipped us, and we were not the ones who worship Allah among those who stand in the pre-dawn hours; for one who stands in the pre-dawn hours among the rest of beings might have chosen something other than this, but we were compelled to obedience." And they took our silence as evidence against us.

The stones declare that they did not possess the power to refuse that anyone should worship them, or to drive him away from them, and they declare his foolishness to him. The poet says: "They have transgressed out of ignorance, as they transgressed against the son of Mary and the disciples. For the excessive one is his reward, and the excessive one in it, the mercy of the Forgiving One saves him."

Thus the Truth will come to them clearly on the Day of Resurrection.

They will ask to return to the world, and this is from their loss; for such an acknowledgment is not faith, since faith is through the unseen and not in the witnessed scene. And even if they were returned, they would not believe!

The Truth says: ﴿Even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ (6:28). It is as if they forgot, at the moment of their acknowledgment, that they were among those who are other than the believers, and the decisive word from Allah came concerning them. ﴿They have certainly lost their own selves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ (part of 7:53): Loss has come upon them after what they used to fabricate against Allah in the world has vanished from them. They rejected His worship, and worshipped others, idols which became fuel for the Fire they will burn in.

Then the Truth says, after that: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, which pursues it swiftly, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (54)

Here is lordship (rububiyyah), and here is divinity (uluhiyyah). "Your Lord is Allah." No one disputes the matter of lordship, because the Truth says on the tongues of the disbelievers and polytheists: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ (39:38). Likewise, if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would say, "Allah." No one has claimed lordship for himself, because lordship has come to them with benefit. But divinity has entered with a method, which is: "Do" and "Do not." For obligation (taklif) comes from the God who is Lord, and obligation is a blessing from Him, and it is for your own benefit. Nothing in obligation returns to Allah. Your good or bad deeds will not give Allah an attribute He did not have, because the attributes of perfection preceded your existence. And if you are still in doubt about this lordship, then your Lord is Allah, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, exalted above comparison. It is like a mother telling her child: "Your father told you not to stay out of the house at night," and the child refuses. So the mother reminds her child: "It is your father who brings you food, drink, and clothing, and gives you pocket money..." etc.

I gave this example to explain how the one who imposes obligations is the Provider, and no one other than Him provides. Therefore you must accept His obligations, because He has already bestowed upon you His grace by giving you and subjecting the world to you. Earlier, the Truth, glory be to Him, detailed for us the creation of man, and here He details for us the creation of the heavens and the earth, because the setting in which man exists is the heavens and the earth, and all the good things that come to him come from the heavens and from the earth. And if Allah has taught us how He created us, He teaches us how He created the heavens and the earth. The creation of the heavens and the earth are two matters that modern science occupies itself with. Some scientists have said that the earth separated from the sun, and some have theoretically supposed that man's origin is a monkey. To these we say: this is a judgment from you that is not acceptable, because you did not witness creation. Therefore you must hear from the One who created creation, so that He may tell you how He created it.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, which pursues it swiftly, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (7:54). The verse addresses the first creation, which is the heavens and the earth, as I have explained, and it is the existential setting of the human being, the successor (khalifah), and man arrived in this universe with all its forces and laws. It is as if Allah prepared for the successor before the successor was created, so that when the successor came he would find a universe subjected to him; and no creature among them can deviate from Allah's will in anything. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created﴾: the meaning of "created" (khalaqa) is to bring into existence something that was non-existent and to originate it without a precedent model. Our Lord, glory be to Him, has arranged everything with a precise order unprecedented; this is the meaning of creation. The active noun of the root "khalq" is "khaliq" (creator), and Glory be to Him, the Exalted, combines them even though He alone is the Creator, when He says: ﴿...So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (23:14). So there is the Supreme Creator, who is Allah, but He, glory be to Him, has also associated with Him another creator, and He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾ How? Because creation is the bringing into existence of something non-existent. One who makes a microphone is said to have created it, one who makes a cup is said to have created it, one who makes a lamp is said to have created it, because it was a thing non-existent in itself, and he brought it into existence. But the difference is that a human creator brings something non-existent into existence from something existent and does not bring a new material. Whoever takes the materials existing in the universe and designs from them a lamp, melts sand, and evacuates the air inside the glass bulb, is said to have created the lamp, bringing a non-existent thing into existence from an existent one.

But the Creator is the best of creators, because He creates from nothing, and He does not deny that His creatures, when they bring a non-existent thing into existence, may be described as creators. And glory be to Him, when He created, He created from nothing. Also, when you make any craft, it remains rigid in the form of its craft: whoever makes a cup from molten sand, the cup remains just so, and we cannot, as I have said before, bring a male cup and a female cup, put them together in a place, and say to them: "Beget for us small cups."

But what our Lord creates He gives the secret of life, and by the law He makes it produce others, grow, and mature. So He is the best of creators. And Allah, glory be to Him, gives us the best news of His creation of the heavens and the earth. He made clear that the heavens are seven, and they came in the plural, while the earth came in the singular. But in another verse He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ (65:12). So whenever He created seven heavens, He created seven earths. Why did He bring "heavens" in the plural and leave the word "earth" in the singular? Why did He not say "seven earths"? Because the word "aradin" (earths) is heavy on the tongue, so He left it for its heaviness, and brought "heavens" in the plural for its lightness and the ease of its pronunciation.

The heaven (sama') is everything that is above you and shades you; this is the meaning of heaven in the language. But is the heaven that Allah intends everything above you? The star is what is above you; it may be said that the sun is above you, and the moon is above us all. We draw attention here and say to people who wish to make the heavens the planets: they are not always above us; the sun rises at times and sets at other times, and so does the moon.

Thus the description of the sun or the moon lapses for some time, and it is not correct to describe either of them as a heaven permanently. Another point: when they said of the planets that were known, that they were seven planets, and said that these are the heaven, they fell into error by this statement. The Truth made clear to us by knowledge that the sun has other satellites. Sometimes scientists saw eight satellites, sometimes nine, and other times ten satellites, and so the idea that the satellites are the heaven collapsed, and the heaven remained what is above all of this. And the Truth is the One who says: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the planets﴾ (37:6). So this is an adornment of the nearest heaven. The heaven our Lord intends is not what they describe; rather, the heaven is another creation that no one can reach, and the jinn used to sit in it in places for listening, ﴿So whoever listens now will find a watching flame lying in wait﴾ (72:9). This happened after his mission, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Truth is the One who told us so. The Truth has not clarified for us the reality of this heaven and its system; that is, our Lord wants our minds to understand only this measure. Glory be to Him, He is the Creator of the heaven above us, and He, the Exalted, is the Creator of earths. And where are these earths? Are they scattered earths?

Science has proven that each galaxy contains a million solar systems, and each solar system contains an earth. So there are many earths. We notice that when the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks of the earth, each addressee is addressed concerning the earth in which he is. Therefore some scholars said: in this higher world there are earths, and to each earth the Truth has sent a messenger.

And the Truth is the One who says: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed in them of creatures; and He is, when He wills, over their gathering, competent﴾ (42:29). Science gives us more discoveries every day. Thus the heaven is what is above you, and the earth is what carries you. Since there are seven heavens, and the first heaven is a great void and expanse, and after it comes the second heaven that covers the first heaven, and every heaven has an earth and another heaven in it. We are not charged with this; we are charged with knowing that the earth we are on is created by Allah.

And the Truth says: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in six days...﴾ (7:54),

And His saying "in six days" is a time frame for the creation. We know the day to be the period from sunrise to sunset and then to sunrise again, and its duration is twenty-four hours. But we must know some of the Qur'anic terminology of the Truth.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿...Travel through them by night and day in security﴾ (34:18). That is, there is night and there is day. Thus the day with the Truth is other than the day with us, because we apply the term to the time period from the rising of the sun until its setting and its rising anew. Thus the day in the astronomical sense is from sunrise to sunrise, or from sunset to sunset. And the Truth's saying ﴿Travel through them by night and day in security﴾ means that He, glory be to Him, made the night a portion and the day a portion. Was there anyone who knew the day before the sun existed? And if the sun is what determines the day, how did the day come to be known before it, especially since when the heavens and the earth were created there was no sun or planets? We must know here that this is His determination, glory be to Him, and He addressed us with it after we knew the length of the day. Have you not read the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿...And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening﴾ (19:62)? In the Hereafter there is no morning or evening; so He, glory be to Him, determined the morning and determined the evening. Likewise "in six days," and these are the decisive verses in the Qur'an concerning the time of creation: six days. But the verse of detail about the creation appears, on the surface, to be eight days. Read with me: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed therein firmly set mountains upon it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, complete for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days...﴾ (41:9–12).

The apparent meaning of the verse of detail is eight days, while the verses of summary all say they are days. From this point the orientalists entered, and they falsely claimed that the Qur'an contains contradiction, and they tried to make it a loud uproar. We say: He, glory be to Him, created the earth and what is in it in four complete days without addition or subtraction, so the meaning is that this occurred and was completed within four days, and to them is added the creation of the heavens in two days, so the number of days in which the heavens and the earth were created is six days; or we carry the detailed upon the summary. So when the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days...﴾ (7:54), does Allah's creation need treatment, that it should require extended time? Our Lord creates by "Be," and we humans work on things according to our capacity to create something, and every process we undertake takes time; but for one who creates by the word "Be," the matter is very easy for him, glory be to Him and exalted. But why did He bring the report of creation in six days?

We know that there is a difference between the birth of a thing and its preparation for birth. We had already given an example earlier, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, of the yogurt maker, who brings cups of warm milk, then puts in each part of them a portion of yogurt culture, and places those cups in the suitable atmosphere. Does this man perform work for twelve hours in each cup, which is the time needed for the cup to ferment? Certainly not; he has been content that each cup contains the elements of fermentation, so that they react by themselves to

Al-Sha'rawi, the commentary (tafsir) on surah 7, verse 55:

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.﴾

Supplication (du'a') is only made by one who is incapable, calling upon One who is able to accomplish and bring about what he cannot, or who can help him to it. When you feel that you are powerless, you lean upon the One who has absolute power, for your power is limited. So if you are tyrannical or arrogant, know your station and rank well, and turn back from that, for you are a passing accident. Supplication is humble submission, lowliness, and reverence, and an acknowledgment from you that you are powerless, and a request from your Lord for support and aid. Keeping your powerlessness and your Lord's power in mind represents for you the continuation of faith's certainty. Our Lord has placed needs upon people only for this reason, for when a person sees things submitting to him, and he innovates and invents, he may be seized by conceit, and then he comes upon a need in which means are scarce and he is powerless, so he stands to supplicate. Whoever is arrogant and haughty and has pride and insolence goes to a "poor" man (ghalban), an ascetic who has stripped himself of status and authority and devoted himself to the worship of God, and says to him: "I adjure you by the Messenger of God that you supplicate for me, for I am in a crisis." The one who asks the poor ascetic is a man who is honored among his people, but he thinks that the poor ascetic is nearer to God than he is.

So supplication is humble submission and the display of lowliness and reverence before God, so that faith's certainty may be sustained.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-A'raf): Beware lest you supplicate while in your mind is the thought that your need will be met by supplication. Rather, you should supplicate only to display humble submission, lowliness and reverence. And if you did not supplicate, your affairs would proceed as they were decreed. Supplication is a display of reverence. Beware lest you understand that you call upon God so that He fulfils your demands, for He, glorified is He, is exalted above being an employee at your service, and there is a system that He has established for the fulfilment of the needs of His servants. Among people there are those who ask in supplication for harmful things.

﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 11): A person's heart may become attached to wishes that may harm him. Therefore we say: "Do not be hasty in supplication, seeking wishes that may be evil for you." The All-Knowing Truth arranges our affairs for us. Beware also of despairing when your supplication that is on your mind is not answered, for God brings good to His servants. And if He fulfilled for you some of what you supplicate, evil may come from it, and God leaves your judgments to show you this, and you say: "That thing I was wishing for has been achieved and it came as evil upon me." An example of this: you may reserve a seat on a plane but you do not catch it, for it took off before you reached it, and you are saddened because some of your interests have escaped you and were not achieved, and then you are surprised to learn that this plane fell into the sea.

So, let your share of supplication be humility, submission and humble entreaty to Him, glorified is He, not your being granted what you ask for. You supplicated to seek good, so leave the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and His knowledge to bring you good, and listen to God's words: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 11). So when the Truth says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾, He asks us to call upon Him because we will face multiple moments in which we are unable to do things. Instead of remaining subdued by the attribute of inability regarding a thing, remember that you have a strong, all-powerful Lord, and when you remember that, means will not carry you away from the fold of faith. We said before: whoever has a father does not bear anxiety for life; if one who has a father bears no anxiety over life's requirements, then whoever has a Lord should be ashamed and know that his Lord will provide him with good. Therefore He, glorified is He, makes clear: when means fail you, remember that you have a Lord. He has commanded you to call upon Him, and do not think that your share of supplication is to be granted what you asked; rather let your share of supplication be the display of humility and reverence before God. What has happened to you may be the result of your having deceived yourself. Qarun was earlier to conceit: what happened to him? The Truth defeated him and brought upon him the worst punishment. The Truth may make the refusal of means and their withholding from you a lesson, so that you turn to God, but your turning to God should not be for the purpose of having your need met; rather make the basis of your turning to God that you show your powerlessness before Him, and submission and reverence, so that He gives you what was not in your mind when you supplicated.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-A'raf): "Secret" (khufyah) has one meaning, which is that supplication should be hidden and concealed, and it has another meaning, which is that it comes from fear, i.e., call upon your Lord out of fear of the implications of the attributes of majesty, such as the Compeller and the Subduer, or out of fear that He will return it to you and not accept it from you.

"Call upon your Lord humbly" (tadarru'an): in lowliness, abasement and submission, "and in secret" (khufyah) between you and your Lord. So do not supplicate aloud and make it your sole act, because the Prophet (ﷺ) taught us when he was on an expedition, his companions descended into a valley, and when they descended into the valley they shouted with tahlil and takbir. He said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; you are calling upon One who is All-Hearing, Near, and He is with you."(1) Supplicating to God in secret keeps you away from ostentation (riya'), and it is more concealing for you in your requests to your Lord, because when He makes clear to you: "Supplicate to Me in your secret, for I am All-Hearing, All-Knowing; I know all that is apparent from you and what is hidden," supplicate with submission, reverence and lowliness, so that the desire for pride, the desire for arrogance and the desire for tyranny are broken within you.

If you look at this, you will find that many scholars say: "We know people who recite the Qur'an in our presence and we did not know any movement of their lips, and we knew people who derive rulings from the words of God and we did not see any agitation diverting them from us." So the matter expresses an inner, internal preoccupation.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to keep us away from ostentation and wants to conceal our requests for us, because a person may ask God, glorified and exalted is He, for something he would be ashamed for another to hear.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-A'raf): If you look at this verse you will find that many people violate it collectively. At night, for example, you find those who climb the minarets or shout into loudspeakers, which have made them independent of climbing minarets, and one of these may be sleeping all day because calling the adhan is his only work. After that he keeps shouting and crying out, saying: "These are supplications." Meanwhile, among people there is one who sleeps to take his rest so that he may work by day, and nobody asks this sleeper except that when dawn comes he wakes and performs the prayer. So why do we disturb people with this? We must warn those who think they are reminding people of God's religion that by this deed they are not taking the right path, for we cannot remind people of God and commit a violation or harm anyone; for He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾. Humility and secrecy require that I do not disturb people, or that I not announce, with a loud voice, matters I want for myself personally, like one who comes at the end of the prayer and makes his supplication aloud while raising his hands. To such a one I say: God, glorified and exalted is He, has made the qunut for us to supplicate in, and He left every Muslim to supplicate with what moves him. When you supplicate at the end of the prayer, there may be a latecomer (masbuq) who joined the prayer after the imam had already gone ahead by one or two or three rak'ahs and who wants to complete his prayer, and when you raise your voice in supplication at the end of your prayer, you are in fact spoiling his completion of his prayer, and occupying him with words of your own invention and speech of your own, diverting him from something obligatory upon him. Whoever does this does it out of good intention, but he harms the worship of another.

So we must be mindful that God, glorified and exalted is He, has demands; these demands may be contravened by the self for a purpose it considers good, but put it within the frame of: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think that they are doing good work﴾ [Surat al-Kahf, 103–104]. We must be mindful of such matters, and we must provide rest for the one who sleeps so that he may get up, pray the dawn prayer and go to his work; therefore there is no need for a person to open the "microphone" and raise his voice in supplication. Whoever does that thinks he is keen on a desired matter, but he disturbs the sleeper, and even disturbs the one who prays at night, or "interferes" with one who recites the Qur'an or studies some knowledge. Whoever does this must leave each person to his own emotions, and be master of himself and master of his choice. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us images like this when He says: ﴿When he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾ [Maryam 19:3] ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with white hair...﴾ (Maryam 19:3–4). So the word "khafi" (secret) is present in the Qur'an, and we must be mindful of secret supplication.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret, indeed He does not love the transgressors﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-A'raf): So if it is not humble, it is transgression in supplication, for you are the one obligated and God is the one who obligates; He says to you: "Supplicate to Me humbly and in secret." If you do other than this, you will be a transgressor, and all those people must understand that they are transgressors, whether the transgression lies in the manner of asking or in what is asked. For the Truth has specified the manner of asking, making clear: "Supplicate to Me in concealment," so if you supplicate other than in concealment you will be transgressing God's method. Likewise the transgression may lie in what is asked: it is not correct, for example, to say: "I supplicate You, O Lord, to make me a prophet." That is not correct, and our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, taught us through what He related about Noah. He said: ﴿And Noah called upon his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges﴾ [Hud 11:45] ﴿He said: O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose deeds are not righteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant﴾ [Hud 11:46] (Surat Hud). Here the Truth alerted Noah to transgression in what is asked, so the Truth said: ﴿So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge﴾ (part of verse 46, Surat Hud). Therefore we find Noah seeking forgiveness, because he asked and supplicated to God with this supplication without knowledge; when he recognised his sin he sought God's forgiveness and said: ﴿He said: My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You for that about which I have no knowledge﴾ (part of verse 47, Surat Hud).

And the Truth, glorified is He, said to him: ﴿Descend in peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat Hud). So whoever does not first hear God's method and then apply it in supplication is transgressing against the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and He does not love transgressors.

(1) Related by Muslim in this wording, and by al-Bukhari. The meaning of "arba'u" is: be gentle with yourselves and lower your voices.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 56:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order, and call upon Him in fear and in hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾

The earth is the place of the khalifah (vicegerent), who is the human being, and in it are the original means for sustaining life. The sky, the earth, the sun and the air are all subjected (musakhkhar) for you. You need no obligation (taklif) regarding them: you do not say, "O sun, rise," or "O air, blow," for all of that is subjected to you. You are required not to corrupt what lies within your choice (ikhtiyar), because you cannot corrupt the higher laws of the cosmos. You cannot alter the course of the sun, nor the course of the moon, nor the course of the wind. You will not be able to set right what you cannot come close to corrupting, because its command is not in your hand, since you have no choice in it. Corruption arises only from the faculties of choice that exist within you. Allah has not left them unrestrained; rather, He has bounded them with a method that protects the movement of life through "do" and "do not." So if He, glorified is He, has sent down the Qur'an, and the Qur'an contains a method that protects your choice, then He has given you the elements of setting things right. For this reason He says to you: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order, and call upon Him in fear and in hope﴾ (part of verse 56, surah al-A'raf). Here the Truth returns once more to speak of supplication (du'a'). First He gave the command that supplication be made with humility (tadarru') and in secret, and here He clarifies a second way of supplicating: ﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope.﴾ Fear is from the attributes of His might and subjugation (jabarut and qahr), and hope is in the attributes of His forgiveness and mercy, because Allah has attributes of beauty (jamal) and attributes of majesty (jalal). So call upon Him in fear regarding the objects of the attributes of majesty, and in hope regarding the objects of the attributes of beauty. Or: in fear that you may be turned away, and in hope for what you are seeking.

﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾ (part of verse 56, surah al-A'raf). So who determines the nearness of mercy to Him? It is the human being: if he does good, mercy draws near to him, and the reins are in the hand of the human being, because Allah does not act arbitrarily and does not dominate anyone. If you want the mercy of Allah to draw near to you, then hold fast to good-doing (ihsan). ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾ That is why we have said that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: "I do not tire until you tire" (from a hadith qudsi).

You enter the houses of Allah and pray at any time, and you stand in any place to perform the prayer. So, the remembrance of your Lord is in your hand, and He, glorified is He, has set for you five times, but all the remaining times are in your hand, and you can stand before Allah at any moment. He, glorified is He, says: "Whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running" (from a hadith qudsi). He, exalted is He, makes clear to you: rest yourself, and I will come to you, for running may tire you, but I am not touched by fatigue, weariness or incapacity. It is as if the Truth asks of the servant only that he possess a feeling that he wishes to meet his Lord. So the whole matter is in your hand. He, glorified is He, says: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself, and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it" (from a hadith qudsi). Thus He, glorified is He, affirms for you that His mercy is in your hand, and He has given it to you; and when you trace it back, you find it to be a bounty from Allah, yet it is in your hand. ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾ We know that in Him there are attributes and there is essence. The essence is ﴿Allah﴾, the Giver of existence, and He possesses all the attributes of perfection, and every attribute has its object: mercy has its object, and raising the dead (al-ba'th) has its object. Among His names, glorified is He, is "al-Ba'ith" (the Raiser). Beware of neglecting the essence; keep yourself always glorifying His exalted essence. You may say: "O Lord, I want You to have mercy on me in such-and-such," and what you asked may not be granted to you, but that does not make you turn away from glorifying the essence, because not achieving what you asked is for your benefit and better for you.

The scholars have paused at this word "near" (qarib). Some of them wondered about the reason the feminine ta' (ta' al-ta'nith) does not appear after the word of majesty (lafz al-jalalah). We know that the Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and among the Arabs there are words in which the masculine and feminine are equal, and what is said of the masculine is said of the feminine in the same way. We say "rajul sabur" (a patient man) and "imra'ah sabur" (a patient woman), and we do not say "sabura." And we say "rajul mi'tar" (a man who uses much perfume, i.e. one who frequently uses perfume) and "imra'ah mi'tar" (a woman who frequently uses perfume). And we say "qarib" just as we say "qatil" in the sense of "maqtul" (killed). So one says "rajul qatil" and "imra'ah qatil," and one does not say "qatila" unless the word "woman" is mentioned with it or something indicates the feminine, because "qatil" applies to the male and the female.

These are the expressions of correct language. Language has established this by means of grounds: when you say "rajul sabur" or "imra'ah sabur," patience entails endurance, resolve and strength; therefore we do not say "imra'ah sabura," but rather bring the description suited to endurance and strength. Beware of weakening it by attaching the feminine marker. Likewise "rajul mi'tar" and "imra'ah mi'tar": the man who is mi'tar is the one whom people recognise by the penetrating fragrance of his perfume, while the woman is built upon concealment; so if she perfumes herself, she has imitated the man, and she is called "imra'ah mi'tar." When we look at the word "qarib," it is of the pattern "fa'il," in which the masculine and feminine are equal, as is evidenced by God's saying: ﴿And if you two support one another against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are supporters (zahir)﴾ (part of verse 4, surah al-Tahrim). The word "mala'ikah" (angels) is feminine in form, yet the Truth did not say "zahirah," because "zahir" means one who helps, and assistance requires strength, resolve and support; so for it He used the word suited to indicate strength, which is "zahir." Likewise His saying: ﴿...indeed the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾ (surah al-A'raf, 56): "qarib" is of the pattern "fa'il" in the sense of "maf'ul" (passive). Some people may understand "qarib" in the sense of "fa'il" (active), i.e. "qarib" as in "raḥim" and "rahim" (merciful; one who shows mercy). That would mean that it is the mercy that draws near to the doers of good; but the matter is not so. Rather, mercy is the thing brought near, and good-doing is what brings it near. So "fa'il" here is in the sense of "maf'ul," which is equal for the masculine and the feminine. Or it is because it was construed according to an interpretation of mercy as "the womb" (rahm) or "mutual mercy" (tarahum); or because it is an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "a thing that is near"; or because the feminine of "mercy" is not real (ghayr haqiqi); or because mercy is a verbal noun (masdar), and the verbal noun by right is masculine.

And then the Truth says:

﴿It is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His mercy, until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land, and We send down water therewith and bring forth from it fruits of every kind. Thus We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember.﴾ (57)

The directing of the winds is the stirring of the air in the universe, and from this stirring of the air come many extremely beneficial results. When we sit in a crowded place filled with breath, we say to the one sitting beside the window, "Let us air the room a little." If the window's air is not enough, you bring a fan to take from the layers of the atmosphere a new layer of air that contains a great deal of oxygen. So the sending of the winds is a necessity, so that the air does not remain stagnant. The atmosphere would become polluted by this stagnation. If every person were to settle in a place with enclosed air, the place would fill with the carbon dioxide exhaled from their breathing, and then they would soon suffocate. For this reason God willed the movement of the winds as a general and continuous mercy in everything. It is also a mercy related to sustenance, just as it is related to the essentials of life: breath, water and food. The directing of the winds serves to renew the air we breathe, and likewise the formation of water, for He, glory be to Him, said about the winds: ﹛until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land…﹜ [Surat al-A'raf]. The winds are what help form the rains that fall upon the earth and water the soil that we plough. Thus the winds are a glad tiding in three things. The first thing is the moving of the layers of air; otherwise the atmosphere would spoil…

[Note: the sentence "The first thing is the moving of the layers of air; otherwise the atmosphere would spoil…" is rendered above as written in the source's phrasing.]

Next, the distinction between بشرى (bushra) and بشرا (bushran). بشرى is singular, and it appears in His saying: ﹛And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the glad tidings…﹜ [Surat Hud, verse 69], meaning the announcement. But بشرا is the plural of بشير (bashir, "bearer of good news"), and it is a lightened form whose original is بشر. The Truth says: ﹛Then when the bearer of good news came…﹜.

The plural of بشير is بُشُر, like نذير and نُذُر, with the vowel of the shin dropped for lightness, so it is pronounced بُشْرًا and بُشُرًا.

(بشرا بين يدي رحمته) means that they are before His mercy, because they will bring us water, which is mercy in itself; through it He gives us the irrigation of the land, and we also drink from it directly. We notice that when the word الرياح (al-riyah, "the winds," plural) is used, it comes for good, whereas when there is harm in it, it uses the singular word ريح (rih), such as the saying: ﹛…by a furious, violent wind﹜ [Surat al-Haqqah, verse 6]. So when you see the word رياح, know that it is good, but when you see the word ريح, know that it is harmful. Why? If you are sitting in a room with an open window through which air comes, and the current strikes a person, the person becomes tired, because the air comes from a single place. But when you sit in the open and the wind blows, you do not tire, because the winds are many. Yet the ريح comes like a rocket.

So the winds are what the Truth sends before His mercy, until when they carry (أقلت, aqallat, "they bear up"), i.e., they carry. One says "أقل فلان الحمل" meaning he lifted the load from the ground and carried it, because it was less than his capacity. For if it had been more than his capacity, he could not have lifted it from the ground. As long as he has borne it, the load is less than his capacity and his effort. "Aqallat" means "they carried," and since they have carried more than they carried, their effort is greater than what they carried. If the effort is less than what they have carried, it must come down to the earth. "Aqallat sahaban" means they carried clouds. We know that clouds are the vapours that rise from the earth; they gather and ascend to the upper layers of the atmosphere, and the winds push them until they meet a cold zone, whereupon the cloud condenses and the rain falls. We see this in distilled water that they make in the pharmacy: the pharmacist brings a burner, with a vessel above it containing water, and the water boils, so the vapour rises to travel through the tubes that pass through a cold current, where the vapour condenses and becomes water. ﹛until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them…﹜

The Truth said: "saqaynahu" (We drove it) with a masculine pronoun, because He regarded the clouds in their collective noun form, or He regarded their wording. He used the adjective in the plural, saying "thiqalan" (heavy), considering that sahab is the plural of sahabah, and the plural is distinguished from the singular by the tā' marbūṭah. As long as all the clouds are included in the driving, they have no multiplicity, so they are as one thing: ﹛until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive it…﹜ [part of verse 57, Surat al-A'raf].

The clouds do not head to one place only; they head to many places. So the Truth directs the heavy clouds to more than one place. Yet the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﹛We drive it to a dead land﹜. The dead is that which has no motion in it and whose choice of movement has ended. Likewise the earth: the water descends from the sky onto the earth while it is dormant, with no movement of life in it. That is, God sends the cloud and drives it to a dead land, in any place on earth.

﹛And when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and brings forth every lovely pair﹜ [part of verse 5, Surat al-Hajj]. So the earth that does not receive water remains dormant, meaning it has no movement of life, like the dead.

﹛We drive it to a dead land, and We send down water therewith and bring forth from it fruits of every kind﹜ [part of verse 57, Surat al-A'raf]. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wanted to draw our attention and alert us to the daily matter that we always see in various forms: the earth is sometimes barren, then some rain descends upon it. As soon as rain falls upon the mountain, two days after the rain, we find on the third day the mountain green. Who sowed the seed for this plant that day? So the plant was waiting for this water. As soon as the water descends, the plant emerges without anyone sowing seeds. This is evidence that every region of the earth has the essentials of life: ﹛…and bring forth from it fruits of every kind. Thus We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember﹜ [part of verse 57, Surat al-A'raf].

The water that descends upon the dead earth gives life to the earth, because He, glory be to Him, brings forth life every day. When He makes clear to us that He will resurrect us anew, there is nothing strange in this. Thus God made the cosmic matter visible and clear to everyone, and no one can be stubborn or obstinate about it, because it is a perceptible, observed matter. From it we deduce the truth of the matter and the truth of the Lord.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 58:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that:
﴿And the good land—its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord, while that which is wicked comes forth only sparingly. Thus do We vary the signs for a people who give thanks.﴾

So the previous verse addressed the matter of resurrection by way of a parable from the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-kawniyya) that exist: the winds that carry the clouds, and the clouds that are driven toward a dead land, from which water descends and by which crops are brought forth. The land was dead, and God revives it with rain; likewise is the bringing-forth on the Resurrection. This is a matter of religion (qadiyya diniyya). In this verse He brings another matter of religion as well: ﴿And the good land—its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord, while that which is wicked comes forth only sparingly﴾. The good land is the fertile land that needs nothing but water, so that crops come forth from it. As for the wicked land, however much water descends upon it, its vegetation will not come forth except after toil and hardship, and even then it is scant and of no benefit. Here the Truth serves a religious matter just as He served the religious matter of resurrection first. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which God has sent me is like abundant rain that fell upon a land. A portion of it was good; it absorbed the water and brought forth grass and abundant herbage. Another portion of it was hard ground that held the water, so God benefited people by it: they drank from it, watered their animals, and cultivated. And a third portion of it was barren plains that hold no water and produce no grass. That is the likeness of one who has understanding in the religion of God and benefits from what God has sent me with, so he learns and teaches; and the likeness of one who does not lift his head to it and does not accept the guidance of God with which I was sent." (1)

Thus the method (al-manhaj) descends to the people, and they are of three categories. One category hears and benefits itself, then transmits what it has to others, so it benefits them too, like the fertile land that drank the water and accepted it and brought forth crops. A second category carries the method and conveys it to the people but does not act by it, and upon them applies the saying of the Truth: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (Qur'an 61:2). Certainly people will benefit from the method, and for this reason the poet said:
"Take from my knowledge, and do not rely on my deeds,
And gather the fruits, and leave the wood for the fire."

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever conceals a Muslim, God will conceal him in this world and the Hereafter." (2)

Concealing a believer is required, and concealing a scholar ('alim) is more emphatic and more strongly demanded, because the scholar is not infallible and has slips. When you see his error and fall, do not broadcast it, for people will benefit from his knowledge. So do not make them doubt him. The third category is one who neither drinks the water nor gives it to others, i.e., one who benefits neither himself nor anyone else.

﴿And the good land—its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord, while that which is wicked comes forth only sparingly. Thus do We vary the signs for a people who give thanks﴾ (Qur'an 7:58). So the method of God is exactly like the rain: the rain descends upon the earth to water it, and vegetation comes forth; there is another land that does not benefit from it but holds it, so others benefit; and there is one that benefits neither itself nor others. Likewise is the knowledge that God sends down upon the tongue of His Messenger. ﴿And that which is wicked comes forth only sparingly. Thus do We vary the signs﴾.

We said before that the signs (al-ayat) are applied to three meanings: the cosmic signs that we see occurring in the universe, such as the Truth's saying: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon﴾ (Qur'an 41:37); the signs that are the verses of the Qur'an; and the signs that are the miracles of the prophets. ﴿Thus do We vary the signs﴾ (Qur'an 7:58): the signs here are cosmic, like the water that descends; it is like the method. Whoever takes it succeeds and is saved, and whoever abandons it goes astray. And all the signs of God require that we thank God for them.

(1) Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.
(2) Related by Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim, who said: sahih according to their criteria.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 59:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Indeed We sent Noah to his people, and he said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day."﴾ (59)

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, spoke of the obedient and the disobedient in this world, and spoke of the situations of the Hereafter concerning the people of Paradise, the people of the Fire, and the People of the Heights (al-A'raf), He wished next to show that every call of Allah, glorified be He, addressed to the people of the earth must meet with obstinacy and harassment, must meet with turning away, and must meet with harm. He, glorified be He, wishes to give immunity (al-mana'ah) to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so He makes clear to him: you are not an innovation (bid'ah) among the Messengers. For every Messenger who came to his people was met with persecution, was met with denial, was met with rejection, and was met with harm. And if every Messenger was subjected to this in proportion to his mission, for a limited time and a confined place, then you, O Messenger of Allah, have taken the whole world as your time and your place. So you must be confronted with hardships suited to your mission and your message. You are at the summit of the Messengers, and the harms that reach you and befall you will be at the summit of harm. So you are not an innovation among the Messengers; prepare yourself for this. When you prepare yourself for this, you will meet every harm and every persecution with patience and forbearance for the sake of Allah. And the telling of the stories of the Messengers to the Messenger of Allah serves this purpose: Allah expressed the aim of relating the stories in His saying: ﴿And We relate to you the news of the Messengers, by which We make firm your heart...﴾ (Surah Hud, 120). So the stories are a strengthening of his heart, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Whenever denial troubles him, or whenever rejection troubles him, Allah, glorified be He, relates to him the story of a Messenger who was met with denial and met with rejection, in order to make firm thereby his heart, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the hearts of his followers, so that they may know everything and prepare themselves for this hardship. The Truth did not say to the followers of Muhammad: "You are about to embark on a matter with the earth carpeted with roses for you." No. Rather, it is hardships, so that you may confront the evil of Satan on earth. The stories have more than one guidance: they make firm the heart of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and make clear to him that he is not an innovation among the Messengers, and strengthen the souls of his followers. For when they see that the people of truth with the Prophets were victorious, and the host was defeated, and they turned their backs, and that they are always made victorious, this strengthens the certainty of the believers, and it breaks, from another side, the souls of the disbelievers. Just as the Truth said concerning a leader of the Quraysh: (We shall brand him upon the snout). Allah said this to them concerning a leader of the Quraysh, while they were then unable to defend themselves or ward off harm, and they went and emigrated to Abyssinia to protect themselves from the aggression of these leaders, and every believer seeks someone to protect him. Then the Truth's saying was revealed afterwards concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: "We shall brand him upon the snout." Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was a chief among his people, and on the day of Badr he came, and his nose was found struck and smashed, and the saying of Allah was fulfilled: ﴿We shall brand him upon the snout﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 16).

So who, then, determines the blow of a sword in the hand of a fighter before the fighting begins? He has determined it, the All-Knowing, by what the matter will be.

Also, the stories of the Messengers were brought so that it would be established for their contemporaries that he received the Qur'an from Allah, because he was an unlettered Messenger, and the nation was unlettered, and none of his opponents claimed that he had sat with a teacher or read a book. So from where did these reports come to him? Listen to the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, in the verses in which He says "you were not" (ma kunta), such as His saying: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Moses﴾ (part of 28:44, Surah al-Qasas). And such as His saying: ﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ (29:48, Surah al-'Ankabut), and such as His saying: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would take charge of Mary﴾ (part of 3:44, Surah Al 'Imran). So from where did these reports come to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when they know that he did not sit with a teacher and did not read a book? They all came from the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, and this is another proof of the truth of his message.

The story of our master Noah is one of the stories that recur often in the Noble Qur'an, like the story of Moses, peace be upon him. Strangely, the snapshots of the story are spread across some surahs, but the surah named after Noah does not contain the scenes that are considered among the finest parts of the story. It deals with other snapshots: his persistence in calling his people, and that he did not fall short in calling them by night and by day, secretly and openly; whenever he called them, they moved away. The story of the ark does not appear in Surah Noah, nor the story of the Flood, and these are snapshots from the finest parts of the story. Likewise, his story with his son does not appear there either; it came in Surah Hud.

So every snapshot came for an intended purpose, and for this reason we see the story of Noah in Surah "Noah" devoid of important elements of the story, and these elements came in Surah "Hud" or in Surah "al-A'raf", which I am now treating with faith-inspired reflections.

So every story of the Qur'anic stories you find has come to serve an idea, and their totality gives the whole story. For when the Truth relates stories, He brings a snapshot in one surah to serve one position, and another snapshot to serve another position, and so on. And when He willed to send us a story perfectly woven, He brought the story of "Joseph" in Surah Yusuf and did not repeat it in the Qur'an, because it is complete in Surah Yusuf, except for one verse: ﴿And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought, until when he died you said, "Allah will never send after him a Messenger."﴾ (part of 40:34, Surah Ghafir). Its origin was reviewed and its hadiths were takhrij'd by Dr. Ahmad Umar Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University.

In Surah Yusuf there appears the life of Joseph from his childhood until he became the ruler of Egypt. Thus we see that when the Truth wills to bring a story woven together, and when He wants to draw our attention to matters containing positions and lessons, He distributes the snapshots of the story across multiple locations, which are fitting and harmonious with those locations, to affirm and serve a purpose.

﴿Indeed We sent Noah to his people, and he said: O my people﴾ (part of 7:59, Surah al-A'raf). Whenever you see the "lam" and "qad", know that this is an oath, as though the Truth says: "By My might and My majesty, indeed I sent Noah." Thus He affirms the thing sworn to.

The "qawm" (people) here means specifically the men of the assembly, because the qawm are ordinarily the ones who confront the message, while the woman is veiled; she hears from her father, or her brother, or her husband. That is why the women said to the Prophet: "The men have overcome you." That is, "We find no means to sit with you and ask you, so set aside for us a day of your days in which you admonish us." So he set for them a day, because the woman is supposed to be in seclusion, and afterwards her husband conveys to her the method if she hears something from the Messenger. Likewise the father tells his daughter, and the brother tells his sister.

When the Messenger speaks, it is said that the Messenger confronted the qawm, from their saying "he stands over such-and-such" (qa'im 'ala kadha) and "qayyim 'ala kadha." That is why the Arab poet says: "I do not know, and I do not think I know, whether the people of Hisn are men or women."

Here He brought the "qawm," and what is meant by them is the men, and the Qur'an says: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule other women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾ (part of 49:11, Surah al-Hujurat). So women do not enter into the qawm; the qawm are those who confront the Messenger, and from them come the hardships and the rigidity of opinion, and denial, disbelief, and war come from them.

Our master Noah, peace be upon him, called his people and alerted them to three things: worship of Allah. He said: "O my people, worship Allah," and he made clear to them that there is no god besides Him, saying: "You have no god other than Him," and he showed them his concern and compassion for them if they opposed and disobeyed, saying: ﴿Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾. Thus he spoke of the creed in one God who deserves worship, and not multiple gods. "Worship" means obeying His command and prohibition. And because if they did not do so, he feared for them the punishment of a great day, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. Or Allah had revealed to him that He would seize them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, and "the punishment of a great day" means the day of drowning. "Fear" is a matter that wearies the thinking of one who encounters it and fears to meet it. So who is alarmed by this? It is the tyrants, the despots, the masters, the notables, and the leading men of the people, who had made themselves masters; as for the rest of the people and the common folk, they are the slaves and the oppressed.

The ones who are provoked by this call are the chiefs, because there is no god but One, command belongs to One, prohibition belongs to One, and worship and submission belong to One. From this, their worldly authority will depart from them. Therefore the Truth (al-Haqq) clarifies for us the stance of these people toward the call when He says:

﴿The chiefs of his people said, "Indeed, we see you in clear error." (60)﴾

The malaʾ (the chiefs) are the leaders of the people, their notables and nobles, or those who "fill" the eye with their bearing, fill hearts with awe, and fill the gatherings with their stature.

They fear that the call of Nuh is the call to the straight path and that his words are guidance, so they flatter themselves that this is error and a departure from the method of truth: ﴿Indeed, we see you in clear error.﴾ That is, "absence from the truth," or "wandering away from the truth." And "mubin" (clear) means encompassing in a manner from which there is no escape.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 7, verse 61:

Nuh (peace be upon him) responds: ﴿He said: "O my people, there is no misguidance in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

They had said to him: ﴿Indeed, we see you in clear misguidance.﴾ The expected reply would be: "There is no misguidance in my affair." But he said here: ﴿There is no misguidance in me.﴾ I say this so that we may know that every letter in the Qur'an is weighed for its place. They said to him: "Indeed we see you in *dalal* (misguidance)," and he replies to them: "There is no *dalala* in me," because *dalal* is a genus (jins) that includes many instances of misguidance, and his statement affirms that there is not even a single instance of misguidance with him. The custom is that negating the lesser entails negating the greater. For example, when a friend asks you: "Do you have dates from Madinah?" you say to him: "I don't have even a single date." By that you have negated the lesser, and this also negates the greater. ﴿He said: "O my people, there is no misguidance in me."﴾

When Nuh negates from himself the existence of even the least misguidance, it is because he knows that he did not bring it from himself. Had it been so, he would have been accused of his own desire having overcome him. Rather, he is sent from a true God: ﴿...but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surah al-A'raf]. His statement "but" (lakinni) is a corrective exception: do not say "I am in misguidance," for there is not a single instance of misguidance in me; rather, I am a messenger conveying from God, and God gives nothing but guidance.

﴿A Messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾ means from the Master of the worlds and from the One who takes charge of the upbringing (tarbiyah) of the worlds. Whoever takes charge of upbringing does not send down a method by which he misguides those he nurtures; rather, he sends down a method to set right those he nurtures. Glory be to Him: before He brought them into existence, He subjected all this universe for them and provided them with sustenance, even the disbelievers among them. And whoever does all that will not send to them someone to misguide them.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary continues with Noah (peace be upon him) and his people, where he says:

﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I give you sincere advice, and I know from Allah what you do not know.﴾ (7:62)

Al-balagh (conveying) is bringing a matter to its owner; one says "balaghtu al-makan al-fulani", meaning "I reached that place". And "al-balaghah" (eloquence) is the utmost in expressing a beautiful phrase. "Uballighukum" means: I communicate to you what the Truth has entrusted me with, a method of guidance for the movement of their lives. "Risalat rabbi" (the messages of my Lord): it would have been sufficient for him to say "risalat rabbi" (the message of my Lord), but he said "risalat" in the plural, because every messenger brings the fixed method as the previous messages did, so that no one would say: he came to contradict what the earlier messengers brought. What any earlier messenger said and brought, he says too. We know that there were scrolls for Shith (Seth) and Idris (Enoch). So he said: he conveys his message, which includes the earlier messages, whether the message of Idris, who is Ukhnukh (Enoch), or Shith and the other messengers.

That is, I convey to you everything that Allah has made a method for the people of the earth, of upright and fixed matters,

as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you﴾ (part of 42:13). These are the settled, fixed matters of belief, and the rulings that do not change. Or "risalat rabbi" (messages): because as a messenger he receives a portion of the message each day; today a message came to him which he conveys, and tomorrow another message comes which he conveys. Had he said "al-risalah" (the message), he would have had to wait until the communications from Allah to him were complete and then say it; but Noah would convey each message as it came to him at the time of conveying it, so it is "messages" (risalat). Or because the subject of the messages is a matter branching out in a way that corresponds to what life needs of benefits: there is a message of commands, a message of prohibitions, a message of exhortation, a message of admonition, a message of good tidings, a message of warning, a message of narratives, and so on, and thus they are messages.

Or each portion (najm), that is, each part of the Qur'an and a share of it, is considered a message; what Allah sends on one day is a message to the Prophet, and the next day another message, and so on.

As for his saying "I give you sincere advice" (wa-ansahu lakum): because conveying requires that he tell them the method of Allah, then he calls the people to follow this method by being gentle, addressing them in a calm manner and advising them. Advice is a matter outside the conveying of the message. Let us consider the understanding of the Qur'anic phrase: ﴿wa-ansahu lakum﴾.
