Nasihah (sincere advice) is to clarify to a person the benefit in an action and to purify your intention from whatever distorts it. Would you advise another with a matter whose benefit returns to you? If you do that, the advice is suspect. If you advise him with a matter that returns benefit to him and to you, this is advice for you and for him. But when you say "nasahtu laka" (I advised you), it means the advice contains nothing particular to you; rather everything in it is for the benefit of the one you convey it to only. Thus the difference between "nasahtahu" (I advised him) and "nasahtu laka" (I advised you for your sake) becomes clear. ﴿And I give you sincere advice and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ (part of 7:62). It is as if our master Noah is addressing his people: beware of thinking that what I tell you now is all of Allah's knowledge, nor all of Allah's knowledge, nor all that Allah has taught me. Rather, I have other matters that I will tell you if you fear Allah and possess readiness of faith; here I will give you doses of them. Or his saying ﴿and I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ means: there will befall you a matter in this world that did not happen to the nations before you, namely that whoever denies the messenger, Allah will seize him for his sin. That experience did not occur with the people of Shith or Idris.

﴿So each We seized for his sin; among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind, and among them those seized by the Cry, and among them those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them those whom We drowned﴾ (part of 29:40). Such punishment did not occur before Noah, and Noah made clear to them: I know that our Lord has ordained for you that whoever denies will be seized with the seizing of the Mighty, the Powerful. Or "and I know from Allah what you do not know," meaning that Allah has informed me not in proportion to what I told you of good, but He, glory be to Him, has taught me that every announcement of good has a birth and an appointed time.

Then He, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿Are you amazed that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among yourselves, so that he may warn you and that you may fear God, and that you may receive mercy?﴾ (63).

﴿Are you amazed﴾ — he could have said "Amazed you are," but when he begins with the interrogative hamza and follows it with a conjunction particle, know that there is an attachment (ʿatf) to a previous sentence. That is, He is saying: you denied Me, and you were amazed that God sent down a "reminder from your Lord" upon my tongue. Dhikr (reminder) is the opposite of forgetfulness: a thing is on the mind, and at times it passes beyond the mind and flows onto the tongue. Many meanings of dhikr occur in the Qur'an, and the first and most prominent of these meanings is that when dhikr is used absolutely, it is meant to be the Qur'an: ﴿That which We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder﴾ (Surat Āl ʿImrān, 58), and likewise in His true word: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the reminder, and indeed We are its guardians﴾ (Surat al-Ḥijr, 9). So dhikr is used and the Qur'an is meant. At other times dhikr is used and what is meant is renown (ṣīt), that is, wide public fame. The Truth said to His Messenger concerning the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, 44 — part of the verse): that is, the Qur'an is a great honour for you and for your nation, and it will give you renown through it until the Day of Resurrection, because people will see in the Qur'an, across the successive ages, every wonder of wonders, and they will know how the universe confirms the Qur'an. So by means of the "Arabic" Qur'an, the name of the Arabs will remain attached and linked to the Qur'an, and every honour that comes to the Qur'an brings a new honour to the Arabs with it; that is, the Qur'an is an honour for you. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder﴾ (Surat al-Anbiyāʾ, 10 — part of the verse): that is, in it is your honour, in it is your renown, in it is your history. Then comes Islam, which abrogates nationalisms and races, and makes all people equal like the teeth of a comb.

﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female and made you nations and tribes that you may know one another﴾ (Surat al-Ḥujurāt, 13 — part of the verse). The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No Arab has any superiority over a non-Arab except by piety." The Qur'an will remain Arabic, and it is a miracle in the language of the Arabs, and by it the word of the Arabs will remain present in this world. Thus the honour of the people comes from the honour of the Qur'an and from the renown of the Qur'an. The Truth says: ﴿Ṣād. By the Qur'an, full of reminder﴾ (Surat Ṣād, 1): that is, its honour is lasting forever. When there comes into the world a scientific precedence, we find those who go looking for the roots of that scientific precedence in the Qur'an, and we find non-Muslims taking care of the Qur'an and printing it on a single page, on fine paper that they may not use in their own books. This is the Qur'an full of reminder, despite the fact that some Muslims deviate slightly from the method, and some of them may neglect it, yet in matters concerning the Qur'an everyone is alert. As I said before: you may find a woman with uncovered face placing a large mushaf on her chest, and you may find one who does not pray riding in a car in which he places the mushaf, and all of this is reminder. And you find the Qur'an being read in measured recitation (tartīl), and read with tajwīd, and with the ten readings, and then recorded on recorders manufactured by people who do not believe in the Qur'an. All of this is reminder and great honour.

We have learned that "dhikr" first came with the meaning of the Qur'an, and it came with the sense of renown and honour. And dhikr is used to mean what was sent down to all the Messengers; the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Their reckoning has drawn near for the people, while they are heedless and turning away. No new reminder comes to them from their Lord but that they listen to it while playing﴾ [Surat al-Anbiyāʾ, 1–2]: that is, everything that was sent down to the Messengers is dhikr.

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous﴾ [Surat al-Anbiyāʾ, 48]: so the meaning of dhikr here too is everything sent down to the Messengers of God's method.

At other times dhikr is used to mean admonition (iʿtibār), remembrance (tadhkīr), and recollection (tadhakkur). He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants and gambling and idols and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to occur among you through intoxicants and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of God…﴾ [Surat al-Māʾida, 90–91]: here the meaning of dhikr is admonition, recollection, and that you live as a Muslim within God's method. At other times dhikr means glorification (tasbīḥ) and praise (taḥmīd). Consider the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered; glorifying Him therein morning and evening, men whom neither commerce nor sale diverts from the remembrance of God and establishing prayer and giving zakah…﴾ [Surat al-Nūr, 36–37]: this is dhikr, because there are those who glorify Him in them morning and evening, and they are men described as not diverted by commerce or sale from the remembrance of God.

Sometimes the dhikr of God, meaning His remembrance of His servants with blessing, is also meant together with their dhikr of Him through obedience to Him; He blesses them with mention, and they mention Him through obedience. If you wish, read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿…He forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression; He admonishes you that you may remember﴾ [Surat al-Naḥl, 90], and in another verse: ﴿…Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater; and God knows what you do﴾ [Surat al-ʿAnkabūt, 45]. Since He, majestic and exalted, said "and the remembrance of God is greater," meaning God's remembrance of them with blessings and good things, His remembrance is a favour and beneficence, and He is the Great, the Most High. So there is then a second dhikr, a lesser one, which is their worship of their Lord through obedience. Here the Truth says: ﴿Are you amazed that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among yourselves, so that he may warn you and that you may fear God, and that you may receive mercy?﴾ [Surat al-Aʿrāf, 63]. What is the aspect of amazement here? We know that ʿajab is the display of astonishment and the stirring of the soul at the occurrence of something other than what the circumstances and their premises require. So astonishment appears and we ask: how did this happen? Had the matter been natural and ordinary, that astonishment and amazement would not have occurred.

Why were you amazed? Then read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Qāf. By the glorious Qur'an. Rather, they were amazed that a warner came to them from among themselves…﴾ [Surat Qāf, 1–2]. The point of amazement here is that a warner and messenger of their own kind came to them; of what kind did they want the Messenger to be? It was from their folly that they wanted the Messenger to be an angel.

﴿Rather, they were amazed that a warner came to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers said, "This is a strange thing"﴾ (Surat Qāf, 2). Amazement also came concerning resurrection: the disbelievers asked, "After we have gone and been lost in the earth and become dust after death, will resurrection gather us a second time?!"

So amazement means displaying astonishment at a matter that the premises do not call for, or at a matter that contradicts the premises. For them, the amazement in the verse we are presently reflecting upon is because Noah, peace be upon him, wants them to investigate belief in the existence of a God. Logic required that when they saw a thing of wondrous and wise design, and this created being, man, came upon it and found the universe ordered and existing before him, logic required that this man seek out who created the universe and insist on knowing who made it. And when a Messenger comes to tell you who made this universe, do you marvel?!

It should have been the case that you would eagerly seek the one who informs you of this truth, because the universe and its kinds of plants, minerals, and animals are at your service, O man. Not by your own strength did you create this universe or those kinds; rather you are a newcomer to the universe and its kinds. Did it not occur to you to ask who made all that for you? So speech about faith should have been the work of the intellect. I said long ago: suppose a person's plane crashed in a place where there is absolutely none of the means of life; then he became hungry, found no food, exhaustion overcame him, so he slept, then woke from this doze and was surprised to find before him a table with the finest food and drink, while he knows no one in the place. By God, before he eats, would he not ask who brought it?! That is what was required.

So you marvel at something that instinct demands we seek and believe in, namely the God who gains nothing from our obedience or worship, and to whom worship returns nothing; rather it returns to us. Worship involves hardships, for it bridles desires, restrains, and prevents sins and prohibited things; but that is matched by reward in the Hereafter.

Some say: why does He not give us the reward without the hardships of obligation, since He gains nothing? Reason is sufficient to guide us without a method to what is good, so we do it, and what we see as evil we do not do; and what we do not know, whether it is good or bad, we do it if we are compelled to it, and if we have no need of it we do not do it.

We say to this speaker: but who told you that reason is sufficient to guide us to the good matter? Did it beautify things for you alone, or for you and for others? For what is good for you may be bad for others, because you are not alone in the universe. Suppose there is one piece of cloth: the good for you is that you take it, and the good for another is that he takes it. But the true good is that the matter of ownership of this piece of cloth be decided by one who judges between you and the other without desire, and that no one be preferred over the other in his sight. So there must be a God who protects us from our desires through a method He sends down, making clear to us the good from the bad; for by human logic our desires will collide over it.

Another example: suppose we entered a certain city and saw a beautiful, luxurious dwelling, and each of us wants to live in it and each wants to take it, because that is good for him, but it is not so for another. So what is good for you may be ugly for others. The good for some men, when they see a woman, is to look at her and speak with her; but is this good for her family, her father, or her husband? No.

What you have marvelled at should have been taken by you as the natural, innate matter that the premises necessitate. The message has come to you through the tongue of a man from among you. And why did the Truth not say "the tongue of a man"? We know there is another verse in which the Truth says: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ (Surat Āl ʿImrān, 194 — part of the verse): as if He is saying to them: the promise that the Truth made to you has come to you through the method that was sent down upon the Messengers. The task of the Messengers is hard; it is not confined to conveying by tongue, because all its hardships rest on the shoulder of each Messenger. Do not think that our Lord, when He chose a Messenger, chose him to make him pampered over the necks of people. No. He chose him knowing the task is hard, and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as you know, never had his fill of barley bread, and his children and family, for example, do not take from zakah; and Messengers do not bequeath, so all that they leave is charity, and all the responsibilities of the call fall upon the Messenger. This is the benefit of his not saying "on the tongue of a Messenger," because if the matter were only on the tongue of the Messenger, it would give only the conveyance; but "upon a man from among you" gives the conveyance, and the responsibility for the conveyance falls upon this man. ﴿Are you amazed that a reminder from your Lord has come to you upon a man from among yourselves?﴾ (Surat al-Aʿrāf, 63 — part of the verse): what is the amazement? Indeed the amazement was that you should reject divinity and prophethood.

Some did not reject divinity, but rejected the idea of prophethood for a human being, and demanded that the Messenger be from the angels; l

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 64:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.﴾

Here the Truth speaks of the narration of the deliverance, and we know the long preface that preceded the preparation of our master Noah, peace be upon him, for the prophethood. God wanted him to learn carpentry and to build the ship: ﴿And whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him...﴾ [Surah Hud, 38]. The Truth did not bring here the account of the Flood, which He related in another place in the Qur'an, where He said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ [Surah al-Qamar, 11]. Instead, the Truth brings here the outcome, which is that they denied him.

﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs...﴾ [Surah al-A'raf, 64]. This was the first punitive event in the history of religions, because the message of Noah, peace be upon him, is the first message to face this kind of denial and this kind of obstinacy. The messengers before Noah had only the duty of conveying the message, and it was not incumbent on them to enter into war or conflict, and it was heaven that disciplined (the disbelievers). When the Truth, glorified and exalted, knew that with the sending of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, humanity would attain its maturity, the followers of Muhammad were entrusted with disciplining the disbelievers. In the denial of Noah, peace be upon him, the Truth brings us the outcome here.

﴿And We saved him and those with him﴾. The Truth did not say how He saved him, nor did He bring the account of the ark; rather, He informed of the fate of those who denied him, and He brings the punishment of the same kind as the Flood: ﴿and We drowned those who denied Our signs; indeed, they were a blind people﴾ (part of verse 64, Surah al-A'raf). There is "a'mā" (blind) for one whose sight has wholly gone from both his eyes, and there is also 'amih and a'mah, and 'amah (confusion) in insight is like blindness in sight... that is, his insight has gone and he has not been guided to good.

Then the Truth moved on to another messenger, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would also have an example in him. After bringing Noah, He brings Hud:

﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary [of Him]?" (65)﴾

When you hear ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud﴾, it means: We sent to 'Ad their brother Hud. The word "أخاهم" (akhahum, "their brother") is in the accusative as the direct object (maf'ul bihi), and its grammatical position (i'rab) is shown by His words in the previous verse: ﴿We sent Noah﴾, and likewise: We sent to 'Ad their brother Hud. The word "أخاهم" carries many implications: he is of their own kind, his language is their language, they are closest to him, and they know everything about him and his history. All of this signals intimacy with the messenger. He did not bring them a foreign messenger who lived far from them, lest they say: "He came to make himself a lord over us." Rather, He brought them one of their own, and sent to them "their brother." This is what is said about Hud.

So Hud was from the people of 'Ad. But there is an opinion that says Hud was not from the people of 'Ad. Brotherhood is of two kinds: brotherhood through a close father, or brotherhood through a distant father, that is, of your kind, descended from Adam. So he is either a brother through a close father or a brother through a distant father. We have mentioned before that Mu'awiya (may Allah be pleased with him) was sitting when the chamberlain (hajib) entered and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, a man at the door says he is your brother." Mu'awiya's features showed questioning and surprise, as if he were saying to his chamberlain: "Do you not know the brothers of the Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "Admit him," and he was admitted. Mu'awiya said to the man: "Which of my brothers are you?" He replied: "Your brother through Adam." Mu'awiya said: "Severed kinship!" meaning that people do not pay attention to this brotherhood. "By Allah, I will be the first to join it."

﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary [of Him]?" (65)﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

We note that the Truth related, on the tongue of our master Noah, his words to his people: ﴿He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ (part of verse 59, Surat al-A'raf).

And the Truth sent Hud to 'Ad, but Hud's words to the people of 'Ad come as: ﴿He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary?"﴾

Here it is "قال" (qala, "he said") alone, without the particle "فـ" (fa); whereas in Noah's account it is "فقال" (fa-qala, "so he said"). This is a precision of expression that we should notice, because the One speaking is God and Lord, sometimes with a "فاء" (fa) and sometimes without, even though the context is the same, the meaning is the same, the messenger is a messenger, and the group are the messenger's own people. The "فاء" (fa) implies immediate sequence and conveys insistence upon them, and this is clarified by Surat Nuh, where the Truth says: ﴿He said: "My Lord, I have called my people night and day. But my calling has only increased them in flight. And indeed, every time I have called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers into their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and became arrogantly prideful. Then I invited them publicly. Then I announced to them and confided to them secretly. And I said: 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving.'"﴾ (Surat Nuh). So the "فاء" is appropriate here. But in the matter of Hud's people, we find that our master Hud spoke to them once, twice, or three times, but without continuity and insistence. This shows us that Noah's insistence on his people requires that, in speaking of him, one says "فقال" (fa-qala), and that it not be used in speaking of the call of our master Hud. A person may wonder, because the duration of Hud with 'Ad is not equal to the duration of Noah with his people. The clarification of the period of Noah's mission comes in the words of the Truth: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years﴾ (part of verse 14, Surat al-'Ankabut). Our master Noah continued for about a thousand years calling his people night and day, secretly and openly, but they kept fleeing from faith. Therefore, in the matter of Noah's call, the Truth uses the "فاء" which indicates continuation. As for the people of 'Ad, the "فاء" was not used for them; rather "قال" (qala) was used: ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him."﴾ (part of verse 65, Surat al-A'raf). Noah had said earlier: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ (part of verse 59, Surat al-A'raf). In the matter of 'Ad He said: ﴿He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary?"﴾ and again in the matter of 'Ad He said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary?﴾

Although the style is the same and the meanings are the same, and that would have called for a warning, the Truth did not say it, because Noah had knowledge of the punishment that would descend, since that was the first experience. But our master Hud did not have knowledge of the punishment.

The event that happened to Noah with his people, their destruction by drowning, was a first for him, since God had already informed him of it. When Hud went to the people of 'Ad, there was a precedent before him, and our Lord had seized the deniers of Noah with punishment. Therefore our master Hud only hinted at the possibility of punishment when he said: ﴿Will you not then be wary?﴾, meaning: punishment may await you and reach you as it reached the people of Noah.

Says the Truth (Allah), the Exalted, after that: ﴿The chiefs of the people who disbelieved from among his people said, "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are among the liars."﴾ (7:66).

In this verse the phrase ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ occurs, whereas in the story of Nuh He said: ﴿the chiefs from among his people﴾, and the phrase "those who disbelieved" does not occur there, because among the people of Nuh there was no one who believed and concealed and hid his faith. This differs from 'Ad, the people of Hud, for among them there was a man named Mutharrid ibn Sa'd who believed and concealed and kept his faith hidden. Thus His saying concerning them, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, comes appropriately to the context, because among them was a believer who did not say what they said in throwing the accusation of foolishness at our master Hud, when they said what Allah related of them in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are among the liars﴾ (part of 7:66). As for the saying of Nuh, they said: ﴿Indeed, we see you in clear error﴾ (part of 7:60), so Nuh, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿O my people, there is no error in me﴾ (part of 7:61).

What is the difference between ḍalāla (error) and safāha (foolishness)? Ḍalāl is deviation from the truth, while safāha is recklessness, lightness, and feebleness of intellect. 'Ad added another accusation against our master Hud: ﴿And indeed, we think you are among the liars﴾. Ẓann (supposition) is the preponderance of a matter without certainty, so there is a likelier and a less likely; or ẓann here means certainty, as in His saying: ﴿those who think that they will meet their Lord﴾ (part of 2:46), meaning they are certain.

The response from Prophet Hud came: ﴿He said, "O my people, there is no folly in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

In this statement there is a denial of the accusation of folly, and an announcement to them that he is a conveyer of a message from Allah, with a methodology that the following verse explains, which is His saying, the Truth: ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a trustworthy advisor to you.﴾

Earlier, the Exalted said, quoting Noah: ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I advise you﴾ (part of verse 62, Surat al-A'raf). So why did He say of Noah's people ﴿and I advise you﴾, while here, regarding ʿAd, He said ﴿and I am a trustworthy adviser to you﴾?

The answer is that Allah said ﴿I advise you﴾ regarding Noah's people because the verb always indicates renewal (tajaddud), whereas the noun indicates permanence (thubut). Since Noah, peace be upon him, kept pressing his people night and day, both openly and in secret, Allah used the verb ﴿I advise you﴾ to convey renewal. But in the case of the people of Hud, He used what conveys permanence, namely His words ﴿a trustworthy adviser﴾, because Hud, peace be upon him, did not press and repeat his call to his people to faith the way Noah, peace be upon him, did.

Almighty God says, speaking through the words of our master Hud:
﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among yourselves, so that he may warn you? Remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah, and increased you broadly in stature. So remember the bounties of God, that perhaps you may prosper.﴾ (Qur'an 7:69)

The truth here has come with "the reminder" for the sake of warning, and so He said ﴿so that he may warn you﴾ alone, unlike what He said about the people of Noah: ﴿and that you may fear God, and that perhaps you may receive mercy﴾. This is because the warning did not come merely for the sake of warning; rather, so that we would refrain and be God-conscious, in order that we might be shown mercy. Thus when He mentions the first link in the chain and the first thread, which is the warning, we infer the rest, which is God-consciousness, so that we arrive at mercy.

﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah﴾: this is a new point, because the people of Noah were the first people to be punished when they did not believe, and after that our master Hud came to 'Ad, conveying the message to them and warning them, so that they would take a lesson from Noah and his people.

﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah, and increased you broadly in stature. So remember the bounties of God, that perhaps you may prosper﴾ (part of verse 69, Surah al-A'raf): Our master Hud reminds them that the Truth has given them bodies, hollow and spacious, with breadth and height. It is said that the tallest of them reached a height of one hundred cubits, and the shortest of them reached a height of sixty cubits. Our master Hud commands them to remember the bounties of God (ala' Allah), that is, His blessings upon them, and the first of the blessings is that He sent to them a messenger who takes them by the hand to the regions of good. So what was their response?

Almighty Allah says: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us so that we would worship Allah alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾

It was logical that they should worship Allah alone, rather than worship partners who neither benefit nor harm them, and cannot hear them. Indeed, one of them would see the wind blow upon the idol, so the idol tilts and falls to the ground and its neck breaks; he then goes to the blacksmith (al-haddad) to reassemble a new head for the idol. How, then, can one worship such an idol? Yet they said to Hud: "We imitate our fathers, and we cannot abandon what our fathers used to worship, for we follow in their footsteps." And if your God threatens us with punishment, then bring it to us, if you are of the truthful. Thus it became clear that there is no hope of their being convinced by the call to faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 71:

What then does the Truth say after that?

The decisive word comes on the tongue of Hud:

﴿He said: "There has already fallen upon you from your Lord abomination and wrath. Do you dispute with me about names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority? So wait; I am with you among those who wait."﴾ (7:71)

He was speaking with them and they were speaking with him. They said to him: "Bring us the punishment," and he said to them: ﴿There has already fallen upon you from your Lord abomination and wrath.﴾ How can he say "has fallen"? He said it because he was reporting from Allah. "Waqa'a" (fell) is a past-tense verb, but we know that the speech of Allah is free of time, whether past, present or future. Our master Hud said "waqa'a" while the punishment had not yet fallen, but since his words were a message from Allah, they affirm that the punishment will certainly befall them, because the One who announced it is able to carry it out at any time, and there is no other god and no other power able to prevent that. What has fallen upon them is the rijs, and rijs means defilement, the opposite of purification and cleansing. The wrath of Allah that has fallen is not specified by this verse, but it must have a form through which it will come.

He asks them mockingly: ﴿Do you dispute with me about names which you have named, you and your fathers?﴾ Every name has a named referent. These names you have bestowed upon these deities: do they have real referents deserving to be worshipped? No. Rather, you have bestowed divinity upon what is not a god, so these are names without referents, and in reality you are imitators of your fathers. What you worship are names without authority from the true God: ﴿for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ (7:71), meaning these names have no proof for what you claim. The evidence is that in the Jahiliyyah they named a deity "al-'Uzza," and when they broke it they found no might or anything else, because this supposed god did not defend itself, so how could it be a god and a guardian over others? Likewise they named "al-Lat," meaning "Allah" with the feminine ta' added, and when they broke it they found in it no power, dominance or tyranny.

Hud says to his people, affirming the coming of the punishment: ﴿So wait; I am with you among those who wait﴾ (7:71). His saying "so wait" makes us understand his earlier words ﴿there has already fallen upon you from your Lord abomination and wrath﴾ as meaning that the abomination and wrath are certainly coming. It is true that he expressed this with the past tense, but let us read the word of the Truth: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (16:1). "Atā" (has come) is a past-tense verb, and apparently it contradicts ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾, since seeking to hasten implies the event has not yet come in its time. But we should know that the One who announced it is Allah, and there is no second power that alters the purposes of Allah, whether they are to be or not to be.

The Truth then says: ﴿So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We cut off the last remnant of those who denied Our signs and were not believers﴾ (7:72). We note that the Truth explained the means of salvation of our master Noah: ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ (10:73).

Here, in the matter of 'Ad, He did not explain to us the means of salvation; rather He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We cut off the last remnant of those who denied Our signs and were not believers﴾ (7:72). His saying ﴿So We saved him﴾ indicates that a general punishment befell, but our Lord had revealed to our master Hud that he should go far from the place, he and those with him, before this punishment came. The Arabs of old, when a matter afflicted them or necessity drove them to something beyond their means, would go to the House of Allah to humbly beseech Allah to deliver them from it, even the disbelievers among them did so. As happened with 'Ad, when Allah sent to them our master Hud as a prophet, they denied him and increased in insolence and tyranny, so drought struck them and lasted three years, and they had no recourse but to turn to the Ka'bah to ask their Lord to lighten the punishment from them. One of them, named Qayl ibn 'Anz, went, and another named Martha ibn Sa'd, who was concealing his Islam, went with a group of them to Makkah. They had maternal relatives there from the 'Amalaqah, from the descendants of 'Umlayq ibn Lawidh ibn Sam ibn Nuh, and they were the ones who ruled Makkah at that time, headed by a man named Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr. They lodged with him, and he honoured their reception in the manner of the Arabs, hosting them with the hospitality of kings and princes, bringing singing-girls, food and drink. They enjoyed the matter and remained for a month. Then Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr said: "They have come to rescue their people from the drought, and they did not think to go to the Ka'bah, nor to think of calling upon our Lord. I fear that if I tell them that, they will say that he has become constricted toward us, and it will be a disgrace upon me." He began to think about the matter. He had two singing-girls named "al-Juradatan." The two singing-girls said: "Compose poetry about that, and we will sing it for them." So Mu'awiyah said:

Would that Qayl, woe to you, would arise and supplicate,
So that perhaps Allah will send us rain-clouds,
And water the land of 'Ad, for 'Ad
Have come to a state where they cannot form speech.

When they sang it, and singing involves repetition, especially when it is sung with direction, "Would that Qayl, woe to you, would arise and supplicate" (huyayn means: call upon Allah). Did you not come for the sake of supplication, that perhaps Allah will send us rain-clouds over the land of 'Ad and the drought will end, since hardship had reached them to the point that they could not express speech? Qayl awoke, and Martha ibn Sa'd awoke, and it had reached the knowledge of Qayl that Martha ibn Sa'd believed in Hud, peace be upon him, so he refused to take him along. Qayl indeed went and began to call upon Allah, and he heard a voice saying to him: "Choose for your people," and he saw a black cloud, a red cloud and a white cloud. The voice alerted him to choose a cloud that would go to his people from among the three, so he chose the black cloud, because it is the most abundant in water, and according to his effort he chose the black cloud. They returned to their lands and found the black cloud, and he said to them: "I chose the black cloud because it suggests much pouring water." The Truth spoke regarding this matter: ﴿So when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ (46:24)

That is, this cloud about which Qayl had said "Qayl" would give us rain. The Truth answers them and says: ﴿Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings...﴾ (46:24-25). So their earlier words to Hud, which the Truth has brought here in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿So bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful﴾ (7:70), that is, their punishment is confirmed by the rain and the wind, which is what the words of our master Hud here in Surah al-A'raf brought: ﴿There has already fallen upon you from your Lord abomination and wrath.﴾

And none escaped the punishment except those who believed, affirming His true word: ﴿So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We cut off the last remnant of those who denied Our signs, and they were not believers﴾.

Allah made it easy for them to submit to our master Hud and to those who believed with him, so that they left the place at the moment the cloud appeared. Hud heard a voice calling out to him, confirming that in this cloud lay a severe punishment. So he took the group who had believed with him and fled to Mecca, and those who had wronged themselves by denying their messenger and refusing to believe in their Lord were destroyed.

Almighty God then says: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you, so leave her to eat within the earth of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment."﴾ [7:73].

Prophet Salih said to Thamud what Prophet Hud had said to 'Ad. He brought them warning so that they would be mindful of God and thereby receive mercy. Prophet Salih said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him.﴾ So warning is for the sake of taqwa (God-consciousness) and for reaching mercy and success. For this reason I always say: when the Qur'an touches upon a matter, it may not come with full detail, but its context suggests the intended meaning, and it does not repeat it, in order to train within us the faculty of alertness in receiving meanings. An example of this is the story of the hoopoe with Prophet Sulayman. The Qur'an, on the tongue of Prophet Sulayman, says: ﴿And he inspected the birds and said, "What is [the matter] with me that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?"﴾ (Surah al-Naml) [27:20]. Prophet Sulayman threatened the hoopoe, saying: ﴿I will surely punish him with severe punishment or I will surely slaughter him﴾ (part of 27:21). Then the hoopoe came and said: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾ (part of 27:22). Then Prophet Sulayman sent the hoopoe to the people of Sheba, saying: ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Naml) [27:28]. Directly after this verse the Qur'an says: ﴿She said, "O eminent ones, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter"﴾ (Surah al-Naml) [27:29]. It is as though the hoopoe had carried the letter and thrown it to the queen of Sheba, and she responded directly. Thus the Qur'an did not repeat what happened; rather, it left some of the events to be understood from the context.

Likewise here, in His saying: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾ (part of 7:73). The word "their brother" here confirms that Prophet Salih was familiar and known to Thamud, his history was known to them, and his past in values and morals was fully known to them; Thamud was attributed to him because he was their brother. His call was consistent with the calls of Noah and Hud.

﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you, so leave her to eat within the earth of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment."﴾ (part of 7:73). The clear evidence (bayyinah) is the proof of the truthfulness of his conveying from God, and it is the she-camel. So what was the story of the she-camel? Did he come out to them with a camel and attribute its ownership to God? Naturally not; there must have been a story such that they would know this camel belonged to no human being. When Prophet Salih made his call, the leaders of his people challenged him and said: "We and you will stand; we will seek help from our gods, and you will seek help from your god. If our gods prevail, we will follow them, and if your god prevails, we will follow you." They sat calling upon their gods, but nothing happened from those gods. Then they said to Prophet Salih: "If you are truthful in your call, here is a solitary rock before you in the mountain called 'al-Kathiba'; let your Lord bring forth for us from this rock a she-camel, pregnant, like the Bukht, the finest kind of camels." So he called upon God, the Glorified and Exalted, and the rock split open, bringing forth the she-camel. The coming out of the she-camel from the rock leaves no room for doubt that it was a sign from God that appeared before them. It is the clear proof. The rock split and they found a pregnant she-camel, *wabra'* (i.e., with abundant wool), whose fetus was moving between her sides; then her labor pains seized her and she gave birth to a young camel (*fasil*). Thus the divine sign was confirmed, without anyone daring to doubt it. She is a camel of God, and He said: ﴿The she-camel of Allah and her drink⁠—﴾ (part of 91:13). Prophet Salih explained to them that she is the she-camel of Allah, and you see her as a visible sight. This she-camel has a day for drinking water, and you have a day on which you drink. The water was scarce for them in the wells: ﴿For her is a share of drink, and for you is a share of drink on a known day﴾ (part of 26:155). That is, a day must be set aside for this she-camel to drink, and another day for you, your camels and your animals. Among the marvels of this she-camel was that she would stand over the spring and drink, leaving no water in it; it was an amount of water that would have sufficed all the camels. After that, all the water she had drunk would turn into milk in her udder, and they would take this milk.

It is true that the she-camel prevented them from water, but they took from her the milk they fed on. And because she was the she-camel of God, she had to have a form and size suited to her, and an amount of food and drink appropriate for sustaining her life, and an amount of milk yield appropriate to her drinking, her food and her size. Since she was attributed to God, she must have had miraculous characteristics. Her young one was with her. When the heat of summer came, the she-camel would settle on the high ground, while the rest of the she-camels would descend to the lowlands; and when winter came, she would descend to the low-lying areas. It is well known that the region of Mada'in Salih was extremely hot, and whoever visits the city or Tabuk can pass by it.

The she-camel was free to choose the place where she lived, in summer or winter, and no one could harm her. Two women had camels, and the she-camel of God would outdo the camels of the two women in pasture and water. The two women brought a man called "Uhaymar Thamud" (the little red one of Thamud), whose name was Qudar ibn Salif, to kill her, and he killed the she-camel. When the she-camel was killed, her young one climbed a mountain called "Qara" and let out three cries. Prophet Salih called out: "O my people, catch up with this young camel; perhaps by your catching it God will lift the punishment from you." They went searching for it but did not find it. God informed Prophet Salih that the punishment was coming: on the first day their faces would be yellow, on the second day red, and on the third day black. The she-camel was the she-camel of God, attributed to Him, glorified be He, and they had been assured of this by the visible sight. It was incumbent upon them, at the moment they found the visible cosmic sign, to take a lesson from it, and to understand that it was a prelude to what had been promised; but stupidity made them forget that she was the she-camel of God.

﴿This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you, so leave her to eat within the earth of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment﴾ (part of 7:73). Indeed the punishment came after the "little red one" of Thamud killed the she-camel.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 74:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land, taking for yourselves palaces in its plains and hewing out the mountains as houses. So remember the bounties of Allah, and do not go about in the land spreading corruption.﴾ (74)

Earlier, the Truth had said to the tribe of 'Ad: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah﴾ (from verse 69 of Surah al-A'raf). Here the Truth says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad﴾, because 'Ad were the closer successors to them, and their story is still well known and its landmarks are clear, whereas the story of Noah is certainly a little older than the story of 'Ad.

He also reminds them that He gave them dwelling places in the land that they might inhabit. They took palaces from its plains, and the plain (sahl) is the flat place that has no hills, rocks or mountains. They used to hew houses out of the mountains, and a person among them lived so long that a house would collapse twice within one human lifetime. For this reason they decided to take houses from the mountains so that they would remain safe. When a person sees the dwellings of Salih carved into the mountain, it is an opportunity to contemplate the greatness of the Truth in alerting creation to what benefits them, and these are indeed among the blessings of Allah. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So remember the bounties of Allah, and do not go about in the land spreading corruption﴾ (from verse 74 of Surah al-A'raf). The bounties (ala') of Allah, as we have known, are His blessings that cannot be counted, and He alerts them to not spreading corruption in the land.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 75:

Then He, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed, "Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent."﴾

We know that there are masters and there are followers. Earlier, the Truth said: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ (part of verse 166, Surat al-Baqarah). Here, in the verse about which our reflections are directed, there is a dialogue between the masters and the oppressed, who have no standing and no tyranny to protect. They saw the call to faith and found in it benefit for themselves, so they turned towards it. As for the al-Mala' (the eminent ones, i.e. the chiefs, the notables and the dignitaries who fill the eye with awe and the hearts with reverence), they said to those among the oppressed who believed, because there were oppressed people who remained loyal to disbelief, these chiefs from among the arrogant said to the oppressed who believed: ﴿Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent."﴾ (part of verse 75, Surat al-A'raf),

And when the arrogant heard the words of the believers among the oppressed.

So what did the arrogant chiefs say? The Truth says: ﴿Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that which you have believed."﴾

Thus they declared their disbelief in words and joined to it an action, which was the slaughter of the she-camel. The Truth says:

﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring us what you have threatened us with, if you are indeed among the messengers."﴾

Al-'Aqr (العقر) is slaughter, referring to she-camels. Here they also say, just as those before them had said:

﴿Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are one of the messengers (77)﴾ (Surah al-A'raf): And "the truthful" (al-sadiqin) also refers back to "the messengers." They accused Salih, peace be upon him, of lying as a messenger sent to them, despite the clear sign that had occurred, namely the camel's emergence from the mountain. Therefore the wrath of God descends upon them, embodied in His words, the Truth: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes by morning (78)﴾.

The earthquake (al-Rajfah) is the tremor that shakes the thing that is shaken. The Qur'an also calls it al-Taghiyah (the overwhelming blast).

In His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah]: and [the blast] after which they became "jathimin" (lying prostrate, motionless). This is the precise expression which indicates that whoever among them was standing remained fixed in his standing, and whoever was sitting remained in his sitting, and whoever was sleeping remained in his sleep. Or, as we say: "they were petrified in their postures."

"Al-Jathim" is one who stays in his place without moving, or who clings to the ground.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 79:

After He had seized them with the earthquake, the Truth (may He be exalted) says: ﴿So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors."﴾

Did Sayyidina Salih address them while they were dead? Yes, he addressed them in order to be fair to himself and to clear his own responsibility, just as a man who falls into a predicament is told by his friend: "I cannot do anything for you now, for I advised you before." Or when a wicked person is killed, you say to him: "How much I advised you!" You speak in order to establish for yourself a proof of excuse. Likewise, the Prophet (ﷺ) did with the slain of Badr, one by one, after they had been thrown into the well of Badr. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people of the well, O so-and-so, O so-and-so, O so-and-so, have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." The Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you speak to them when their bodies have decayed?" He said: "By Allah, you are no better at hearing what I say than they are, but they are unable to answer me."

It is as if Sayyidina Salih said this so that they would remember how he conveyed to them the messages and methods of Allah, advised them, and, out of tenderness toward them, urged them to adhere to the way of Allah, but they did not listen to the advice, and they did not love the advisors. This is because the advisor wants to bring the one advised out of the evil to which he has become accustomed, and when someone advises him, he becomes angry with him.

Having finished the story of Thamud and their prophet, He (glorified is He) says:

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has committed before you?"﴾ (7:80).

As the Truth (al-Haqq) said, ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah﴾ and ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud﴾, and ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih﴾. Here He brings the name "Lut" in the accusative case (naṣb), because it is coordinated (ma'ṭūf) with those before him among the bearers of messages.

What is the time of the sending? The words ﴿when he said to his people﴾ indicate that the time of the saying was the time of the sending. This is the Qur'anic indication, with clear meaning, that the Messenger, when he is sent and delivers the message to them, does not delay for a moment in carrying out the task. It is as if the delivery of the message coincided with his saying, "O my people." The style wants to show you that, at the very hour of delivery, there is no gap between them. ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people﴾ (part of 7:80). The word "his people" means that he was one of them. Why did He not say "their brother Lot"? This carries a meaning that applies to the earlier messengers: they were from the environment of the peoples to whom they were sent. Hud was from the environment of 'Ad, and Salih was from the environment of Thamud. If the Truth did not say "their brother Lot," note that He made clear that He sent him to his people. This alerts us that Lot was not originally from this place, because Lot and Abraham, peace be upon them, were from a distant city, and they came to this place fleeing persecution, he and Abraham, peace be upon them. This shows us that Lot was a newcomer to this place, and was not their brother who lived with them in the same environment. Yet they were "his people," because he lived among them for a period, so they came to know one another, came to know some of his qualities, and became familiar with him.

I say this so that we may notice the precision of the Qur'an's expression. Although the stories are one, He (glorified is He) gives us precise distinctions. Lot did not say to them, "My Lord has forbidden you this filthy act, namely having intercourse with men." Rather, he wanted to question them in a way that might deter them from the act and make it repugnant.

The question of Sayyidna Lot was a question of rebuke and a question of denunciation. He did not say to them, "Our Lord says to you: refrain from this action." Rather, he denounces the act as something contrary to the natural disposition (fitrah), a denunciation that comes from innate nature.

﴿Do you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾ (part of 7:80). This indicates that he wanted to put to them a question of denial, in order to embarrass them, because the innate intellect refuses this act. That is, this matter had not occurred before, because it is a loathsome act; a man naturally comes into a place of filth. Yet they did it, and this act shows that it is a matter that a deviant soul may desire. But it is a filthy act that the sound natural disposition rejects.

The word "fāḥisha" (abomination) gives the meaning of excess in ugliness. It is not merely ugliness, but an increase, an intensification, and a deepening of ugliness and exaggeration in it. For "fāḥisha" also applies when a man has intercourse with a woman who is prepared for this act, since he has not contracted marriage with her and has not taken her as a spouse; when he marries her she becomes lawful (ḥill) to him. But the intercourse of a male with a male is an increase in abomination. If this matter is forbidden with a woman who is not lawful to him and is considered an abomination, then a man is not created for such an act and it can never become lawful. His doing it is an abomination in a compound sense.

﴿...Do you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾ (7:80). We said earlier that the particle "min" (from) may come as an extra (zā'ida) particle. You may say that it is extra in human speech, but it is shameful to say that about the speech of our Lord. His words ﴿that no one in the worlds has committed before you﴾ mean: no one from the worlds preceded you. The word "aḥad" (anyone) is the subject (fā'il), and the "min" (from) came to clarify for us that no one had committed it at the outset. This is like what we said long ago, when you say to someone, "I do not have wealth." You have denied that you possess wealth of any worth, though something that may be called wealth may be with you from the start. His saying the Truth, ﴿...that no one in the worlds has committed before you﴾ (7:80), means that no one preceded them from the beginning of what can be called "someone." He (glorified is He) wants to negate it even more. The "min" in His words ﴿from the worlds﴾ is partitive (tab'īḍiyya), meaning: no one preceded you in it "from among some of the worlds." So what is this matter? He called it an abomination, and it increases in ugliness. His description of it as something that no one among the worlds had committed made it an extremely terrible matter.

When we investigate this matter intellectually, we find that man was created as a vicegerent (khalīfa) on earth, and it is incumbent upon him to preserve his species, because each individual has a limited lifespan, and people succeed one another, and the continuation of the species is necessary. God has guaranteed to man the sustenance that sustains him, and He made marriage lawful for him as a means of preserving the species. The task of vicegerency requires that some of us succeed others. Every vicegerent needs sustenance (iqtiyāt) and procreation. The word "iqtiyāt" (sustenance) refers to God's creation on earth in which He determined its provisions.

From the human species, He made male and female, and from them comes procreation of successors. Man is first carried as a drop (nuṭfa) in the back of his father, then in his mother as a fetus (janīn), then she gives birth to him and raises him with his father, and the two of them raise him until he reaches maturity. These are five stages, and each stage is arduous. The mother's carrying of the child for nine months is an arduous matter, because if a person carries something all day he will become tired, but the mother carries the fetus for nine months. God wished the pregnancy to be smooth (insiyābī), meaning that the fetus in its first formation does not reach more than a very small weight, then it grows calmly and slowly for nine months until its development is complete.

This fetus was small at the beginning of its formation, then its weight generally became three kilograms on the day of its birth. Between the beginning of its formation and the moment of its birth there is a period of time in which this fetus grows gradually and smoothly. It does not gain weight every hour; rather, it grows in every millionth of a second by an amount suited to that fraction of a second. This means that the fetus grows smoothly in proportion to time.

We also notice this in weightlifting training: they do not train the young athlete to lift a hundred kilograms the first time; rather, they train him to lift twenty kilograms at the beginning, then the load is increased successively without making the weightlifter suffer hardship. They call this "smoothness of training" (insiyāb al-tadrīb), because lifting these weights requires habituation. For this reason he is not trained to lift weights suddenly, but smoothly, so that time is not perceived along with the movement. Likewise with growth: if you look at your newborn child the hour his mother gives birth to him, and I assume for the sake of argument that you kept looking at him continuously, he does not grow in your sight at all, because he grows in a manner imperceptible to you. But if you were absent from him for a month and then returned to see him, you would perceive his growth, and this extra growth would have accumulated in the time between the last time you saw him before your absence and the first time you see him after your return.

Thus, among God's gentleness in pregnancy is that the fetus grows smoothly, and for this reason the womb expands every day from the beginning of pregnancy until its last day. You see the pregnant mother walking weakly and slowing her movement. Then birth comes accompanied by the hardships and pains of delivery. After the child is born, he receives the care of his mother and father, and he takes years until he reaches maturity. We know that the longest-lasting childhood among the species is that of man. For this reason we find that the father who wants children bears with the mother the hardships of upbringing. God linked this matter with desire, the most intense desire that comes from man. After the child is born, we find the woman saying, "I will never conceive again," yet she conceives after that.

So it is as if desire is the bait placed in the trap to bring the prey, which is procreation. For this reason the Truth linked procreation with desire, so that we would approach it. After we approach it and become entangled in it, we exert ourselves and make the effort to raise the children. If you separate this desire from procreation and continuation, you have deviated from and turned away from the sunnah of the cosmos, because you would take pleasure without procreation, and if procreation ceases, the vicegerency of the earth ceases. Another point: in intercourse the man plays the active role (fā'il), whereas in deviance, which is the opposite act that the people of Lot committed, the man is turned into a passive partner (munfa'il) after having been active.

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has committed before you?"﴾ (7:80).

(Surah al-A'raf). "Fāḥisha" is the abnormal sexual act. He (glorified is He) did not specify it from the beginning, as evidence that it is a matter known by innate nature. At the moment He says ﴿Do you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾, they know what they did. And if we suppose that there are fools, or those who claim foolishness and refuse to understand, then after it He brought the clear statement:

﴿Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed the limits.﴾ (7:81).

Extravagance (al-israf) is going beyond the bounds of what is right, and God has given desire (al-shahwa) a natural and fruitful outlet for you. Whenever you take more than that, you have crossed the limit. God made for the man a woman of the human kind, and made her a vessel for procreation. Desire comes to you from her and from you to her, and procreation comes to you from her; after that, the two of you share in the raising of the children. Any departure from what God has set down is driven by desire alone, whereas the drive toward this act with a female ought to be desire and procreation together, for the survival of the species. Therefore the Truth described the deed of the people of Lot: ﴿Nay, you are a people who exceed the bounds﴾ [7:81].

And the Truth, glory be to Him, brings what they answered with, in response to the question of our master Lut (Lot):

﴿And the answer of his people was none but that they said: "Expel them from your town; indeed they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ [7:82]

Thus these people persisted, refusing to let anyone rebuke them for their deviance. Therefore they said: ﴿Expel them from your town...﴾ [7:82]. What was the pretext for which Lut and those who believed with him were to be expelled from the town? ﴿...Expel them from your town; indeed they are people who keep themselves pure.﴾ [7:82]. Is purity a defect? No. But they had lived in filth and grown accustomed to it, and they refuse to leave it, so they came to hate purity. An example of this: a young man wishes to join a group of friends his own age, but he finds them drinking wine, so he advises them to stay away from it; he finds them flirting with women, so he warns them of the consequences of gossiping about people's honour. But the group of friends came to dislike his presence among them, because he had not grown used to corruption. They say: "Let us keep away from this upright, ascetic, austere fellow," as though these qualities have become a term of abuse in the eyes of people of a deviant disposition, just like the animal that lives in filth and, if it comes out into cleanliness, dies.

Then the Truth (Allah) says, after that: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾ (7:83)

When they wanted to expel Lot and his family, they were only acting recklessly. By doing so they hastened their own punishment. The punishment came upon them, and Allah, glorified is He, saved Lot and his family through a wise arrangement in which He, glorified is He, had no need for any limit. If someone asks: who were Lot's family whom Allah saved with him? Were they his blood relatives or those who adhered to his religion and followed him? If "his family" refers to blood relatives, then the Truth excepts from them "his wife," and this is evidence that the people of the household believed in what Lot said, and likewise the followers as well: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾ So there were with Lot also some of his family and some of his followers, and they were among the purified (al-mutatahhirin). Purification (tatahhur) is that a person elevates himself above filth and evil. This is why we find our master Shu'ayb, when he advises his people:

﴿Give full measure and weight, and do not defraud people of their things...﴾ (11:85 — in Surat al-A'raf, 7:85 [Surat al-A'raf]).

And the people marvel, asking Shu'ayb: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped...?﴾ (11:87 [Surat Hud]). They marvel that prayer forbids such things. Their misguidance had blinded their insight, so they did not realize that prayer forbids every kind of wrong. Likewise some of the disbelievers did when they accused our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), of being mad: ﴿And they say: O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are surely mad!﴾ (15:6 [Surat al-Hijr]). From their saying, the foolishness of their thinking is confirmed: since they said ﴿the Reminder has been sent down upon him﴾, who sent down this Reminder? The Reminder is the Qur'an, and the One who sent it down is Allah, glorified and exalted. How then do they acknowledge the Qur'an as a Reminder, and then accuse the Messenger of being "mad"? For since they themselves said of the Qur'an that it is a Reminder, and that it was sent down to him and he did not bring it from himself, how could he be mad? It is they who are the liars, and their saying confirms that their thinking is low and degraded.

In the verse we are reflecting upon, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind (al-ghabirin).﴾ (7:83) The wife of our master Lot was not included in the salvation because she was among those who remained behind. "Ghabara" comes with several meanings: it means staying and dwelling in a place, or it means anything that has passed, as one says: "this thing, its days have ghabarat," i.e., its days have passed. One may ask: how can one word carry a meaning and its opposite? Ghabara means "remained," and ghabara also means "passed and ended." We say: the meaning converges here in this verse. Since the Truth saved him from the punishment that descended upon the people of Lot in the town, we find his wife did not go out with him, but remained in the place where the punishment descended, and remained in the past; thus the meaning converges. If you say she was among those who remained with those upon whom the punishment came, this is correct. And if you say she became a past history that has passed, this is also correct: ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾. We do not enter into the details of why his wife was among those who remained behind, because some have spoken about her in ways that should not be said, as though God were deceiving one of His prophets. No; we take only what the Truth has said: that she was opposing His method and was not believing in Him.

We also note that the Truth spoke of the wives of Lot and Noah in the matter of disbelief, saying: ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot; they were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them...﴾ (66:10). Scrutinize the phrase ﴿under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them﴾. Some have asked about the meaning of "betrayal" and whether the betrayal intended is adultery. We say: our Lord does not deceive a prophet of His, but whether a wife believes or disbelieves is a matter of choice. It is as if Allah, glorified is He, makes clear to us that the Messenger, although he is a messenger from Allah, cannot impose faith on his wife; the matter is freedom of belief. Consider the Qur'anic expression: ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot.﴾ Beware of thinking that either of them was arrogant toward her husband, for the Truth says: ﴿they were under two of Our servants﴾, meaning that the authority and guardianship of the man over her is affirmed; His saying ﴿they were under two servants﴾ points to this. But faith is a matter of choice, and this choice is left to every person. The Truth confirmed this in the case of Noah's son: ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾ (11:46). Some have tried to attach the accusation of adultery to the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, and in doing so they depart from truthfulness; it is pure fabrication. The Truth has alerted us to this when He said of the wives of Noah and Lot: ﴿they were under two of Our servants﴾ (66:10). Let us understand that choice in belief is what made them disbelievers, and that the two messengers, Noah and Lot, could not put faith into the hearts of their two wives; so that it becomes clear to us that belief can be produced by no one but the person himself. Therefore He, glorified is He, gave us another example: ﴿And Allah sets forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deed, and save me from the wrongdoing people"﴾ (66:11). This is the wife of Pharaoh, the tyrant who "claimed divinity," yet he could not prevent his wife from believing in Allah. Thus we find a prophet unable to persuade his wife to believe, and we find the claimant to divinity unable to make his wife a disbeliever like himself. This shows that belief is a matter of choice, protected by every kind of safeguard, so that a person chooses his religion only on the basis of his conviction and not on the basis of compulsion.

And Allah sets forth another example: ﴿and Mary, daughter of Imran﴾ (66:12).

We note that the Truth did not give the names of the wives of Noah and Lot, nor the name of Pharaoh's wife, but He mentioned for us the name of Mary and the name of her father. Why was there vagueness at first? So that we know it is entirely possible that such a thing happens to any woman: she may be under a tyrant and a disbeliever while she herself is a believer, and she may be under a believing servant while faith does not touch her heart.

﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind (al-ghabirin).﴾ (7:83) The word "anjayna" (We saved) indicates that a punishment was about to fall upon the place where Lot's people were. Because He, glorified is He, willed to punish one group and not another group, He had to move the group destined for salvation to leave. This departure was desired for them by those who hated them, for they said:

﴿Expel them from your town; indeed they are people who keep themselves pure (yatatahharun).﴾ (7:82) But our Lord is the One who brought them out, and the bringing out was from the punishment that descended upon these criminals; it was for the salvation of Lot and his family from what descended upon these wicked people.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 84:

The punishment comes from the Truth: ﴿And We rained down upon them a rain, so look at how was the end of the criminals﴾.

Was that rain like the rain that falls ordinarily? No, rather it was a rain of another kind. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿To send down upon them stones of clay, marked by your Lord for the transgressors﴾ [Surat adh-Dhariyat].

The Truth says: He will punish them with rain. So let us be mindful that it was not the customary rain, but rather He punishes and uproots them with another kind of rain.

As for His saying "fa-unzur" (so look), it means: so take a lesson, O you who hear this text. This story makes clear and manifest that Allah does not leave the criminals who oppose the call of Allah, delivered through His messengers, without punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 85:

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight and do not deprive the people of their due and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers."﴾

"Madyan" is a son of our master Ibrahim who came and settled in this place. So it is a proper name for his person and a proper name for the place in which he settled, and the place was named after him. When his descendants multiplied and became a tribe, the tribe took his name. Thus "Madyan" is a proper noun for the son of Ibrahim, and it was applied to the place where he settled, from the Mount Sinai (Tur Sina') to the Euphrates, and it was applied to the tribe: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb.﴾ Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, repeats "brother" to make clear to you that if He is harsh with them once, He will be tender with them another time, because they are his brothers and he is familiar with them; he lived among them and they know everything about him. Madyan had married Raqabah, the daughter of our master Lut, and when the two multiplied they became a tribe. Our master Shu'ayb conveys to them the doctrinal matter that every messenger conveys: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him.﴾ And worship (ʿibadah) is obedience to a command and obedience to a prohibition. You do not obey the command of one who commands, nor the prohibition of one who prohibits, unless he is above you, for if he were equal to you, after he tells you, "Do such-and-such," you would ask him: why? And after he forbids you from something, you would also ask him why. But when a father says to his little child, "Do not do such-and-such," the son does not argue, because he knows that his father is the one who feeds him, gives him drink and clothes him. When the child grows up, he argues, because his selfhood is forming and he wants to know the matter he is about to undertake.

﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord..." [Surah al-A'raf] (85): Since he said to them, ﴿Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾, he is a messenger who has come and been sent from Allah, and there must be a miracle that establishes him. However, Shu'ayb did not bring us a miracle; rather he brought clear evidence (bayyinah). ﴿There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf] (85): Because all sins and disbelief lead to imbalance in measure and weight, and if Shu'ayb said that to his people, then it must be that imbalance in measure and weight was the common matter among them. So he comes to treat the common matter. And they used to deprive people in measure and weight.

People think, on the surface, that this is an easy matter, and that the ugliness in it is small, and that cheating in it is trivial and slight. When one shortchanges in the weight, even by a small amount, he ultimately takes for himself a large portion. When you measure and weigh and cheat, you are doing that to the one who buys from you. Then you will go to buy from many people, who will do just as you did. So when you give full measure and weight, you are doing what is in your interest, because you spread behavioral justice among people, beginning with yourself, and all your interests are bound up with others.

When you sell any commodity, even unripe dates (balah), and you reduce the weight, you will achieve for yourself a profit to which you have no right. If you measure wheat to sell and reduce the measure, you are taking what is not yours. If you measure wheat to sell and reduce the measure, you are taking what is not yours. Wheat and dates are some of the essentials of your life, because you need many goods from the one who weighs and from the one who measures. If you reduce the weight or the measure, they will do to you just as you did with what they possess, and thus you will lose and the loss will become general.

﴿So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive the people of their due.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf] (85): If the loss in measure and weight is slight and tolerable, then all the more reason not to deprive people of their things, so we do not wrong them by taking their wealth and seizing their rights. We should not be extravagant, for the thief takes whatever his hand reaches; nor should we usurp, nor embezzle, nor take bribes. For if giving full measure is the first thing God requires of you, even though the loss in it is slight, then depriving people of their things is all the more so.

He, glorified is He, continues: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf] (85):

Thus we are before more than one command that the Prophet of God, Shu'ayb, brought: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him.﴾ This worship is to instill in them awe and to increase their love and respect for the Supreme Commander, and likewise that they fear His tyranny, glorified is He. After that, it is necessary that there be the command to give full measure and weight, and the rebuke against depriving people of their things, then the prohibition and warning against corruption on the earth: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ The reformation that God asks of us is that we sustain it or elevate it, and that is achieved by establishing the essentials of life in a beautiful way.

An example of that is the air, which is the first element of life subjected to you; He, glorified is He, directs it so that it does not become corrupt. The second blessing of life is drink: He, glorified is He, sends down water for you from the sky, and then the sustenance that He brings forth for you from the earth. And the livestock from which you take milk, wool, fleece and hides, all of that God has subjected for you, and this is reformation on the earth. But are these all the essential foundations? No. For if all these essential foundations exist, and then usurpation, theft, bribery and embezzlement appear, everything will be corrupted, and nothing will set all that right, make it upright and sound, except religion, for as a method it prevents corruption on the earth. ﴿There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord.
