So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive the people of their due, and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ (part of verse 85, Surah al-A'raf): So these things, which are giving full measure and weight, are what the command concerns; then it follows with what is prohibited: that we do not deprive people of their things and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. All of that gathers the method: commands and prohibitions. It may appear on the surface that these are matters that restrict human freedom, and we say: do not look at yourself, O human, as if you were apart from the wide society, for you possess only one of your interests, and this one interest you possess is the least of your things, while the other matters you need are in the hands of others. If you give full measure and weight, that is better for you, for the one who measures cloth for you does not cheat you, and the one who weighs for you what you do not have does not cheat you, and the one who measures for you what you do not have does not cheat you. So you are one forbidden from doing that, and all people are forbidden from doing that to you, and in this way you are the gainer.

When you come to His saying, ﴿and do not deprive the people of their things﴾, you are commanded not to deprive people of their things, and all people are commanded not to deprive you of anything. And if you cause corruption on the earth after its reformation, people are likewise commanded not to corrupt this earth, and thus you will be more fortunate than them in everything. Therefore every responsible person, when he receives an obligation that may be hard on himself, should reflect on that obligation and say to himself: beware of looking at the hardship of the obligation upon yourself, but look at what it secures for you. Beware of looking at the obligation as a burden: do not look at the forbidden things of others, for He has commanded others not to look at your forbidden things, and in this is dignity for you. If the obligation commands you not to put your hand into another's pocket and steal, then He has commanded all people not to put their hands into your pockets to rob you, and by this we live in security.

If the obligation asks of you, while you are wealthy, to pay the zakat of your wealth, beware of saying: "my wealth, my effort, my sweat," for the wealth is God's. You, as a created human being, have only the direction of movement, and movement is by a created energy, and the intellect that plans is created by God, and the emotion that moved you on earth is from God's creation. But the Truth has honored your work and its product and imposed upon you that you pay from it a specified zakat. So beware of saying: "it takes from me." Why? Because the world of changing circumstances is manifest before you, and how many strong people have you seen weakened, and how many rich people have become poor. If He, glorified is He, has asked you to give to the poor and strengthen them, then if you become poor, He will do the same for you, and in that is the securing of your life, for you live in a society, so do not despair for yourself if changing circumstances pass over you, because your faithful society will not abandon you, you or your children. And the Truth says: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them; so let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ [Surah al-Nisa'] (9). If you want to be reassured about your small children after your death, then look at the orphans in your society and be a father to them, and when you become a father to them, and this one is a father to them, and that one is a father to them, the orphan will feel that he has lost one father, but he lives in a faithful society that has provided him with fathers from all the believers, so he does not grieve. Likewise you will not fear for your children if they become orphans after you have departed to the meeting with your Lord, because you cared for the orphans and lived in a society that looks after them. But you grieve when you see an orphan neglected in a society that does not attend to his affairs, and you say to yourself: if I die, my children will be lost in this way.

Thus the obligations of faith are a securing of life. An example of that is when we say to the woman: ﴿Veil yourself, and do not display your adornment to anyone except your mahram.﴾ A woman may think, on the surface, that we have constricted her freedom, because she forgets that the method secures for her against the ugliness of old age. For when she marries young, and then her age reaches beyond forty and her appearance changes from the hardships of pregnancy and raising children, then her husband sees a girl of twenty who is not modest, who may captivate him and turn him away from his wife, and he looks at his wife with the look of one who is indifferent to her and not desiring her. The Shari'ah has commanded the veil for the woman while she is young, and it has forbidden it to her when she is old; all of that, then, is among the securities of the method for life.

So giving full measure, not depriving people of their things, and not causing corruption on the earth after its reformation is good for everyone in this world, in addition to the good of the Hereafter. That is why the Truth ends the noble verse with His saying: ﴿...That is better for you, if you should be believers.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf] (85). "That" refers to what preceded: the command to worship Allah, that there is no god but Him, and the command to give full measure and weight, not to deprive people of their things, and not to cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. The Truth placed that within the frame of ﴿if you should be believers﴾, although the good will also come to a non-believer. Thus the word "good" includes good in this world and, for the believer only, good in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he will take good in this world only, and has no good in the Hereafter. So if you are believers, the good will be multiplied for you, to become constant good in this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Sha'rawi said, regarding Allah's words: "And sit not on every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He multiplied you. And look at the end of the corrupters" (7:86):

"Sit not on every path" means: do not sit on every road, for whoever sits on the road may prevent the one who seeks to go toward the Messenger. Satan had said:

"I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path" (7:16). So when you sit on a path, each one of you becomes a devil, and we seek refuge in Allah. For Satan said to our Lord: "I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path," and here the Truth forbids sitting on every path, because a path is a way (sabil). When the Truth gathers the ways together to forbid them, it is only to remind us that He has one straight path and one way which we must follow. Therefore He says: "So follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way" (6:153). So Satan has many ways, while the ways of uprightness are one, because the many roads have diverse misguidances: this road misguides through wealth, that road misguides through women, and another misguides through status. So the misguidances are many. Or, the guidance to which every messenger calls is widespread in everything around him; whoever comes toward any guidance finds someone who blocks him. And whoever seeks the guidance of the Messenger meets threats, intimidation, and prevention from the way of truth.

And why do they do this? The Truth gives the answer: "and seeking to make it crooked." They wish and desire that the law of Allah be crooked, inclined, and deviating from uprightness, or they describe it as not straight, so that they may turn people away from entering it and make them averse to it. An example of this is mocking the prohibition of wine and claiming that it gives the soul joy and harmony. Each of these people only recoils from the law of Allah and claims that it is a crooked law. We find someone who makes usury lawful, because the prohibition of usury, in their sickly and deviant opinion, restricts people's opportunities. They wish the law of Allah to be crooked so that they may benefit from its crookedness and turn people away from it.

"And remember when you were few and He multiplied you, and look at the end of the corrupters" (7:86): We know that every admonition and every guidance aims at two things: encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib). For example, the teacher tells the pupils: whoever works hard, we will give him a prize; this is encouragement. The professor adds, telling the pupils: whoever neglects his lessons, we will expel him from the school; this is warning. Since people are fit for doing good and doing evil by the choice Allah created in them, it is necessary to confront them with both: encouragement toward good and warning against evil.

Here the Truth speaks in encouragement: "And remember when you were few and He multiplied you." It is as if He is asking them to be people of refinement and good manners. We know that Madyan married and had a number of offspring, and they were few in number, so He multiplied them until they became a tribe; they were weak, so He strengthened them; they were poor, so He enriched them. So whoever has done all these things for you and to you, is it not proper that you obey his commands? It was incumbent upon you to obey his commands. This is encouragement and tenderness.

We know that Shu'ayb is the fifth prophet to come after Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot. Therefore the Truth reminds them of what happened to those who denied the four earlier prophets. Perhaps the people of Noah were excused, because they were the beginning, so no one before them had been punished for denying their messengers; then afterward it became a rule that whoever denies the messengers receives punishment, in confirmation of His saying: "So each We seized for his sin" (29:40). So if Shu'ayb was warning them to look at the end of the corrupters among those before them, this is a reminder of those whom He drowned, those seized by the Cry, those whose cities He overturned, flipped, and destroyed, and those upon whom He sent a rain of baked clay. If they do not recognize their duty toward Allah, who blessed them by making them many after being few, then they must fear the end of the corrupters. Thus he combined for them encouragement and warning.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 7, verse 87:

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And if there is a group among you who believe in that with which I have been sent, and a group who do not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.﴾

This statement clarifies for us that one group believed and another group did not believe. Then the command came to both groups: the command to the believers to be patient is a consolation (تأنيس) for them, and the command to the disbelievers to be patient is a threat (تهديد) to them.

This is the precision of the Qur'an in its expression, the greatness of its exposition, and its eloquence. So the word "اصبروا" (be patient) served well in expressing the command to patience for those who believed, and it served well in revealing the destiny that awaits those who did not believe. The patience of the disbelievers leads to their outcome and end: either they will be ashamed of themselves and believe, or they will meet the punishment. The patience of the believers leads them to Paradise. And that the One who judges is Allah, and He is the best of judges, because those being judged are equal before Him; none of them has a preference over another, and none of them is closer to Him by kinship, for nearness and proximity to Him are not by lineage. He, glory be to Him, is the Just with absolute justice, and He does not wrong anyone.

[Quran 7:88] The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said: "Even if we were unwilling?"

We have learned before that al-mala' (the chiefs, the notables) are the leaders and dignitaries who fill the eyes with awe, fill the hearts with awe, and fill places with their presence. The chiefs of the people of Shu'ayb were arrogant towards believing in him; they transgressed and threatened him that they would expel him from their land, and they said the same as those who came before them. Some of the people of Lut had called for Lut and those who believed with him to be expelled from their town. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Expel the family of Lut from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ [Surat an-Naml 27:56].

The word "qaryah" (town) in our lives has taken on a status other than its true one: the qaryah now is a place lower than the small city. But in earlier times it was the place where all the necessities of life were found, as evidenced by the fact that they used to call Makkah "Umm al-Qura" (the mother of towns). The chiefs placed Shu'ayb and those who believed with him between two matters: either they would expel them so that they would not corrupt those who had not believed, so that they would believe, or they would return to the religion. Here is a "verbal observation" that I would like you to pay attention to in His saying: ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾, because "al-'awd" (return) implies a previous existence from which one departed, and we want to return to the origin. So were Shu'ayb and those who believed with him previously on their religion and then believed, and what is demanded of them now is that they return?

We must pay attention to the fact that the address here includes Shu'ayb and those with him. The command to return to the old religion may apply to those with Shu'ayb, but it does not apply to Shu'ayb himself, because he is a messenger prophet. Here we also note that the speakers are the chiefs of the people of Madyan, who placed Shu'ayb and those who believed with him before two choices: either return to the religion or leave. They forgot that Allah may will a division other than these two divisions. He, glory be to Him, may will a third matter in which neither Shu'ayb nor those who believed with him leave, and they also do not return to the religion of disbelief, such as a calamity that prevents that.

The chiefs of the people of Shu'ayb isolated themselves from the higher decrees, because Allah may will other than these two matters. A matter beyond your capacity may prevent you from expelling Shu'ayb and those who believed with him: weakness may befall you so that you cannot expel them, or Allah may set against you a matter that annihilates you and saves Shu'ayb and those who believed with him. So you, O human, a created and helpless being, should not presume or lie and invent against the supreme power that you choose between two matters when Allah may have a third matter that you do not know.

The reply comes from the tongue of those who believed with Shu'ayb: ﴿He said: "Even if we were unwilling?"﴾ (part of verse 88, Surat al-A'raf): Shu'ayb and those with him asked: can someone be forced to abandon faith for disbelief? As if the disbelievers had forgotten that moral responsibility (al-taklif) is grounded in choice, so that a person chooses between the path of faith and the path of disbelief.

Continuing the speech of Shu'ayb and those who believed with him: "We would be fabricating a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has delivered us from it. It would not be for us to return to it, unless Allah, our Lord, should will it. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of deciders" (7:89).

Their saying, "We would be fabricating a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion," means that they know that returning to such a religion is a kind of deliberate lying against Allah. For lying (kadhib) is that you say something that does not correspond to reality, and you declare a matter that is not true; if you say it while knowing its reality, it is simply a lie. But if you know the truth and then say something other than it, this is fabrication (iftira'), invention and lying. The believers with Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, know that the old religion is a false religion, and they had witnessed with Shu'ayb the sweetness of faith in Allah; therefore they rejected deliberate lying against Allah. They then say: "after Allah has delivered us from it. It would not be for us to return to it, unless Allah should will it" (part of 7:89).

They knew that obligation (taklif) is a matter of choice, and they had chosen faith. They affirmed and confirmed their faith by acknowledging that He, glory be to Him, has absolute power, so they said: "unless Allah should will it." The will of Allah, glory be to Him, is above every will. Did not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The hearts of all the children of Adam are between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like one heart, He turns it wherever He wills" (1)? Did not our master Abraham, who is the father of the prophets and messengers, say: "Keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols" (part of 14:35)? He did not say "keep us away"; rather he said it plainly and asked his Lord to keep him far away, and to keep his sons far away, from worshipping idols, because he knew His absolute power, glory be to Him. Thus those who believed with Shu'ayb showed respect for absolute power in truth; therefore they said: "It would not be for us to return to it, unless Allah, our Lord, should will it" (part of 7:89). But Allah does not will that one who is protected (ma'sum) should return; and He, glory be to Him, guides those who believe with the guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala) and increases them in the guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'una) upon the straight path.

The people of faith continue with Shu'ayb: "Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of deciders" (7:89).

Their saying, "In Allah we have put our trust," came because their opponents from the chiefs, by their strength and tyranny, said to them: "You are between two matters: either you leave the town, or you return to our religion." The believers, with their messenger Shu'ayb, declared that return to the religion can only be by choice, and we have chosen not to return. Therefore there is nothing before them except expulsion by compulsion; so the believers put their trust in Allah that He would take charge of them and prevent these disbelievers from dominating them: "In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of deciders" (7:89).

Whenever we hear the word "iftah" (open), "fataha" or "fath," we understand that there is something closed or problematic. If it is a sensible thing, the object is closed and opening is by removing the locks, which are the padlocks; if it is in matters of meaning, opening is removing the difficulty. The physical sense of opening has a parallel in the Qur'an. When we read Surah Yusuf, we find His true saying: "And when they opened their goods, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said: O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us..." (12:65). The phrase "when they opened their goods" means that the goods they had were closed and needed physical opening so that they might find their merchandise as it was. Also the Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted, says: "And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups; until, when they reach it and its gates are opened..." (39:73). Since there are doors that are opened, this is physical opening. Opening may also be opening of knowledge, as we say: "Our Lord opened to us with faith and knowledge." The Truth says: "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?" (2:76). Since our Lord has taught them much of the Book, this is opening of knowledge. Opening may also be the sending down of good and its provision. An example of that is His saying: "Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it" (35:2).

Likewise His saying, glory be to Him: "If the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened to them blessings from the heavens and the earth..." (7:96). The blessings from the heavens, such as rain, come from above, and it is the cause of what comes from below, that is, from the earth. Opening may also mean the removal of a difficulty in a dispute between two adversaries; in Yemen, even now, they call the judge who handles people's cases "al-Fatih" (the Opener), because he removes the difficulties between people. Opening may also mean victory, as in the saying of the Truth: "And before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved..." (2:89). They were awaiting the Prophet (ﷺ) so that they might be victorious over those who disbelieved through him. Also among the meanings of opening is deciding a matter, as in the saying of the Truth in the verse about which we are reflecting here: "Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of deciders" (7:89). This saying is a supplication to the Truth: "O Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, by granting victory to faith and defeat to disbelief; and You are the best of deciders, for You have no inclination against any of Your creatures or in favour of any of them."

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, and by Muslim from Ibn 'Umar.

And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved said: "If you follow Shu'ayb, then you will surely be losers."

Here the chiefs of the people of Madyan say to those who had believed, and to those who were prepared and disposed to believe, warning them against following Shu'ayb, so that the chiefs and the great ones should not remain alone in misguidance. And when we see the "lam" in "la'in" (the oath-marker lam), we know that there is an oath here, indicated by this "lam." Also here is "in" (the conditional particle), and the oath requires an answer, and the condition also requires an answer. When a condition and an oath come together, we suffice with the answer of the one that precedes, of the two, as in our saying: "By God, if you do such-and-such, such-and-such will certainly happen." So: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then you will surely be losers.﴾

And what will they lose? They will lose, because they used to take more than their due when they gave short measure and cheated in the scales, and the strong takes from the weak. So when they are bound to the method and follow it, they lose what they used to take through short-weighting and cheating in the scales by means of this method. This is the loss in the eyes of the deviant.

﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became lifeless in their homes, prostrate.﴾

Al-rajfah is the violent tremor that shakes a person with a shaking beyond his control. Jathimin means they were left sitting on their knees, motionless, dead, in a state of humiliation. This indicates that each of them, at the moment he was seized, remembered everything he had done of disbelief and disobedience, wished to make up for what he had missed of his opposition to the Messenger, and began to rebuke himself and regret what he had done. Pride and arrogance did not overtake him, because there is a moment that passes over a person in which he cannot deceive himself. For this reason we find that whoever has wronged, transgressed, and taken the rights of others, and then death comes to him, tries to call out to everyone he oppressed or wronged, so that he may give him his right, but he does not find them. For this reason they call that moment the moment in which the wicked believes, but does his belief benefit him? Of course not. In this state, no soul's belief benefits it if it had not believed before.

The commentary continues describing what befell them after the earthquake: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, it was as though they had never dwelt there. Those who denied Shu'ayb—they were the losers.﴾ (7:92)

To "ghaniya bi-al-makan" (to dwell in a place) means to stay or reside there. So when they became prostrate corpses and their dwellings were emptied of them, it was as though they had never had any residence there, since they were utterly uprooted and destroyed, a complete destruction.

And since these deniers had said: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you would be losers﴾ (7:90), their final outcome was what our Lord described in His saying: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, they were the losers.﴾

Then he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had indeed conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and given you sincere counsel. So how could I grieve over a people who are disbelievers?" (7:93)

And "turned away from them" means he left them and went far from them, and he addressed them in his imagination: "I had indeed conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and given you sincere counsel." It is as if the human, emotional outlook, upon seeing how they had become, felt compassion for them and grieved on their account. But this compassion is answered by a questioning, astonished rebuke: "So how could I grieve over a people who are disbelievers?" They are the kind of people over whom a believer does not grieve. So what of a Prophet and Messenger? He speaks to himself as if saying: I did not fall short in my mission; rather I conveyed to you my messages that I received from Allah. The "messages" (risalat), when plural, are taken to mean either his message and the messages of the earlier Messengers concerning matters that will not undergo abrogation (naskh) or change, or "his messages" meaning every matter he conveyed, since whenever a ruling was revealed to him he would convey it to them. Or it may mean that every good has a message and every evil has a message, and he conveyed to them everything that reached him from Allah. He did not limit himself to conveying (al-balagh) but added to it sincere counsel (al-nasihah), and sincere counsel is other than conveying: conveying means you say what has reached you and the matter ends, whereas "sincere counsel" (al-nasihah) is insistence upon them that they return to their right guidance and follow the way of Allah.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 94:

Then the Truth says (exalted is He):﴿Never did We send a prophet to a town but We seized its people with adversity and hardship, so that they might humble themselves.﴾

We have already learned that the qarya (town, a settlement that gathers all the interests of its inhabitants in their worldly life) is the city.

The intent here is that the town to which the Truth sends a messenger and which then denies him, He (glory be to Him) seizes its people with al-ba'saa' (adversity) and al-darra' (hardship). Al-ba'saa' is the calamity that befalls a person in something external to himself: wealth that is lost, trade that goes bad and perishes, or a house that collapses. Al-darra' is the calamity that befalls a person in his own self and soul, such as sickness. The Truth afflicts them with al-ba'saa' and al-darra' because they forgot God in ease, so He struck them with al-ba'saa' and al-darra' so that they might return to their Lord and come to know Him, so that He would be with them in ease and in hardship. The Truth says:﴿When harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us to remove a harm that touched him.﴾ [Surah Yunus] 

It was incumbent upon man that, whenever hardship touches him, he should turn to his Creator. God has made hardship a means of awakening by which a person remembers that he has a Lord. At this very moment the Truth answers the distressed person and relieves him, in confirmation of His saying, the Truth:﴿Is not He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god with God? Little do you remember.﴾ [Surah al-Naml]. When God does this for the one in distress, he may come back to his senses and say: "The God for whom I found no refuge but Him is not one whom I should forget."

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surat al-A'raf, verse 95:

It is as though the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, reminds us of the all-encompassing power of His command when He says: ﴿Why, when Our might came upon them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 6:43]. It is as though He, glorified is He, asks of us that when hardship comes, we turn to Him in fear and do not believe that we live in life alone. Rather, we live in life through the created causes (al-asbab) of God and through the Causer (al-musabbib), who is God. So the one whom the causes have overwhelmed and exhausted turns to the Causer. For this reason, He, glorified is He, seizes every town that does not believe the messengers with misfortune and adversity, so that perhaps they will humble themselves, and this is out of mercy towards them.

He says: ﴿But their hearts hardened﴾ [6:43].

So does God leave them in ease and in hardship forever? No. He, glorified is He, sends them trials of misfortune and adversity to draw their attention to Him. If they do not turn to God, He, glorified is He, replaces the evil with good. Therefore He says: ﴿Then We replaced the evil with good until they multiplied [in numbers]...﴾ [7:95].

Then, after that, He gives them provision, health and wealth. This is because the Truth, when He wishes to seize a tyrant, seizes him as the Mighty, the Omnipotent. He gives him respite and lets him loose, so that he becomes arrogant like Pharaoh, in order that He may seize him suddenly. It is as though he falls from a height: He raises him higher and higher so that He may bring him down, as they say, "by the root of his neck." ﴿Then We replaced the evil with good until they multiplied﴾.

﴿Until they multiplied (ʿafaw)﴾, i.e., they increased in number, wealth and strength. That is, God did not seize them with misfortune and adversity except that the purpose of it was to draw their attention to Him. But they did not pay heed, so He gives them more, grants them health and what delights them, and then afflicts them with punishment suddenly. ﴿Then We replaced the evil with good until they multiplied and said, "Hardship and ease touched our forefathers too." So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive﴾ [7:95] (Surat al-A'raf).

We note that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, after speaking about the vicegerency (khilafa) of man on earth, and that He supplied him with everything his life requires, and supplied him with values through the methods (manahij) of the heavens, and sent down the method, explaining what is permitted and what is forbidden, after they had been making lawful what God had forbidden and making forbidden what God had permitted. Thus the Truth made clear to them that the One who created creation knows what will benefit them, so He permitted it, and knows what will corrupt them, so He forbade it. So it is not for you to propose to God what is lawful or unlawful. But some who doubt the method of God have said, and continue to say: "If God has permitted something and forbidden something, why did He create what He forbade?" We say: God, glorified is He, created everything for a wisdom that may be other than food, drink and clothing. Some things are created for a purpose, even if it is not directly for you. For example, petroleum is created for the purpose of producing energy, so we do not drink it.

The pig is created for a wisdom that we do not know; rather, the One who created it knows it. It may be that it is a means of catching the microbes that arise from the decay of the things people use in their lives. So everything is created for a wisdom, and you should not remove the wisdom of things from the intention of their Creator, because the maker of a craft is the one who determines the thing that comes into being and gives it its power. We know, for example, that types of fuel are many: there is pure "benzene," which they label number 1 and which is designated for aircraft, and car fuel, which is "benzene" number 2. If we use the fuel of one machine instead of another, we damage it. Likewise, God created man and subjected all creatures to him, and made clear: this suits you directly, and this is created to serve you indirectly, and this is created to serve you indirectly, so leave it in its place.

After the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presented the states of Paradise, the states of Hell, and the states of the people of the heights (ashab al-a'raf), whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, and after explaining the whole method, He wished to show that this is not merely theoretical, but is also a cosmic reality. He distinguished between a thing that is described as a theory and a thing that actually happens. So He related to us the stories of the prophets when He sent them to their peoples. Whoever denied the messengers, God seized him with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, through a reality witnessed by all. He mentioned Noah with his people, and 'Ad and their brother Hud, and Thamud and their brother Salih, and Madyan and their brother Shu'ayb, and the people of Lut and our master Lut. He explained what happened to the believers, which was deliverance, and what happened to the disbelievers, which was destruction and humiliation.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, clarifies: "I seize people with misfortune and adversity so that perhaps they will humble themselves, because man is a created being upon whom God has bestowed much of the attributes of His majesty and the attributes of His beauty. God is Powerful, and He gave man of His power. God is Rich, and He gave man of His richness. God is Wise, and He gave man of His wisdom. God is All-Knowing, and He gave man of His knowledge."

If you wish to comprehend what brings you close to the perfection of knowledge in God, then consider what He has taught every creature of God. Yet even so, their knowledge is deficient. They are returned to the essential knowledge of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. Perhaps man is deceived by the causes when they respond to him: he ploughs, sows and irrigates, and behold, the earth gives him its produce. He makes a thing and it responds to him. All this may tempt him into thinking that things have responded to his own essence, so God reminds him: "Remember who subjected them to you."

﴿Nay! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [Surat al-'Alaq, 96:6–7]. Whenever a person finds that all the causes are favourable to him, he must remember God. Indeed, a person, merely by willing to stand up from his place, stands up; and merely by willing to slap someone, he slaps him, because the parts of the person are subject to his will. If your parts are subject to your own wills, and you are a created being, how could the whole universe not be subject to the will of the Truth? So when a person becomes self-sufficient through causes, the Truth draws his attention to Himself. The one who was capable, who used to act through his youthful strength, has his power taken from him by God through sickness, so another person extends a hand to help him stand; and the one who took pride in something is humbled by God through other things. Why? So that he is drawn to the Causer and is not seduced by the causes.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, leaves for us wonders in His universe. We find the world has now advanced enormously in space, and man has been able to discover whatever secrets of God's universe he willed. Yet the Truth sometimes makes for them things that show them they are still powerless. After they complete the manufacture of advanced machines, they discover a single error that corrupts and destroys the machine, or a whirlwind or hurricane blows and destroys everything, or a massive fire breaks out. Does God intend corruption in His universe, when He has set it in order? No. He wishes to draw our attention so that we do not become deluded by the means we have been given. Those who made "radar" so that it might show them an event before it happens are surprised by our Lord at times with things that work like "radar," and so they know that they still have deficient knowledge.

Thus, the seizing with misfortune and the seizing with adversity is a cosmic sunna (established pattern), so that man remains aware and knowing that he is God's vicegerent on earth. The corruption of man is that he believes he is essential in the universe. For if you were essential in the universe, you would preserve yourself in it and not depart from it by death. And if you were essential in the universe, you would subjugate the universe to your desires. But you will not be able to do so, because there are natures in the universe that rebel against you and that you can never control.

You see more than one nuclear reactor explode after it has been secured and controlled. Why? To show the all-encompassing power, and that the hand of God is above their hands. So the seizing of people with misfortune and adversity, and with what we call evil, is only a call to moderation for man the vicegerent, so that when he is deluded, God, glorified and exalted is He, turns him from the causes to the Causer. When God seizes a people with misfortune, which afflicts a person outside his own self, such as wealth being lost, a child being lost, or a house being demolished, or He seizes them with adversity, which are things that afflict a person in his own self, that is so that He may strip them of the pride of arrogance, so they find no refuge except to submit to the Lord of earth and heaven, and so that they may humble themselves before God. The meaning of humbling (tadarru') is, as we have known, the manifestation of humility before God. If this does not benefit them or bring them profit, and they say: "No, misfortune and adversity are merely cosmic laws, and they may come upon people at any time or place," we say to them: True, misfortune and adversity are cosmic laws from a Creator higher than the universe. So if they are not restrained by misfortune and adversity, and do not return to their Lord and repent to Him, God tests them with blessings. He is the One who says: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair﴾ [Surat al-An'am, 6:44]. Thus, when societies turn away from the method of the heavens, the Truth takes revenge on them in a manner suited to their crime. Had He seized them in their modest state, the blow would not be strong. Therefore He widens everything for them, until, when He takes it away from them and seizes them suddenly and unexpectedly, the blow is strong and shattering, and despair and regret overtake them.

In the old days we used a rural expression: if a man wants to bring down another, he does not throw him from a mat on the floor; rather, he throws him from a high place. Our Lord gives the deniers much and extends them in their transgression, then seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. The events of life have demonstrated this, and we have seen more than one tyrant and oppressor on earth, while the Truth grants him respite in height and extends these means for him, then seizes him with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, even if through his own guard.

﴿Then We replaced the evil with good until they multiplied and said, "Hardship and ease touched our forefathers too." So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive﴾ [7:95] (Surat al-A'raf).

Sometimes a person may foresee, through what he has learned, the reality of evil in his future, like the "radar" that reveals any danger on the horizon before it arrives. When He, glorified is He, says: ﴿while they did not perceive﴾, it means they have no calculation and no measures that show them that evil is about to befall them.

If you consider this matter, you will find that man, with his intellect and thought, has not followed the path of God, but has taken a road that is not organized by the method of God. While a person does not pay attention to the coming of disaster, and asks: "Why are these animals running?" in this state he is less than the animals, because the animal, from the reality of events in a land where earthquakes happen, is the first to leave the zone of the earthquake. God has deprived it of this knowledge so that the blow may strike us. We find a donkey running to leave the place of the earthquake, while man remains standing until danger comes upon him and surrounds him. What perception and what sensing does the animal have? It is an instinctive sensing that its Lord created in it, because He deprived it of reason and gave it the wisdom of instincts.

Since the Truth has alerted man through adversity, yet he did not heed, and through hardship, yet he did not pay attention to the method, the Truth therefore lets him have his way, and rebellion is extended to him.

But the situation of the people of faith is different. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened up to them blessings from the heavens and the earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.﴾ (7:96)

That is, if they had believed in the Supreme Existent, and been mindful by following His method, in commands and prohibitions, their instruments would have been sound. For when a human maker produces a machine, he specifies and explains its purpose before he invents it, and designs for it a particular method of use and a special law of maintenance so that it may perform its task. So what of the One who created man? If people leave the Lord of man to set the method for maintaining man, this man would live in every good. He, glorified and exalted is He, made clear that if they are mindful, blessings will come to them from the heavens and the earth. If you wish these to be material blessings, you find them in the rain that falls from above, and blessings from the earth such as plants, and likewise its treasures from which the desired luxuries of life are extracted.

What is the meaning of blessing (barakah)? Blessing is that a thing gives more than its size requires. For example, a man whose salary is fifty pounds, yet he and his children live in contentment and happiness, without hardship. So we ask: how does he live? And he answers you: it is the blessing. Blessing also has a cosmic interpretation, because people, as we said before, always look at their incomings with regard to positive provision and overlook negative provision. Positive provision is that He, glorified is He, makes your income thousands of pounds, yet you may need many times that. Negative provision is that He makes your income a hundred pounds and takes away from you many expenses, such as granting you health so that you need neither a doctor's fee nor the cost of treatment.

So His saying, ﴿blessings from the heavens and the earth﴾, means that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives abundance from little in lawful provision, and erases the abundance that comes from the unlawful, such as usury (ribā). This is why the money we take out of surplus beyond need is called zakāh (obligatory almsgiving), although zakāh outwardly appears to be a loss. When you own a hundred pounds and give out two and a half pounds from it, your wealth has outwardly decreased. Yet if you lend someone a hundred pounds at interest, you take back a hundred and ten from him. But the Truth called the decrease in the first case growth (namā') and zakāh, and called the increase in the second case obliteration (maḥq) and illicit gain (suḥt). He, glorified is He, is the Withholder and the Expander.

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened up to them blessings from the heavens and the earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf). So if a man takes the law of his own maintenance from his Creator, all matters will be set right for him. But man may not do this. The Truth says: ﴿But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.﴾

Thus we know that seizing is not an act of tyranny from the Creator, but rather a justice from Him, glorified is He. For if the Truth did not hold the corrupters accountable, what would non-corrupters say? One of them would say: since we are equal with the corrupters, and the corrupters' condition goes on well, then I too shall corrupt. This tempts the non-corrupter to corrupt, and gives himself comfort and his desires. But when Allah seizes the corrupters for what they used to earn, the non-corrupter knows that the bad end of the corrupter is evident, so he protects himself from error.

The analogy would have been that He, glorified is He, says: "for what they used to acquire" (yaktasibūn), because the matter of the unlawful requires various emotional states. We gave the example before: a man sits with his wife, looks at her beauty and fills his eyes with her. But if he sits with a woman who is not lawful to him and wants to flirt with her to enjoy her beauty, he schemes and contrives, and his faculties conflict among various emotions. He differs in this from the owner of the lawful, whose faculties are harmonious as he enjoys what Allah has made lawful to him. But these corrupters have trained themselves in corruption, so that it became a habit approaching a faculty, and so the Truth said of them that they acquire corruption, and do not find in committing it any difficulty.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 97:

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿Do the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the forenoon while they are at play?﴾

We observe the presence of the interrogative hamzah (hamzat al-istifham) and the conjunctive fa' (fa' al-ta'qib) in His saying ﴿Afa-aman﴾ (Afa-aman, "Do they then feel secure?"). This means that there is a conjoined element and a element it is conjoined to, and then the interrogation entered upon both of them. That is: they committed and did disbelief and disobedience, so We seized them suddenly. After that, do the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment and Our chastisement will come upon them by night or in the forenoon, as was done to those who were before them from the earlier nations? They, then, did not take heed of what happened to the earlier nations of punishment and destruction.

The Truth makes clear: as for those among the people of the cities who denied, have they been able to secure themselves so that punishment does not come upon them suddenly, as it came upon the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, the people of Lot and the people of Shu'ayb? Al-ba's (al-ba's, "severity") is the severity by which the Truth, glorified is He, seizes nations when they turn away from His method. What, then, made them feel secure about themselves that calamities like those that descended upon the nations before them would not descend upon them?

When the Truth speaks of events, He speaks of what events require in terms of time and place, because every event must have a time and must have a place, and no event exists without a time or a place. Here the place is the cities in which their people live, and the time is the moment in which the severity will come. It may come upon them by night while they are sleeping, or come upon them in the forenoon while they are at play. These are divine expressions. When a person faces the sun, the world is day for him, and its opposite is night. Severity may come upon the people of a city by day or by night, at any point in the cycle of time. We know that every moment, the sun is at sunrise for one place on earth and at sunset for another place, and in every moment a day begins and a night begins somewhere. Therefore, O man of the day, you cannot feel secure that severity will not come to you by night or by day, and O man of the night, you cannot feel secure that severity will not be by day or by night.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 98:

﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping?﴾

Wait, the verse as given reads: ﴿Did the people of the towns feel secure that Our might would come upon them in the forenoon while they were at play?﴾

The people of the towns are those about whom Allah said:

﴿But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾ (part of verse 96, Surat al-A'raf): Since they denied, this means that they did not believe in a messenger conveying from Allah, and consequently they did not believe in a method (manhaj) that defines the regulation of their movement with "do" and "do not do."

Thus their daytime is a movement that is neither fruitful nor beneficial; rather it is play (la'ib) in the life of this world. Their night is sleep and loss of movement, or idle pleasure, debauchery and deviation. Everyone who walks without the method of Allah spends his night sleeping, heedless or disobedient, and his day playing, because his deed, however great, has no counterpart in the Hereafter of good reward.

Then the Truth (Allah) says, after that: ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feel secure from the plan of Allah except the people who are losers.﴾ (7:99)

"Al-amn" (security) is the state of being at peace with a matter that raises no fears or troubles. One says: "So-and-so is secure" (ʾāmin), meaning nothing exists that disturbs his life. The Truth says: ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah?﴾ When we hear some words that He attributes to Himself, we consider them grave and say: "Does our Lord plan?" This is because we view "planning" (makr) as an unseemly action. Here we say: pay attention to the fact that the Qur'an has said: ﴿And the evil plan does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ (35:43). So there is a good kind of planning.

For this reason the Truth said: ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾ (3:54). Makr (planning) originally means "entwining" (iltifāf). When we go to a garden or a forest, we find the trees with their branches intertwined, as if braided together, such that you cannot attribute a leaf at the top to a particular branch, because the branches are wrapped around one another. Likewise we see this entwining in climbing plants, whose branches are braided like a rope.

Thus the essence of makr is that you wrap matters up so that they are not made clear. In order to overcome your opponent, you devise for him a matter he does not perceive. If a human being, when he plots evil against his brother and tempts him with trials that blind him to the face of truth, does so, while a person does not possess the vast and strong knowledge with which he can outwit everyone before him among his opponents, because they will also plan against him.

If there is a planning and scheming that no one detects, it is the planning and scheming of Allah against the people of evil, and this is the good kind of planning, because Allah protects existence from evil and its people by destroying them. ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feel secure from the plan of Allah except the people who are losers.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf). Someone may ask: Did the prophets feel secure from the plan of Allah? We say yes. They felt secure from the plan of Allah by being chosen for the message. Someone may ask: How, then, is it that none feel secure from the plan of Allah except the losers?

We say: The method of all the messengers has taught that the one who feels secure from the plan of Allah is the loser, because Allah is the Able, and He is the One who sent down the method so that the human being may, through it, gain the good of this world and the Hereafter if he acts by it. If he does not act by it, he loses the tranquility of faith in this world, even if he gains wealth, status, or knowledge in it, and he also loses the Hereafter.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 100:

And He, glorified is He, continues: ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people that, if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, and seal over their hearts so that they do not hear?﴾

"Yahdi" means: it makes clear to those who inherit the earth the path of goodness. The meaning of ﴿who inherit the earth after its former people﴾ is that the earth was owned by others, and they came after them. When a person surveys the civilizational existence in the universe, he finds that every civilization came upon the ruins of a civilization, and what is in your hand and your possession came upon the ruins of someone else's possession. That which comes upon the ruins of others is called inheritance (irth). Since you have seen that you have inherited from others, it should be in your mind that others will inherit from you.

So the matter is one of turns of fortune (dual, duwal), and a person should not be deceived by a position or a rank. We see in our lives someone who occupies a great post, and then he is dismissed and removed from his post, or he is retired and another comes after him. Hence it is said: "If it had lasted for others, it would not have reached you." If you are a person of standing, who has entered well into your situation, your status and your post, then you must be mindful and remember the exit before the entry into this post, so that its parting does not grieve you one day. Beware of entering well into a matter before you try to exit it well. Listen to the words of the poet on this meaning:

Indeed, the commander is the one who becomes a commander in the evening, the day he is deposed;
If the authority of command ceases, the authority of his virtue does not cease.

When the Truth says: ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth﴾, we note that He, glorified is He, did not place the ones guided here in the object position. He did not say "Has it not guided those," but said "guided to those who..." So what is the wisdom in that? We know that "guidance" (al-hidaya) is indicating the path that leads to the goal, and its benefit may return to you, that is, you have guided another for your own benefit. Guidance, which is indicating the doing of good, may be for a matter that returns to both the one who guides and the one guided. But if guidance returns only to you and does not return to the one who guided you, would you doubt his guidance to you? No. You have the right to doubt guidance if that matter returns to the one who guides, or if its outcome returns to both; there is in that a suspicion of self-interest. But if the matter does not return to the one who guides, and all of it returns to the one guided, then there is no slightest doubt in that.

Therefore the Truth says in His hadith qudsi: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not add anything to My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not diminish anything of My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one plain and asked Me, and I gave each human his request, that would not diminish what I have except as a needle diminishes when it is dipped into the sea" (1).

So when the Truth guides you to the straight path, what returns to Him, glorified is He, of the attributes of perfection through this act? He created you with the attributes of perfection within Him, so His creation of you will not produce for you an attribute of perfection in excess of what is already His. Thus we see that every guidance returns to the one guided. And thereby His saying is confirmed: ﴿guided to those who inherit the earth﴾ is their benefit.

﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people that, if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, and seal over their hearts so that they do not hear?﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). When the Truth, the Mighty and Majestic, speaks of will, He says ﴿if We willed﴾ and specifies the causes of the will in His saying:

﴿We could afflict them for their sins﴾. Thus we know that will is not only the will of our Lord, but also the will of the servants whom He distinguished with choice. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Did not those who believe despair that, if God willed, He would guide all of mankind?﴾ (part of verse 31, Surah al-Ra'd).

And what prevents Him, glorified is He, from willing the guidance of all people? No one prevents the Creator. But He, glorified is He, created a creation guided by its nature, with no capacity for disobedience, which is the angels, and He made the rest of the species of the earth subjected and glorifying. This establishes the attribute of power, for no one can step outside the will of God. But this does not confer the attribute of being beloved upon the supreme Legislator. Furthermore, He, glorified is He, created a creation that has choice in obeying and disobeying.

So the creature whom He singled out with the power of choice, to believe or disbelieve, to obey or disobey, and who then believes, his faith becomes proof of establishing the attribute of being beloved to the God.

Thus those compelled in action establish the power, and those who choose the action establish the beloved status of the supreme Legislator. He, glorified is He, continues in the same verse: ﴿If We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, and seal over their hearts so that they do not hear﴾ (part of verse 100, Surah al-A'raf). We note that the Truth did not say that if We willed We would afflict them for their sins, as a mercy from Him; rather He made the punishment for the sins which they themselves choose, and likewise made the sealing upon the hearts a consequence of their choice. We have previously discussed in the beginning of Surah al-Baqara the word "tab'" (sealing), which is the stamping: ﴿God has sealed their hearts﴾ (part of verse 7, Surah al-Baqara), because hearts are the vessel of faithful certainty. When a person fills the vessel of certainty with disbelief, this means that he has loved disbelief and made it his creed. Therefore God helps him toward his aim, as if He is saying to him: "I will be according to your aim, and therefore I seal your heart so that what is in it of disbelief does not leave, and what has left it of natural faith in which God created people does not enter it."

Because you have already put into your heart a certain matter without faith; the foundations of faith are that you remove from your heart any belief, and then receive faith in God. But you receive disbelief and prefer it over faith.

Indeed, God, glorified is He, has not made for a man two hearts in his body: a heart that believes and a heart that does not believe. Rather, He made for the human one heart, and the one heart is a container (hayyiz), and a container, as we have said, does not admit the entry of another into it. So when we bring an empty bottle and say that it is "empty," what proves the falsity of this word is that when we put water into it, bubbles of air come out of it, and the emergence of the air bubbles is what allows the water to enter it. For the bottle is not empty; rather that seems so to us, because air is not visible to us. Had the bottle been emptied of air without precise preparation in its manufacture for that task, it would inevitably have shattered.

Likewise the heart has a container: if faith in God enters it, it does not accommodate disbelief, and if disbelief enters it, God forbid, it does not accommodate faith. The intelligent person is the one who casts both matters outside the heart, then studies this and studies that, and what he finds beneficial for his life and his hereafter he allows to enter. As for debating the matter of faith with the certainty of the heart against disbelief, this is a process that does not lead to a result.

﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people that, if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, and seal over their hearts so that they do not hear﴾ (Surah al-A'raf): that is, has it not become evident to those who are made successors in the earth, after the destruction of those who preceded them because of what they did of sins and disbelief, that they followed the conduct of those who came before them, did their deeds and disobeyed their Lord, and that if We willed, We could do to them the punishment as We did to those before them? His saying ﴿so they do not hear﴾ means: they do not hear the call that leads to reflection and admonition, so it is as though they did not hear.

(1) Narrated by Muslim, and the wording is his; also narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 101:

The Truth (Allah) then says: ﴿Those were the cities; We relate to you some of their tidings. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.﴾

This is the purpose in narrating stories with regard to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which the Truth clarified in another place in the Qur'an, when He said: ﴿And We relate to you the tidings of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart﴾ (part of verse 120, surah Hud). So whenever you encounter from your ummah and your people any obstinacy, insistence, or arrogance, know that you are not unique among the messengers, for every messenger has faced this same wave of denial from the people he addressed. And if every messenger receives his share of trial in proportion to the greatness of his message, then you too must receive trials equal to the trials of all the messengers.

﴿Those were the cities; We relate to you some of their tidings. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf)

Al-tab' (sealing), as we have said, is the khatm (sealing or stamping). Their hearts are filled with misguidance, and therefore they openly declare their denial of the Messenger. Allah has sealed their hearts not by compulsion from Him, but because they conceal disbelief and hide it within their hearts.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 7, verse 102:

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And We did not find in most of them any covenant; and indeed We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient (fasiqin).﴾

These people who denied the messengers and rejected the method of Allah which He sent through the tongues of His messengers had many covenants. Yet they did not fulfil any of them. An example of this is the covenant that encompasses all creation, which is the covenant that Allah took from the descendants of Adam from his loins, when Allah wiped over the back of Adam, brought forth his descendants, and said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify.﴾ (part of verse 172, surah al-A'raf).

The intellect may stop short of grasping the taking of such a covenant from the descendants present within Adam. Therefore we say: if Allah has said it, then it is true, whether or not we comprehend it. If you look at "individual humans", meaning the existing persons, you will find that you and others each find yourselves to be an offspring of your fathers. This indicates that a human being came into existence from a sperm cell until it reached a living egg cell of his mother, and so this human came into being. If death befalls the sperm cell, or death befalls the egg cell, reproduction is prevented.

Thus every human among us is a part of the life of his father, and his father is a part of the life of his own father, and his father is a part of the life of his father, and if you trace this chain you will reach Adam. Every one of Adam's descendants until the Hour is established contains a living part of Adam. And as long as there is a living part of Adam within him, he has witnessed the first creation. Therefore, when Allah questions them with a question of affirmation and says: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾

They say: ﴿Yes.﴾

To bring the matter closer, we gave an example: a coloured particle that spreads through a thing spreads through its parts. We have said before: if we take a red coloured substance, for instance one cubic centimetre in volume, and dissolve it in a flask, then every part of the flask will contain a part of the coloured substance. If you take the flask and pour it into a wide barrel, then every drop of the barrel will contain a part of the red substance. If you take the water of the barrel and pour it into the sea, then every particle of the vast sea will contain a part of the coloured substance. In this way it comes close to the mind of each of us that in every human there is a particle of Adam, and this particle witnessed the first covenant. And someone may ask: how does Allah address the particles that were present in the loins of Adam? We say: as He addressed the earth and the heaven. He is the One who said:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ (surah Fussilat, 41:11).

Therefore our failure to grasp the manner of address between the Lord and the one addressed does not negate that this matter has a basis and an existence.

This is with regard to the first covenant. After it comes the second covenant, which Allah took from His messengers, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden on this condition?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (surah Al 'Imran, 3:81).

Then there are particular covenants created by specific events, as the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea; until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the waves come to them from everywhere, and they think they are encompassed, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful."﴾ (surah Yunus, 10:22). They do not surrender themselves to ruin, nor do they deceive themselves with their standing or with the means they possess, since these have been cut off. Therefore they do not delude themselves, but turn humbly to Allah saying: ﴿If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.﴾ (part of verse 22, surah Yunus). Thus we see that they gave a covenant in a particular crisis, but when Allah saved them, they turned away. Concerning this the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us concerning a harm that touched him...﴾ (part of verse 12, surah Yunus). So a covenant is either a general covenant or a particular covenant.

And the Truth says: ﴿And indeed We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient (fasiqin).﴾ That is: the state and condition of most of them remained in fisq (defiant disobedience), breaking the covenant and departing from it. This is because a covenant is a framework that governs the movement of the one who chooses, regarding the commitments he has placed upon himself. He is free to act or not to act, but if he covenants to act, he becomes bound, and it becomes obligatory upon him to fulfil the covenant by his own choice, because he has bound himself by it, so he must regulate his movement within the framework of this covenant. If he departs by his movement from the framework of this covenant, this is fisq. The original meaning of fisq is the exit of the date (rutab) from its skin, because the skin forms a protective enclosure around the fruit so that nothing corrupting from outside enters the fruit. It is said: "The date fasaqat," meaning it came out of its skin.

It is as though our Lord made obligation a wrapping, a protection for the human from ruin. So when one departs from religion, like the date leaving its covering and skin, he becomes exposed to contamination and to microbes. Therefore Allah named the one who rebels against His method "fasiq," because he has gone out of the framework which Allah established for him to protect him from corruptions and from the ruin that befalls him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 103:

After the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, and what passed between them and their peoples, and how He destroyed the deniers and saved the believers, He wished to bring the account of a messenger from among the ulu al-'azm (the possessors of resolve) among the messengers, that is, of those who in their missions encountered things that only a strong and steadfast constitution can bear. I think you know that Musa's dealings with the Jews took a generous share of the Qur'an, indeed the story of Musa with his people is the longest of the Qur'an's stories, because their deviations, their whims and their rebellion against their prophets were numerous, and their prophets were many. For this reason they boast that they have the most prophets, and they said: "We are the nation with the most prophets." We said to them: "The abundance of your prophets is evidence of the deep-rootedness of your disease, for physicians do not multiply except when the treatment of the patient becomes a difficult matter." So the abundance of your prophets is evidence that one messenger is not enough for you, and that many prophets are necessary.

As for His saying, the Truth: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa﴾: The word "sent" (ba'atha), as we understand it, suggests and indicates that He, glory be to Him, sent Musa as a messenger to Pharaoh. The word ba'atha was chosen for the messages because "ba'th" (raising up/resurrecting) implies that something existed, then was buried over, then the Truth raised it up anew. Faith is embodied in the first covenant of fitrah (primordial nature) that was from Adam, for Allah created him with His own hands, a direct creation, and charged him with a direct charge, and Adam transmitted the form to his progeny. This original form is what contains the realities of faith that Adam possessed. When Allah raises up a new messenger, he does not initiate a new creed, but revives what existed and was buried. When corruption overspreads, Allah raises up the messenger. It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, when He charged Adam with the first charge, asked him to transmit this charge to his descendants. Had a person taken the obligations of religion as he took the necessities of life from those who preceded him, faith would have remained a dull matter among mankind.

We take the things that our forefathers bequeathed to us and that benefit us in worldly affairs; we keep them and hold fast to them. So why have we not taken religion from them? Because religion restrains freedom of movement and places it within its correct framework. Man wants to slip out of the restriction of freedom of movement. When our Lord says once that He "sent" the messengers, and once again that He "raised them up," this indicates that He did not bring anything new, but He brought something that was supposed to remain among you as the things that your ancestors bequeathed to you remain among you and you benefit from them. An example of this: we benefit from a loaf of bread and we benefit from the sewing of a needle, so why have we benefited from these material things and forgotten the methodological things? Because material things may assist a person in his desires, whereas the values of religion fight against desires. ﴿Then after them We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ (part of verse 103, surah al-A'raf).

The "ayat" (signs), as we know, is the plural of "aya," which is the marvelous matter at which the intellect stands bewildered. The term "ayat" is used in three senses: it is applied to the Qur'anic verses, because they are stylistically marvelous, expressing every perfection found in existence until the Hour comes, and every reader takes from them according to the capacity of his mind and his understanding. The cosmic signs exist in the creation of the earth and the heavens and other things. Likewise, the term "ayat" is applied to the miracles that testify to the truthfulness of the prophets. Ba'th (sending) requires a one who is sent, who is Musa; it requires one who sends, who is Allah; and those to whom he is sent, who are the people of Pharaoh; and that with which he is sent, which is the methodology.

Dr. Ahmad Umar Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University, reviewed its origin and verified its hadiths. The signs with which Allah sent Musa are proofs of the truthfulness of prophethood, and they are also the expressive words of the methodology, for Pharaoh and his chiefs to witness and listen to. The "mala'" (chiefs), as we learned before, are the people who fill the eyes with awe; people who are not noticed by anyone are called "mala'" or they are the people who fill the chests of gatherings, that is, the nobles and lords. Why did the Truth specify here that Musa was sent only to Pharaoh and his chiefs? Because the rest of their followers, their guidance is easy if the great ones are guided. It is the general custom that those who stand before the path of good are those who benefit from evil, namely the leaders or those around them, and they do not desire the path of good because it collides with their aims and desires, so they fight it. As for the rest of the common people, they are the ones overpowered in their affairs, and when they see that one has come and stood against those who oppressed them with their injustices and subdued them with their tyranny, their hearts turn to this savior!

﴿Then after them We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ (part of verse 103, surah al-A'raf): Even if the signs are the words conveying the methodology found in the Torah, or the signs are the miracles that testify to the truthfulness of Musa, that would have required their belief.

We know that the Qur'an enumerated the miraculous signs that the Truth sent with Musa: ﴿And We gave Musa nine clear signs﴾ (part of verse 101, surah al-Isra'): Among these signs were the staff, and the hand that he would insert into his garment or under his arm and armpit, and it would come out white without any defect or ailment; and the afflicting of the family of Pharaoh with years (of drought). The word "sinin" (years) is used for severe dearth that continues for a period of time, such that it draws people's attention to an event in time; for this reason we say: "It was a grievous year," because the year is a bite of events, which demolishes life's luxury, and then brings them what destroys the necessities of life, the first of which are food and drink, so it afflicts them with a loss of fruits, namely drought and famine. Dearth was called a year (sanah), and its plural is sinin, because it is something by which time is dated. So what was Pharaoh's and his chiefs' reception of the signs that were with Musa, peace be upon him? The Truth says: ﴿but they wronged themselves thereby﴾.

Were the signs an instrument of wrongdoing, or did they wrong themselves because of them, by rejecting them as a way of life? They wronged themselves by them, because they rejected the followers of the true methodology and remained upon their corruption. The corrupters, as we know, are those who deliberately target the good in itself and corrupt it, although what is required of man is that he receive existence as one who sees that there are things beyond his choices and desires, and things within his choice and desire. When a person looks at the things upon which the necessities of life depend, which do not fall within his choice, he finds them in perfect uprightness.

We find that man has no control over the movement of the sun or the movement of the moon, or the stars, or the wind, or the rain; these beings are upright as God wills them, and corruption comes only in the matter in which man has a part. People do not complain of a shortage of air, for example, because no one has any role in the movement of the air; but they complain of a shortage of food, because humans have a part in it; and we find their complaints about a shortage of water to be less, because man's share in water is small.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, makes the matter that moves your fuel-like metabolism have some share that is in your power; He makes your body, for example, a storehouse of fats, so that at the moment of hunger it gives you the energy you have stored in it. And it is marvelous that these fats are one substance, and when we need nutrition from them, the one substance transforms into the other substances that we need.

You need, for example, albumin, and the fat turns into albumin; you need carbon, and fat gives you carbon; you need phosphorus, and it gives you phosphorus; you need magnesium, and fat gives you magnesium; and so on. So if we can endure food according to what is stored in our bodies, and endure water also according to what is stored in these bodies, we cannot endure air, because breathing is inhalation and exhalation. If a person owned the air and gave it to you at the moment of his pleasure and withheld it from you at the moment of his anger, you would die before he became pleased with you. But if water were withheld from you for a period, perhaps your enemy's heart would soften, or someone would bring you water, or you yourself might strive by some stratagem to reach it.

So the matter in which man has no part we find in perfect uprightness, and corruption comes only from the matter in which man has a part.

﴿Then after them We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged themselves thereby; so behold how was the end of the corrupters﴾ (surah al-A'raf): That is, in the end Allah will punish the corrupters.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on Surah 7, verse 104:

He, glory be to Him, wished to recount the sequence of the story not from its beginning, but He begins from its end.
