Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 130:

The Almighty introduced the destruction with His words: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, so that they might take heed.﴾

Thus we see that the destruction did not occur all at once, but in stages, so that when hardship befell them they might humble themselves before Allah.

We know that sanah (sanah, "year") means the year, that is, from a period to the end of a similar period. But it is also used for drought and famine. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), in his supplication against his people, said: "O Allah, make it upon them as the years of Joseph." That is, Allah sends down upon them some measure of drought so that they may learn humility a little.

It is said: "asnata al-qawm" (the people were struck by drought), meaning they were afflicted by famine and dearth. Therefore the sanah intended here is famine and drought.

Why did He call it sanah? Because the blessings of Allah are continuous and many, while His trials of His creatures with evil are few in the cosmos. He bestows blessings upon them for a long period and then tests them in a moment. When He tests them at a time by which they date events, it is said: the trial occurred in such-and-such a year. It is said: "the year of the locusts," "the year of the fire of Cairo." Thus we find people dating events by the calamitous ones, because pleasant events are usually more numerous than bad ones. For this reason we have said that whoever counts the days of affliction should compare them with the days of ease, and each of us should look at the days of the year he has lived. If a day of grief comes to him, let him be told: how many times have you lived and enjoyed ease? We find that the days of ease are more numerous than the days of affliction: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits﴾.

We have understood that years, as we have said, mean drought and famine. As for His words, ﴿and shortage of fruits﴾, they indicate that some fruit still existed, or that the drought and famine were in the desert, whereas the "shortage of fruits" was in the settled areas. It is said that in the settled areas a single palm tree would bear only one cluster (balah) in a year. And why only one cluster? Because the causes of His mercy must remain among His creatures; had the whole palm stock not produced even a single cluster, the lineage of palm trees would have been cut off. Therefore Allah preserves the causes of His mercy for us.

We see in our reality that however much they try to cultivate seedless fruits through contemporary scientific progress, we find a fruit that has come out with a seed in it. Why? We are told: to preserve the species. For if all fruits came out without seeds and we ate them all, how would we plant a new crop? For this reason we have said before that the Real, glorified is He, in His mercy towards creation in preserving blessings and the essentials of life, did not make fruits sweet and palatable until their seeds have ripened. When you cut open a watermelon and its seeds are white, you find its taste unpalatable and you throw it away. But when its seeds turn black and are fit to be replanted, then the watermelon is ripe and sweet in taste. Thus the Real makes clear to you that fruits will not become acceptable and palatable until their seeds have ripened so as to be fit for regrowth, and in this there is the preservation of mercy; and even with the disobedient we find Him, glorified is He, preserving mercy towards them.

{And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, so that they might take heed.} (Surah al-A'raf). His words: {so that they might take heed} mean that man must remember that he is the vicegerent on earth and that he is not original in the cosmos, so that the world remains upright. But what corrupts the world is that when the causes of life, its cosmic laws, respond to a person, and he ploughs, sows, the crop sprouts, he kindles fire and draws water from wells, he forgets that all of this is "causes," and does not remember the Causer except when the causes are withheld from him.

An example from our daily life: when a person goes to open the water tap in the house and finds no water, he first turns to the water valve that controls the house's water and sees whether there is a fault or whether it is closed. If he finds it sound, he checks whether the main water pipe is broken. If the pipe is intact, he looks for a fault in the water-lifting device, and he keeps searching among the many causes. Formerly water came only from wells, and when there was no water in the well the servant would say: "O Lord, give me drink." Civilization now has distanced us from the Causer through causes.

Allah seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits in order to shake their hands free of their causes. When the hand is shaken free of causes, nothing remains but for them to turn to the Causer and say: "O Lord." The Qur'an says of man: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾ (Surah Yunus, 10:12). Thus man remembers the Causer when the causes are withheld from him, for they are the essentials of life; when the essentials of life are withheld, man says: "O Lord." And so it was that Allah's trial of the people of Pharaoh, by seizing them with years of drought and shortage of fruits, was so that they would remember their Creator.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in the book of Tafsir, and by Muslim in the book of the Hypocrites, and by Ahmad (1/280, 441).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 131:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿So when good came to them they said, "This is ours," and if evil afflicted them they ascribed their misfortune to Moses and those with him. Surely their omen is with Allah, but most of them do not know.﴾

When the word "hasanah" (good) is used without qualification, it refers to a matter from which good comes. But good is sometimes yours, and sometimes it is asked of you. The good that is yours in your own self is first that you be in well-being and peace, then the good in the foundations of the self and the foundations of life, which are in plants, animals, fertility and wealth. The good that is asked of you is also for you. He, glory be to Him, asks you to do something that will earn you good in the Hereafter, and for this reason He says: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof﴾ (part of verse 160, Surah al-An'am). This is the good that gives a person benefit afterwards. So the good in your self, such as health and safety, or in the foundations of the self, such as fruits, animals, fertility, herbs and prosperity, all of it is bound to a fixed time, which is this world. The second good is not limited, because its time is not fixed. Which of the goods is then weightier and better for a human being? It is the good of the Hereafter.

As for the Truth's saying: ﴿So when good came to them﴾, meaning, when a measure of fertility, fruits and other sustenance came to them, they say: "This is ours," meaning that we deserve it. One of them says: "I deserve it because I planned for it and perfected the farming and the harvest," just as Qarun said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess﴾ (part of verse 78, Surah al-Qasas). Allah puts such a claim to the test: since he claims that he obtained the wealth through knowledge from himself, let the knowledge he has preserve the wealth for him, or preserve himself for him. They said of the goods that Allah bestows upon them: "They said, 'This is ours'," meaning we deserve it, because we made preparations that give us these results. It was the custom in ancient times that the Nile would overflow every year and cover the land, then they would sow the grain and wait for the harvest. If evil came to them, such as Allah seizing them with years of drought, they attributed that to Moses.

﴿And if evil afflicts them they ascribe their misfortune to Moses and those with him. Surely their omen is with Allah, but most of them do not know﴾ (part of verse 131, Surah al-A'raf). So when evil comes to them, they say "yatatayyaru", meaning they take omens of ill fortune, because tiyara is taking ill omen, and its opposite is taking good omen. It is said: "So-and-so's omen is bad," and "So-and-so's omen is blessing and happiness." In ancient times, when they wanted to seek a matter, they would bring a bird, the owner of the matter would place it on his hand, shoo it and stir it up. If it flew to the right, this was a good sign, and if it flew to the left, this was a bad sign. Here the Truth makes clear: do not wrong Moses, for your ill fortune or your bad luck is not from Moses, because Moses owns nothing in Allah's dominion; the owner of the universe is the Lord of Moses. It seems the Truth also wants them not to be tempted by Moses if he does something that brings them good, and here He tells them: do not take omens from Moses, for your omen is from Allah.

Life's events are of two kinds. One is an event in which you have a part, like the student who did not study and failed, or a person who does not drive his car well, so it overturns and injures him or injures someone else seriously. Here this person has no opponent except himself. And there is something that befalls you, called a compelling event (hadath qahri). So in events a person stands between two things: either a calamity that has entered upon him from his own self because of his negligence in something, or fated events that descend upon a person, which we say are from Allah for a wisdom that the person does not know, because a person looks at the surface of things and at the immediate aspect of the matter, but does not look at its outcome. For this reason some events happen to him in which he has no part.

An example of this: a person has a gifted and intelligent son who is always among the top ten. Then on the night of the examination, or on the first day of the examination, he gets a headache that prevents him from knowing how to answer the exam questions, and he fails. This is a calamity in which he has no part. People usually grieve over such calamities, but the believer says: the boy did not fall short, and this is a matter that came from Allah, and He, glory be to Him, is exalted above futility, rather He is wise, and there must be a wisdom in such matters. After a time the wisdom becomes clear, for had the boy succeeded, the evil eye of the envious would have struck him. Something he disliked happened to him, as if Allah were making him an amulet by which He protects him from envy. In ancient times, when they wanted to protect a beautiful child, they would make him a "fasukha" (a dirty amulet), and not care about his cleanliness or his clothes. Why? It is said, so that the eye of the envier does not turn toward him.

I say: what makes you sure that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, arranged the sudden event to ward off the eye from him and silence people about him? And what makes you sure that Allah wanted him to fail this year because he could not obtain the aggregate that would admit him to the faculty he wanted, and then he studies in the following year and the study is easy for him, and we say to him: praise your Lord that you did not succeed the previous year and that Allah wanted good for you, so that you exert effort, succeed and obtain the aggregate you wanted for yourself.

So the decrees that run over people without any part of theirs in them contain a wisdom from Allah, and of these it is said: ﴿Their omen is with Allah﴾. But if a person has a part in what happens to him, it is said: your omen is from yourself, and your ill fortune is from your own self and your disobedience.

﴿So when good came to them they said, "This is ours," and if evil afflicted them they ascribed their misfortune to Moses and those with him. Surely their omen is with Allah, but most of them do not know (131)﴾: Did not the Jews in Medina take ill omen from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they said: rain has ceased and prices have risen because of the ill fortune of this man's coming? They did not understand the wisdom of Allah. They were lords of the Arabian Peninsula, for they were people of knowledge of the Book, controlled the commercial market, dealt in usury and the arms trade, and had fortresses and weapons. Allah wanted to occupy them by taking away some of their means and to demolish their structure, so as to draw their attention to the fact that they had departed from the method, and that there was a messenger who had come to return them to the method.

As for the Truth's saying: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, it implies that there is a minority who know. So what was the position of this minority, and why did they not reject the position of the majority? Their position was silence, out of fear of tyranny, for the tyrant coerced and subdued them and made them keep silent and not object to falsehood. We see in our lives many people who know falsehood and know oppression, but they do not speak.

The Almighty then says: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not be believers in you."﴾

That is, the people of Pharaoh said to Musa, peace be upon him: "Whatever miracles you bring us, to turn us away from what we are upon, we will not believe you." They called what Musa brought a "sign" in mockery and derision. All of this is a set of preliminaries that justify the destruction of which God said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy﴾ (part of verse 129, Surah al-A'raf). They declared that what Musa brought was sorcery, despite the fact that they had seen the sorcerers, who excelled in magic, knew its methods, and surpassed all others in it, fall down prostrate and believe. How could this happen, when all the sorcerers had been gathered for an appointed time? All the people witnessed the real trial in which Musa's staff swallowed all the sorcerers' magic, so they believed and prostrated. How could those who do not know magic accuse Musa of sorcery? And how could they imagine that what he brings from the signs of God is a kind of magic?

They say the word "مهما" (mahma, "whatever"), which indicates the persistence of obstinacy in their souls, just as one man says to another: "I have resolved not to accept your words," and the man repeats: "Wait, so you may hear my second proof, for it may convince you," and he says: "Whatever proofs you bring, I will not listen to you." This means persistent obstinacy, denial and rebellion. They then present the grounds for this denial, saying: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not be believers in you."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). If they think that the signs of God that came with Musa are sorcery, can the one who is bewitched have any will against the sorcerer? And if the matter were sorcery, he would have bewitched you and the matter would have ended. We said long ago, in answering those who said that Muhammad (ﷺ) bewitches people so that they believe in him: if he had bewitched people so they would believe in him, why did he not bewitch you so you would believe and the matter be settled? Your remaining in obstinacy is proof that he possesses nothing of the nature of sorcery.

When you hear the word "مهما" (mahma), you know that there is a condition and that it has an answer. The scholars say its original form is "مه" (mah), meaning: "Desist from bringing us any sign, for we will not believe you." This means there is insistence and obstinacy against faith.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary states that the Truth (Allah) shows His punishment for them because of that:

﴿So We sent upon them the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs. But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people.ﴩ (7:133)﴾.

The word "al-Tufan" (the flood) is used to mean an overflowing of water. Water, as we know, is the cause of life, and Allah may make it a cause of destruction, so that you do not understand that things operate by their own nature, but by the directions of the One who has power over them. When we look at the flood that drowned the people of Nuh, no one survived except those who boarded the ship with Nuh; here, with the people of Musa, there is no ship, because Allah wants to affirm the punishment for their tyranny. If the flood struck the family of Pharaoh together with the Children of Israel, to the point that the water reached the collarbones of one of them, so that he remained standing, for if he sat he would die, and it continued like this, and the sky rained upon them for seven days, during which they could not tell night from day, while they saw before them the houses of the Children of Israel untouched by the water, this is a clear miracle. The flood spread widely, and the Truth wished to save the Children of Israel from it without any scheme on their part, so that it would not be said that it was a cosmic sign that came in the form of a flood and the matter ended. But the flood came to their houses and did not touch the Children of Israel.

The narrators said: The flood entered upon Pharaoh until he cried out and sought help from Musa, and said to him: "Remove this from us, and we will believe in what you have brought." Musa called upon his Lord, and the flood was lifted from them.

But they returned to disbelief.

Allah made among His signs glimpses and indications, beginning with the flood. When our Lord makes clear: "I punished the people of Nuh and the people of Pharaoh with the flood," He gives us features that make us feel the truth of the matter. The torrent descends upon any land, destroys homes, and drowns crops and animals, so that we see a cosmic image. Likewise, Allah sends the locusts at intervals, and they descend at any time, and we set up campaigns to combat them. This is evidence for the truth of what Allah related about them; for if there were no locusts or flood, we would be prone not to believe. Allah also afflicted them with lice. "Al-Qummal" (the lice) is different from "al-Qamal." Al-Qamal is the pest that afflicts a person's body and clothing and arises from filthy clothes. As for al-Qummal, it is said to be the weevil that affects grains, its singular being qummala; and it is said to be what we call the tick; and it is said to be the insects that destroy plants and tillage. When we see it, we become alarmed and seek to rid the crops of it by hand and by pesticides. All of this is among the Truth's reminders to creation, and they are merely a warning, guidance, and a turning of attention toward the Truth.

Likewise Allah sent upon them "the frogs." When any one of them puts his hand into something, he finds frogs in it; the food vessel, when its lid is lifted, shows frogs in it, and the water he drinks contains frogs! And if he opens his mouth, a frog enters the mouth! This is a sign and a miracle. Likewise with "the blood": everything turned to blood for them.

It is said that a woman of Pharaoh's people wanted to drink water, so she went to a woman of the Children of Israel and said to her: "Take the water into your mouth and spit it into mine," as if she wished to outwit our Lord and take her water without blood; so it passes from the mouth of the Israelite woman as water, but when it enters the mouth of the woman who is of Pharaoh's people, it becomes blood.

﴿So We sent upon them the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs﴾ (part of 7:133). As for His words, glorified is He, ﴿distinct﴾: it means that He did not bring them all together at once to frighten them in one go and test them, to see whether they would declare faith or not. Rather, He brought each sign separated from the others; no sign came together with another at the same time. Or He brought them as clear signs containing admonitions and lessons, which indicates the continuous succession of warnings out of desire that they would be mindful, and would refrain. For if they had been mindful and refrained after a single sign, He would have removed the affliction from them.

Allah sent the signs, which are: flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood. These are five signs in this verse which we are discussing. Earlier the Truth said that He seized them with years of drought and with the loss of fruits, so the signs became seven. Earlier there was also the staff of Musa, which swallowed what the magicians had made, so it became eight signs; and likewise the "white hand" that Musa showed to Pharaoh and his people, so the number becomes nine signs. Thus the signs in order are: the staff, the hand, the seizing by years, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood.

The "distinct signs" are wonders; each of them is a wonder which Allah directs at whomever He wishes to humiliate, and Allah afflicts one people with them and does not afflict other peoples. So what was their stance toward the signs and wonders? We find the Truth concluding the verse: ﴿But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people﴾. They did not believe; rather they were arrogant and committed crimes against their own selves, and they severed what lay between them and faith.

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And when the punishment (ar-rijz) fell upon them, they said, "O Moses, call upon your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you."﴾

They, then, after they had become arrogant and were a criminal people, and events followed one another upon them. Ar-rijz (the terrifying calamities, the punishment that came down upon them). Here they went to Moses to ask him to call upon Allah to lift and remove from them the punishment that had descended upon them. Thus they believed that Moses was a messenger from a Lord, and they understood that the calamity they were living in would not be lifted except by that Lord. This nullifies the lordship of their god Pharaoh, for if the lordship of Pharaoh had been in their belief, they would have gone to him and not gone to their enemy Moses to ask him to call upon Allah for them. From this we derive more than one doctrinal matter: first, that the divinity of Pharaoh is false; second, that Moses' supplication is accepted by his Lord; and third, that if his Lord does not remove this punishment, the punishment will continue. All of these are premises that lead to faith in Allah.

﴿They said, "O Moses, call upon your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and we will surely send the Children of Israel with you."﴾ (Part of verse 134, Surat al-A'raf): That is, call upon your Lord by the covenant that Allah has given you, that He will support you, because you are His messenger, supported by His miracles, and He will not abandon you. Call upon Allah to lift the punishment from us; by Allah, if You lift and remove from us what we are in of punishment, we will surely believe in you, we will surely affirm what you have brought, we will surely send and release the Children of Israel with you. They had been employing them in the basest and most degrading tasks. But each time, after the Truth removes the punishment from them, they return to breaking the covenant, as evidenced by His saying, glory be to Him, concerning them:

﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word.﴾

So it is as if, with every sign, they broke their covenant. Notice the difference between the two expressions: between His saying, the Truth:

﴿So when We removed the punishment from them, until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word.ﴩﵿ

and between His earlier saying: ﴿Pray to your Lord for us, by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you﴾. So who, then, removes the punishment? Here the removing is attributed to God, and every removal of punishment has a term known to the Truth. He is the one who says: ﴿until a term which they were to reach, behold, they break their word﴾. And "nakth" (نكث, breaking) is the breaking of a covenant.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 136:

He, glorified is He, continues: ﴿So We took retribution from them, and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾

Here He, glorified is He, makes clear that since He had seized them with punishment in their own selves, in the foundations of their lives, and in the things that spoiled their pleasures, nothing remained but that they should be destroyed, for there was no benefit in them. Therefore the command to drown them came, not out of the tyranny of power, but out of the justice of decree, because they denied the signs and persisted in their disbelief. It should be noted here that the most important part of the matter, which is the drowning, has been mentioned in brief, and it is the event that came in detail in another surah. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 52)

The Truth did not give the details of the story of the drowning here, because every verse of the Qur'an addresses a situation and treats one snapshot of events; the story comes in summary in one place and in elaboration in another. Here the scene of the drowning comes in summary: ﴿So We took retribution from them, and drowned them in the sea.﴾ The phrase "and drowned them" has a long, well-known story which is presented in a different manner in another surah. When Moses and the Children of Israel left Egypt, Pharaoh went out after them. When the Children of Israel saw that, they said, by the logic of events: ﴿Indeed, we are going to be overtaken.﴾ They would be overtaken by Pharaoh and his people, because in front of them was the sea and they had no means of crossing it. But Moses, sent by God, knew that God would not forsake him, because He wanted to complete the blessing of guidance through his hands. Moses, peace be upon him, was full of certainty and trust, so he said with full conviction: ﴿"No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-Shu'ara')

He was saying: "No!", meaning they will not overtake you, not by their means, but by the means of the One who sent him. The proof is that he came with its premises together with it and said: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ He spoke in the manner of the believer who has taken refuge in a firm support, and that matters cannot end in this situation, because he had not yet fully accomplished the mission. Therefore he said "No!" with full conviction, even though the means were certain: the sea was before them and the enemy behind them. He followed this with his words: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me⦆ — with protection and victory. That is, the means that God had previously sent with me are beyond the bounds of human means. The staff had previously been used by God to give him victory over the magicians, and it is the very staff that He revealed to him to use in this grave situation, saying to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ (part of verse 63, Surah al-Shu'ara'). We know that the sea is a container of water, and the first law of water is fluidity, which enables it to spread out and level. If water were not fluid, but had rigidity and thickness, it would become uneven pieces; it is fluidity that enables it to spread out level, and that is why, when we want to check the precise evenness of any surface, we resort to the water level.

The Truth, glorified is He, said to Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ (part of verse 63, Surah al-Shu'ara'). When Moses struck the sea with his staff, the water refrained from the law of fluidity and lost the law of spreading out level. God depicts this matter for us with precision, saying: ﴿So every part was like a mighty mountain.﴾ That is, each portion of it became like a *tawd*, which is a mountain; in a mountain we find firmness, and thus the water lost its fluidity and each divided part became like a standing mountain. Only the Creator can do this, because fluidity and the spreading out of water are a cosmic law, and He who created this cosmic law is the One who can nullify it. When Moses and his people walked on dry ground, and all of them crossed the path that had appeared in the sea, Pharaoh and his soldiers followed after them. Moses wanted to strike the sea with his staff so that it would return to fluidity and spreading out, so that Pharaoh and his soldiers would not follow him. This too is human thinking. Then a command from God came to Moses: ﴿And leave the sea as a calm (*rahwan*) road⦆ (part of verse 24, Surah al-Dukhan). That is: leave the sea still in the state it is in, so that Pharaoh and his people may enter it. He, glorified is He, did not want the water to return to fluidity and spreading out until the dry path would lure Pharaoh and his people, so that they would come after you to overtake you. When they entered and the dry ground had received them all, We would restore the fluidity and spreading out of the water, and they would drown. Thus the Truth establishes that He saves and destroys by one and the same thing. All of this the Truth summarises here in His words: ﴿So We took retribution from them, and drowned them in the sea.﴾ The "*yamm*" is the place where there is deep water, and it is used sometimes for salt water and sometimes for sweet water. For example, in the story of Moses' mother, the Truth says: ﴿And We revealed to Moses' mother: "Suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the *yamm*."﴾ (part of verse 7, Surah al-Qasas). The intended *yamm* there was the Nile, but the intended meaning here in Surah al-A'raf is the sea. The cause of the drowning comes in His words: ﴿because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ How then does He punish and drown them as a consequence of heedlessness, when we know that heedlessness carries no accountability? The proof is that the fasting person may forget and eat, and his fast remains valid. It is said that our Lord gave him a meal of nourishment and reckoned his fast for him because he was heedless. But here the matter of heedlessness is different: the meaning of "heedless" here is that they had denied the signs of God and then turned away with a turning away that could only come from one heedless of God and of His method. Had they been servants mindful of God's method, it would not have been valid for them to be heedless. This statement confirms what He had said earlier: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy﴾ (part of verse 129, Surah al-A'raf).

Then comes the statement that fulfils what He, glorified is He, had previously said: ﴿And He will make you successors in the land and will see how you act﴾ (part of verse 129, surah al-A'raf). And the Truth, to confirm this, says: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been erecting﴾ (137).

That is, Egypt and the Levant came under the command of the Children of Israel, and it is the land which Allah blessed with fertility, growth, crops, fruits, livestock, and everything that sustains life and the comforts of life: ﴿and the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient﴾.

﴿And the word of your Lord was fulfilled﴾, meaning the word remained upon them, and the true promise of Allah was accomplished: the establishment of the Children of Israel in the land and His granting them victory over their enemy, and the blessing was completed, because Allah destroyed their enemy and gave them the land as inheritance, and His word, which came through the tongue of Moses, was realised:

﴿And He will make you successors in the land and will see how you act﴾ (part of verse 129, surah al-A'raf).

Thus the word of Allah was fulfilled by His saying: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land﴾ (part of verse 137, surah al-A'raf). We know that the expression "eastern and western [parts]" is used in relative terms: there is no place called "east" and another called "west," rather these are relative directions. One place is called east relative to some location, and likewise it is called west relative to another location. When a person moves to another place, there is another east and another west. For example, those who live in India and Japan know that the Middle East is west for them, while those who live in Europe know that the Middle East is east for them.

We have said before that when the Truth mentions "the east and the west" in the plural form, as here, this indicates that every place has an east and every place has a west; when the sun sets in one place, it rises in another. In Ramadan we find that the sun sets in Cairo a few minutes before Alexandria.

We know that the reason for this cycle is that the remembrance of Allah should remain with all that Allah requires at all of Allah's times. For example, when we pray the dawn prayer, we find people praying the noon prayer at that very moment, others praying the afternoon prayer, another group praying the sunset prayer, and others praying the night prayer. Thus Allah's will is realised that there is worship at every time and every moment: when a Muslim calls out "Allahu Akbar" to announce the dawn prayer, another Muslim is saying "Allahu Akbar" calling to the noon, afternoon, sunset or night prayer. This is the difference in the risings, which He, glorified is He, intended so that His name would remain mentioned on every tongue in every place, so that "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar" would be raised everywhere.

And if you calculate time to less than a second, you will find that Allah's being is never free of "There is no god but Allah": ﴿and the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled﴾. We know that the word "fair" (al-husna) is an adjective for the feminine, and "word" (kalima) is feminine, and the word is the saying of the Truth: ﴿And We wished to confer favour upon those who had been oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors (5)﴾ (surah al-Qasas). The Truth stated the account concisely, and this is the word which our Lord spoke, which is "the fair," because He, glorified is He, did not give them a blessing contemporaneous with the enemy's blessing, but a blessing upon the ruins of the enemy. So it is a blessing that includes the destruction of their enemy, and then He gave them, after that, that He made them leaders and guides and made them inheritors of the land: ﴿and the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient﴾. And indeed they were patient over the harm they suffered, which He, glorified is He, mentioned earlier when He said: ﴿They inflicted upon you the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive﴾ (part of verse 49, surah al-Baqarah). The punishment of Allah came upon the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been erecting﴾ (part of verse 137, surah al-A'raf). Destruction (tadmir) means that you crush a thing and ruin it. What Allah did to the people of Pharaoh has remained in the monuments that show you the greatness of what they did, and you find scholars discovering many monuments under the earth every day. It is remarkable that all archaeological discoveries are beneath the earth, and no archaeological discovery has ever come from above the earth.

The word "destroyed" (dammarna) indicates that the things destroyed were of great height, then erosion factors came to cover them, and Allah left evidences of them to show us the nature of what they built, such as the pyramids for example. Every day we discover new monuments existing beneath the ground, just as we discovered the city of Thebes in the Valley of the Kings, which was covered with sand through the action of erosion factors that move sand from one place to another. If you are absent from your house for a month, even though you close the doors and windows before travelling, and then return to find dust covering the whole house and its furniture, all of this is by the action of erosion, which penetrates the finest openings. Likewise, if you look at ancient villages before paving operations that stabilise the ground were undertaken, you will find that the village roads leading to the houses rise over time little by little, and each house sinks a little, and every so often they fill in the floors of the houses so they rise, and all of this is from erosion factors that increase the height of the street surfaces.

All the antiquities of the world are discovered only through excavation, so the word "destroyed" has its basis. And the Truth says about Pharaoh's structures: ﴿And Pharaoh of the stakes (10)﴾ (surah al-Fajr).

We find the pyramid, for example, as a witness to the strength of construction, and to this day no one has discovered how it was built, or how its stones hold together without a material such as cement. It is said that the building of the pyramid was accomplished by the method of evacuating air, and no one knows how the Egyptians moved the stone that is on top of the pyramid. So they had vast knowledge. When we look at this knowledge in architecture, monuments and embalming of the bodies of the ancients, and you consider that those who carried it out were priests attributed to religion, we become certain that the secrets of all these matters were with religious men, and the origin of religion is from heaven, even if it has been distorted. This confirms for us that the Truth is He who guided people from the beginning of creation to vast knowledge.

﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been erecting﴾ (surah al-A'raf). And "yaʿrishūn" means they erect trellised gardens (jannat maʿrūshāt). We said before that some crops lie flat on the surface of the ground and have no stalk; sometimes they have a stalk; and a third kind has a soft stalk, so they make a trellis (ʿarīsha) for it, or what we call here the "tikʿībiyya" (trellis frame), to bear its fruit.

Then the Truth says: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to idols they had. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed you are a people who are ignorant."﴾ (7:138)

They said this while they were still immersed in the blessings of Allah: deliverance from an enemy, and their being made successors in the land. Yet as soon as they came out onto dry land and saw a group worshipping an idol, they asked Moses to make for them an idol to worship. They envied those who were ignorant of the value of faith and who devoted themselves to worshipping idols. The verb ya'kufu (to devote oneself, to remain in a place constantly) means to stay in a place continuously, and from it comes i'tikaf (retreat, seclusion) in the mosque, meaning withdrawal from the movement of life outside the mosque in order to worship Allah in His house. ﴿They came upon a people who were devoted to idols they had. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods."﴾

(From verse 137 of Surah al-A'raf.)

This statement by the people of Moses is the pinnacle of foolishness, as if the god were unknown to them, though He had bestowed upon them many blessings. This is the first failure. They wanted the god to be something made, although God, in His perfection and the absoluteness of His power, is the Maker. Their mentality did not grasp the overwhelming blessings, and their hearts were closed, not penetrated by faith. They said: "Make for us a god!" They wanted the idols to be carved for them. One of them might say: "The head of the god is a little large; let us reduce it somewhat, and its nose is not straight, so let us straighten it with a chisel." Their saying ﴿make for us a god﴾ makes us understand that their minds had not grasped the reality of faith; therefore Moses says to them: ﴿Indeed you are a people who are ignorant.﴾

He did not say to them "you do not know" (la ta'lamun), but said "you are ignorant" (tajhalun), because there is a difference between not knowing a thing (adam al-'ilm) and being ignorant of a thing (al-jahl). Lack of knowledge means that the mind may be empty of any proposition, whereas "jahl" means that you hold a belief contrary to the proposition. So there is a proposition that the ignorant person believes, but it is not real. As for the one who does not know, there is no proposition in his mind, and when the proposition comes to him he is convinced by it, and this does not require a single mental operation, like the unlettered person (ummi) who does not know, for his mind is empty of a proposition. But the one who knows a contrary proposition needs from the Messenger two mental operations: the first is to remove from his soul the proposition of ignorance, and the second is to give him the new proposition. It is the ignorant who burden the teacher, not the unlettered, because when you give information to the unlettered person, he has nothing that contradicts it. But the ignorant person has something that contradicts it and opposes reality.

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿Indeed, those—what they are engaged in is destroyed, and what they have been doing is baseless.﴾ (7:139)

"Mutabbar" means ruined and destroyed. Here Moses makes clear to them that this group who worship idols, along with their idols, are doomed, and that what they are doing is false. As for the nature of existing things: if you want to know their reality, it must have a firm basis, and the truth is firm and never changes, because it has an actual reality that can be investigated. An example of this: if an incident has truly occurred before all of us, and then each person is asked separately to say what he saw, we will not differ in describing it, because we are deriving from a real event. But if the matter did not actually happen, each one will tell it in a different way. For this reason, it is one of the finer points of judicial practice that the judge questions the witnesses at length, so that it becomes clear what they agree upon and where they contradict one another. If the witnesses are describing a real fact, they will not differ in their testimony; but they differ when one of them is not certain of the event, or when the event is not true.

The Arabic proverb says: "If you are a liar, then be a good rememberer" (إن كنت كذوبا فكن ذكورا). That is, if you lie, God forbid, and say something untrue, then you must remember your lie, and you will not remember it, because it is something imagined and not something established. It may also be that what is not real takes on glitter and shine, so we say: beware of being deceived by this glitter, for Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus Allah strikes [the example of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum cast out; but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth. Thus Allah presents the examples.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:17). He, glorified is He, has likened falsehood to foam, which is the froth that rises on the surface of flowing water, along with the chaff and refuse that float on the surface of water: it dissolves and disappears, while what benefits people remains. We also test metals to know whether they are adulterated or not, placing them over the fire, so that the impure material and the dross float to the top, and the genuine metal remains at the bottom.

And here the Truth says, on the tongue of Moses: ﴿Indeed, those—what they are engaged in is destroyed, and what they have been doing is baseless.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:139).

Actions are either deeds or speech. Speech is the activity of the tongue, and deed is the activity of the rest of the limbs; all actions arise either from speech or from deed, and speech and deed together are "amal" (work/action). For this reason the Truth says: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (part of verse 2, Surah al-Saff). So "amal" includes both speech and deed.

As for His saying, ﴿and what they have been doing is baseless﴾: the idols that they fashioned and worshipped were established upon speech and deeds. They would say: "O Hubal! O Lat! O 'Uzza!", they would address these idols in private prayer and ask them to fulfil some of their needs, and they would stand before them humbled and abased. Thus there proceeded from them speech and action, which together are encompassed by "amal".

Al-Haqq continues upon the tongue of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿He said, "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾

When they said to Musa, "Make for us a god just as they have gods," he first said to them: ﴿Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant.﴾ Then he said: ﴿Indeed, these—what they are in is destroyed, and worthless is what they have been doing.﴾ After that he returned to the proof that this request was an act of ignorance, and that those who worship idols besides Allah are only doing something false. So he said: ﴿He said, "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾

His words ﴿Ghayra Allah (other than Allah)﴾ mean: the God whom you have known through practical experience, that He preferred you over the worlds, and you saw what He did to your enemy who subjugated you and inflicted upon you the evil torment—indeed He destroyed him and annihilated him. Is it possible that you would seek a lord other than Him?

His words ﴿Aghayra Allah abghikum﴾ mean: "Shall I seek for you a god other than Him?" In this question there is a rebuke, because it is followed by Allah's preferring them over the worlds.

Then He wished to remind them of the peak of the favour bestowed upon them, so He, glorified is He, says on the tongue of Musa:

﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.﴾ (7:141)

When you hear "idh" (when), understand that its meaning is a temporal adverb: Truth wants us to remember what happened at that time. And "idh" means: remember well, and let it not escape your minds, when Allah delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment and the most severe and grievous of it.

Then He says, explaining and clarifying that torment:

﴿They slaughtered your sons and kept your women alive﴾.

We notice that He did not use a conjunction here. He did not say: "who afflicted you with the worst torment and slaughtered your sons and kept your women alive." This indicates that He has mentioned the very peak of the worst torment, because humiliation and subjugation are part of the torment, but the peak of the torment is the killing of the sons and the keeping alive of the women.

In a second verse He says: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons﴾ (from verse 49 of Surat al-Baqarah). That is, they were exposed to killing and they were exposed to slaughter.

In a third verse He says: ﴿When He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment and slaughtered your sons﴾ (from verse 6 of Surat Ibrahim). Here He used the conjunction "wa" (and) for coordination, because the speaker here is different. The speaker may be Allah, and He, glorified is He, bestows favour with the peak of blessings. But [in the verse]: ﴿When Musa said to his people, "Remember..."﴾, Musa is bestowing favour with every blessing that Allah brought to the Children of Israel, great and small.

The Truth concludes the noble verse with: ﴿And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾: it is a trial of severe pain and impact through separation from those who were killed or slaughtered, and another trial in the anxiety and sorrow over those women who were kept alive, to be violated in their honour and degraded in service.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 142:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters."﴾ (7:142)

We have already learned, in the matter of numbers, that there are two methods: the first is summary (ijmali) and the second is detailed (tafsili). Sometimes the detail agrees with the summary, and then there is no doubt or difficulty. In surah al-Baqarah, He (glorified be He) says: ﴿And when We appointed for Moses forty nights﴾ (2:51). There He gave the number in summary. But here, in surah al-A'raf, He willed not to give it once in summary. Rather, He detailed it as thirty nights, then completed them with ten more, for a purpose we will come to know later, so that the appointed term came to be forty nights. When a number comes once in summary and once in detail, and the summary agrees with the detail, there is no problem. But when the summary differs from the detail, the usual practice is to interpret the detail in light of the summary, because the detailed parts can overlap so as to become the summary.

We earlier gave the example of the creation of the heavens and the earth in six days. All the verses of creation speak of the six days in summary. But in another place in the Qur'an, He (glorified be He) willed to say: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.﴾ (41:9–10, surah Fussilat).

The apparent meaning here is that the matter was completed and created in six days. But after that He said, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly."﴾ (41:11) ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ (41:12, part). Here, in the context of the days of the creation of the world, we find summary and detail: the detail, in its apparent meaning, reaches eight days regarding the days of creation, while the summary states that they were six days only.

So are they six days or eight days? We say: they are six days, because we can fold the detailed parts into one another. If you say: "I travelled from Cairo to Tanta in two hours, and to Alexandria in three hours," the meaning of this statement is that the two hours are included within the three hours.

﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten.﴾ The promise was that after the deliverance of the Children of Israel, God promised Moses that He would send down to him a Book comprising the entire method by which the movement of their life would proceed. But as soon as Moses went to the appointed time with his Lord, they worshipped the calf during the thirty days. God did not will to send Moses after the thirty days, but completed them with ten more, so that Moses would not return and see what his people had done; for when he returned, he seized his brother by the head, rebuking him severely and taking him by the beard, dragging him toward himself, asking how he had allowed the Children of Israel to worship the calf. On this, the Truth says on the tongue of Aaron: ﴿He said, "O son of my mother, do not seize my beard nor my head. I feared that you would say, 'You have caused division among the Children of Israel and have not observed my word.'"﴾ (20:94, surah Ta-Ha).

So it is as if the ten days were added beyond the thirty days, to give you the final picture found in surah al-Baqarah.

Here the Truth says in surah al-A'raf: ﴿And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters."﴾ (7:142, part). "Ukhlufni" means: be my successor among them until I return, and that concerns what is specific to Moses in the mission. So Moses's appointing Aaron as successor was not an assignment to Aaron to extend the sending of God to Moses and Aaron. The style of Moses and Aaron presenting themselves to Pharaoh came with the dual pronoun that unites Moses and Aaron: ﴿Indeed we are two messengers of your Lord﴾ (20:47), because each of them is a messenger. And His words, the Truth: ﴿And Moses said to his brother Aaron﴾ contain tenderness, meaning: I have a bond with you before you are a partner with me in the mission. I am your brother and you are my brother, and it is my right over you that you hear my words and succeed me. So brotherhood is joined with your being a partner with me in the mission. Thus we find that Moses presented the basis of brotherhood and partnership in the mission. Moses (peace be upon him) also emphasized with the word "my people" that they are dear to him, and he wants for them only the good he wants for himself. So if he brings you a command, know that it is for your benefit, and if he forbids you something, know that Moses is the first to apply it to himself.

It was also said that Moses (peace be upon him) had prepared himself to meet his Lord, and preparation must be with purity, with purification, and with purifying the soul through fasting. So he fasted thirty days. After that, he disliked the smell of his mouth, so he took a siwak and cleaned his teeth with it to remove the smell of his mouth. God, glorified be He, made clear to him: "Did you not know, O Moses, that the odour from the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Me than the scent of musk? Since you have removed the odour, and I want you to come to Me with the scent of musk, add ten days, so that you may come likewise." Some scholars said: the detailing of the forty into thirty and ten is because the thirty days are the days in which the people worshipped the calf after Moses, so there had necessarily to be a period, so that God might distinguish the wicked from the good.

﴿And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters."﴾ (7:142, part)

Here there is a command and a prohibition: "aslih" (act righteously) is a command, and "la tattabi'" (do not follow) is a prohibition. We know that all the obligations of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, are confined to "do such-and-such" and "do not do such-and-such." The Truth does not say to those who are obligated, "Do such-and-such," except when they are capable of both doing and not doing. And if He says to them, "Do not do," they must likewise be capable of both doing and not doing. For this reason we explained earlier that God concentrated all the obligation in the matter of Adam and Eve in the Garden, when He said: ﴿And eat from it in abundance wherever you wish﴾ (2:35), and this was the command. He said: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ (2:35), and this was the prohibition. ﴿And act righteously and do not follow the way of the corrupters.﴾

The word "aslih" entails that the one who is righteous remain upon his righteousness and not corrupt it, and if he wishes to increase it in righteousness, let him do so. His words: ﴿and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ are addressed to a prophet, Aaron, who is not capable of corrupting. But Moses informed him that a trial would arise shortly, as if Moses had been inspired that corruption would occur. So the utmost of what he asks of his brother Aaron is that he not follow the way of the corrupters. For this reason Aaron would later, justifying his leaving the Children of Israel to worship the calf, say, after he had exerted his utmost effort in preventing and warning them, until they overpowered and oppressed him and nothing remained but for them to kill him:

﴿I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and have not observed my word."﴾ (20:94, part)

And the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿When Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me." And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down unconscious. When he recovered, he said: "Glory be to You! I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers."﴾

The miqat (the appointed time, a term for the time set for an action) is the time fixed for a deed, and we call it the time of the action. It has come to be applied to certain matters in Islam, such as the appointed times of the Hajj (the pilgrimage to Makkah). We know that every action and every event requires two things in which it is contained, that is, they are its containers: it must have a place in which it occurs and a time in which it occurs. These two are called the container of time and the container of place. However, the container of time is not fixed, that is, it is not stable: the dawn comes and goes and is followed by the noon, the afternoon, the sunset and the night. But the container of place is fixed and stable.

So the appointed times are either governed by time, or governed by place, or governed by both time and place together. If we take the appointed times to be the time of each act, we find that the obligation of fasting has a specific time, which is Ramadan. So it is time that governs fasting, and it takes place in any location. Likewise is the fasting of the Day of Arafah: whoever sits anywhere fasts the Day of Arafah, but this is not required of the pilgrim. However, standing at Arafah is governed by both place and time together.

Entering the state of consecration (ihram) for Hajj or Umrah is governed by place, and this is what is called the spatial appointed place (al-miqat al-makani). For each region there is its own spatial appointed place, which they are required not to pass without being in the state of consecration. So at times time governs, at times place governs, and at a third time both govern together.

And Moses came to Our appointed time, which was fixed for him after forty nights. Did Moses come to the appointed time, or did he come in the appointed time? He came in the appointed time, and the particle "li" (lam) comes in the sense of "at" ('inda). We know that the lam comes in the sense of "at" frequently in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ (Qur'an 17:78). That is: establish prayer at the decline of the sun, that is, at its departure from the middle and center of the sky, until the darkness of the night. From the decline to the darkness we find the noon prayer, then the afternoon prayer, then the sunset prayer, then the night prayer, and these are four obligations. The fifth obligation remains, which is the dawn prayer, and about it the Truth said: ﴿and [the recitation of] dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ (Qur'an 17:78). Why did He begin with the decline of the sun? And does the day begin with noon or with dawn? The Night Journey (al-Isra') and the Ascension (al-Mi'raj) took place at night, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came in the morning to Makkah, and prayer was made obligatory during the Ascension, so the first obligation was the noon prayer. It is as if the Truth means: take the end and take the beginning: the prayers of noon, afternoon, sunset and night, and the dawn remains, and about it He said: ﴿and [the recitation of] dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾. Then God singled out His Messenger with tahajjud (the night prayer, the voluntary prayer at night), because it was obligatory upon the Messenger of God alone and not upon others; for the rest of the community it is voluntary: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ (Qur'an 17:79).

Whoever imitates the Messenger of God will have great reward and a mighty recompense, but this matter is referred to the choice of the Muslim. ﴿When Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him﴾. This matter needs investigation. His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and his Lord spoke to him﴾ is a statement indicating that speech took place from Allah to Moses. How could that happen, when He, glorified is He, has spoken in general terms about speech with respect to human beings: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals by His permission what He wills﴾ (Qur'an 42:51). In this there is a denial that Allah speaks to human beings, except through three means: revelation, or from behind a veil, or sending a messenger. Revelation for the prophets takes place by the meaning being cast into the heart of the Prophet all at once, with certain knowledge that it is from Allah, mighty and majestic. Revelation may also refer to inspirations, such as the revelation to the mother of Moses, the revelation to the disciples (al-hawariyyun), and likewise to the angels. It may also refer to revelation in the sense of subjection (taskhir), like the revelation to the earth and to the bee.

After that: "or from behind a veil" means that one hears speech without seeing the speaker. "Or by sending a messenger" is Gabriel, peace be upon him. The Qur'an was not sent down except in one way, through the descent of Gabriel upon our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Qur'an was not sent down by inspiration, nor was it sent down from behind a veil; rather it was sent down through a messenger from God, who is Gabriel, and he has signs.

As for the speech in the case of Moses, we say that the speech occurred from behind a veil, and here we refrain from delving into what lies beyond that, because it is an unseen matter that has not been revealed to us, and we leave the matter of it to God.

We have already said that the attributes of God have no counterpart among human beings. Human existence is not like the existence of God, and human independence is not like the independence of God; likewise, your speech will never be like the speech of God, because everything that belongs to God we take within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (Qur'an 42:11). Allah, the Exalted, has shown that His speech to Moses was distinctive to Moses, and for this reason the Truth says: ﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech﴾ (Qur'an 7:144).

We must take every attribute that exists in human beings, and for which a similar one exists, and in the description of God, such as "istawa" (He established Himself), "sat", "face", and "hand", we take all of that within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾.

﴿When Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You"﴾ (Qur'an 7:143). When Allah singled out Moses with the distinction that He spoke to him, there arose in Moses an aspiration of being chosen, as if he said to himself: since He has spoken to me, perhaps I may be able to see Him; for the sweetness of intimacy opens for the soul paths of hope in extending itself to things. Moses had said earlier, in answer to God's question: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?﴾ (Qur'an 20:17). The answer would have sufficed by saying "a staff," but he said: ﴿It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep﴾ (Qur'an 20:18). He said that although the Truth had not asked him: what do you do with it? He wanted by speech to prolong the intimacy with his Lord, as if he knew that it was not fitting for the answer to be a mere word in reply to a question. And by the Most High Similitude (wa-lillahi al-mathal al-a'la), we find that when one of us sees a small child, he plays with him and prolongs his speech with him to make him feel at ease. And when Moses found that God was speaking to him, his soul aspired to see Him: ﴿When Moses came at Our appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You"﴾.

Moses did not say: "Show me Your essence." Rather he said: ﴿Show me Yourself, that I may look upon You﴾, as if he knew that by his natural constitution he could not see God, but if God showed Himself to him, this is a matter of the will of the Truth. Moses made the request conditional upon God's will and His desire, because he knew that he was not prepared to receive the vision of God, since his constitution could not bear it. Even in revelation and speech, our Lord did not speak to people directly; rather He must choose messengers from among the angels, and then comes a second stage in which He chooses messengers from among human beings, and these messengers convey to people the speech of God, because the supreme perfect attributes that create cannot be comprehended by the created.

We have given the example earlier, and to God belongs the Highest Similitude, from the crafts of human beings: a person sleeps at night and may wake up for anything. If the world is in darkness, he may break things that are weaker than him, or things that are harder than him may break him; if he collides with a small object, he may break it, and if he collides with a wheel or a wall, the person may be broken. For this reason a person leaves in the house a little faint light, so that he may benefit from the stillness and darkness of the night, and he places what we call the "wanasa" (a night light), with the power of two candles or five candles, and he cannot connect it to the strength of the current in the house, because it would burn out immediately; therefore he brings for it a transformer that takes from the strong and gives to the weak.

So if human crafts show that the weak does not take from the strong except through an intermediary, then, a fortiori, the creation cannot receive from God except through an intermediary. Intermediation among human beings is by selection, and not everything is suitable for this matter: a chosen one from among the angels gives to a chosen one from among human beings.

After that, the chosen one from among human beings gives to human beings. Likewise is the vision, and this will become clear to us when God gives the evidence that He created you not in a form that would let you see Him now, but you will be raised in the Hereafter and prepared with a different preparation, and so it is possible for you to attain the honour of seeing Him:

﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ (Qur'an 75:22-23). People are not equal in this, because the believer is the one who attains the honour of looking upon God, whereas the unbeliever is veiled from seeing the Truth. The Exalted says concerning the disbelievers: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ (Qur'an 83:15). So the believer and the unbeliever are not equal in this state: as long as the unbeliever is veiled, the believer is not veiled and sees his Lord. Moses said: ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You﴾. The Truth said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾.

In the language, "lan" (never) comes for perpetuity, that is, it makes the future perpetually negated, so that what follows it does not happen and is not realized. Does this mean that the Truth's saying ﴿You will not see Me﴾ means that Moses will never see God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter? We say: who said that the time of the Hereafter is the time of this world? This has its time, and that has another time: ﴿On the day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ (Qur'an 14:48).

So the time of the Hereafter and the re-creation in it will be a different matter; it is enough that the people of Paradise will eat and will have no waste; it is a new creation. The "never" in the Truth's saying ﴿You will not see Me﴾ is limited in its perpetuity: that is, relative to this world, and within it is an explanation for Moses' inability to see God. The Exalted added: ﴿but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me. And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down unconscious﴾ (Qur'an 7:143). Here, glorified is He, explains to Moses by a concrete event, and makes it clear: "You will not see Me, but so that I may reassure you that you have been created in a form that does not enable you to see Me, look at the mountain." The mountain is by nature characterized by hardness, strength, firmness and solidity; so if it remains in its place, you may see Me. In reality, by reason and by logic, the mountain is stronger than a human being, harder and more solid than him. Yet when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, it was crushed. "Dakk" is the pressing of something from above until it is leveled with something below it. And the Truth is the One who said: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, pounded and pounded﴾ (Qur'an 89:21). Here, in the situation of Moses and his dialogue with God, it becomes clear to us that God manifested Himself to one of His creatures; but is the one upon whom He manifests able to bear this manifestation or not? If God enables him, he is able; but if God does not enable him, he will not be able. The mountain is the harder, so why did his Lord manifest Himself to it at that time? It is possible, then, that God may manifest Himself to some of His creatures, but the important question is: is the one who receives the manifestation strong enough, or not? The nature of Moses was not strong enough to bear the manifestation of God, as evidenced by the fact that one stronger than him was not strong enough. Then God wished to draw our attention in an ascending manner, and to show us that Moses was struck unconscious by seeing the One who manifested Himself to him. How then if he had seen the One who manifests Himself?! ﴿And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down unconscious﴾.

And it is said: "kharra al-sh"

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-A'raf (7), verse 144:

Al- istifa' (choosing and selecting) is the drawing out of the elite. His saying, ﴿I have chosen you above the people﴾, is an expression of precise delivery, because if He had said "I have chosen you" alone, without saying "above the people," the choosing might also be understood as above the angels. But the choosing here is specified within the sphere of human choosing:

﴿Indeed, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech﴾. Someone may say: God also chose others among the messengers, and God Himself said: ﴿Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah﴾ (Qur'an 3:33). We say: there is a difference between choosing for a single message and choosing with a message accompanied by something additional. Let me give this example, and to God belongs the highest comparison: if you come as a teacher to students and give one of them a gift in the form of a pen as a reward, then you give the second a pen and a bottle of ink, you have thereby chosen the first student with the gift of a pen, and chosen the other by combining a pen and a bottle of ink in one gift. The choosing here of Musa is by the message, as He chose other messengers, in addition to the honour of speech: ﴿Indeed, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech﴾.

We have already noted that "My messages" (risalatī) in its totality is one message. But the message with our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), continued in its parts being revealed over twenty-three years, so it is as if each star were a message, or each gate of goodness a message; so they are multiple messages, or his message gathered the messages of those before him. ﴿He said: O Musa, indeed I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful﴾ (7:144).

That is: do not look at what I have withheld from you, but remember that I have chosen you and spoken to you, and it is incumbent on you to thank Me for this. Therefore the believer, when he receives God's decree concerning himself, must always look at what remains to him of blessings, not at what has been taken from him of blessings. This is why we find the optimistic believer looking at the cup half full of water and saying: "Praise be to God, the cup is half full." As for the pessimist, he says: "The cup is half empty." Although each of them states a fact, the optimistic believer looked at what remains of God's blessings.

We find that Ibn Ja'far, when he went to the Umayyad caliph in Damascus, and his leg was wounded during the journey from Medina to Damascus, and there was no medical care, so it became infected; when they brought him doctors and they decided to amputate his leg, some of those present said: "Seek for him a sedative, a drug that makes him not feel the pain." He said: "No, for I do not want to be heedless of my Lord for the blink of an eye." When they amputated it, they took it to bury it, and he said: "Bring it to me." They brought it to him, he held it and said: "O God, if You have tested me in one limb, You have granted me well-being in other limbs."

This is the outlook of the believer who does not look at what has been taken from him, but looks at what remains to him. And thus was God's direction to Musa, peace be upon him: He made clear to him: do not look at the fact that I withheld the vision from you; no, rather look at the choosing and the honour of the speech with the Creator, and be grateful for that.

Almighty God says after that: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of every matter as admonition and clear explanation of all things. So take hold of them firmly and enjoin your people to take hold of the best of them. I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient.﴾ (7:145).

Al-kitb (writing) is recording with a pen on whatever is written upon, such as paper, skin, bone, or anything else. When our Lord says ﴿And We wrote﴾, God did not Himself practise the writing; rather His messengers from among the angels write by command of the Truth, who says: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have sent ahead﴾ (part of 36:12).

The writing of the angels of our deeds is by God's command, and the command is sometimes attributed to the highest (the Supreme), sometimes to the immediate agent, or to the intermediary: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of every matter as admonition and clear explanation﴾. We know tablets, and in earlier times they wrote on them. The reason for writing on tablets is that in earlier times they wrote on any flat surface. The traces show that there were books written on animal skins; for example, we find the ancient Egyptians wrote on stones, such as the Rosetta Stone, which enabled us to know their history. The Arabs used to write on the palm-rib (qahf) taken from the date palm, and likewise they wrote on the bones of slaughtered animals, taking from them the flat piece of bone like a board (lawh) and writing on it. This method was very well known among them, and everything written on such an object came to be called a lawh (tablet).

﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of every matter as admonition and clear explanation of all things﴾ (part of 7:145): God's words ﴿of every matter﴾ mean: of every matter that the human vicegerency (khilafa) on earth requires at its appropriate time. The messengers bring a creed, but a legislation suited to the period in which the messenger came may also come, and God adds to another messenger who comes after him, until Muhammad (ﷺ) came with the complete method until the Hour.

He, glory be to Him, has made clear that He wrote on the tablets the admonition and the explanation of the method of life.

Admonition (maw'iza) means that you do not create a ruling for the listener, but rather exhort him to carry out what he already knows. That is why one says "wa'iz" (preacher), who is one who does not create new matters, but knows that the listener knows the pillars of the religion and admonishes him with what he knows.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and a clear explanation of all things. So take hold of them firmly﴾, meaning that the speech did not come in summary, but comes in detail, and the Truth commands Moses to attend to the admonition and the details that are in the tablets with firmness. Why did the command come here that he should take them firmly? Because when a person is commanded something, the command may oppose the routine of what he is accustomed to, and when he is forbidden something, the prohibition may oppose the routine of what he is accustomed to. Thereby this prohibition or that command pulls the person away from what he is used to, and he takes it and moves him out of what he has become habituated to.

In this state, a person needs a strength of soul that overcomes the monotonous desire created by habit. Therefore, whoever wants to adhere to God's method must know that the method will take him out of what he is used to, and he must adhere to the method with strength and resolve to confront the habituation of the soul, because the soul's habit may say to him, "Do not do it," while the method says to him, "Do." So the believer must take up the obligations with strength, because the desires of the soul achieve the pleasures of the fleeting world, while the method gives a long-lasting enjoyment.

Desire may achieve for a person a pleasure proportionate to his capacity and readiness, but obligation gives the believer a benefit commensurate with the boundless capacity of God to benefit. So you must charge your soul with what God gives you of the method, and beware, at the moment you see the method demanding some effort from you, of saying: "These are difficult matters," for you are not alone in the method; rather, others are with you. If it tells you, "Do not steal," beware of saying, "Does the method restrict my freedom?" No, do not look at the prohibition and forbiddance of theft as a restriction of your freedom; rather it is a safeguarding of you from others transgressing against you.
