For the method has said to all people, "Do not steal from one another," and you are the gainer in this case. The Truth continues to explain what is in the tablets of values, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And enjoin your people to take hold of the best of them﴾. "Best" (ahsan) indicates that there is a lower rank than it, which is "good" (hasan). So the Truth commanded them to leave the good and take the best. We know that a person is among the changing things: if some calamity befalls him from someone, he regards that person as his creditor, and if a person has a creditor, the impulses of his soul move him to punish him with the same as what was done to him. This is what God permits in retaliation (qisas), but God asks the believer, if he is able over himself, to pardon. So punishment by retaliation or otherwise, as long as it is legislated by God, in the same measure as one was punished, this is the rank of the good; but if you leave the impulses of your soul and pardon, this is the rank of "the best." These gradations came because the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, created in man emotions and instincts important in the movement of life, but emotions cannot be controlled by man, so God does not legislate for emotion, but He, glory be to Him, legislates for instincts. How?

We know that "love of food" is an instinct, but the love of food must not reach the level of gluttony and voracity. Likewise, "the continuation of the species," or sexual pleasure, was created by the Truth for the sake of the continuation of the species. But it is not right that it turn into a degree of debauchery and falling into people's honour and violating their sanctity. Curiosity is an instinct, and those who made scientific discoveries did their work out of their curiosity about the secrets of existence. But it is not right and should not be that curiosity reach the level of degrading espionage.

Man has instincts that the Shari'a elevates; but love is a matter of emotion. The Legislator says to you: love whom you wish and hate whom you wish, but do not wrong the one you hate, and do not wrong people for the sake of the one you love.

And in the Messenger of God we have a good example when he said: "None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his self, his child, his father, and all people" (1), and 'Umar said: "How?" And the Messenger of God repeated it, and 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, knew by his nature that this is a matter of obligation (taklif). And he understood that the love intended is rational love. So the believer says to himself: who am I without the Messenger of God (ﷺ)? Every believer loves the Messenger of God with rational love, and it may ascend until it becomes emotional love. And a person among us, as we said earlier, loves medicine with his reason, not his emotion, because it is bitter, but he becomes angry if the medicine disappears from the markets and rejoices at whoever brings it.

So obligation requires rational love. Among the reports about our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: when the killer of his brother Zayd ibn al-Khattab passed before him, 'Umar said to him, "Turn yourself away from me, for I do not love you." The man replied with complete faithful boldness: "Does your not loving me prevent me from a right of mine?" 'Umar said: "No." The man said: "Only women weep out of love."

And the Truth says here: ﴿take hold of the best of them﴾. For example, when a person is killed, the blood-avenger has the right to retaliate, but the Truth softens the heart of the blood-avenger toward the killer, saying: ﴿But if the killer is pardoned by his brother in any way, then pursuit should be made according to what is reasonable﴾ (part of 2:178).

When the Truth calls the killer a brother, He calms the conflict of emotions and reduces the desire for vengeance. He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ (42:43), and we find Him, glory be to Him, affirming that such a matter is "of the matters requiring resolve," because it is a matter that requires patience and forgiveness. Since the believer has been able to be patient and forgive an opponent, will he not be patient when a calamity falls upon him without an opponent, such as a sudden illness or the loss of a beloved? Who, then, is your opponent in the illness? And with whom are you angry, and against whom do you rage, and where does your agitation go? Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says to you: ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you﴾, that is, over what you have no opponent in, and He, glory be to Him, makes clear to you: ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾. We notice that here the Truth emphasises with "la-" (the emphatic lam), but He emphasised the other with "la-" too, because you have an opponent who stirs you up the moment you see him. And in the verse which is the subject of our reflections, the Truth says to Moses: ﴿and enjoin your people to take hold of the best of them﴾.

That is, if you find for them a means, a way, and a cause toward something, and there exists what is better, then command them to take the best. Why? Because when a person disciplines his soul, tames it, and accustoms it to the best, he has understood God. Suppose someone wronged you and you could wrong him back; in your response to the wrong you must take care that it be in proportion to it, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿So punish with the same as that with which you were punished﴾ (part of 16:126).

But who among us is characterised by precision in psychological balances, so as to be able to know equivalence by desire? If someone slapped you and you want to return the slap, from where will you be able to measure the amount of pain in your slap? You cannot determine this amount of pain, because this is a matter proportionate to strength. So why do you enter yourself into labyrinths, and why do you not pardon and the matter ends?

When the Truth guides you that pardon is better, He intends thereby to end the savagery of souls and the rancour of hearts. When a person kills another person, there will be retaliation and blood-price, but if the blood-avenger pardons, the life of the pardoned becomes a gift from the blood-avenger, so the killer then becomes ashamed to make any movement of this life against the blood-avenger or against anyone attributed to the blood-avenger, and then any rancour or desire for vengeance ends. Therefore we find that in lands where blood-feuds occur and the custom of seeking vengeance spreads, such as Upper Egypt (Sa'id Misr), when the killer takes his shroud in his hand and enters upon the blood-avenger and says: "I have come to you...", the blood-avenger pardons him, and the whole family understands that the life of the one sought for vengeance has become a gift from the blood-avenger, and the feuds are cleared and end. Therefore the command came from the Truth to take the best: ﴿and enjoin your people to take hold of the best of them﴾. Another example of taking the best: we may find a debtor unable to repay the debt; here the Truth says: ﴿then [let there be] postponement until a time of ease﴾ (part of 2:280). The man borrowed because he was in need, since a loan is only given out of need, unlike a request which may be made out of need or not out of need. For this reason the reward of lending is greater than the reward of charity, because the borrower borrows only out of need, and because the one who gives charity, when he gives some of his wealth, has removed this wealth from himself and is no longer attached to it. But a loan attaches the soul, so whenever the lender is patient while his soul is attached to his wealth, he takes a reward, and thus lending is better than charity.

Therefore there is the good (hasan) and there is the better (ahsan): the good is that you take your lawful right, and the better is that you relinquish it. Those who relinquish it are those who understand God with a broad understanding. For us there is the example and the model in our master al-Hasan al-Basri, may God be pleased with him, who did good to one who wronged him, and said his word: "Shall we not do good to one whom God has placed on our side?" I always give this example, and to God belongs the highest example: suppose a man has children and one of them wrongs another. The father's heart goes with the one who was wronged, and likewise with us, God's creatures. If one of God's creatures wrongs another of God's creatures, we find the Lord of creation with the one who was wronged, and the one who was wronged should say: "This person who wronged me has put our Lord on my side, and therefore he deserves that I do good to him." Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it﴾ (part of 39:18), and in another verse the Truth says: ﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ (part of 39:55).

The Truth concludes the verse which is the subject of our reflections with His saying: ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient.﴾

---
(1) Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 146:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ (7:146)

The word āyāt (signs) is the plural of āyah, which means a wondrous matter. It is used in three ways. It may be a cosmic sign (āyah kawniyyah), such as the Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾ It may be a sign that testifies to the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying the message. And it may be a Qur'anic verse (āyah qur'āniyyah) containing one of God's rulings. Here the Truth says: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right﴾ (part of 7:146). So, here Glorified God makes clear that He will turn away those who are arrogant on earth without right from looking with contemplation at the signs of the cosmos. Or it means that the scheme of those who are arrogant on earth without right will be nullified in its attempt to turn toward the truth by demolishing it, because each one of these, at the moment he sees a sign of God's signs, will regard it as sorcery or magic, or will say that it is among the fables of the ancients.

Thus the manner of turning away is that the Truth imposes upon him such arrogance that makes him unable to weigh the sign on its correct scale. The arrogant person is one who thinks that others are lower than him and of lesser rank. The constituents of arrogance may be strength, but has the arrogant person not seen a strong man who became weak? Wealth may also be a constituent of arrogance, but has the arrogant person not seen a rich man who became poor? Or the arrogant person may be one of high standing; has he not seen a person of standing who became humiliated?

Thus whoever is arrogant must be arrogant with something intrinsic that is never taken from him. If you want to apply this to human beings, you will not find anyone deserving to be arrogant at all, because there is no intrinsic property in man that accompanies him and never leaves him; rather, all of them are bestowed, and they are among the changing things that occur and may pass away. All of them are from God, and they are not intrinsic matters. For if strength in you were intrinsic, then preserve it, and you will not be able. If wealth were intrinsic, then preserve your riches forever, and you will not be able. If honour were intrinsic, then preserve your honour forever, and you will not be able. Thus the constituents of pride in human beings are not intrinsic.

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿who are arrogant on earth without right﴾ indicates that there is a rightful pride for the one who possesses in his very essence all the elements of strength, wealth, standing and honour; and therefore pride belongs to God alone. Know that every arrogant person on earth does not bring God to mind, because if God with His perfection and majesty came to his mind, he would shrink; for God comes to mind only of the humble among people. So we strike this example: we find around us a person who is the supreme head, and there is one who is head of a group and subordinate to another, and there is one who is only a subordinate. The subordinate head cannot sit with his subordinates in arrogance, placing one leg over the other and giving orders, because he may turn and find his superior has entered upon him. If the subordinate head did that, his subordinates would laugh at him. Likewise, people who do not bring God to mind are found to be objects of mockery; but those who bring to mind God, to whom belongs pride in the heavens and the earth, never become arrogant.

Indeed, He, glorified be He, turns away from the arrogant the contemplation of cosmic signs, so they do not take heed; He turns away from them the affirmation of the signs that indicate the prophethood of the prophets; He turns away from them the capacity to affirm the rulings of the Qur'an; and He seals their hearts, so that what is within these hearts of disbelief does not come out, and what is outside these hearts of faith does not enter. And despite their movement in life, the Truth renders them incapable of seeing His signs in the cosmos. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way﴾ (part of 7:146). When the people of arrogance see a cosmic sign, or a miraculous sign, or verses of rulings, they do not believe in them; and when they see the way of guidance, they do not take it as a way, because the way of guidance presses upon the desires and passions of the soul, forbidding evil deeds, and they cannot restrain the rush of their desires because these have taken hold of them. But the way of error gives free rein to the desires of the soul, and this is only the case when one has become heedless of the givens of faith, which deprives one of something in order to give him things more precious. Thus the outlook of the people of arrogance is superficial. We note that the word sabīl (way) comes once as masculine, as in His saying: ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾, and once as feminine, as the Truth says: ﴿Say: this is my way﴾.

Here the Truth says concerning those who follow the way of error among the people of arrogance: ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ We have said long ago that heedlessness does not necessitate punishment for it, because the heedless one is forgetful and inattentive; but these turned away from the matter with deliberate intellectual aversion, to the degree that they give faith no attention whatsoever.

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have failed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾

The word "signs" (āyāt) has come here more than once. Allah says: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it.﴾ He also says: ﴿That is because they denied Our signs.﴾ And He says: ﴿And those who denied Our signs.﴾

So the whole matter revolves around three kinds of signs: the cosmic signs, by which one reasons to the One who brought them into being; the miraculous signs, by which one establishes the truthfulness of the one sent as a messenger; and the Qur'anic signs, by which one takes God's method for straightening and balancing the movement of man.

﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have failed﴾ (part of verse 147, Surah al-A'raf). It is said: "habita al-shay'" means the thing swelled and became puffed up from an ailment or disease. That is, outwardly it appears to them that they have done good deeds, but in reality these deeds are vain and corrupt. There may be someone who does a good deed beneficial to people, but it is not in his mind to do it seeking God's pleasure; rather, for fame, so that his name spreads, his renown circulates and people praise him, or for status, position and influence. This is why, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who is the martyr?", he said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah" (1), because a man may fight out of zealotry, or so that people will know, for example, that he is brave. So there is one who does an action in order to boast of it. It is said, for example: "The disbelievers are the ones who discovered the microbe and went up into space." We say: yes, they took the appreciation of people, because people were in their minds, and they will not take appreciation from Allah, because they did their deeds and Allah was not in their minds. A person takes his wage from the one for whom he worked, and Allah, glorified and exalted, will not waste the reward of their good deeds; rather He gave them their wages in this world, but the tilth of the Hereafter is not for them.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it﴾ (part of verse 20, Surah al-Shura). One who sows, chooses the seeds well, chooses the soil well, and waters according to a system, the crop brings him fruit, because he has taken the causes. This is called the bounty of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ al-rubūbiyya), and it is a general bounty for all whom Allah created, whether believer or disbeliever, disobedient or obedient. But the bounty of divinity (ʿaṭāʾ al-ulūhiyya) comes through following the method with "do and do not," and this is specific to the believers. So when they make good use of the causes of life within the cosmic laws, they take their share of them, and the disbelievers also take their share of them when they make good use of the causes; this is achieved through perpetuating their memory, erecting statues for them, receiving rewards and prizes, and honoring ceremonies. As for the reward of the Hereafter, it is taken by the one who acted for the Lord of the Hereafter. As for those who did not act for the sake of meeting Allah, He, glorified be He, says concerning them: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (verse 23, Surah al-Furqan). And likewise He says: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water﴾ (part of verse 39, Surah al-Nur).

The disbelievers are like the thirsty one who walks in a desert and imagines that ahead of him there is water; he keeps walking and walking, but finds no water. As for one who is not thirsty, it does not matter to him whether there is water or not; but the thirsty one, at the moment he sees the mirage, deceives himself that the water is coming and that he will obtain it. ﴿Like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ (part of verse 39, Surah al-Nur).

What matters is not merely that he finds nothing. Rather he is surprised: ﴿and finds Allah with him﴾. He is surprised that the God whom he did not believe existed is found before him on the Day of Resurrection, so He settles his account and recompenses him for his ugly deed. So whoever does a deed should await the reward from the One for whom he did it, and whoever does a deed without Allah in mind should not expect a reward from Him; yet despite that, He gives those people their reward under the law of the natural order of life, because whoever does good takes his recompense for it. ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have failed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). They therefore denied the signs of Allah and denied the Last Day, and did not act according to the method of faith, so they have a recompense and punishment from the Truth who sent down this method; but they turned away from it and denied it.

For this reason He, glorified be He, says: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort has gone astray in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well in works﴾ (verses 103–104, Surah al-Kahf).

1 Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 148:

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And the people of Moses, after him, took from their ornaments a calf, a body with a lowing sound. Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾

His words ﴿after him﴾ mean: after his departure to the appointed time with his Lord, after he had said to Aaron ﴿Take my place among my people﴾.

After that, the people of Moses took from their ornaments a calf, a body with a lowing sound. We know that ornaments (hilyah) are what one adorns oneself with of gold, jewels and precious things, and the chief of these ornaments is always gold. We know that a skilled goldsmith shapes gold as he wishes, and if it breaks it is easy to repair; and gold breaks slowly. For this reason it is said: gold is like a good person, its breaking is slow and its mending is easy.

When we hear the word "adornment" (zinah), diamonds, emeralds and rubies may enter into it, but gold is the chief of these ornaments. We know that however far the world advances, the reserve behind its wealth will be nothing but gold. For this reason the Glorified did not mention rubies, jewels or diamonds. Therefore, when the word "ornaments" (hilyah) is used alone, what is meant by it is gold.

It was this adornment from which Moses' Samaritan (al-Samiri) fashioned the image of the calf. Naturally he took the golden ornaments, because diamonds and jewels cannot be melted. But where did the people of Moses get the ornaments, when they had been oppressed and humiliated? They had tricked the people of Egypt and took the ornaments from them as a loan that they would return afterwards. Then their departure came, and they took the ornaments with them.

The people of Pharaoh drowned, and the ornaments remained with the people of Moses. Al-Samiri made a calf from the gold of these ornaments. The calf (ʿijl) is the male of the young of the cow. When you hear His words ﴿a calf, a body﴾, it means that it had a definite form, a clear bulk. The exegetes took from the word "body" (jasad) that this calf was a body without a soul, just as we say: "So-and-so is merely a corpse (juthah)", meaning as if he were a corpse without a spirit.

His word, the Truth: ﴿a calf, a body with a lowing sound﴾ indicates that the bodily form of the calf had no life, because if it had been a body with a spirit, there would have been no need to say "a calf, a body with a lowing sound"; it would have sufficed to say "a calf." But His words ﴿with a lowing sound﴾ are evidence that corporeality in the calf does not give it life. The description in His words ﴿with a lowing sound﴾ comes, and lowing (khuwar) is the voice of the cow. He made it of gold, as if he wanted it to be distinguished from the idols that were of stone, and he tried to make it a precious god. He made it, as we know, from the stolen ornaments, and he made it in such a way that when this bodily calf received the blowing of wind from its rear, a sound was produced and generated in its hollow, resembling the lowing of a cow coming out of its mouth. We see this matter in the flute (nay), which is a tube of reed of the kind called local cane (al-ghab al-baladi), in which holes are made, and the player plays upon it to bring out the note he wants.

When al-Samiri made the calf by this trick, this sound occurred, resembling the lowing of a cow. The story of this calf comes clearly in Surah Ta-Ha, and we shall address it when we address Surah Ta-Ha with our faith-inspired reflections, God willing. ﴿A calf, a body with a lowing sound. Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾ (Part of verse 148, Surah al-A'raf). Why did al-Samiri choose the calf? Because when they left Egypt, they saw the ancient Egyptians worshipping the calf for a quality in it; they saw in it a manifestation of strength, just as others worshipped the sun when they saw in it a manifestation of strength, and likewise those who worshipped the moon and the stars. The ancient Egyptians worshipped the calf because the flooding of the Nile covered the land with water, and they used the calf when they wanted to plough the land. It was ʾayyid, that is, strong and powerful in ploughing the land, and this is one of the manifestations of strength. But how did the people of Moses, after him, take a calf to worship after God had bestowed upon them the great favour of rescuing them and drowning Pharaoh and his household? Here God made clear to us that He had brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they passed by a people who worshipped idols, and they said to Moses, peace be upon him: "Make for us a god just as they have gods."

The Truth says: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾ (Part of verse 148, Surah al-A'raf). This is a matter that demolishes every worship other than the worship of God, because the servant must receive commands from the one worshipped, and the worshipped must have a method which he wants the servant to carry out, and the method must come through messengers who convey the messages of God and His word to mankind. As for those who worship the sun, for example, we ask them: Why do you worship it? And what method has the sun sent to you? Worship is the servant's obedience to the one worshipped in "do" and "do not do." Has the sun said to you "do" and "do not do"? No, because there is no verbal intermediary that tells you the method. And how then can there be a worshipped one without a method for the worshipper? Has it said: whoever worships me, I will shine upon him and give him light and heat, and whoever does not worship me, I will give him none of that? The sun has said no such thing; it gives to those who believe in it and to those who disbelieve, and it has not sent news of the Hereafter and the Resurrection.

Thus every worship of other than God is refuted before us, in that worship entails a command and a prohibition, in "do" and "do not do," and none of these so-called worshipped ones said what we should obey and what we should disobey. The essence of the worshipped is that he guides the worshipper to the path that leads to his good in this world and in the Hereafter. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾ And ﴿they were wrongdoers﴾ because they gave a right to one who had no right, whereas the Truth, glory be to Him, is the highest summit of truth; therefore He said concerning associating partners with Him: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a tremendous wrong.﴾

And the Almighty says after that: ﴿And when they were seized with remorse, and saw that they had gone astray, they said: "If our Lord has not mercy upon us and forgive us, we shall certainly be among the losers."﴾ (7:149)

This makes clear to us that the worship of the calf found a following among the people of Moses. But those among them who had some measure of insight, or a remnant of faith, said: "This story is foolish, and it was not for us to do such a thing," and they regretted what had happened. It is said: "suqita fi yadihi" (he was seized with remorse; literally, it fell into his hands). This is one of the natural, innate indications in which no nation differs from another; rather it exists in all races and in every language, pointing to the fact that when a person does an act and the opposite of what he intended happens to him, he bites his fingertips out of remorse and grief. This is one of the innate signs that remain with us from the natural common ground of human expression, found in all races. A person bites his fingertips because he has done something he should not have done; if the matter is grave, he does not content himself with a fingertip but bites his whole hand. And the Almighty says: ﴿And on the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands﴾ (25:27).

"And they were seized with remorse" means: their teeth came down upon their hands, as though the remorse had reached its height. This occurred among the repentant who saw with their own eyes and realized that this was falsehood and loss. That is, they said: "If God does not reach us with His mercy and forgiveness, we shall certainly be among the ruined." This is their acknowledgment of their sin and their turning to Almighty God.

And the Truth (Allah) says after that: ﴿When Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, "Evil is what you did after me in my absence. Did you outstrip the command of your Lord?" And he threw down the Tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me among the wrongdoing people."﴾ (7:150).

Moses' returning to his people in a state of being angry and grieved shows us that he had learned the news of the calf. Anger and grief are psychological processes that contain sadness, and they are called "the psychological sensations" (al-mawājīd al-nafsiyya), meaning the thing a person finds within himself. These sensations may be expressed through impulsive reactions. For this reason you find a difference between one who grieves and keeps it inside himself, and one who gets angry. The one who gets angry has his veins swell, his face reddens, his agitation continues, his eyes flash with ill will, and his hands lash out; this is what is called "angry" (ghaḍbān). Moses went through both states, and anger was mentioned first because it is the messenger that carries its own method. In such a matter grief alone is not enough; there must be anger as a result of the agitation of the limbs.

We have said in the past that every conscious perception has three stages. The first stage is the cognitive stage (idrākiyya). Then comes the stage of feeling within the soul (wijdāniyya). Then comes the stage of impulsive movement (nuzūʿiyya bi-l-ḥaraka). We gave the example of the rose for this. Whoever sees the rose has perceived it. He may admire it, be pleased with its shape, feel at ease with it and find rest in it; this is feeling. But whoever stretches out his hand to pluck it has moved into impulsive action. Legislation did not regulate perception or feeling, but it did regulate behavior, except for lowering the gaze from what God has forbidden, out of regard for the sanctity of honor.

Moses' grief will not appear toward those who oppose the method. Rather anger appears, which is an impulsive process. We note that he uses the word ʾasif, which is an intensive form. There is a difference between ʾasif and āsif: āsif is slightly mild, but ʾasif is an intensive form, indicating that grief had grown strong upon him and taken hold of him. ﴿He said, "Evil is what you did after me in my absence. Did you outstrip the command of your Lord?"﴾ (part of 7:150).

As for His words, glorified is He, ﴿Did you outstrip the command of your Lord?﴾, meaning: did you consider me slow in returning? This resulted from Moses having gone for thirty nights and completed them with ten. So Moses asked: did you think I would not come, or that I had been slow to return to you? And did you believe and have faith for my sake, or for the sake of a capable God? For this reason our master Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed to the Highest Companion: "Whoever used to worship Muhammad, Muhammad has died; but whoever used to worship Allah, Allah is living and does not die." Here our master Moses says: suppose you hastened the matter, considered me slow, or feared that I had died. Would you have worshipped me, or worshipped our Lord? ﴿Did you outstrip the command of your Lord?﴾ And he threw down the Tablets, and we know that the Tablets contained the method. Moses then seized his brother ﴿by the head, dragging him toward him﴾, and this is the "angry impulse" that made him take his brother by the head, as though brotherhood here had no benefit. So what was Aaron's reply?

﴿He said, "O son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me among the wrongdoing people."﴾ (part of 7:150). We note that he said "son of my mother" and did not say "son of my father", because the father of Moses and Aaron is passed over in the history of the prophets and no report about him has appeared. The knowledge of them came to us through their mother, because she was the one who faced hardships in the affairs of their lives. Therefore he came here with the common element most prominent in their lives, and because motherhood is the place of the wombs. For this reason you find brothers from the mother, brothers from the father only, and brothers from both father and mother, and the situation of full brothers is well known. But among maternal brothers we find evident tenderness, while tenderness diminishes among paternal brothers. The Truth here uses the element common to them both, Moses and Aaron, which is being maternal brothers, and it has a present presence in their history. As for the father, Imran, we know nothing about him, and all the verses that came about Moses relate to his mother. Thus we find his brother Aaron speaking to him in the manner that softens him: ﴿He said, "O son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me."﴾ Since he said ﴿and nearly killed me﴾, this is evidence that he stood against them in the position of opposition and resistance, fulfilling what was incumbent upon him to the point that they planned to kill him. The Truth continues in Aaron's tongue: ﴿so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me among the wrongdoing people.﴾

Shamatah is showing joy at a calamity befalling an opponent. The enemies are the people who took the calf, and he described them as enemies as evidence that he stood against them in hostility, and that the disagreement between Moses and Aaron would delight them. As for His words ﴿and seized his brother by the head﴾, it is a general reference to the head in its entirety; and in another verse He says: ﴿Do not seize my beard nor my head.﴾ (20:94).

Moses did this so that he would hear the excuse from Aaron, because he knew that Aaron was a messenger like himself, and he wanted to let us and the world hear his brother's argument when he made clear that he had not fallen short. He said: the people deemed me weak because I was alone, and they nearly killed me. This shows that he resisted them with a resistance that reached the utmost limit of human capacity in life, to the point that they nearly killed him. Thus he had not agreed with them on anything, but he resisted to the extent of human ability. Therefore the Truth concludes the verse with His words, glorified is He: ﴿and do not place me among the wrongdoing people.﴾

It is as though he is saying to Moses: if you take me to account in this manner in your state of anger, perhaps it will be thought of me that I was with them, or followed their course in making the calf and worshipping it. Allah, glorified is He, wanted to show us the position of Moses and the position of his brother. Moses's position appeared when he was angry with his brother and son of his mother, and Aaron's position explained the cause for which the people deemed him weak and nearly killed him, and nothing more could be required of him. When Aaron said that, Moses was alerted to two matters. The first: how could he throw down the Tablets when they contained the method? The second: how could he seize his brother in this way before the truth of the matter had become clear to him?

The Truth then says on his tongue: ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ (7:151).

Moses said: "My Lord, forgive me, and my brother Aaron, if anything has come from me that departs from the standard of right and truth. And forgive my brother for what he did, for it was incumbent upon him to take up the fight against those who worshipped the calf, until he either repelled them or inflicted upon them some harm, even short of killing—a wound, a scratch, or... or... etc."

Moses asks for mercy for himself and for his brother: ﴿And admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ (part of verse 151, Surah [al-A'raf]).

When you hear ﴿the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, or ﴿the best of providers﴾, or ﴿the best of inheritors﴾, or ﴿the best of creators﴾, and every such plural form, these are descriptions of Allah. In this too He calls His creation to take on this character, and His creation is described by it. Know that Allah has not deprived them of being described by these attributes, because they have a share in them, though it is limited and proportionate to their power, their createdness, and their servanthood—over and above the fact that it is a gift and a bestowal from Him, glory be to Him. As for the attributes of Allah, they are unlimited and boundless in majesty, perfection, and beauty. Glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. So if Allah is ﴿the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, this means that He, glory be to Him, has not withheld mercy from His creation toward His creation; whoever shows mercy to his brother is called merciful (raheem) and one who shows mercy (raahim), but Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful. This is because the mercy of every human being is a guarantee against the manifestation of anger in this one: it is said, "I had mercy on so-and-so," meaning, "I held back your anger against him and your punishment," and your punishment is in proportion to your strength; but when Allah wants to take one person for a sin, His strength has no end, and likewise His mercy has no end.

Almighty Allah says after that: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will be overtaken by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world. And thus do We recompense the fabricators.﴾

When it is said ﴿took the calf﴾, one may ask: did they take it slaughtered to eat, or to plough the earth, or to water the crops and turn the waterwheels? For the calf is suitable for these tasks, but they did not take the calf for those tasks. Rather, they took the calf as a god and an object of worship. As for taking it for what it was created for, there is no objection to it. Here the object is omitted and left to the discernment of the listener. So if we take the calf for what the calf was created for, anger from Allah does not befall us. Those who will be overtaken by the anger of Allah are those who took the calf for other than what it was created for; they took it as a god: ﴿will be overtaken by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world﴾.

His saying ﴿will be overtaken﴾ indicates that the time of the anger and humiliation has not yet come and will occur in the future. The future of this world is the Hereafter. Yet here the Truth says that humiliation will occur in this world. How then will ﴿will be overtaken by anger﴾ apply, when they repented? He, glorified is He, clarifies this for us in His saying: ﴿So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator, and He accepted your repentance﴾.

Some of them repented to their Creator and killed themselves, so why then the anger? The Truth explains to us that the anger which befell them is what compelled them to be told, "Kill yourselves." Thus we understand that His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿will be overtaken by anger﴾ means before they repent. And killing oneself is the peak of pleasure and the peak of humiliation.

﴿will be overtaken by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world. And thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾ (part of verse 152, Surah al-A'raf): that is, this matter is not specific to them. Every fabricator who transgresses his limit beyond what Allah has prescribed must receive this recompense, because when our Lord tells us what happened in their history, and when He narrates this story to us, He, glorified is He, intends through that that the listener to the story should take a lesson within himself. The listener's taking a lesson within himself is achieved only when Allah says to him, as a warning and admonition: ﴿And thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾, meaning: beware of being like these people, lest there befall you what befell them. He, glorified is He, alerts each of us so that he may benefit from this lesson and this episode, for history is related in order to draw a lesson, and an admonition so that the listener may be admonished by it.

And the Truth (Allah) says afterwards: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed — indeed your Lord, after them, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (7:153).

This is what happened. After they took the calf, and He said to them: "Kill yourselves in repentance to your Creator (bari')," then they repented, returned to Allah, and believed in what had come to them, and Allah forgave them. And if the Truth has related to us the manifestation of His majesty (jabbariyyah), He has also not willed to leave us in the manifestation of tyranny (al-jabbariyyah), and He wished to bring us into the tenderness of His Compassion (al-Rahmaniyyah). Therefore He says here: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed — indeed your Lord, after them, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf). His saying "then repented" means they regretted what they had done, resolved, and determined not to return to it. We know beforehand that repentance (tawbah) has three manifestations: first, the manifestation of legislation (tashri'); second, the manifestation of the act of the penitent; and third, the acceptance by Allah of repentance from the penitent. The legitimacy of repentance itself contains absolute mercy. Had our Lord not legislated repentance in itself, all creation would have been exhausted, because everyone who committed a sin for whom Allah had not legislated repentance would be bound to continue in evil deeds. But when our Lord legislates repentance for the one who has done wrong, and calls the servant to refrain from the sin, this is mercy toward the sinner and toward the society in which the sinner lives. After that the servant repents, and then there is another manifestation of the Truth, which is that He accepts his repentance.

Repentance, then, has legislation from Allah, and that is mercy; and an act by the servant in that he repents, and that is the response; and acceptance from Allah, and that is the peak of His giving and mercy, glory be to Him.

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed﴾ (part of verse 153 of Surat al-A'raf). This statement indicates that committing an evil deed damages faith, so He, glory be to Him, commands His servant: renew your faith, and bring your Lord to mind with a receptive remembrance, because your evil deed shows that you have become heedless of the Truth in His commands and prohibitions; and when you repent, you renew your faith and find your Lord Forgiving and Merciful: ﴿indeed your Lord, after them, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

The sin of the servant occurs in what opposes the method of his Lord regarding "do" and "do not do," and as long as the servant has sought forgiveness from Allah and repented, He, glory be to Him, accepts repentance. He clarifies: if I am Forgiving and Merciful, then beware, O my creatures, of reminding a sinner after he has repented, because the one with authority has forgiven. So beware of saying to a repentant thief, "O thief," and beware of saying to a repentant adulterer, "O adulterer," and beware of saying to a repentant briber, "O briber," because the sinner, as long as he has renewed his repentance and believed, and Allah has forgiven him, then do not be a parasite who brings his sin back to him afresh.

Then the Truth says, after that: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.﴾ (154)

Can anger have subsiding? Can anger have feelings so that it can subside? Yes; because anger is the agitation of the soul, moving it to act impulsively against the one who has wronged, so it is as if anger insists upon him and says to the angry person: strike, revile, kill. It is as if anger were depicted and portrayed in the form of a person who has the power to issue commands, so God likened anger to the image of a human being who insists on Moses to do this and do that. When God said that, it was as if anger had subsided from him.

Or it is as our scholarly brethren have said: it is an inversion (qalb, "transposition") in the language, meaning that it reverses the matter, relying on the listener's intelligence to return everything to its origin. As we hear in the language: "the cloth tore the nail" (kharaqa al-thawbu al-mismāra). We understand from this statement that the nail was what tore the cloth, because we would not imagine that a cloth tears a nail. This is called "qalb" (inversion), meaning that one brings a reversed matter which the listener's intelligence understands. Or the nail remains fixed in its place, and the cloth is what came upon it and tore, so the cause of the tear lies in the cloth; thus the true agent is the cloth: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses﴾. Or the word "subsided" (sakata) may be a metaphor (kināya) for the anger having ceased and ended. ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

The first act Moses performed when he was angry and grieved was that he threw down the tablets; and as soon as the anger left him and departed from him, he took up the tablets. This is a logical matter: anger caused him to throw the tablets and to seize his brother by the head. Then he understood what his brother had done and accepted his excuse, and he asked God to forgive him and his brother; the anger ended, and the tablets had been lying down, so he took them up again.

﴿And in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord﴾ (part of verse 154 of Surah al-A'raf): The "nuskha" (copy) of a book is derived from "the thing copied," that is, transferred from one place to another; it is said: "I copied such-and-such book from such-and-such book." That is, there is a manuscript which we then transferred by printing or writing into a copy or a number of copies; I took it from the original into a form, and its name is "mansūkh" (copied). The word "nuskha," on the pattern "fu'la," comes in the sense of "maf'ūla" (the thing done), so "nuskha" means "mansūkha" (copied), and the Qur'an contains many such examples. The Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, God will test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who scoops a scoopful with his hand﴾ (part of verse 249 of Surah al-Baqarah). And "ghurfa" (scoopful) means "maghrūfa" (scooped), namely the small amount of water in the hand to moisten the mouth only; and "ghurfa" also means a room in houses, because it is a place cut off from another place and has walls that define it, and it is called "ghurfa" because it is scooped from the space into a specific enclosure. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And in their inscription was guidance and mercy﴾.

And "guidance" (hudā) here means the method that leads to the goal in "do" and "do not do." It leads to the goal, which is the reward of the Hereafter. Thus guidance and mercy are one thing with two sides: guidance is the method which, if you follow it, you reach mercy; therefore the Truth says: ﴿guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord﴾.

Thus we find the method to be guidance and mercy: whoever hears the words of God, follows them, and is guided, our Lord will have mercy on him, because he has placed God in his mind and feared the attributes of might (al-jabbāriyya) of the Truth. Therefore a person or believer must keep in mind his awe of his Lord and his fear of Him, glory be to Him, so that the method may be guidance and mercy for him, and he may be among those who fear their Lord.

When you see the object (maf'ūl) placed first, as in His words here: ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾ (part of verse 154 of Surah al-A'raf), we understand that this is what is called in the language "ikhtiṣāṣ" (restriction/exclusivity) and "qaṣr" (limitation), just as the Truth said in the Opening of the Book: ﴿You alone do we worship﴾.

What is the difference between ﴿You alone do we worship﴾ and "we worship You"? If we say "na'buduka" (we worship You), it is a statement that does not prevent conjoining others with it, for we may worship You and worship partners alongside You; but our saying ﴿iyyāka na'bud﴾ means we have specified You for worship and restricted it to You, glory be to You, so it does not extend to other than You.

Thus, when you place the object first, this is the function of ikhtiṣāṣ. An example from our life: when we say "I honoured you" (akramtuka), there is no objection to then saying "and I honoured Zayd and I honoured 'Amr." But if you say: "iyyāka akramt" (it is you I honoured), this means I honoured none but you. Here the Truth says: ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾. Someone might say: could not someone claim outward fear and obedience to God's command out of show or reputation, so that people say "so-and-so has good Islam," and praise him? But here we find the specification which indicates that the servant fears none but God, that fear is sincerely for God, and is not show, nor reputation, nor for the purpose of praise.

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 155:

The Truthful, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. So when the earthquake seized them, he said: "My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? This is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of those who forgive."﴾ (155)

The word "chose" (ikhtar) indicates that in a voluntary act the intellect actually favours one thing over not doing it or over doing something else. Otherwise there is no choosing in the matter, because ikhtar means to seek what is good and to select. It was within your power to take something other than it. This applies only to voluntary matters, which are the basis of moral responsibility (taklif). For example, the tongue is subject to its owner's will. It submits to the believer when he says, "There is no god but God," and it submits to the atheist when he says, may God curse him, "There is no existence of God." The tongue has not disobeyed in either case. What prefers one matter over another is the believer's preference for faith when he says, "There is no god but God," and the atheist's preference for unbelief when he says the opposite. Here the Truth says: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men﴾.

Those who studied the language say that there is an action (hadath), and that there is an existent doer of the action, which we call the subject (fa'il), as in our saying: "Zayd wrote the lesson," meaning that Zayd is the one who performed the writing. We call "the lesson," upon which the writing fell, the direct object (maf'ul bih). Sometimes there is what we call the object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), or the object for the sake of (maf'ul li-ajlih), as in the son's saying: "I stood up for my father out of reverence (ijlal)." The one who stood is the son, and the reverence was the cause for performing the act, so we call it the object of purpose. We say: "I fasted on such a day," and we call that the object of time (maf'ul fihi), because the act occurred in this time. Thus sometimes the action falls upon a thing and it is a direct object; sometimes it occurs for such-and-such a reason and it is an object of purpose; sometimes it occurs on such-and-such a day, the afternoon or the noon, and it is an object of time. And sometimes it is the object of accompaniment (maf'ul ma'h), as in our saying: "I walked with the Nile (wa-l-nil)," meaning that the person walked alongside the Nile, and whenever he walked he found the Nile at his side.

Here the Truth says: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf). Since Moses' choosing of the seventy was from the people, the object comes from those people, and it is called the object "from" (maf'ul minhu), because he did not choose all of them but chose from among them seventy men for his appointed time with God, glorified is He.

They said regarding the reason for the seventy that those who followed Moses were tribes (asbat), so he took a number of men from each tribe, so that all the tribes would be represented at the appointed time. The word "appointed time" (miqat) occurred earlier when God said: ﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him﴾ (from verse 143 of Surah al-A'raf). Is this appointed time the first appointed time? No, because the first appointed time was for Moses' speaking with God, and the second covenant (mithaq) was for the apology concerning the worshippers of the calf.

﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. So when the earthquake seized them, he said: "My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before"﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf). Why did the earthquake seize them?

Because they did not oppose those who worshipped the calf with the appropriate opposition, and God wanted to give them a glimpse of His punishment. The rajfah is a severe quake that shakes the thing shaken (marjuf), hides it, and terrifies it, from the one who quakes (rajif). When the earthquake seized them, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾.

Moses explained: "I brought them out from among their people, and their families know that the seventy men came with me. If You destroy them, O Lord, their families may think that I brought them out so that they would die, and that I handed them over to destruction. And if You were to cause them to die, O Lord, and Your will had so decided, You would have destroyed them before this matter, and me with them as well." The Qur'an adds, in the words of Moses and the people together:

﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? This is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf). "You, O Lord, are too merciful to destroy us for what the foolish among us did." This statement shows that the matter is one of action, and the action is the worship of the calf. If this had been the first appointed time, there would have been no need for such a statement, because the people of Moses had not yet worshipped the calf. But after the first appointed time they said: "Since Moses has spoken with God, we must see God," and they actually said to Moses: ﴿Show us God plainly﴾ (from verse 153 of Surah al-Nisa').

So we find that what happened among the people of Moses after the first appointed time was their saying: ﴿Show us God plainly﴾, not the act. Here, however, the verse speaks of the act: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? This is only Your trial﴾.

Thus we learn that the verse speaks of a second appointed time, set after some of them had worshipped the calf. Fitnah means trial (ikhtibar), and trial is not blameworthy in itself. No examination is called blameworthy in itself. What is blameworthy is the outcome for the one who fails, while the examination is not blameworthy for the one who passes.

So fitnah is affliction (ibtila') and trial. It confronts the ignorant human who does not know what matters will turn into and how they will end, so that he may choose the path and reach the outcome. This does not apply to God, because He knows eternally every conduct of His servants. But this knowledge is not a proof against the servants. The action must come from the servants so that it becomes manifest, appears, and has existence in reality, and so that the proof may be established against them. Taking reality into account is the most just.

The words of Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿This is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf). This statement means: "You, O Lord, have made the trial because You created them choosing, so it is right that they obey and it is right that they disobey." God, glorified is He, is the one who leads astray and guides, because since He made the human being choosing, He gave him the capacity for misguidance and the capacity for guidance.

God, glorified is He, has made clear whom He wills to guide and whom He wills to lead astray, saying: ﴿God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (from verse 86 of Surah Al 'Imran). The reason for their not being guided is their wrongdoing. Likewise the Truth says: ﴿God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (from verse 264 of Surah al-Baqarah).

Thus we see that disbelief is what prevents them from guidance. So God has made it possible for the servant to choose guidance or to choose misguidance, and what the servant does and chooses he does not do against God's compulsion, because, glorified is He, if He had not created each of us choosing, a human being could not have acted contrary to God's will. But He created the human being choosing. Whenever you choose, O human, guidance or misguidance, this is what God has granted you. God has made clear that the one who does wrong and the one who transgresses is fit for God to help him in his misguidance, just as He helps the one who chooses guidance, because he is fit for God to help him toward guidance.

The Truth says, in the words of our master Moses at the end of this verse: ﴿You are our Protector (walyuna), so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of those who forgive﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf). The walī is the one who is close to you, and no one is close to you except one whom you have brought near by your affection for him, and whom you have brought near only for a quality in him that pleases you and benefits you, that helps you if someone transgresses against you, or from whose work you take, because he is knowledgeable. So the first meaning of the word walī is the one close to you whom you have brought near because he has a quality that may benefit you, or support you, or teach you.

Moses' saying "You are our walī" means "You are our supporter and the nearest to us." If a person among us commits a sin, You are more entitled to it, and You alone are able to forgive his sin. Therefore Moses says: "So forgive us." From this we know that he seeks to repel harm (dar' al-mafsadah) first, because repelling it takes precedence over securing benefit (jalb al-maslahah). Moses, peace be upon him, put first the request for forgiveness of sin, then asked and prayed to his Lord that He would have mercy on them, and this is securing a benefit. Our Lord has said, regarding repelling harm: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire﴾, and this is repelling harm, which is keeping away from the Fire, and then: ﴿and is admitted to Paradise﴾.

This is securing benefit and advantage.

So repelling harm takes precedence over securing benefit. For example, you see an apple on a tree and you want to stretch out your hand to take it, then you turn and find a young man who wants to hurl a brick at you. What do you do? In such an emotional state you first push the brick away, then afterwards take the apple. This is repelling harm, which takes precedence over securing benefit. Here repelling harm is embodied in Moses' saying: ﴿So forgive us﴾, then he said after that: ﴿and have mercy on us﴾, and this is securing benefit. The Qur'an says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy﴾ (from verse 82 of Surah al-Isra'). Because the illness occurs first, and when you turn to the method of the Qur'an, it heals you from this illness, and mercy is that no illness comes to you at all. If you take the Qur'an as your helper, no illness will ever come to you.

﴿So forgive us, and have mercy on us, and You are the best of those who forgive﴾ (from verse 155 of Surah al-A'raf).

Like the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿the best of providers﴾, and ﴿the best of schemers﴾, and ﴿the best of inheritors﴾, and ﴿the best of those who forgive﴾ here. This is because forgiveness may come from one human being to another, but we know that the forgiveness of the Lord is above that of creation. The forgiving person among men may forgive out of show, may forgive for reputation, may forgive because he fears the retaliation of the other party. But He, glorified is He, fears no one, and He is the best of those who forgive without any return.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 156:

The Truth (Allah) then says, after that: ﴿And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter; indeed we have turned back to You. He said, "My punishment – I afflict with it whom I will; but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses."﴾

We note that this verse contains new requests from our master Musa (Moses) to his Lord after his saying: ﴿Forgive us and have mercy upon us﴾. We see that "the best of forgivers" returns to the words of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿Forgive us﴾. As for the "good" in his saying: ﴿And prescribe for us in this world good﴾, it returns to the request for mercy: ﴿And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter﴾.

So he asks for good in this world and likewise in the Hereafter. "Good" has a linguistic (lughawi) meaning and a legal (shar'i) meaning. As for the linguistic meaning, everything a person finds good is called "good" (hasanah). But the legal good is what the Shari'ah (sacred law) has deemed good. The Shari'ah is the watchman over every one of our deeds and conduct. So "good" is not what a person finds good, because a person may find sin good; that is human approval, far from the method. Legal approval, however, lies in implementing the method through "do" and "do not do."

The good that is considered by the accountable servants from God is the legal good, because a person may find something good while it is not legal, since he looks at the immediacy of its benefit and not at its deferred benefit, nor at the quantity of its benefit. Benefit in this world, as we know, is according to your conception of benefit, whereas the benefit of the Hereafter, its measure is known only to the Knower of the Unseen, glorified is He. So His saying: ﴿And prescribe for us in this world good﴾ means by it the legal good in this world as action, and in the Hereafter as reward.

We note that Musa intended by the first "good" what encompasses both the legal good and the linguistic good; so it is a supplication for well-being and noble, pleasant blessings, and all the good of this world in the light of God's method. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world, purely, on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (part of verse 32, surah al-A'raf). So the special good is on the Day of Resurrection, but there are those who benefit from it in this world: the inanimate benefits from God's mercy, the plant benefits from God's mercy, the animal benefits from God's mercy, and the disbeliever benefits from God's mercy. All of that is in this world, and it is the mercy that "encompasses all things." But the matter of the Hereafter, as a reward for righteousness, is a reward specific to the believers.

The Truth continues on the tongue of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿indeed we have turned back to You﴾.

"Hada" means "returned," so "hadna ilayka" means "we have returned to You." This is the speech of Musa about himself, his brother, and the people who worshipped the calf and then repented. Since we have returned to You, O my Lord, You are too generous to send us back disappointed. The Truth, glorified is He, replies: ﴿He said, "My punishment – I afflict with it whom I will; but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses."﴾ (part of verse 156, surah al-A'raf).

His saying, the Truth: ﴿My punishment – I afflict with it whom I will﴾ means that there is no one who can push Me or guide Me in directing punishment at anyone. When a servant commits a sin, I either punish him or forgive him. Therefore no one should say to a sinner that God must surely punish him, because He, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿My punishment – I afflict with it whom I will; but My mercy encompasses all things﴾ (part of verse 156, surah al-A'raf). And what is meant by mercy here? Is it mercy in this world or mercy in the Hereafter? It is the mercy of this world that includes the obedient and the disobedient, the believer and the disbeliever, but it is purely for the believers on the Last Day, as we have said.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So I will decree it﴾ indicates that this will be in the Hereafter. That is, God's mercy encompassed all things in this world, but it is a mercy that ends for the disbelievers within the framework of this world, whereas for the believers it is a continuing mercy that God decreed from eternity and which He gives to the believers as grace, favour and bounty from Him, glorified is He: ﴿So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses﴾ (part of verse 156, surah al-A'raf).

When some Jews heard that, they said: "We are the God-fearing." It was said to them: "In which method are you God-fearing? In the method of Musa? If you were God-fearing in the method of Musa as you claim, you would have believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), because among the teachings of Musa is that you believe in the Messenger of God, Muhammad, peace be upon him. This is why the saying of the Exalted came: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the vile things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honour him, help him, and follow the light that has been sent down with him – it is those who are the successful﴾ (verse 157)."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 157:

So these are nine attributes of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that Allah revealed to him a Book specific to him, which is the Qur'an; that he is the possessor of miracles; and that he conveyed and announced the best and most complete beliefs, acts of worship and morals. He (peace and blessings be upon him) was the unlettered one (al-ummi), who did not practise reading and writing and did not sit with any teacher. Thus he, peace be upon him, remained in the state in which he was born. His Lord, majestic and exalted, has mentioned him by his name, his attributes and his descriptions among the Jews and Christians, in the Torah and the Gospel. The disbelievers among them concealed these or misinterpreted them. Likewise his Lord described him as one who commands them to what is good and obliges them to do everything that upright natures and sound instincts call for, because in that lies success in this world and salvation in the Hereafter. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) forbids them and restrains them from every reprehensible evil which a sound disposition and upright creation find abhorrent. He makes lawful for them the good things which were forbidden to them and which Allah prohibited for them as a recompense for their transgression and misguidance. He forbids them everything harmful and foul, such as eating carrion and unlawful wealth gained through usury (riba), bribery and fraud. He lightens for them what was burdensome and heavy of the obligations which were in the law of Musa (peace be upon him), such as cutting off the sinful limbs and the prohibition of spoils of war for them and the obligation to burn them. Likewise Allah lightens and removes from them the severe covenants that were imposed upon them as a punishment for their wickedness and wrongdoing.

He, majestic in His glory, says: ﴿Because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been made lawful for them, and because of their hindering many from the way of Allah (160), and their taking usury though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming people's wealth falsely. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment (161).﴾ (Surah an-Nisa').

Thus Allah informed the messengers before our master, the Messenger of Allah, that they should convey to their peoples the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that the peoples who witness and live in the time of his message should believe. It is true that the Messenger of Allah was not contemporary with any of the messengers, but the glad tidings of him were brought by their prophets and recorded in the books revealed to them. Every messenger who preceded our master Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, Allah commanded him to convey to those to whom he was sent that they should follow the Messenger Muhammad and believe in him, and not cling to worldly authority, fearing that it would be taken from them. And since the Messenger (peace be upon him) has come with a miracle and a clear proof, it is necessary that they believe in him.

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets﴾ (part of verse 81, Surah Al 'Imran).

Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, has created a leaven of faith so that the followers of religions do not conflict, and so that the people of an existing religion do not understand that another religion has come to abrogate it and take away its worldly authority; for the message of faith is connected, and judgments arise for people through the extension of time. All the messengers are keen that life be safe and happy, in which talents support one another and movements do not oppose one another. The Truth demanded this of the messengers, took the covenant from them, and afterwards confirmed it, saying: ﴿Do you affirm?﴾ and drew from them words that support this method. Therefore it is not proper for a follower of a prophet to clash with a new message supported by a miracle and supported by a method that guarantees for humanity life, its soundness and its happiness.

The Truth did not suffice with making belief in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a mere report; rather He placed for Muhammad alone a mark in the books that preceded him, and described him to them as a concrete figure. When He describes him as a concrete figure, this is clearer than reporting about him in words. For this reason Abdullah ibn Salam said, when Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I know him better than I know my son." He said: "And why?" He said: "Because I have no doubt about Muhammad that he is a prophet, but as for my son, perhaps his mother betrayed [me]." So Umar kissed his head. For this reason the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿They recognise him as they recognise their sons﴾.

There is no doubt that a person knows his son with precise knowledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had particular marks which establish his physical personality (ﷺ), and the matter in the Night Journey and Ascension is not merely words. Indeed, when he was asked about that journey he said: "I saw Musa, and he was a man of lean flesh, a man (rajul) of the type of the men of Shanu'ah; and I saw Isa, and he was a medium-built (rab'ah), reddish man, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse; and I am the most similar of the children of Ibrahim to him." (2) Likewise Allah gave in the Torah and the Gospel not only the news about Muhammad (ﷺ), but gave the details of his form, so that it would be concrete for them, so that when he came, with the concreteness, no partner would be confused with him. So He, glorified be He, says: ﴿They recognise him as they recognise their sons﴾. But a group of them concealed the truth in order to keep their worldly authority, because they were thinking that when a new religion came it would take from them this worldly authority and lead the nations and peoples. Allah, glorified and exalted, wished to make the messengers of heaven to earth cooperators, not opponents, supporting one another. As came in Surah al-Fath: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah; and their description in the Gospel is like a seed that sprouts its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows thick and stands firm on its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage the disbelievers by them. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward (29).﴾ (verse 29, Surah al-Fath).

The Truth brought the image of the believers in the message of the Messenger of Allah into the Torah and the Gospel, because the Islamic religion revealed to Muhammad will have no religion after it; therefore He brought the biography of the Messenger of Allah, his attributes and the attributes of his followers into the Torah and the Gospel. In this religion is what Judaism lacks, for it drifted into pure materialism and abandoned spirituality; therefore the description of Muhammad's followers comes in the Torah: ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration.﴾

When the Jews went to excess in materialism, Allah wished to send a messenger who inclines towards spirituality, and he is our master Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him), so that moderation might be achieved in dealing with life without excess or deficiency. Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted, prepared for every messenger that the previous messenger should announce him, because there are no contradictions among the messages. And since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the seal of the procession of messengers, it was necessary that Allah describe him, glorified be He, with a description not in words but as a picture, so that when they see him they recognise him. For this reason we find that our master Salman al-Farisi, when he saw the Messenger of Allah in Madinah and saw in him many signs, wished to see a physical sign, so he saw in the Messenger's shoulder the Seal of Prophethood.

But did that benefit? Yes; many people believed in him. The Messenger of Allah also held a debate between himself and the Jews through the agency of Abdullah ibn Salam, who said after he embraced Islam in the presence of the Messenger of Allah: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander (bahit); if they learn of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me before you." The Jews came, and Abdullah entered the house. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What sort of man among you is Abdullah ibn Salam?" They said: "Our most learned and the son of our most learned, and our best and the son of our best." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you think if Abdullah embraces Islam?" They said: "May Allah protect him from that!" Then Abdullah came out to them and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "Our worst and the son of our worst!" and they fell upon him (3)... (4)

So the descriptive words and the concrete personal attributes came so that it would not be said that the religions of heaven conflict; rather they are all converging on joining earth to heaven according to what the condition of the age requires in time and place. In former times the world was isolated from one another, and every environment had its atmosphere and its ailments; so a messenger would come to treat specific ailments in a specific place. But Allah sent His messenger (ﷺ) after these ailments had become unified in the world; our noble Messenger came to treat these universal ailments, and the Messenger of Allah came supported by his attributes and supported by his teachings, which lighten for them their burden and their fetters. The "isr" is the heavy load, and the "aghlal" (fetters) are the plural of "ghull," which is the iron piece that joins the two hands to the neck to restrict movement.

1 ḍarb: light of flesh; rajl: his hair is between straight and curly; his saying "of the men of Shanu'ah" means tall, because this tribe was famous for the tallness of its men; rab'ah means of moderate build, neither tall nor short.
2 Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh).
3 bahitūnī: they say about me what I did not do; from bahn and buhtan, which is falsehood, lying and fabrication.
4 From a hadith recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, Kitab Bad' al-Khalq, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).

The Divine has mentioned the attributes and prepared minds for the coming of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), so that He might lift from them the shackles through the light that was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). The Muhammadan message is the all-encompassing and all-restraining one. For this reason, the Divine says after that:

﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God to you all, the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him. He gives life and causes death. So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet who believes in God and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.﴾ (7:158)

Here the Divine commands His Messenger with the following: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾, in a message that encompasses time and encompasses place.
