So they take the goods of this lower life, and in their taking of these goods they judge that He, glory be to Him, will forgive them. By this they made the unlawful lawful and moved from the sphere of disobedience to the sphere of disbelief; for there is a difference between doing a thing and calling it a sin, and a person who commits a sin and says it is not a sin, this is a passage from disobedience to disbelief. An example of this is usury: when we find someone who makes it lawful, we say to him: accept being a sinner and do not enter yourself into disbelief; for if you make lawful what Allah has forbidden, disbelief falls upon you and you are described by it, God forbid. But if you say: it is unlawful, but my circumstances are difficult and I cannot control myself, then perhaps Allah will forgive you. But the people of Moses persisted in disobedience and said: "Allah will forgive us." And the Truth says: ﴿And if goods like it came to them, they would take it.﴾

After that they abandoned the higher and took the goods of the lower life, and they persist in their error, committing sin upon sin without knocking on the door of repentance. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, admonishes them: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they should not say about Allah except the truth?﴾ (Part of 7:169.)

They inherited the Book, and in the Book a firm covenant was taken from them that they should not say about Allah except the truth. But does the corrupt person turn away from falsehood and return to truth? Certainly not. Thus they ignored what is in the Book, although they had studied what is in it, in confirmation of the Truth's saying: ﴿And they studied what is in it.﴾

The word "darasa" indicates the repetition of an action. It is said: "So-and-so studied jurisprudence (darasa al-fiqh)," meaning he learned it with continuous study until jurisprudence became a habit (malakah) in him. This differs from one who read the Book once; for him jurisprudence does not become a habit. To understand the difference between "knowledge" ('ilm) and "habit" (malakah), we say: knowledge is the receiving of information, whereas one who studies information, applies it, and it becomes automatic for him, this is the one who has mastered knowledge until it has become a habit in him.

If a fasting person, for example, meets a jurist and asks him a ruling on a matter of fasting, the jurist answers him immediately, because he knows every small and great matter of jurisprudence. But if he asks a novice student at al-Azhar, the student may become confused and ask to return to his books to find the answer, because jurisprudence has not become a habit for him.

Habit in matters of meaning is the counterpart of mechanical skill in material things, which requires practice. One who holds the loom to weave cloth and masters passing the shuttle between the two threads does so only by practice. He learned it with difficulty and repeated training.

Thus His words ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾ mean that the study of the Book was repeated until they knew what knowledge is in it. We have taken "darasa al-'ilm" (studied knowledge) from a sensory matter, "darasa al-qamh" (threshed the wheat). Whoever was raised in the countryside knows how we thresh wheat: when the threshing sledge (nawraj) turns over the wheat ears, it brings out the grain from its husks and cuts the stalks for us; this process is called "threshing the wheat."

What they did of disobedience was not from heedlessness of this covenant, that they should not say about Allah except the truth, for they studied what was in the Book revealed to them, which is the Torah, with a comprehensive study; but they took the lower goods. It was necessary that the counterpart of the lower goods be presented to us, to clarify that the destiny of one who desires the Hereafter is lasting reward. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿And the Last Abode is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then use reason?﴾ (Part of 7:169.)

This means an admonition that before you do an act, you must consider what good it gives, and leave it if it gives much evil. Weigh the matter with your minds, and when you weigh the matter with your minds you will know that doing good outweighs.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 170:

The Truth (Allah) then says: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers.﴾ (170).

Indeed, many of the Children of Israel inherited the Book, but they took the lowest of this world's goods, and did not weigh matters with their minds. Therefore they did not hold fast to the Book, and they abandoned it and followed their own desires, as if they were not bound by a method of "do this" and "do not do that." Opposite them are some of those who hold fast to the Book they inherited, and who do not say about Allah except the truth.

The root m-s-k (م س ك) indicates a firm connection. What makes a person connected to a thing is the one who grips it. You say "masak" (مَسَك), "massak" (مسَّك), "amsak" (أمسك), you say "istamsak" (استمسك), and "tamassak" (تماسك), and all of them are one root. His saying, the Truth: "yumassikūn" (يُمَسِّكون) is an intensification of the grip, like qata'a and qatta'a (قطَّع), but qatta'a is more emphatic.

"Massaka" means that the one who grips has gained control over what he grips. "Istamsaka" means he sought (to grip). "Tamassaka" means that there is an interaction between two parties: between the one who grips and the one who is gripped. Among the mercy of our Lord is that He does not ask us to grip the Book. Rather, He asks us to hold fast to the Book (istimsak). Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes clear to you: if you turn towards nearness to Me and drawing near to Me, then leave what is other than Me, for the help is from Me alone. And therefore He shows us that whoever implements the method of the Qur'an will never meet humiliation: ﴿Whoever rejects the transgressor and believes in Allah has grasped the most reliable handhold, which has no breaking.﴾ Here the Truth, glory be to Him, uses the word (istamsaka) and not the word masaka. So whoever directs his intention to act, Allah gives him help. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says in the Hadith Qudsi: ("I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.") (1).

So by your faith in Allah you strengthen yourself and fortify it with Allah's help to you. If you want Allah to remember you, then remember Allah; for if you remember Him in yourself, He remembers you in Himself, and if you remember Him in a gathering, He remembers you in a gathering better than it, and if you draw near to Him a span, He draws near to you a cubit. So what more do you want than that, especially since you will add nothing to Him? Thus the matter is in your hand. If you want Allah to be with you, walk in His way and help will come to you immediately. Thus the situation will be with you and will move toward you, through your faith in Allah and your turning to love of connection with Him.

Therefore we said before: when a person wants to meet a great man of this world, and he has in hand an interest of human concern, he writes a request. Either this great man agrees or does not agree. When he agrees, he sets the time and sets the place, and his office manager asks you about the topics you will speak about. When you meet him and the time ends, he stands from his chair to end the meeting. This is the great man among humans. But what about the Supreme Great One whom you meet in faith? You meet Allah at any time and in any place, you tell Him what you want, and you are the one who ends the meeting. Does all this not suffice to make you hold fast to faith?

﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer﴾ (part of verse 170, surah al-A'raf).

(Surah al-A'raf).

The Book here is the inherited Book, and what is meant by it is the Torah, which they studied. Allah took from them in this Book a covenant that they would not say about Allah except the truth. The Truth says here: ﴿and established prayer﴾. Is there nothing in this Book but prayer? No, but He singled out prayer for mention, because we know that prayer is the pillar of religion. We know from the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) that prayer was obligated directly, while all the obligations of Islam other than prayer were obligated through revelation.

We said before, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, that the head of any government department, when he wants an ordinary routine matter, signs the paper bearing this matter and writes on it "to be presented to so-and-so," and the paper takes its course. When he is concerned with a more important matter, he telephones the competent employee, and when the matter is of the utmost importance, he asks the employee to come to him. Thus prayer was obligated in this form, because it is the constant declaration of loyalty to Allah five times a day, and if you wish to add to that voluntary and night prayers, you may do so.

By prayer you show loyalty to Allah in all His rulings. You show loyalty to Allah by zakat every year, by fasting in one month, which is Ramadan, and by pilgrimage once in a lifetime if you are able. But prayer is constant, renewed loyalty. And because prayer has all this importance, it never falls away. The pillars of Islam, as we know, are five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, which is faith in Allah and in the Messenger as one unified whole that cannot be separated. It suffices that a person utters it once for it to be recorded for him. Then come the pillars of prayer, zakat, fasting, and pilgrimage, and pilgrimage is not an obligation except upon those who are able. A person may have no wealth from which to pay zakat, so nothing is then obligatory on him to give, and a person may be sick or traveling, so he does not fast.

Thus some obligations of Islam may fall away from the Muslim, except prayer, which never falls away, because in prayer, on the surface of the matter, there is a cutting off of some of your time from the movement of your work. Even if each obligation takes, for example, half an hour, a person sets aside two and a half hours of his time every day for performing prayer. Time is precious to a person. In prayer there is a sacrifice of some of the time in which a person could earn money. There is also in it fasting from eating, drinking, and intimacy with wives, so it contains all the essentials of the pillars of Islam, and therefore it never falls away.

﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer﴾ (part of verse 170, surah al-A'raf).

So holding fast is very clear here, and performing prayer is an expression of commitment to holding fast to the method of faith. Therefore we hear someone say: when we went to Mecca and Medina we lived in inner serenity and spiritual illumination, and we lived with the manifestation and light that floods the depths. I say to whoever says this: our Lord here is our Lord there. Only you there were committed, and whenever you heard the call to prayer you ran and hastened to the prayer. If you do here what you did there, you will see the same manifestations. So if you remain in constant loyalty with the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, then the Truth will not waste your reward as one of the reformers, for He is the one who says: ﴿Indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers.﴾

This is a general matter: the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, does not waste the reward of the reformer. His saying: ﴿We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾ after His saying: ﴿hold fast to the Book and establish prayer﴾ is evidence that any reform in society depends on those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, because society is not reformed unless your connection with the One who created you and created society, and who sent down for you the straight method, is maintained.

(1) From Sahih al-Bukhari in the Book of Tawhid; Muslim also reported it in his Sahih by three routes from Abu Hurayrah, and al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also reported it.

And the Truth (Allah) says after that: ﴿And [remember] when We raised the mountain over them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them: "Take hold of what We have given you with determination, and remember what is in it, that you may become righteous."﴾

The mountain is well known to be made of rocks fused together, forming a massive body that may reach a thousand meters or more. Allah says concerning the mountains: ﴿And the mountains He has set firmly (arsaha)﴾. The verb arsaha (to set firmly, anchor) is not used except for something that has weight. You do not say, "I set the paper on the desk," but you say, "I set the glass sheet on the desk to protect it," and by that you are setting firmly something that has weight and heft.

Our Lord has set the mountains firmly and placed them in the earth as pegs (awtad). The peg (watad), as we know, is named from being fixed and set into something, as evidenced by the fact that if it becomes loose in its place, we apply what we call "takhshina" (a filler/adhesive) to stick it and bind it to what it is fixed in. Here the Truth says: ﴿When We uprooted the mountain﴾. "Nataqna" means "We uprooted," and there is another statement: ﴿And We raised over them the Tur with their covenant, and We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating," and We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾ (4:154).

And the Truth also said: ﴿And [remember] when We took your covenant and raised the Tur over you﴾ (2:63). Here there is a difference between "nataqa" and "rafa'a" (raising), because the mountain is fixed in the earth and held like a peg; therefore it needs, before being raised, a process of pulling out and uprooting from the earth, and after that comes the raising. "Nataqna" means We pulled the mountain out from the place where it was set, so that We could lift it, and Allah lifted it to make it a canopy over them. That is, there are three operations: nataq, i.e., pulling out and dislodging; then raising; then His making it a canopy over them, and this requires a direction for what is raised toward some side. The Truth says: "[Remember] when" — i.e., mention when We uprooted the mountain, meaning We pulled it out and dislodged it from the earth, and We do not pull it out and dislodge it from the earth except for another purpose, namely to make it a canopy. The overshadowing by clouds had previously been a mercy for them, but the mountain became a canopy of "punishment," because the Truth had sent down the Torah to them through Moses, and they said to him: the rulings of this Torah are harsh. A person may ask: why all this foot-dragging with the legislations that came for the benefit of mankind? So the punishment came to them from the Truth in that He raised the mountain over them like a canopy bearing a threat, as though it were about to fall upon them: ﴿as though it were a canopy and they thought it would fall upon them﴾.

For this reason we find that every Jew prostrates on his left eyebrow, although prostration requires the forehead to be placed evenly on the ground. But they prostrate with a tilt toward the left eyebrow, because their predecessors saw the mountain above them and fear of its falling overtook them; they used to prostrate while at the same time watching the mountain, and this matter remained ingrained in them, and they came to prostrate only on their left eyebrow, because of the story of the mountain that Allah uprooted, lifted, and made to be above them. ﴿And they thought it would fall upon them﴾: thought (zann) is the prevalence of a proposition, and it may also be meant to indicate a strong prevalence that may reach the level of certainty, such as the Truth's saying: ﴿those who think that they will meet their Lord﴾ (2:46).

When matters remained in this state, and they feared that the mountain would fall upon them, and because there was a book sent down to them, the Torah, and they were disobedient and rebellious toward what is in it, the Truth said to them: ﴿Take hold of what We have given you with determination, and remember what is in it, that you may become righteous﴾ (7:171).

"Khudhu" (take hold) is an imperative verb, and an imperative requires one who commands and something to be commanded. The word "quwwa" (determination, force) here is the active energy, and the origin in the whole universe is that we approach everything with force, because the universe that you see as subjugated has no opinion as to whether it acts or does not act; rather it is always acting when commanded. As we said before: the sun did not become angry with people and say, "I will not rise today," and likewise the air did not refuse, nor does a donkey, for example, refuse to carry dung, or refuse when its owner cleans it and brings the saddle-cloth to make it a distinguished mount. The donkey, then, does not disobey here or there, and the whole universe is subjected to fixed material laws.

﴿The sun is not permitted to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each in an orbit is swimming﴾ (36:40).

The Truth has clarified this order of the universe because it is compelled and has no obligation (taklif), and what is governed by instinct (ghariza) of the cosmos is more suitable for life than what is governed by actual choice. And along with this choice, a human has things that act upon him and of which he knows nothing, although the sustenance of his life depends on them: no one holds his heart and regulates it and says to it, "Beat"; and likewise the lung and the movement of breathing, the peristaltic motion of the intestines, the ureter, and a person desires to enter the lavatory when the bladder fills with urine. All these are regular matters in which a human has no choice at all. Matters governed by instincts are not subject to our choice, such as when a person eats and speaks during a meal, and a grain of rice falls into the windpipe, and the person tries to expel it by coughing. This is called "ghariza" (instinct), i.e., a matter governed by an act that is not chosen.

Likewise the animal: if you bring food to it, it does not eat more than its capacity even if its owner beats it. As for a human, he may eat after he is satisfied, and when his host says to him, for example, "You have not tasted this kind of meat," he eats. Hence we find that diseases in humans are more numerous than in animals, because human choice extends to many scattered fields that may harm him and hurt him.

We all know this example of the difference between human and animal: we find a human boils mint and drinks it, and cooks molokhia (jute leaves) to eat it, and he did that because he tested both; he did not eat the mint, and he ate the molokhia, despite the similarity of their leaves. But put a mint plant before a female buffalo or a donkey, and put dry grass before the buffalo or the donkey, and you will find the buffalo and the donkey heading toward the dry grass and leaving the green, moist mint plant, and they do that by instinct. The one governed by instinct has an order, and had the animal been free to choose, the whole movement of life would have been thrown into confusion and its affairs would have become hard for people.

Thus we know that the foundations of life rest on the laws of instinct, and these laws exist in the universe to serve us, the children of Adam. Electricity, for example, existed before we benefited from it, but afterward we benefited from it; and likewise gravity existed in the universe from eternity, but we did not notice it, and when we discovered it our capacity to benefit from it increased. Thus we see that a human is one part of this universe, except that he is distinguished by having a domain of choice in some matters and a domain of compulsion in others: he shares with the universe in compulsion, and is distinguished from the rest of creation, apart from the jinn, by choice in other matters. For example, we find that a person whose heart suffers some weakness, when he climbs a staircase, becomes breathless and his breath comes in gasps from exhaustion and much movement, because his instinct that governs him signals the body that the lung must work more to give the oxygen that helps the climbing.

Another example: we find the male of animals approaches its female to smell her; if he finds her pregnant, he does not come near her. The animal in this matter differs from the human, because the animal is moved by instinct which shows it that the sexual act between male and female is for preserving the species, and since the female has conceived, the male does not approach her. Thus the human differs from the animal in this matter: the human's pleasure in sex is higher than the animal's, because in the animal it submits to instinct alone, whereas in the human it submits, together with instinct, also to the choice that Allah gave to the human.

Thus it is out of Allah's mercy that a human should be compelled in some things and free in others, with "do" and "do not," so that he may choose among alternatives.

Here the Truth says: ﴿Take hold of what We have given you with determination﴾, i.e., take what He has given you in the Book with earnestness and diligence. This statement was an introduction to what science has brought in explaining the meaning of force (quwwa). The knowledge of it reached us before its material reality reached us, and we came to see the energy that gives force. Newton came to disclose to us the law of gravitation, the first, second, and third laws, and discovered that every body remains in what it is: if at rest, it remains at rest until a mover comes to move it; and if the body is moving, it does not stop until something strikes it or a holder holds it. Scientists called this effect inertia (al-qusur al-dhati), or "ta'attul" (inertness), meaning that what is at rest is kept from motion unless a mover moves it, and what is moving is kept from rest unless a stopper stops it. When you ride in a car while sitting and still, and the car is moving, you remain still until the driver stops it suddenly, and then you move from your place unless you hold on to something.

In the markets we see the jugglers (hawa) performing some games to bewitch people's eyes: he brings a table with a cloth on it, smooth and slippery, then places plates and cups on it, then moves the cloth lightly so as to pull it gently from under the cups, so that they do not move with the movement of the cloth.

When Newton came, he drew a comparison and balance between force, motion and inertia, and we said: inertia means that what is at rest is kept from motion, and what is moving is kept from rest. This is the material fact in the universe that served the space science concerning spaceships and rockets. We see spaceships and think they move in space by fuel, although their size cannot contain the fuel that would propel them for years; in truth they move by the law of inertia, being without fuel. They are propelled into space by the force of the rocket until they exit into cosmic space, and they remain moving unless a stopper stops them. We see this in the simple experiment when a person fires a bullet from a pistol: the bullet is launched with the force of the shot for a distance and then falls if no barrier stops it, and it falls after a certain distance, because the air opposes it and collides with its motion until it stops. But in outer space there is no air, so the spaceship does not stop, because it moves by the law of inertia.

These spaceships rely in their ascent into space on rockets to reach the outer orbit. Rockets move by the escaping gas, which took up Newton's third law, the law that says: every action has a reaction equal to it and opposite to it in direction; and when this gas is heated it exits from behind the rocket with force, so the rocket is pushed forward.

Thus we see the Truth's saying: ﴿Take hold of what We have given you with determination﴾ in material reality and in moral reality. Look at non-religious people: you find them at rest in some matters, not moving from them nor going beyond them. One of them does not pray, does not give zakat, and does not say a word of goodness, and in that he needs a force to move his stillness toward obedience to Allah. We also find among non-religious people someone who drinks wine, or commits fornication, or steals, or takes bribes; here he needs a force to restrain him from such movement. Therefore we say: a human in his voluntary acts needs two things: first, if he is still from doing good, we bring him a force that moves him toward this good; and if he is moving toward evil, we bring him a force that stops him from it. This is what the faith-based method provides in "do" and "do not." So whoever is lax about prayer and is still from it, we say to him: pray. And whoever goes to gambling and moves toward it cannot stop unless a force comes to him that halts him from that and prevents him. Thus the legal force in the method is "do," to move what is still, and "do not"…

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying]: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify." [This He did] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed, we were unaware of this"﴾ (7:172).

"Idh" (when) turns to time, meaning: remember the time when God took from the children of Adam. The One who takes is God, the one taken from is the children of Adam, and the thing taken is their offspring. These are the elements. Let us consider this carefully. The Lord here is the one who takes, the children of Adam are those from whom it is taken, and what is taken is the offspring. The children of Adam are the descendants of Adam from his time until the Hour is established. Here the thing taken and the thing taken from become one, and we must find a distinction in this text, because it is required that the thing taken from be a whole and the thing taken be a part of it.

The example: if I take something from you, then the thing taken from is the whole, and the thing taken is a part. But here we find that the thing taken is the very same as the thing taken from. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved this difficulty in this verse when he said, as Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him) narrated from him: "When God created Adam, He wiped his back, and there fell from his back every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection. He placed between the eyes of each person of them a gleam of light, and presented them to Adam. He said: 'O Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' He saw a man among them and was impressed by the gleam between his eyes. He said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is a man from the last of the nations, from your descendants, who is called David.' He said: 'Lord, how long have You made his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'O Lord, add to his life forty years from mine.' When Adam's life was completed, the Angel of Death came to him. He said: 'Has not forty years of my life remained?' He said: 'Did you not give it to your son David?' He said: 'Adam denied, so his descendants deny; he forgot, so his descendants forget; he erred, so his descendants err.'"¹

So the descendants of Adam were taken from the back of Adam. We have known before that each of us, before his mother conceived him, was a particle in the loins of his father, and his father was a particle in the loins of his father, back to Adam. Thus we find that every individual is taken from the loins as offspring. There are people who are taken as offspring but from whom nothing is taken, such as those upon whom God has decreed that one of them be barren. Likewise the last generation upon whom the Hour will be established, and they will not beget. Adam is one from whom [others] are taken, because he is the first of creation, and he was not taken from anyone. Between the father Adam and the last child, [each is] taken and one from whom [others are] taken. Thus every individual is taken and one from whom [others are] taken, and the meaning is sound.

The one from whom [others] are taken is Adam, then every child of Adam, down to the last generation that will cease from procreation.

The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified that our Lord, glorified and exalted, wiped His hand over Adam's back and brought forth the offspring from it, and said to them: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." From this we know that every particle has been taken from what came before it, and from it what came after it has been taken; all are taken and one from whom [others are] taken, except for the two ends: the first end is Adam, because he is one from whom [others are] taken and was not taken from anything; the second end is the last child of his offspring, who is taken but from whom nothing is taken, because each of us was found from the living sperm cell of his father. Had the sperm cell suffered death, the father would not have begotten. And whoever is born from a sperm cell of a father, that father was taken from a living sperm cell of the grandfather as well, and so on in a chain back to Adam. You will find that every one of us contains a living part from the time of Adam that will never encounter death.

Therefore our Lord says: ﴿And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾ (part of 7:172).

Do not say that everything will be in his back, because the thing taken from is the foundation present in his back, and since everything multiplies, it was created from the smallest thing, and we know that the smaller contains the greater hidden within it. Our Lord took from the backs of the children of Adam the offspring, and addressed the offspring with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾.

Here someone may say: Did these offspring have the capacity for speech? They are offspring awaiting another formation, so as to unite, for example, with the "ovum" in the mother's womb? We answer him: Why do you think that our Lord addressing them is a difficult matter? A human being can learn ten languages, marry four women, and each woman bears offspring from him. He may sit one day with one woman and her children and teach them English, for example, then sit with another and teach her German, teach the third and her children Arabic, and so on. Indeed he can communicate even by gesture with one who does not know his language. If a human can diversify the means of expression, can He not diversify the means of expression for His creatures? He is able to diversify and address. Did not the Almighty, blessed and exalted, say to the mountains: ﴿O mountains, echo with him﴾ (34:10)?

How then should a human's horizon not be broad enough to realize that God is able to address any of His creatures? He is able to address every creature of His in a language that the other does not understand. And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] with David﴾ (21:79).

We also know from the Noble Qur'an that the mountains glorify [God] apart from David, just as all creatures do, in confirmation of the saying of the Almighty, blessed and exalted: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Him] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ (17:44).

Even the particles of the unbeliever's hand glorify [God], though their glorification does not accord with his will.

The saying of the Almighty, glorified is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] with David﴾ shows us that the mountains used to echo David's glorification and his recitation of the Psalms. The command of the Almighty is not limited to the mountains but extends to every creature. For example, we read in the Noble Qur'an that our Lord revealed to the bee: ﴿Take for yourselves houses in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they construct﴾ (16:68). Thus God has, with His creatures, means of address: since He is the One who created the universe and its creatures, He, glorified is He, has address by words, address by signs, address by inspiration, and address by revelation. So when we read that the Almighty, blessed and exalted, said to the offspring of Adam: "Am I not your Lord?", this means He said it to them in the language they understand, for He, glorified is He, is the One who said to the heaven and the earth: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly.' They said: 'We come willingly'﴾ (41:11).

The ant spoke and Solomon understood her speech; had God not taught Solomon how to understand her speech, we would not have known that she spoke: ﴿An ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you"﴾ (27:18).

She understands what humans do when they tread upon small creatures without seeing them. But Solomon is a prophet of God's prophets, and he would not transgress against God's creation. The ant that spoke was guarding the rest of the ants. Likewise the hoopoe spoke to inform Solomon, may peace be upon him, about the kingdom of Sheba and the state of Bilqis and her people.

Thus God, Mighty and Majestic, addresses all His creatures, and all His creatures respond to Him. So let us not say: How did the Lord, glorified is He, address the atoms, when the atoms were not yet obligated? The scholars did not try to enter into this question, because on its surface it is far from reason. It suffices that our Lord, the Creator, the Capable, has informed us that He addressed the particles, saying: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." It appears from this statement that the matter is a representation of the innate disposition (fitrah) deposited in the human soul. As if He, glorified is He, deposited in the human soul and human self a disposition affirming to Him that behind this universe is a Creator God, capable, governing.

It was said long ago: Suppose an airplane crashed with you in a desert, and when you came to from the fainting spell of fear, you thought about your condition and how you find no food, drink, or companion, and grief over this state befell you, so you slept. Then you awoke and found a table laid with the finest food and drink. Would you not look around to ask who prepared this banquet before you extended your hand to the finest food? Likewise, the human who has come into this universe of wise design and marvelous formation: should he not ask himself who created this universe?

We know that the electric lamp required for its manufacture many scientists and skilled craftsmen and countless resources to light a limited room. When we see the sun illuminating the whole universe, not suffering weariness or fatigue, and not needing maintenance from us, should we not ask who made it? Especially since no one has claimed to have made it, and the Almighty, glorified and exalted, has informed us that He is the One who created the sun and created the moon. So either this statement is true, and we worship Him, or it is not true, and we search for who made and created the universe, in order to worship him.

Since no one has claimed for himself the making of these beings, they yield to their owner, and there is no god but God. Thus the innate disposition guides us that behind this great universe is a power commensurate with this greatness, a power commensurate with this precision. From this precision we have taken measures for our time: we took from the celestial spheres a measure of time, and had the motions of the spheres not been made with extreme precision, we could not have counted them as a measure of time. When we consider the saying of the Almighty, glorified and exalted: ﴿The sun and the moon [run] by precise reckoning﴾ (55:5), we find that the expression "bi-husban" occurs twice. The Almighty, glorified and exalted, informed us that He made the sun and the moon by reckoning, or as a reckoning, and they are among the signs indicating the perfection of His power and the magnitude of His dominion, and He did not create them in vain, but for a great wisdom:

﴿That you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ (10:5).

We have taken from the revolution of the sun and moon a measure, and we would not do so unless they were created with reckoning; because the universe is made and created to this degree of precision and firmness. Therefore we must turn our attention to the fact that there is a power behind this world commensurate with its greatness. But do we know, by reason alone, what this power wants? Reason guides us at most to know that there is a power, but reason does not know the name of this power, and likewise reason does not know what this power requires. There had to come to us a messenger from that power to tell us its purpose. The prophetic procession came, and the messengers came, so that each messenger might convey the will of the Truth concerning creation. Each messenger said: The name of the power that created you is God, and He has absolute authority over this universe, and the purpose of the Truth in creating is the cultivation of this universe. All these matters could not have been grasped by reason.

Thus we know that the limit of reason is faith in a creating power behind this universe, and the rational faculties of people are equal in this matter. As for the name of the power and the method required for this God, there must be a messenger.

The philosophers exhausted themselves seeking this power and its purpose. They named the field of inquiry "metaphysics," that is, "what is beyond nature." Usually, when a believer asks the philosophers: "Who told you that behind matter there is a power you must seek?", the philosopher usually answers: "It is the innate disposition that guided me to that." Philosophy branched into many schools. The philosophers tried to imagine this power, and this is the flaw, because a human can rationally conceive the existence of a creating power, but cannot imagine it. Many philosophers drowned in destructive psychological anxiety, and some of them saved themselves through faith. Every philosopher should have pricked up his ears and listened to what the messengers said, so that they might resolve for us this riddle, instead of exhausting himself by confusing the rational conception of the existence of a power behind matter with the imagining of this power.

In this regard I strike this example, and I hope you never forget it: If we were sitting in a room with its doors closed, and the bell rang, and we all agree that someone is knocking at the door; and this thing agreed upon by all is counted...

¹ Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, and he said: "a hadith, ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ" (sound and good).

Al-Mawla (glorified and exalted be He) continues His words:

﴿Or you should say, "Indeed, our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?"﴾ (7:173)

It is as though the Truth wishes to cut off from them the argument of opposing the method of Allah. So He draws attention to the covenant of fitrah (the innate disposition), the nature and the natural inclination buried within every human being, in which every existent testified that He is one, the Unique. And He, glorified be He, reminds us of this primordial covenant before the changing desires came into being within us.

﴿"Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ Could any one of the seeds of humanity, while in the knowledge, will and power of Allah, dare to say, "No, You are not my Lord"? Of course this is impossible, and all the seeds answered by fitrah, "Yes." Yes carries the negation of a negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation, like the words of the Truth: ﴿"Is not Allah the most just of judges?"﴾ (95:8, the verse of Surat al-Tin). The interrogative "alaysa" (is not) asks for confirmation of a negative; therefore we are told: when you hear "alaysa," you must say "bala" (yes), and thereby you negate the negation, meaning you affirm that there is no judge more just than Him, glorified be He. Here the Truth says, "Am I not your Lord?" and the answer came: "Yes, we testify." And why all of that? The Truth said it so that He would confirm to all creation that by fitrah they believe that Allah is the Lord. What causes them to become heedless of this fitrah is the stirring of their desires within the sphere of choice. If you ask them, "Who created you?" they say, "Allah," and since Allah is the One who created them, He is their Lord.

﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ (part of 29:61). The Truth brought the account of this testimony so that no one would say, ﴿"Indeed our fathers associated [others with Allah] before."﴾

Thus we know that the excuses of the disobedient and of the disbelievers, by which they make pretexts and offer apologies, are confined to two matters: heedlessness of the covenant of the seeds, and imitation of the fathers.

And what is heedlessness? And what is imitation? Heedlessness may not be preceded by disbelief or disobedience, and it is imitated by the people who come after. The clear example is that our master Adam (peace be upon him) conveyed to his children the upright, straight method, but they became heedless of it, and it is no longer fitting for any one of them to say that his father associated [others with Allah]. Yet this matter arose from heedlessness, and then the association of the fathers came in a second stage, because if each one imitated his father in association, association would trace back to Adam, and Adam was not a associator. Rather, heedlessness of the straight method of Allah occurred among some of the children of Adam, and this heedlessness resulted from the illusion that the method entails heavy obligations. So some of Adam's children went after what they desired and forgot this method, and it no longer stood in the focus of their awareness, because a person always acts upon what is present in the focus of his awareness. As for what will burden him with hardship, he tries to forget it and to be heedless of it. Thus was the first stage of the separation from the method of Allah: heedlessness, in their fathers. Here two factors are added: the factor of heedlessness, and the factor of the example set by one's family and fathers. Faith matters were not in the focus of awareness, and therefore it is said: generally no one forgets what is his (due to him), but he forgets what is upon him, because a person keeps in the focus of his awareness what is owed to him by others, and pushes what he owes far from the focus of his awareness. And since some people imagine that there is hardship in the commandments of faith, they try to keep away from it and forget it, and likewise such people try to distance themselves from these obligations.

Let us take an example from our own lives: we may find a person indebted to a grocer or to a carpenter who has no money to give him, so he tries to stay away from the grocer's shop, or to walk far from the carpenter's sight. Likewise, feigning heedlessness may outwardly appear to be a means of escaping the hardships of obligations. But humankind, in the covenant of the seeds, said, ﴿"Yes, we testify."﴾

That covenant was taken from them; they acknowledged it, and the Truth called them to witness against themselves, so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿"Indeed, we were unaware of this."﴾ For it is not right that we should ever be heedless of this covenant. But the Truth, blessed and exalted, knew that we are human, and He said of our father Adam: ﴿"And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot."﴾ (20:115)

Since Adam forgot, his forgetting falls upon him. Islam has clarified that the nations before Islam are held accountable for forgetfulness. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought a clear report, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Allah has lifted from my nation error, forgetfulness, and what they were compelled to do."(1)

Error is known: that a person intends one thing and another occurs. Forgetfulness is that the ruling does not come to the mind of the person. The one under compulsion is the one overpowered by someone stronger, by threat to his life or by threat to his freedom and its restriction, unless he does what he is ordered to do. In all three cases, the obligation is lifted from the Muslim. The Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned that Allah honored the Muhammadan community in particular by lifting what the Muslim forgets. This is evidence that those who lived before the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were held accountable for it. If we trace the line back before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we reach our master Adam, who was created by the direct hand of Allah, whereas we, the children of Adam, are created by the ordinary law: a man exists, a woman exists, a marital relation exists, and then offspring come.

Allah imposed on Adam, in the Garden which He prepared for him, so that he might undergo training in the cultivation of the earth, a command and a prohibition. He, glorified and exalted be He, said to him: ﴿"And eat from it freely, wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree."﴾ (2:35)

Thus the essence of every obligation is a command in the form "do," and a prohibition in the form "do not do." Adam forgot the obligation in the one simple command, he who was created by the hand of Allah and was charged by Allah directly with one matter: to eat wherever he wished and to refrain from eating of the tree. If Adam did not remember that, then what did he remember? And it was not proper for him to forget, because he was created by the direct hand of Allah and charged directly by Allah. Though the obligation was in two parts, the apparent weight of it lay in one matter: eating from wherever he wished is a matter for Adam's benefit, while "do not approach" is the single obligation.

Therefore the Truth said in another verse: ﴿"And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred."﴾ (20:121) This is disobedience, because it was forgetting one matter, which it was not proper for him to forget, given that it was singular and not multiple. And the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿"Or you should say, 'Indeed, our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?'"﴾ (7:173)

This statement came to alert us that heedlessness must not become a model, because obligations are burdensome, and a person may become forgetful of them, and this forgetfulness is then inherited by later generations, so the children say: ﴿"Or you should say, 'Indeed, our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?'"﴾

This indicates that their faith is the faith of imitators, even though the Truth had sent them the message; and if the fathers, by their method, nullified the message, it is not proper for the children to be heedless of sound faith.

(1) Narrated by Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban, and al-Daraqutni, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

And God, exalted is He, says after that: ﴿And thus do We detail the signs, so that they may return﴾.

The signs that God has detailed here are the particular covenants, and the lifting of the mountain so that they would take the Torah with strength, and likewise the general covenant in which all creation participated from the time of Adam until the Hour is established. He, glorified is He, brought all of that to confirm to them that the matter of faith (īmān) is a creed that must be at the core of consciousness. Whoever has been heedless should remember, and whoever has imitated his father in something contrary to the straight path should turn back from this imitation; for the obligations of faith are personal obligations, and He, glorified is He, does not charge you while you are in need of your father, or of your mother. Rather, He charges you after puberty (al-bulugh), because after puberty you are independent in your selfhood with complete independence, like your father. And as long as you have reached full manhood like your father and are capable of procreation, your father has no faith-based guardianship over you at all. So do not say, "I am imitating my father," even if he was not on the sound path; for such a statement could be acceptable if the obligation were addressed to a human being while in the stage of childhood, where he strives to feed and care for his children. But the obligation does not come to a person except after puberty, and the meaning of "after puberty" is that you are fit to beget someone like yourself and to take care of yourself.

Therefore, God, glorified and exalted is He, asks fathers to train their children and accustom them to what the obligation requires before the time of God's charge arrives. The Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, says: "Order your children to pray when they are seven years old, and strike them for neglecting it when they are ten years old, and separate them in their beds..." etc. (1). The father, then, commands and punishes before the time of obligation so that the children are trained in it and it becomes an easy practice from which a person does not tire after puberty.

﴿And thus do We detail the signs, so that they may return﴾. That is, the heedless one must turn back from his heedlessness and remember, and the one who imitates his fathers must turn back from imitation and become convinced by conviction, in confirmation of His words, the Truthful: ﴿No father will avail his son at all, nor will a son avail his father at all﴾ (from verse 33 of Surah Luqman).

(1) Narrated by Abu Dawud with a sound chain (Riyad al-Salihin, p. 181).

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who go astray.﴾

Because they said: ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of this﴾, Allah, glory be to Him, wants to give us the account of these people, so He says: ﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾.

Naba' (news) is important information that has a practical benefit and from which we can gain; it is not just any news. For this reason, Allah, glory be to Him, says about the Last Day: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ (Surah an-Naba').

He also says: ﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, as if this news was very well known. It is said that it was said about "Ibn Ba'ura'" or Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, or 'Amir the monk, or he is one of these. What matters is not his name; what matters is that a person to whom Allah gave His signs then detached himself from the signs. Instead of benefiting from them to protect himself and draw near to his Lord, ﴿he detached himself from them﴾, followed his desire and inclined toward Satan.

The word "insalakha" (detached himself) is evidence that the signs surround a person with a strong encompassing, to the degree that it takes a great act of disobedience for a person to be stripped away from them, because the original meaning of salkh is removing the skin of a sheep. It is as if our Lord clarifies that He, glory be to Him, gave the person the signs and he stripped himself of them. This means that the signs surround a person as the skin surrounds the body, to protect the general structure of the person, because this general structure contains arteries, veins, flesh, fat and bones. Allah made the commandments of faith a protection for the human being, and for this reason the one who goes outside the method of Allah is called "fasiq" (defiant), just like the ripe date (rutaba) of the palm fruit. After the sun strikes the unripe date, some of its water evaporates, the date shrivels inside its skin, and the ripe date appears separated from the skin. For this reason, the one who leaves the method is called "fasiq", from the separation (fusuq) of the ripe date from its skin. Allah, mighty and majestic, says here: ﴿We gave him Our signs﴾. He should not have been heedless of them, because the giving is a blessing that came so that the human being would preserve it, but the human being detached himself from the signs.

We all know the snake's skin, which is exactly the shape of the snake, and the snake changes its skin every period. It only sheds the old skin when the skin beneath it has matured and become fit to bear the climate and atmosphere. Likewise, when hot liquid spills on a person's skin, you notice the affected area swelling and some water forming in it. If a person drains this water, the area becomes infected, but if he leaves it, it protects the affected area until the skin beneath it grows, dries and separates from the body. Likewise, we know that a sheep, for example, does not skin itself; rather, we skin it. And Almighty Allah says: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ (part of verse 37, Surah Ya-Sin).

So it is as if the night was a skin and was wrapped around by the day. The night is black, and the day contains light. We know that black is not one of the colours of the spectrum, and white is also not one of the colours of the spectrum, because the colours of the spectrum are: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. Black absorbs the colours of the spectrum and makes them invisible, because you do not see things unless rays from them reach your eyes. Black absorbs all the rays that come to it, so no ray returns to the eye and you see it as dark. White is a mixture of many colours which, if you mix them together, you can produce white. Thus we know that white is exactly like black: black absorbs the rays so no ray comes out to your eyes, and white reflects the rays so no ray comes out to your eyes. His saying, the Truth: ﴿We strip from it the day﴾ is as if the darkness of the night came wrapping the whiteness of the day.

When one to whom the news of faith came detaches himself from the method, Satan says: "He is suitable; he will not follow me." It is as if Satan, when he finds one in whom there is hope, runs after him, fearing that he will return to what Allah gave him of the Book that carries the method, and Satan beautifies in this person's soul the matter of departing from the method of our Lord.

We said before that sins come sometimes from the desire of the self (shahwat al-nafs), and sometimes from Satan's embellishment, and we clarified the difference. We said that Satan does not dare against you unless you show Satan through your conduct that he has hope in you. But if you are guided and reform your condition, Satan whispers to the person to disobey in obedience and tries to make him hate it. Satan does not go, for example, to the tavern; rather, he sits at the straight path to see the group of people heading toward good, while others have their souls ready for him. So when Satan sees someone who has begun to be heedless of the signs, he pursues him, fearing that the signs will attract him again. Therefore we must distinguish between the impulse to sin: is it from the self or from the prompting (nazgh) of Satan? If a sin comes and your self tells you to do it, then that sin is hindered for some sudden reason, and then the same sin insists on you a second time, know that it is the desire of your self. But if it is hindered for you and then you think of a second sin, this is a prompting from Satan, because Satan does not want you to be disobedient in a particular sin; rather, he wants you far from the method altogether. But the self wants a specific sin and stops at it. So if a sin stops your self at it, know that it is from your self. And if a sin was refused to you and you left it, then you thought of another sin, this is a prompting from Satan. The Truth says: ﴿So Satan pursued him, and he became of those who go astray﴾ (part of verse 175, Surah al-A'raf).

Al-ghawi and al-ghawiyy (one who goes astray) is the one who strays from the path, and is one who persists in error. We know that guidance is the path that leads to the goal, and whoever deviates from the path that leads to the goal goes astray or gets lost in the desert. This is what is called "al-ghawi", and as long as he is among those who go astray from Allah's method, corruption arises from him, because he has become corrupt in himself and corrupts others.

Then Allah says:

﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they may reflect.﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:176)

Here there are two matters. The first is *ar-rif'ah* (elevation), which means height and loftiness. The second, which follows it, is *al-ikhlad ila al-ard* (clinging to the earth), meaning descent to the lowest level. The two verbs are attributed to two different agents.

﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him﴾: the verb *rafa'a* (to elevate) here is ascribed to Allah. But he chose to cling to the earth. This is how it should be, because it is fitting that elevation be attributed to Allah, whereas descent cannot properly be attributed to Allah, since every act is by the command of the Owner of the universe. Our Lord elevates those who walk the path. When the Exalted and Glorified says ﴿Had We willed﴾, it means that the will is Ours. Had We wished to elevate him, the will would have been suitable, but this would diminish his choice, and Allah wants to leave man his choice. If he chooses what is right, welcome to him, and his reward is Paradise; but if he desires misguidance, he will surely meet the true punishment. For further reflection on the stories of the Qur'an, read with me the story of the righteous servant with Moses, peace be upon him:

﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us. Moses said to him, "May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, [as] guidance?"﴾ (Al-Kahf 18:65–66)

Although Moses was a messenger from Allah, he was not too proud to follow a servant of Allah who had drawn near to Allah, so Moses followed him to say: ﴿May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, [as] guidance?﴾

In this is an affirmation of Moses' desire to increase in knowledge from one whom Allah had given knowledge. The Qur'an brought this story to teach us the etiquette of learning.

And what did the righteous servant say? He excused Moses and said:

﴿He said, "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ (Al-Kahf 18:67–68)

That is, you, O Moses, will not be patient, not because of any deficiency in you, but because you will see matters whose inner realities you do not know. But Sayyidina Moses said to him: ﴿You will find me, God willing, patient﴾ (Al-Kahf 18:69), and Moses insisted on following the righteous servant and that he would not disobey him in any matter. The righteous servant stipulated that Sayyidina Moses should not ask him about anything until he himself informed him. All of this was merely theoretical talk, with give and take, but when reality came the situation changed completely. After they boarded the ship and the righteous servant damaged it, Sayyidina Moses could not be patient but said: ﴿You have certainly done a dreadful thing﴾ (from Al-Kahf 18:71).

Thus practical experience proved that Moses could not be patient with the deeds of the righteous servant. When the righteous servant reminded him of his promise not to ask, Moses retracted, the questioning recurred, and the reminders recurred, until the righteous servant clarified for Moses all the secrets of that which he did not encompass in knowledge. Here Allah says: ﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾. Why? Because Allah's will is absolute. He does what He wills. Yet He, glory be to Him, had already determined that choice carries its consequence, so He did not elevate him although he opposed Him, because this is the sunnah of Allah, and you will not find any change in the sunnah of Allah (Al-Fath 48:23). The sunnah of Allah is that whoever does a good deed, Allah rewards him for it, and whoever does evil, He punishes him. His will, glory be to Him, is absolute; none can repel His will, and none can challenge His judgment.

By the requirement of Allah's will, He punishes the guilty by His justice and rewards the obedient by His grace. He, glory be to Him, has absolute will; He is the Mighty, the Wise in every act.

﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire﴾ (from Al-A'raf 7:176).

And ﴿clung to the earth﴾ means that he chose to descend into the abyss, although Allah guided man and showed him the path of goodness to take, so that he would ascend to loftiness. Allah says: ﴿Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited for you"﴾ (from Al-An'am 6:151).

We err when we understand *ta'ala* ("come") merely as "approach." This is an incomplete understanding. It is a call to acceptance and to loftiness, because He, glory be to Him and exalted, legislates for us so that we do not adhere to the lower earthly path, but rise up and take the path of Allah, which guarantees us loftiness. It is as if He, glory be to Him, says: "Come, and rise up in taking your path from Allah, the Most High, and beware of taking your path from what humans have laid down that contradicts the law of Allah, for in that is descent and falling to the lowest depth."

﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾ (from Al-A'raf 7:176).

It is said: "I charged at the dog" (*hamaltu 'ala al-kalb*). When you are sitting and the dog approaches you, and you shout at it, drive it away and rebuke it, this is an explanation of His saying *tahmil 'alayhi* ("you chase it"), that is, you charge at it by driving it away or shouting at it. Therefore it pants. And if you leave the dog without charging at it by driving it away or shouting at it, it still pants, because its nature is that it always pants. This characteristic belongs to the dog alone: it always breathes rapidly with its tongue hanging out.

We know that animals do not pant except when they are frightened and run, to escape pain or torment pursued by another creature. When an animal runs, it needs energy, so the heart beats strongly to push blood, with its nourishment, to the whole body, and the heart must cooperate with the lungs, which supply the blood with air. We notice that a living creature, when sitting calmly, does not notice its breathing, but when it runs, it notices that the chest cavity, or the capacity of the chest, contracts and expands to draw in *al-oksijin* (oxygen) from the air and carry it to the blood in an amount suited to the new movement, so it tries to breathe more. Animals do not do this except when they are hungry, tired or agitated. But the dog alone does it, whether hungry or full, thirsty or not thirsty, chased or not chased; it pants always.

Why does Allah, glory be to Him, liken him to the panting dog? Because whoever appears in this image is always found to be despised, since he follows his desire and his appetites control him. When one of his appetites is fulfilled now, he wonders whether he will do the same tomorrow, and desire occupies all his time. Therefore he lives in constant distress, fearing that the pleasure will escape him or that he will escape the pleasure. His state becomes like that of the dog, panting whether safe or unsafe, hungry or not hungry, thirsty or not thirsty.

﴿So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they may reflect﴾ (from Al-A'raf 7:176).

Thus is the fate of one who denies the signs.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿So relate the stories﴾ makes clear to us that Allah does not want to teach us history, but teaches us how to draw a lesson from history. The evidence is that He repeats the story more than once, and each time the Exalted brings a new glimpse, to multiply the lessons contained in a single story. Had He wished to narrate history to us, He would have related its account once. In the Qur'an we find many stories of truth against falsehood, of the falsifiers against the believers, and of the obstinate against the messengers, because the story is a realistic matter, while the codifying of methods is a verbal matter. Glory be to Him, He wants to clarify for us the method suited to reality, because the reality of life gives the spoken story warmth and heat, so the method does not remain mere theoretical talk detached from reality.

Thus Allah, glory be to Him, has shown in this verse that He has sent down the knowledge of His method through the messengers to some of His creatures. Among them is one who first takes Allah's method by comprehension, and secondly employs what he has learned, and by this he rises from the logic of the earth to the logic of the heavens. Whoever Allah gives that method should not be permitted to abandon his ascent to the heavens in order to descend to the level of the earth. This is what humans do when they legislate for themselves, setting the systems of life according to their desires and their own arrangements, and abandon the method of Allah, who created and fashioned them and laid down for them the law of their preservation.

This theoretical talk has a real instance in the case of Ibn Ba'ura' (Bal'am ibn Ba'ura'), whom Allah gave knowledge, but he clung to the earth and did not follow what he knew, so he stripped himself from the method as a sheep is stripped of its skin. Concerning him the Truth said:

﴿So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾ (from Al-A'raf 7:176).

As for the one whom Allah wishes to raise to heaven through revelation and method but who then descends to the earth, the Exalted and Glorified depicts his state by the state of the dog, with the difference between the two: the dog pants by instinct. It is not blameworthy when it pants while being chased, nor when it pants while not being chased, for this is an instinct in it, and it is not blamed for this or that. But a human whom Allah has created with love of goodness and distinguished his instincts with a rational method that safeguards his movement, it is not right for him to do this, and you should not say: "What is the dog's fault in panting, and why is it used as an example of disbelief?" Because the dog does it by instinct, without obligation, so it does what it wills. But the human who has elevated himself by thought, and whom Allah distinguished by being able to choose among alternatives, is not permitted to reach this level. Such behavior in the dog is praiseworthy, since that is its nature. Beware of saying: "Why does our Lord give examples with things, and what is their fault?"

And the Truth, glory be to Him, is the one who said about the Jews:

﴿The example of those who were charged with the Torah and then did not carry it is like that of a donkey carrying volumes﴾ (Al-Jumu'ah 62:5).

Does the donkey, when it carries volumes, deserve blame because it does not understand what is in the volumes? The answer is no, because its task does not involve understanding and comprehending what is in the volumes; its task is only to carry what is upon it. It is as if the Truth says: "Do not be like the donkey, which is content with good merely by carrying it. Rather, I want you to carry the method and to benefit from the legislation it contains." So these examples are not a disparagement of the dog, nor of the donkey. They are a disparagement of whoever imitates them, because he has descended to a rank that Allah did not intend for him, while Allah intended the example in them to be drawn from something that is not blameworthy in itself, yet the blame falls on the human.

The person who does not follow Allah's method has an agitated movement in life, even if he is in blessing, because he is cut off from Allah. As long as he is cut off from Allah, you will find him constantly asking: "Will this blessing last for me or not?" He always lives in anxiety and terror, fearing that the blessing will escape him or that it will not endure for him. He is like the dog that pants when at rest and pants when weary.

﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they may reflect﴾.

Thus when Allah gives us an example from realistic examples in this man called "Ibn Ba'ura'," He gives us a reality of what actually happened.

That is, the one whom Allah wanted to elevate by the method of knowledge, but who then stripped himself from his religion, is like the people who denied the signs of Allah. You are not unique in this: Allah wants to elevate you by the method of heaven, while you cling to the earth. This happened with Ibn Ba'ura'. The word *mithl* ("example"), when you hear it, comes from the root *m-th-l*, and it is pronounced in the following way: either you pronounce it *mithl* (with a kasra on the *m* and a sukun on the *th*), or you pronounce it *mathal* (with a fatha on the *m* and the *th*). *Mithl*

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.﴾

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had already said of them earlier that they denied Our signs, and He struck for them the example of Ibn Ba'ura' (Ibn Ba'ura', a man well known in their days). But they surpassed Ibn Ba'ura', because he was one individual while they were a group. Therefore do not say that there is repetition in the matter, for the earlier example concerned one individual: he was given the signs of Allah and then slipped away from them, but they were a group. Thus their departure from the methodology makes their position even worse.

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾: "sa'a" (evil, ugly) means "qabuha" (became ugly). When we say "sa'a fulan," meaning "his affair became ugly," then which of his affairs is ugly? We say: "sa'a sihhatuhu" (his health became bad), meaning he became ill; or "sa'a halan" (his condition became bad), meaning he became poor; or "sa'a khuluqan" (his character became bad), meaning he became harsh. When you say "sa'a," this badness is general and has many aspects, and the matter requires specification.

"Sa'a mathalan" means it is bad in respect of the example. The example in itself does not become bad, because Allah, the Exalted, strikes examples for us. An example comes only to clarify, explain and make clear. The meaning here is: the condition of the people is evil as an example. Or, the people themselves are the ones who are evil, because when they denied the signs they wronged themselves. Their denial did not obstruct Allah's methodology on earth, nor did they obstruct anything in Allah's creation with their denial: the cosmos proceeds by His will and order, and the signs of the cosmos continue. Therefore their denial of Allah's signs will never harm anything at all. The loss falls only upon them. If the denial concerned the miraculous signs, the mention of the miracles has remained to this day, and they are the ones who lost. If they denied the signs of the methodology, they are also the ones who lost, and the miraculous or Qur'anic signs suffered no harm whatsoever. In this they wronged themselves, like the patient who does not heed the doctor's words: he harms himself, and the doctor is not harmed at all. Allah, glorified is He, has given us the methodology so that the movement of life may be set right by it. Whoever takes it benefits himself, and whoever does not take it will not harm Allah in the least.

So they wronged themselves, and whoever wrongs himself is the first enemy of himself, and he will not harm Allah at all, nor the Messenger, nor society.

﴿And they were wronging themselves﴾ (part of verse 177, Surat al-A'raf).

When you find a object of a verb placed before its verb, a grammatical rule, then know that there is what is called "qasr" (restriction, exclusivity) in the science of rhetoric (balaghah). We may say "yazlimuna anfusahum" (they wrong themselves), and it would be correct to add, "wa yazlimuna al-nas" (and they wrong people). But when we say "anfusahum yazlimun" (themselves they wrong), the meaning is that their wronging does not go beyond themselves, and the statement contains restriction and specification, just as we say: ﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after﴾, meaning that the command never extends to anything else.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 178:

The Lord, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided, and whomever He leaves astray, it is they who are the losers.﴾ (178)

This verse is the only one in which the Lord, glorified and exalted, uses the word "al-muhtadi" (the one guided) with a ya', whereas in several other verses the Lord uses the word "al-muhtad" without a ya'. Consider His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided﴾ (part of verse 97, surah al-Isra').

And the Truth says:

﴿So among them is one guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ (part of verse 26, surah al-Hadid).

Likewise the word comes without the ya' in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided, and whomever He leads astray, you will not find for him a protecting guide﴾ (part of verse 17, surah al-Kahf).

The dispute concerning the question of guidance and misguidance has existed since ancient times, and the remnants of this dispute still exist until now. We have clarified this question before, but we repeat it for emphasis and so that it settles in minds, because there is always someone who says: "If God is the Guide and the Misleader, then why does He punish me if I go astray?" This question has spread, and the orientalists and philosophers have taken it up, and its purpose is to find a justification for the disobedient soul that does not commit itself. We say to every disputant: Why do you restrict your objection to the matter of harm and punishment if you go astray? Why do you not mention the reward if you do good and believe? Your restricting yourself to the first and not the second is evidence that the guidance that came to you is a gain you have left, and you have taken up the matter in which there is harm. Only those who waste their own souls say such a thing.

We have previously cited many examples, so that we may distinguish in these matters between the disputants, because the aspect is separate for them. They have debated the question of "the creation of the acts of servants," and asked: Who created these acts? Did Allah create them, or does the servant create his own acts?

We ask: What is the act? It is the directing of energy to bring about an event. The energy of the hand is that it performs whatever work you want from it: you may strike a person with it, or lift a person lying on the ground with it, or pat an orphan with it.

So in the hand there is energy suitable for doing good and for doing evil. And at the moment you strike a person, what muscle do you move when the hand rises to strike? When you merely wish to strike, you strike, unlike the mechanical man when he lifts something: he has parts and buttons that operate, and all of them are machines.

And when you pat the shoulder of an orphan, what organs and apparatus do you move to perform this action? So God is the One who created in you the impulse to act. If you look at it this way, every act is from God, but directing the limb toward the act is the locus of responsibility.

Thus you are held accountable because you did it, not because you created it; for the Creator of acts is Allah, glorified and exalted, and you act merely by will and choice. Like the tongue, which has created energy for expressing what is in the soul: if you wish to say with it "There is no god but Allah," it is right, and it is likewise right for the atheist to say, God forbid, "There is no god." The tongue has not disobeyed in this nor in that.

So He who created the limb's capacity to act is Allah. And you direct the limb, so all acts are created by Allah, but the directing of energy to the act through inclination and choice comes from the servant. The Truth, glorified and exalted, guides everyone through the method, and whoever turns to it with the intention of faith, He helps him in that. Therefore it is not right for us to dispute a matter like this, asking who created the acts; rather we must define the acts, how they come into being, and what the role of the human being in them is; because we know that Allah may remove the energy of acting upon events, like one who wants to harm a person with his hand but is struck with paralysis so that he cannot raise his hand. Had he been the one who creates, he would have raised his hand and harmed whomever he wished, but he does not create the energy that produces the act.

On this basis, guidance is of two kinds: the guidance of indication (hidayat dalala), which is for everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, because the Truth does not indicate only to the believer, but indicates to both the believer and the unbeliever the faith in Him. Whoever turns toward faith in Him, the Truth, blessed and exalted, finds in him one worthy of help. So He takes him by the hand, assists him, makes faith light upon his heart, gives him energy to do good, expands his breast and eases his affair. And He, glorified, says:

﴿And fear Allah; and Allah teaches you﴾ (part of verse 282, surah al-Baqara).

The Lord, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And whomever He leaves astray, it is they who are the losers﴾ (part of verse 178, surah al-A'raf).

So if God has generalized a ruling and then particularized it, the particularization is what governs the generalization.

Our Lord, mighty and majestic, says: whomever He wills to guide, He, glorified and exalted, gives him guidance, and whomever He wills to be misguided, He increases in misguidance. He has made clear that whoever He wills to guide is guided, and this is help from Allah; the unbeliever is not guided, and likewise the wrongdoer and the defiantly disobedient, because He, glorified and exalted, has left each of them to his choice, and thus He withholds from them the guidance of help. We read in the Noble Qur'an what clarifies this matter. He, glorified, says:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ (part of verse 17, surah Fussilat).
