The guidance that was given to the people of Thamud was the guidance of indication, not the guidance of help.

He, glorified, says:

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their God-consciousness﴾ (verse 17, surah Muhammad).

That is, He, glorified, has increased those who chose guidance with help, and placed between them and the Fire a shield. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger:

﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ (part of verse 56, surah al-Qasas).

That is: you, O Muhammad, will not help anyone to obedience, because this is a matter that your Lord possesses.

He, glorified, says to His Messenger:

﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ (part of verse 52, surah al-Shura).

That is: you, O Muhammad, guide with the guidance of indication, by the method that Allah has sent down to you.

So if you see an act or event affirmed of one and denied of another, know that the aspect is separate, and the speech here is that of the Wise, the All-Knowing. Why does the Truth, glorified and exalted, say:

﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided, and whomever He leaves astray, it is they who are the losers﴾ (178) (surah al-A'raf)?

Because when the Truth, glorified and exalted, turns away from the help of His servant, the servant must face the movement of life alone, without support from his Creator, and lives in a state of being a lord to himself, whether in material ease or in hardship. This is if one considers that the world is everything; but if one adds to that his heedlessness that the world is a passage to the Hereafter, then the loss is indeed great.

And the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾

Dhara'a (ذرأ) means to scatter and spread. Allah, glorified and exalted, said at the beginning of Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And He spread from both of them many men and women﴾, and He also says: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾.

Here Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾ (part of verse 179, Surat al-A'raf).

We know that in the universe there are things that worship by their very nature, namely everything other than mankind and the jinn, because each of these two is within the sphere of choice. These are the ones our Lord speaks of in Surat ar-Rahman: ﴿We will attend to you, O two worlds﴾.

Dhara'na (ذرأنا) means We scattered, spread and multiplied. The word kathir (كثير, many) does not mean that its counterpart is few; a thing may be many and its counterpart also many. Allah, glorified and exalted, says in His Noble Book: ﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures﴾ (part of verse 18, Surat al-Hajj).

So all creatures, inanimate, plant and animal, prostrate to Allah and glorify Him. But the matter divides only among humans, for the Truth says in the same verse: ﴿And many among mankind, and many deserve the punishment﴾ (part of verse 18, Surat al-Hajj).

That is, there are many who prostrate and submit to Allah, and in contrast there are many who disbelieved, did not prostrate, and for whom the punishment is due. Since the Lord, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾.

A question may arise in minds: Are You, O Lord, the creator of them for Hell? What then can they do, and what power do they have, if You created them for that?

We say: No. Let us draw attention to the fact that in the language there is what is called "the lam of consequence" (لام العاقبة), which is what a matter ends up in, in a form different from what you intended and wanted. The purpose of creation is worship, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ (Surat adh-Dhariyat, 56).

The meaning of worship is obeying the command and refraining from what is forbidden, and the one commanded is capable of doing and of not doing. Worship therefore requires an obedient one and a disobedient one. I give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, and He is exalted above it: someone comes to you relating a fragment of a person's biography and says: Why does he take this hostile stance toward you? Is it not he whom you brought with you to employ? You reply: "I planted him so that he would uproot me." Was it at the time you brought him that you wanted him to uproot you? No. But the outcome and the end became thus.

Allah, glorified and exalted, did not create humans for the sake of Paradise and Fire. Rather, He, mighty and majestic, created them to worship Him. Some of them believed and did righteousness and so entered Paradise, and some disobeyed and so entered the Fire. This is called "the lam of consequence," meaning that what the matter came to is not what you intended from it. An example of this is when Allah, glorified, said to the mother of Musa: ﴿So when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾ (7). ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ (8) (part of verses 7 and 8, Surat al-Qasas).

Did the family of Pharaoh pick him up so that he would become an enemy to them? No, because Pharaoh's wife said: ﴿A delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us﴾ (part of verse 9, Surat al-Qasas).

So the reason for the picking up was that he would be a delight of the eye, but he ended up an enemy, and this is called, as I said, the lam of consequence.

Thus the cause of creation is not that many of the jinn and mankind should enter the Fire, in the saying of the Truth: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾.

Because the original cause of creation is worship, and worship requires an obedient one and a disobedient one; whoever obeys enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys enters the Fire. And to Allah belongs the highest likeness. I remind you of the example I gave before, when the Minister of Education asks the director of one of the schools or the dean of some faculty about the state of study and the students, and the dean or director says: We know well who deserves to fail and who deserves to succeed, and if you wish I will tell you about them and specify them. The dean or director did not say that because he controls the students' answers, but because he knows their conduct and where it leads them, and knowledge is an attribute of disclosure, not an attribute of influence.

On that basis, His saying: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾

means that We spread and scattered for Hell many of the jinn and mankind, those who turn away from Our method. Then the Truth gives the grounds for that, and they are, first: ﴿they have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ (part of verse 179, Surat al-A'raf).

Second: ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ (part of verse 179, Surat al-A'raf).

Third: ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ (part of verse 179, Surat al-A'raf).

One may say: If their hearts are created such that they do not understand, what is their fault? And as long as their eyes are created such that they do not see, what is their fault? Likewise, as long as the ears are created such that they do not hear, why are they punished? We say: No, Allah did not create them for punishment, but they were occupied with what took hold of them through their desires, and their minds came to think of nothing but that and plan only to obtain desire. Likewise the eyes see only what pleases them, and likewise the ears. Each of them sees other than the purpose of seeing and hears other than the purpose of hearing.

The difference between the understanding of the heart, the sight of the eye and the hearing of the ear: the understanding of the heart is grasping the matters at which perceptions arrive. We know that perceptions come through the five senses: we know that silk is soft by touch, we know that musk has a pleasant smell by smelling, and we know that honey is sweet in taste by tasting.

So each means of perception is among the sensibles, and after the sensibles form, the person possesses a scientific leaven in his heart, which matures to become a rational proposition, settled and accepted.

We all know that fire burns, because a person, the first time he touches fire, is stung, so he knows that fire burns, and perception turns into sensation and then into meaning. So information reaches the human soul through its faculties, the outward senses, and there are other senses not apparent, such as measuring the weight of things by carrying them. Scholars have noticed this and discovered a sense called the muscular sense (حاسة العضل), because when you carry something, the muscle strains more if the load is heavy.

When you see one person nearby and another far away, this is called the sense of distance (حاسة البعد), and likewise the sense of thickness (حاسة البين), by which you distinguish, for example, the thickness of cloth.

All the senses, then, nurture meanings in the human being, and when meanings are nurtured in the human soul, the propositions form that settle in the heart.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted, reminds His creatures of the favour that He taught them, saying: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the bellies of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts, that perhaps you would be thankful﴾ (78) (Surat an-Nahl).

Returning to the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted: ﴿they have hearts with which they do not understand﴾.

Understanding (fiqh) is comprehension, and comprehension becomes a weighted proposition at which conviction has arrived from the evident and the sensible. But these disbelievers see with their eyes only their own desires, and their ears hear only what pleases them, so they do not listen to guidance, nor do they turn to the signs by which they might infer the Creator, and so their hearts live without understanding. They therefore have hearts, eyes and ears, as evidenced by the fact that they understood with them, heard with them and saw with them the things that suit their deviation.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, describes them, saying: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾

Here is a pause to raise a question: What is the fault of the livestock to which the disbelievers are likened? Livestock are not charged with duties, and none of them has a heart that understands or an eye that perceives the signs of Allah or ears that hear the signs of Allah. They merely see pasture and go to it, see the wolf and flee from it, and become accustomed to sounds that move them. All animals live by the mechanism of instinct, and the animal is guided to what benefits it and what harms it by the instinct that Allah placed in it, not by reason.

A human does not keep away from harm except when he experiences it and finds harm in it. But the animal keeps away from harm without experience, purely by instinct, because the animal has no reason, and likewise it has no capacity to choose between alternatives. Allah created it with an instinct that directs it to suitable necessities. An example: an animal may be found in some environment, and Allah gives it a colour resembling that environment to protect itself from animals stronger than it.

Another example: we know that the animal was created to benefit humans, and it must reproduce so that its offspring supply what humans need. The animal performs the sexual act as a means of reproduction, not as it is in humans, where it sometimes becomes an end in itself, besides being a means of offspring. For this reason we find many aspects of human life that humans have learned from animals, as the Truth, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the body of his brother﴾ (part of verse 31, Surat al-Ma'idah).

So the crow is guided by its instinct to all its requirements. For this reason some say: How do we liken the misguided to livestock? We say: The misguided differs from livestock in that he possesses choice and has been elevated above livestock, but he has placed himself in the position of livestock by not using reason to choose among alternatives. Thereby he became more astray than livestock. The word "more astray" (أضل) shows us that livestock are not astray, because they are governed by instinct and have no choice in anything. But the disbelievers whom our Lord created for Hell, from the jinn and mankind, do not know their Lord, whereas livestock, inanimate things and plants know their Lord, because the Truth says: ﴿And there is not a thing but it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their exaltation﴾ (part of verse 44, Surat al-Isra').

So livestock know our Lord and glorify Him and praise Him. In another verse the Lord, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ (part of verse 41, Surat an-Nur).

On that basis, all inanimate things know their prayer and their glorification.

For this reason we relate a story from among those who know Allah, when they sit with one another as a means of stimulating one another toward lofty goals and aims. The knower of Allah among these righteous people greets one who is better than him in worship with laughter, but greets one who is better than him in worldly matters with a frown. One of them said to another: Do you long for your Lord? He replied: No.

The other asked: How can you say that? He said to him: Yes. One longs only for the absent.

﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾ (part of verse 179, Surat al-A'raf)

And do not suppose that their straying is due to lack of a method, or lack of a reminder, or lack of a warner or a bearer of good news. Rather, it is heedlessness on their part, for the matters are clear before them, but they neglect them and are unmindful of them.

And the Exalted says after that: ﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾ (Qur'an 7:180).

When the Lord, glory be to Him, says ﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names﴾, we say: there is no name for anyone other than Allah that is described as being among the most beautiful. If you say of a human being that he is "generous" (karim), that is a description, and likewise if you say he is "forbearing" (halim). These are accidental attributes in a created being, and they do not become "most beautiful names" unless they are attributed to Allah. For example, you have a power by which you perform many actions, and Allah has power, but your power is created and contingent, as proof of which it can be taken from you so that you become incapable, whereas the power of Allah, exalted is He, has an absoluteness that nothing limits. His power is absolute. You may be wealthy, you have wealth, and Allah has wealth, but your riches are limited, whereas the richness of Allah is not limited. So the most beautiful names in their absolute sense belong to Allah, and if they are found in other than Him, they become limited attributes, however far they may extend.

﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾: "al-husna" is the feminine of "al-ahsan," an elative form, and it refers to the names that are fitting for divinity and suitable for the attribute of lordship. When you say of Him, glory be to Him, that He is "Merciful" (rahim), this is a good thing in my view and in yours, because I look at His mercy toward me, and you look at His mercy toward you. When you say "Forgiving" (ghaffar), you, I, and everyone who hears us benefit from it. When we say "Subduer" (qahhar), you will fear if you are sinful, and this is a most beautiful name in relation to the Deity, because the Deity must have attributes of beauty and attributes of majesty. The attributes of beauty belong to the one who obeys, and the attributes of majesty belong to the one who disobeys. Therefore do not take the blessings according to their meaning for you, but take the blessings according to what Allah intends by them.

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, speaks saying: ﴿We will attend to you, O you two burdens (ath-thaqalan), so which of the favours of your Lord will you deny? O company of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority. So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny? There will be sent against you a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be helped. So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (Qur'an 55:31–36, Surat ar-Rahman).

Is the sending of a flame of fire and molten brass a favour, after which He says: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾?

We say: yes, it is a great favour, because He, glory be to Him, warns us before the fire exists, that the fire is powerful, and He gives you the favour of admonition and taking heed. His admonition and warning before the fire exists is therefore a great favour. It is also a favour in relation to the opposite: when the believers obey Him in this world and bind themselves to the way of Allah, they have the reward of fulfilling the obligation, while for those who did not commit themselves and took deviation from the way as their aim, He threatens them with punishment, and this is a great favour.

﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾: the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has made us know His name through His own communication, because we may know its referent (musamma) through the powerful faculties that are known through reason, but reason cannot know the name. I have said before: suppose some people are sitting in a room and then a knock is heard at the door. Here all agree that someone is knocking at the door, but when they begin to imagine, they differ. One says the visitor is a man; the other replies, no, it is a woman, because the knock is light. A third says this knock on the door comes from above and is a sign that the visitor is large, and it is a warning because he knocks forcefully. Each person present has a different conception of the visitor, and none knows his name. So when you want to know who the visitor is, you ask him: who are you? And he tells you his name.

Thus the name is not grasped by reason. Whoever created all creation is powerful, capable, wise, and knowing, because the process of creation requires all of this. But the name of Allah is a matter that reason does not know and that requires revelation (tawqif). Therefore the names of Allah, blessed and exalted, are tawqifi: when He tells us, "these are My names," we call upon Him by them, and what He has not told us, we have no basis to call upon Him by. That is why He, exalted, says: ﴿so call upon Him by them﴾.

If you transfer this to other than Him, you are calling upon other than Allah by the most beautiful names. For example, the liar of al-Yamama, Musaylima, named himself "al-Rahman," and by doing so he deviated concerning the name of Allah, transferring one of the names of our Lord to his own self. Others did likewise. Did they not name "al-Lat" from Allah? Did they not name "al-Uzza" from al-Aziz? Did they not name "Manat" from al-Mannan? All of these deviated concerning the names of Allah, which we do not call upon other than Him by. That is why the Prophet (ﷺ) is reported to have said in his supplication: "O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment over me is forever executed, and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that You have, which You named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the dispelling of my sorrow, and the removal of my grief and anguish."(1)

So these names our Lord has assigned to Himself, because they are not known through reason. As for the creative attributes of creation, you come to know these attributes, because He, exalted, created the universe with wisdom, planning, and power. I will give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: we establish many large factories to manufacture light bulbs. We make glass and evacuate it of air, and place inside it filaments that withstand the vibration of electricity. After these bulbs are used for a period they break, whereas the sun has lit the universe throughout this whole span, from the beginning of creation, and does not need from us a spare part.

When we say He is "Wise" (hakim), we say it and see the effect of that in the movement of the planets, which move in harmony, each planet revolving in its orbit without colliding with another. This is evidence that the planets were created with wisdom.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, alerts us to call upon Him by the most beautiful names in His saying: ﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾, because He wants His creation always to remember Him, for He is the Lord who created from nothing and sustained from non-existence, who preserved creation through His self-subsistence (qayyumiyya). When a need comes upon you, you must mention Allah's most beautiful names and call upon Allah by them. When you want to draw near to Allah, do not call upon Him except by the name He assigned to Himself, which is "Allah," because this is the proper name (ism 'alam) denoting the Necessarily Existent (wajib al-wujud). The most beautiful names of Allah are all attributes that have reached the rank of names, and there are names that denote the totality of attributes.

To give a parallel, exalted be the example: you say "Zayd," and the listener knows this is a proper name for a person called Zayd, who also has other attributes, such as being a merchant, a learned scholar in knowledge, or an engineer. The proper name is Zayd, which none of your acquaintances shares with him in this, but the other attributes may be shared with him by others.

The names of Allah are of two kinds: a name that denotes the Essence of Allah, the bare Essence free of anything, which is "Allah"; and attributes of Allah such as al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Malik, al-Quddus, al-Salam, al-Mu'min, and al-Muhaymin. These are attributes that have risen to a loftiness and elevation beyond which there is none, so that when they are applied absolutely, in the sense of the highest perfection, they refer only to Allah. Thus they have become names.

We may say of someone "he is rich," "he is generous," "he is wise," but richness in its absolute sense belongs to Allah, exalted is He.

The most beautiful names arise from attributes intensified in their elevation, because He, glory be to Him, is the most perfect in them. They are originally attributes that have actional correlates (muta'allaqat fi'liyya), and these are of two kinds: one kind is applied to Allah with a name and its opposite, and another kind is applied to Him as a name without its opposite being applied. We form an attribute resembling derivation: we say "Ghani" (the Self-Sufficient), and we say "Mughni" (the Enricher). He is Ghani in the attribute of His essence before any who might be enriched exists, and Mughni is after the existence of those among His servants whom He enriches. Likewise He is Hayy (Living) in His essence, and Muhyi (Giver of Life) to others, and giving life is an action-attribute with respect to another. It necessarily has an opposite: we say Muhyi and Mumit (the Causer of Death), and we do not say Hayy and its opposite. So a name for which you see an opposite is one of the attributes of action, whereas the attributes of essence are those that have no opposite.

They "deviate concerning the names of Allah" (yulhidun fi asma' Allah), meaning they incline them toward other than Allah: one of them transfers a name of Allah to other than Allah, or brings a name belonging to another and applies it to Allah, or applies to Allah a name that has no meaning, or whose meaning is not understood, upon Allah. So "ilhad" occurs in three things: either one transfers one of Allah's names to other than Allah, or brings a name for another and applies it to Allah, or applies to Allah a name that Allah has not sent down through revelation (tawqif).

﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names; they will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾: We know that "'amal" (deed) is a term for an event from any organ. The utterance of the tongue is an deed, the smelling of the nose is a deed. We know that there is what is called [qawl (speech) and fi'l (act)]: act is the deed of the limbs other than the tongue, and speech is the deed of the tongue, and both are called deed. That is why the Truth, blessed and exalted, says in Surat as-Saff: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾

Thus speech stands in contrast to act, and the recompense here is for act and speech, because both are deeds.

If Allah has many names, may we take from one of His acts a name for Him? Especially since He says: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾ (Qur'an 2:31), and He also says: ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾ (Qur'an 4:113).

Can we say that Allah is "Mu'allim" (the Teacher)? And may we take from His saying: ﴿And I plan a plan﴾ (Qur'an 86:15) a name: "Kaid" (the Planner)?

This is not permissible, because the names of Allah are tawqifi. If you see an act attributed to Allah, stop at the act only, and do not take from it a name for Allah, exalted is He.

(1) Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, and by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 181:

The Truth (Allah) says after that: ﴿And among those whom We have created is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice.﴾

After He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾, He wished to reassure the people of Allah's method, so He did not say "all people" but "many of the jinn and mankind." We know that the opposite will also be many, by the evidence of His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Hajj: ﴿And many among mankind [prostrate to Allah], and many deserve the punishment﴾, meaning: many people prostrate to Allah, and many are those upon whom the punishment is due.

The saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And among those whom We have created is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice﴾ (Surat al-A'raf) means:

That Allah does not leave the earth without guiding guides who are guided, so that the behavioural model in society continues. The behavioural model in society is what shapes the beliefs of children. The small child does not know how to pray, nor how to fast, nor does he distinguish between lying and truthfulness, but he learns by imitating his parents. When a child sees his father and mother, at the time the call to prayer is made, each of them rises to perform ablution and pray, here the child learns how to pray. And when a person speaks about the conduct of another, the father and mother say: there is no need to delve into the conduct of others, lest we nullify our good deeds. Thereby the child learns how to guard his tongue from delving into the conduct of others, because the behavioural model seeps into him. This is evidenced by the fact that the small child who has not reached the level of understanding, when he hears the muezzin afterwards, rises of his own accord to bring the prayer mat and imitates his father and mother.

From His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and by it dispense justice﴾, we understand that in their judgments on things they establish justice through the truth. Or justice may mean the negation of association (shirk), or it may be justice in the matter of major sins, or they establish justice in the matter of rights between people.

﴿And among those whom We have created a community﴾: His saying in the noble verse, "community" (umma), means that the qualities of methodological perfection are too many for one person to embody them all, so each one has a part he carries. There is one who is distinguished by truthfulness, another by courage, a third by generosity, and so on; the model thus remains in the totality of good qualities. Allah distinguished our master Abraham over our Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community (ummatan), devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 120). That is, he combined the virtues of good that are found only in a broad society. ﴿And among those whom We have created is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice﴾: And which community of the earth's nations, then, is the one that guides by the truth? He, glory be to Him, has already spoken of the people of Musa!

﴿And among the people of Musa is a community that guides by the truth﴾ (part of verse 159, Surat al-A'raf).

Then came the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and there is no messenger after him, therefore this Muslim community remains entrusted with preserving the method of Allah until the Hour is established.

So if you see atheism spreading, know that Allah has a supply (of help), and whenever people increase in atheism, Allah increases the supply. Even if a Muslim country becomes immersed in wickedness, there may be one person who combines all these noble qualities that guide to the truth, so that the law of Allah remains preserved by the behaviourally exemplary who follow the method of Allah.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has left corruption to produce evil. And a questioner may ask: what is the necessity of this evil in a creation that Allah has made in a sound form? We say: were it not that people are harmed by evil, they would not have become aware of the sweetness of good; and if a person had not been harmed by the people of falsehood, no one would have been zealous for the truth, nor would people have recognised the necessity for truth to be rooted in existence. So evil, then, has a message in existence: that it stirs one towards good. Just as Allah created many of the jinn and mankind for Hell, He, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear in His saying: ﴿And among those whom We have created is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice﴾ in judgment, justice at the summit; which is that they do not associate anything with Allah, because the first violation of the principle of justice is the violation of shirk, and it is a great wrong, for shirk, we seek refuge in Allah, transfers a matter from its rightful place to other than its rightful place. Likewise forbidding what Allah has made lawful, or making lawful what Allah has forbidden; all of that is wrong. Likewise failing to maintain balance in the rights among people: if justice is not safeguarded by protecting the rights of people from a ruler, a guardian, or an oppressor, you will find every person, grudging his effort in life, content to produce only according to his need, so that he does not leave the oppressor anything to take from him; he moves in life only in a limited movement and works only to the extent that suffices him. When that happens, the weak who cannot engage in productive activity will find no surplus to live on.

Thus Allah willed to guarantee through justice the sweat and toil of each person. He made clear to him that what you earn lawfully is your property, but God has a right in it, and the remainder is yours, so that the weak one who cannot move in life may find his sustenance. Therefore the faith-based method warns you: beware of thinking it too much to give to the weak, for the strength you used in acquiring this wealth is an accident that will not last for you; if we take from you while you are strong and able to move, we will take for you when you are incapable and unable to move. That is insurance and justice.

As for the community in that verse, ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice﴾:

It has come in the traditions (al-athar) that the intended community in this verse is the Muhammadan community. Qatada said: It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say, when he recited this verse: "This is for you, and the people before you were given something like it: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice﴾" (1). The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed his companions with the words: "This is for you," meaning within your community. This is confirmed by the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong﴾ (part of verse 110, Surat Al 'Imran).

The word "for mankind" here indicates that Allah did not make the excellence of the Muhammadan community, which is the community of response, for believers only, but made its excellence for all people, its believers and its disbelievers alike.

﴿And among those whom We have created is a community﴾: The word "community" is mentioned because the qualities of good cannot all be gathered in one person; rather each one takes a touch of good. This one has intelligence, that one has courage, another has wealth, and another has character. It is as if the Muhammadan community has, among its individuals, what gathers the good gifts suitable for vicegerency on the earth.

(1) Tafsir Ibn Kathir, vol. 2, and al-Tabari, vol. 6.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) follows this with its counterpart, because placing a thing beside its opposite makes it more firmly settled in the soul. So He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, We will lead them step by step from where they do not know.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 7:182)

These are the counterparts of those whom God created as a community (ummah) that guides by the truth and by it dispenses justice. The word "ayat" (signs) is the plural of "ayah." We have said that the signs in the cosmos are of three kinds. First, signs you contemplate so that you may be guided by them to the One who made this cosmos, with its vast expanse, its precise exactness, and its perfect firmness: signs that strike you, such as the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Second, signs that break the ordinary order of the cosmos to confirm the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from God. Third, Qur'anic verses that carry God's method (manhaj). Those who denied God's cosmic signs, and did not take heed from them, nor drew from them the existence of a Mighty, Capable, Wise God, and who denied the miraculous signs that attest to the truth of prophethood, likewise denied the verses of the Qur'an, so they did not act upon them and did not hold fast to them. These people will receive the judgment of God. Therefore, the Truth will not merely admit them to the Fire; rather, they will have a punishment nearer than that in this world, because if the entire matter were deferred to the Hereafter, the transgression of the wrongdoer who does not believe in the Hereafter would run rampant. But whoever believes in the Hereafter is the one who will live in the cosmos with the courtesy of faith, and whose movement will be beautiful and in harmony with the method, unlike one who rampages through the cosmos. Therefore, punishment must come to whoever rampages through the cosmos during the life of this world. And the One, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong is a punishment short of that﴾ (part of verse 47, Surah al-Tur): that is, they have a punishment before the Hereafter.

Then the Truth says, concerning the punishment in this world:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, We will lead them step by step from where they do not know.﴾

When you say, "I istadraj-ed so-and-so" (I drew him on gradually), you mean that you began to maneuver against him until he confessed to what he had done, like a public prosecutor who investigates a criminal and besieges him with questions from here and from there until he admits and confesses; this is istidraj. The word "istidraj" derives from "darj" (a stairway), which we call in our everyday language "al-sullam" (the ladder), and it is a means of moving from below to above and from above to below. It is impossible for a person to leap in one step to, say, the fifth floor of a building; therefore they designed ascent by steps to multiple levels in accordance with the natural movement of the soul. Some make the height of each step, for example, twelve centimetres, so that every person can raise his foot and place it on the staircase without exhausting himself. This means that we draw the height step by step in order to reach it or to descend from it.

In the Hereafter they have specified the highest levels (darajat) for Paradise and the lowest depths (darakat) for the Fire.

Here the Truth says:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, We will lead them step by step from where they do not know.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 7:182)

That is, We take them degree by degree, We grant them blessing, and then We overwhelm them with what they have reached, as He, glory be to Him, said earlier:

﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly.﴾ (part of verse 44, Surah al-An'am)

For when God wishes to punish someone in this world in proportion to his crime against his fellow human being, He seizes him from the very first offence, because a seizing in this manner would be gentle; but He gives him respite, raises him up, and then casts him down from on high.

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly.﴾ (part of verse 44, Surah al-An'am)

Thus the seizing is the seizing of the Mighty, the All-Powerful.

When humans practice istidraj, the one being led on is also clever and knows that this is a kind of scheming and a trap set for him; but when it is our Mighty, Powerful Lord who leads step by step, no one will know how to escape. The reason in His words "We will lead them step by step" is His words "from where they do not know," because humans know the methods by which some lead others on.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 7, verse 183:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾

Al-imla' (giving respite) is al-imhal (granting time), that is, delay. This means He does not seize them all at once. At times the corrupt person does much evil in society, and we find the people of goodness increasing in good deeds. We always hear someone say: "If there were no faith, people would devour one another," for faith gives solace and certainty. The respite granted to the wrongdoing disbeliever is not neglect on the part of the Master (al-Mawla), exalted is He, but only a granting of time. Then Allah seizes him with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. Here the Truth makes clear: if I am going to draw them on gradually and grant them respite, then know that My plan (kayd) is firm. Al-kayd is al-makr (scheming), and makr is seizing them from where they do not perceive, a hidden process that harms the one plotted against.

It is a hidden arrangement so that the one plotted against does not possess the means of defense. If human beings scheme and plan in a way that is hidden from some of them, then what of when God plans a stratagem or scheme against the disbelievers? Can anyone uncover anything of it? Of course, no one can. This is the meaning of ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾. Matin (firm) means strong, and matana (firmness) is derived from al-matn, which is the back. We know that the back is composed of a spinal column and bony vertebrae surrounded by muscles. Were the spinal column only bone, any load upon it would break it. So the manifestations of our Lord, mighty and majestic, willed, and His mercy and power required, that these bones be surrounded by two large muscles, which we call in the terminology of butchers the "filet," to protect, strengthen and shield the back.

When we look at the word "matin," we find that al-matn is the upright part of things. In knowledge, for example, we study fiqh and we study grammar, and it is said: "This is the matn in fiqh," meaning the concise text that condenses the knowledge into specific words, and the student (al-kayyis, the one who absorbs it) is the one who comprehends it. Often we find with the concise matn an explanation of the matn (sharh), and then a marginal gloss (hashiyah) on the matn.

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner.﴾ (7:184)

Here Allah, glorified and exalted, calls all creation to reflect on the matter of the Messenger who conveys what the Supreme Power wills for mankind. The first thing deserving of reflection is whether this man who claims to be a Messenger is truthful or not. The truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was established before the revelation came to him, and the message came to lead people by the hand to faith in Allah. But they do not want to listen, so that they may create for themselves pretexts for turning away from the method. Some of them accused the Messenger, saying: "He is mad," just as some had said before: "He is a magician and a soothsayer," and they said: "He is a poet." Our Lord responds to all these claims.

We ask: who is the madman?

We know that the madman is one who has lost the mental balance needed to choose between alternatives. When Allah takes from him this capacity for mental balance, he becomes unfit for legal responsibility (taklif), because taklif involves choosing whether to do this or to do that, and the madman does not possess the ability to make this decision.

Allah, the Truth, does not impose taklif on a person except when he reaches maturity and has reason, because when he reaches maturity he acquires an individuality independent of his family, his father and his mother. Therefore we observe a small child, whose father or mother chooses his clothing and food, and after he grows up we find that the child has become an adolescent who rebels and decides to choose for himself what he wants, because he has acquired individuality. Individuality, as we know, exists in plants, in animals and in humans, as soon as the individual becomes capable of producing its like, whether that individual is a plant, an animal or a human. But if a human has acquired individuality in reproduction and offspring, yet does not have a successful, rational individuality in thinking, then taklif falls from him, because he is compelled by the loss of reason.

Thus we know that taklif falls from one who has not reached maturity, and from the madman and the one under compulsion who is overpowered by something stronger than him. This is the justice of the recompense from the Truth. Thus we find that taklif applies only to one whose body has matured and whose reason has ripened, and by this our Lord guards the universe through His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah).

If the madman is one who lacks the mental balance by which one chooses between alternatives, how then can they say this about our master Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, who lived among them and was never at all lacking the balance for choosing between alternatives? Rather, they used to regard him as the truthful and trustworthy (al-Sadiq al-Amin), and they used to keep with him every precious thing they had, even while they disbelieved in him. His noble character is continuous and enduring.

They said this about Muhammad unjustly, and out of clamour and mob-like noise, and each one throws out an accusation that has no share of reality. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, said to the makers of these accusations:

﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.﴾ (34:46)

That is, let each two people sit together and study: is Muhammad rational or mad? Each of them will find, from the reality of his own experience, that Muhammad is the most trustworthy of people, and everyone called him "the Trustworthy" even before revelation reached him. It is not reasonable that revelation would harm him or that through revelation he would lose his moral balance. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, said:

﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed you are of a great character.﴾ (68:1–4)

The character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a great character, because character consists of the qualities that qualify a person to live in a sound and peaceful society. And since his character was sound, his standard of judgment was sound.

After that they said of him that he is a "magician." We say to these people: then why did he not bewitch the great men of Quraysh so that they would believe in his message? All of that is vain argument, and there is no magic in the matter at all.

﴿Have they not reflected on their companion? There is no madness in him; he is only a clear warner.﴾ The madness you speak of and slander the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with is the utmost of reason and the utmost of character. Muhammad (ﷺ) is a clear warner: he came to you first with good tidings, but in your error you do not heed the good tidings, and instead you deserve the warning.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿Do they not look into the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth, and at everything that Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has drawn near? So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾ (7:185)

Thereby the argument moves from the direct messenger to them, who takes them by the hand toward the higher faith. The argument moves to reflection (tafakkur) and its responsibility: ﴿Do they not look into the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.

Reflection is the exercise of the intellect, so that no one says: "The Messenger of Allah is mad." For mere contemplation of the cosmos makes a person see the sky raised without pillars, the earth spread out, and the air moving with precise regularity.

﴿Do they not look into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾

So above us is a sky, and there is what is beyond the sky; below us is the earth, and there is what is beneath the earth; and there is what lies between the heavens and the earth. What we see on the surface is what they call "mulk" (dominion). As for what is hidden from you, which you cannot reach by equations through which results are extracted, it is called "malakut."

And He, glorified is He, says concerning our master Abraham: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the malakut of the heavens and the earth﴾ (part of verse 75, surah al-An'am).

The word "malakut" means an intensification of "mulk," like rahabut, meaning intense awe, and rahamut, meaning intense mercy; all of them are the form "fa'alut," which is the form of intensification.

﴿Do they not look into the dominion of the heavens and the earth and at everything that Allah has created?﴾

We see the heavens and the earth clearly, but greatness and mystery are not in the heavens and the earth alone. Rather, there are very fine things, so subtle that they cannot be perceived by sight, and yet in them lies the supreme wisdom of creation. You may see the famous "Big Ben" clock in London, which is almost the largest clock in the world, but the skilled human craftsman has made a small wristwatch the size of a ring, and we are amazed and marvel at the precision of his work and craft. How much more so the Greatest Creator, who magnifies His creation of the heavens and the earth because they are beyond human comprehension, and who has also created fine, subtle creatures that you cannot perceive merely by looking, such as the microbe, or perceive only with difficulty, such as the fly and the mosquito. Every one of these creatures has all the essentials of its life: even the creature that has no stomach is equipped by its Creator with the ability to draw blood directly, by its mind or its instinct, and it strives to eat and fill its belly, and it has systems that convert its food into blood.

Thus greatness is not confined to the creation of the heavens and the earth alone. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿and at everything that Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has drawn near? So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾: that is, from the very first thing that is called "a thing" (shay'), it became existentially subject to judgment. If you look at it, you will find the systems that give it life and help it, even if they are sensory perceptions within this creature's very being, which the possessor of intellect cannot master. An example of this: what flees before earthquakes is the donkey, which we accuse of stupidity.

When the intellect reflects on what science has reached in the study of the animal world and the world of the seas, it will find faith in the necessity of the existence of a wise Creator. And if the disbelievers are turned away from looking into the malakut of the heavens and the earth and into what Allah has created of creatures that the naked eye may not see, they should have considered their own interest, for perhaps their term has drawn near.

We know that man is a genus, and that it has two types: a male type and a female type, while there is an ambiguous genus we call the khuntha (hermaphrodite), and genera have multiple individuals. Each one has a creation, each one has a talent, each one has a mission. The Truth asks of us at every moment: beware of belittling anything of yourself against others, and beware of overvaluing anything of yourself for others. You must make the word "shay'" (thing) this measure. For this reason the Law tells you that when you do a good deed, beware of magnifying it; rather say, it is not a thing of significance. And if someone resolves to commit a sin, let him not say: "What can one sin do to me?", belittling that sin. We say to him: No, because the word "shay'" must govern the cosmos. If you look at this matter, you may find a person of slight build and no physical stature, yet who may have a great talent, and you may find another person of sturdy build who has no talent at all; for God may give the slight person profound thought, or great cunning, or a special gift in some field. So do not look at the little in any person, but look at the beautiful thing in him, which is hidden from you within himself.

﴿and that perhaps their term has drawn near; so in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾

And why does the mention of the drawing near of the term come here? In answer I say: it is very important, because as long as we are individuals, two or three genera, and our Lord has said of us that we are successors on the earth, we must know that the successor on the earth came to succeed those who went before him. Our Lord may cause any person to die at the age of a month or a year, or two years or fifty years, because age, for each person, is a matter that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has reserved for Himself, and no one knows it; for the goal of equals must be equal. As an example: if we asked students of the Faculty of Law about their aim in studying law, they would say: to obtain the licence degree. Among them you will find tall and short, white and black, intelligent and dull, strong and weak, and they agree on nothing except studying law. Likewise we are not all equal as human beings except before death: there is one who dies in his mother's womb, one who dies as a child, and one who dies as a youth. Whatever differences remain after that, the believer and the disbeliever both see these events before them and cannot say: "No, I will not die."

And since you will die, look to your own interest, so that you may be rewarded for what you did in this world rather than punished; perhaps your term has drawn near while you do not know when the term will come. And Allah's concealment of the term from us is a means of making the term known in general, and concealment is the clearest form of clarification: when our Lord wishes to make a matter fully clear, He makes it ambiguous.

An example of this: if God had given death a fixed age, the matter would be determined with no hope. But He, glorified is He, has not given death a fixed age or cause, and has made it general across every time, so that a person is liable to meet death at any moment. The descent of death is not contingent on a cause: it may come with a cause and it may come without one. Since a person meets death at any time, the disobedient should not meet death while in disobedience to God.

And beware of saying: "How did so-and-so die when he was not sick?" For there are many causes of death, and know that death without apparent causes is itself the cause. The person whom we lose through death has died because his term has ended. And the Truth here makes clear: O disbelievers, do you not know that among you is one who died at the age of one year, and one who died at the age of two years, and one who died at three years old, and one who died as a wrongdoer, and one who died as one wronged? And if there were no second life, what would this life be worth? And what is the fault of the one who lived in this world only a month? There must then be known to you another end awaiting you: individual ends, which are the terms of people in their own persons, and collective terms, represented by the Day of Resurrection.

And in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾

Al-Sha'rawi explains that Allah, the Exalted, makes clear: if this revelation that We sent down to them, with all its inimitability and originality, and which gathers every kind of perfection, then what more do they want?

Is there happiness for them in following their desires and in their legislating for one another? On the contrary, they are made wretched by it. It was incumbent upon them to show proper courtesy towards Allah and towards the Messenger.

For this reason, He, glory be to Him, says:
﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ (7:186)

Allah has repeated this warning many times, because the matters in which the intellect may stall, or which the currents of life may carry it away from, are repeated by Allah so that they remain at the centre of attention at all times; perhaps this repetition will meet an awareness in the listener. Look at how the Truth enumerates His blessings in Surat ar-Rahman, saying after each blessing:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

He repeats the mention of the blessings so that the matter becomes firmly fixed in the mind of the listener.

﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him.﴾ Glory be to Him, He does not compel anyone to be guided. If one is guided, it is for his own self; and if he is not guided, let him taste the bitterness of misguidance.

We all know that a physician prescribes a course of treatment for the patient so that recovery is achieved by the permission of Allah. The medicine is, then, a means to wellbeing. If the patient refuses to take the medicine, is that an offence against the physician? No. Likewise is the method of Allah.

﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him.﴾ But does Allah desire misguidance for anyone? No. Rather, He, glory be to Him, has called all people to the guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala), so whoever is guided, He increases him in the guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'huna), and whoever goes astray, let him go to disbelief as he wills. For this reason the Shari'a tells us: beware of associating anything with Allah in any deed, because our Lord says to us in the sacred hadith which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates to us from his Lord, saying: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association."(1)

The meaning of partnership in human custom is that a group of people recognise that the work of each of them, the wealth of each of them, and the talent of each of them, is not sufficient to establish a particular project, so they form a company for a specific production. Is there anything lacking in our Lord that He would complete it with another? Far be it from Allah! Indeed, the mere supposition by the servant that there is a partner causes Allah to reject the worship of the associating servant. For this reason He says in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association." And since our Lord has relinquished His care of him, let him meet hardships from where he does not know.

From His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾:

We learn that when Allah decrees the misguidance of a person or the guidance of another, no human being will be able to alter Allah's judgment so as to make something of misguidance into guidance, or something of guidance into misguidance.

It is also made clear from this noble verse that those in whose hearts is a disease, Allah increases them in disease and leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly. Blindness of the heart (al-ʿamah) is the heart's loss of insight, and blindness (al-ʿama) is the eye's loss of sight.

(1) Narrated by Imam Muslim in his Sahih, in the chapter on the prohibition of showing off.

The Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it arrive? Say: "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None but He will reveal it at its time. It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly." They ask you as if you were well informed about it. Say: "Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know."﴾ (7:187)

The one being asked is the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the askers may be the Jews, who asked him about the Hour, about the soul, and about Dhu al-Qarnayn. His answer matched what they had in the Torah, because they thought that the speech Muhammad delivered came from him haphazardly, without any control, and was not sent down from a Lord. When he answered with what was in their Torah, they knew that he did not speak from himself. For this reason they also asked him about the People of the Cave and what happened to them. They were a group in past times, and they agreed with him on everything that happened to the People of the Cave except the time period, so the Qur'an came down to specify that period with His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine.﴾ (18:25) The Jews said: "The three hundred years we know, but the nine we do not know." They did not realize that the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, dates the history of the universe by the most precise calculations of the universe, for our Lord is the One who said:

﴿Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God﴾ (9:36, part of the verse).

Therefore all timekeeping follows the Arab (lunar) calendar. We know that those who want to determine history precisely date it by the crescent moon, and an example of this is that all the calculations of the tides in the seas are made by the crescent, because it is more precise. Also, the crescent is a sign that tells us when the month begins, whereas we cannot know from the sun when the month begins, because the sun is a daily indicator of day and night, while the moon is a monthly indicator, and the total of the twelve is the yearly indicator. But they did not grasp this, and they reckoned the three hundred years by solar calculation. The Almighty added: ﴿and added nine﴾, because if you calculate three hundred solar years by the lunar year, it comes to nine more years.

The practice of asking in the Qur'an is a healthy phenomenon in faith, because faith came to govern the movement of life through "do" and "do not." When the Law says "do," there is apparent hardship in that action, and when it says "do not," there is apparent ease and desirability in that prohibition, while prohibition contradicts the desires of the soul. To confirm that questions are a healthy phenomenon among believers, we find many questions addressed to the Messenger of God by his community, which the Qur'an recounts in various forms. The question came once in the present tense, such as His saying: "They ask you," and once in the past tense: "And if they ask you." The question often came in the present form "yasaluunaka," because the present tense refers to the present and the future.

The questions came in the Qur'an in the present form ten times, and in the past form once. If you look at the fifteen instances, you will find that each one came to clarify a ruling. If we look at the root of the verb "yas'alu" in the Qur'an in the order of the Mushaf, we find the Qur'an says:

﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are timekeepers for the people﴾ (2:189, part of the verse).

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents and relatives﴾ (2:215, part of the verse).

The Almighty, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is a great matter, but barring from the way of God, disbelief in Him, barring from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it are greater in the sight of God, and sedition is greater than killing﴾ (2:217, part of the verse).

He, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people﴾ (2:219, part of the verse).

He says in the same earlier verse again: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus﴾.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿And they ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best﴾ (2:220, part of the verse).

He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And they ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an injury, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾ (2:222, part of the verse).

The Almighty, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿They ask you what is made lawful for them. Say: What is good is made lawful for you﴾.

After that, in Surat al-A'raf, He says:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it arrive? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ (7:187, part of the verse).

He also says: ﴿They ask you as if you were well informed about it﴾ (7:187, part of the verse). Then the Almighty says: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger﴾ (8:1, part of the verse).

The Almighty, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And they ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is of the command of my Lord﴾ (17:85, part of the verse).

The Lord, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a mention of him﴾ (18:83).

The Almighty says: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast﴾ (20:105).

He concludes these questions with His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it arrive? (42) In what are you concerned with mentioning it?﴾ (79:42–43).

These are fifteen verses in which the Almighty says "they ask you." There is one verse in which the Almighty, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, I am near; I respond to the call of the caller when he calls Me﴾ (2:186, part of the verse).

In the fifteen verses in which the Almighty uses the present form "they ask you," every answer is introduced by "Say," an imperative to the Messenger: say this, say that. But in the single verse in which the past form "if they ask you" appears, He did not say "Say: I am near," but said: ﴿I am near; I respond to the call of the caller﴾, because God knows Muhammad's love for his community and his concern for them. Therefore He says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe﴾ (26:3).

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So perhaps you would consume yourself in grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message﴾ (18:6).

Therefore, when the Almighty knew the Messenger's concern for his community, his preoccupation with them, and his eagerness that God should cover them with His forgiveness and mercy and that nothing should grieve him concerning them, the Lord, mighty and majestic, informed him that He would please him regarding his community. This is supported by a hadith: it was narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of God, mighty and majestic, about Abraham (ﷺ): ﴿My Lord, they have led many of the people astray. Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (14:36).

And the saying of Jesus (ﷺ): ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (5:118). He raised his hands and said: "My community, my community," and he wept. God, mighty and majestic, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best; ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told him what he had said, while He knew best. God, the Exalted, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will please you regarding your community, and We will not grieve you." (Narrated by Muslim.)

As confirmation of the knowledge of the Almighty, blessed and exalted, and of His Messenger's concern for his community, He wished to honor this community with the kind of honor given to the Messenger. So the address in the verse of supplication came without "Say": ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, I am near﴾ (2:186, part of the verse).

God wished to show Muhammad and his community that God knows not only what you ask him, but also what you will ask him about. Therefore we find fourteen verses in which "they ask you" appears and the answer is "Say," while the fifteenth verse has "they ask you" with the answer "then say" (fa-qul), to show that the particle "fa" indicates that the question has not yet occurred. It is as if the "fa" indicates an implied condition: if they ask you, then say: "My Lord will blow them away with a blast." Here the Almighty says:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it arrive? Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None but He will reveal it at its time. It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly. They ask you as if you were well informed about it. Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know.﴾ (7:187)

"Yujalliha" means it reveals it, manifests it. There is what is called "al-jalwa" (appearing openly to people) and what is called "al-khalwa" (withdrawing from people). "Al-jalwa" is for a person to show himself to people, and "al-khalwa" is to withdraw from people. "La yujalliha" means He does not reveal it. As for "li-waqtiha," you see that it is preceded by the lam, which in Arabic grammar is called "lam al-tawqit" (the lam of time), as the Almighty says: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ (17:78, part of the verse).

It means "at," and the meaning of the sun's decline is that it passes the zenith of the sky and inclines slightly toward the west. His saying "None but He will reveal it at its time" means none but He, glory be to Him and exalted, will make it clear at its time.

﴿It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly.﴾ "Weight" means that the mass of a thing is greater than the force that carries it, for if the mass equals the force, it does not weigh upon the one carrying it.

Or the force that carries it is unable to withstand the pull of the earth's gravity, so the thing is heavy. This weight may be physical, as a man may carry on his back an ardeb of wheat and be able to bear it, but if it rises to an ardeb and a half, the load becomes heavy on his back because his strength cannot bear such weight, so he collapses under it.

﴿It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth.﴾ Weight is not only physical, but also intellectual and mental. An example of this is when a student solves a geometry exercise or an algebra exercise: the student sometimes feels that such an exercise is heavy on his mind and difficult to solve.

The matter may also be heavy on the soul in its faculties, like worry that sits on the chest and weighs upon it, which is the harshest kind of weight. For this reason the ancient poet says: "It is not a burden the back can bear; the real burden is what the chest holds."
Thus there are three kinds of weight: physical weight, intellectual weight, and emotional weight.

As for ﴿It has weighed heavily upon the heavens﴾, we know that the heavens contain the angels. We also know that the angels likewise do not know the time of the Hour, and no one seeks to know it except man with the appetite of thought. As for the angels, they are not charged with it, because they have no choice, and some of them serve mankind, namely the angels who prostrated to Adam and who are entrusted with his affairs and his life. They submitted to the command of the Truth that there is a new master of the universe. So they are all made subservient to his service: the noble recording guardian angels, who have an affinity with creation, an affinity that abhors the disobedient and loves the obedient. And whoever walks on...

(1) Narrated by Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 7, verse 188:

The Most High says: ﴿Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm, except what Allah wills. And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.﴾

The Blessed and Exalted Lord says, on the tongue of His Messenger: "You ask me about the Hour, but I am a human being and merely one who receives. The sending of the method (al-manhaj) comes from Allah, and I convey it. I have no knowledge of the appointed time of the Hour. I do not possess for myself either harm or benefit," meaning: I do not have the ability to repel harm from myself or to draw benefit to myself. Rather, when Allah brings benefit or withholds harm, a person possesses what Allah gives him. The intelligent person, when he possesses something, says: "This is a temporary possession (mulk 'aradi); I am not secure that it may be taken from me." For this reason the Blessed and Exalted Lord told us: ﴿Say: O Allah, Possessor of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will. You exalt whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things Competent.﴾ (Surah Aal 'Imran).

Here the Blessed and Exalted Lord says: ﴿Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm, except what Allah wills.﴾

Meaning: no one possesses anything except what Allah wills for him to possess, and the Messenger of Allah is among mankind. He adds: ﴿And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ (part of verse 188, Surah al-A'raf).

Muhammad (ﷺ), if he knew the unseen, would have acquired much good. He fought and won, and he fought and was defeated, and he traded and profited. What applies to humans applies to him: sometimes he manages a matter for which there was no method from the heavens, so sometimes he is right and sometimes he errs, and Allah corrects him. Therefore the statement comes on his tongue by command from Allah: "If I knew the unseen, I would not have fallen into all these matters." The people of the Messenger of Allah from Quraysh had said: "We are your relatives, so tell us the appointed time of the Hour, so that we may prepare to meet it."

The Lord, glorified is He, continues His statement: ﴿And no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.﴾

When you see "in" (inna), it is sometimes conditional, like: "If you study, you will succeed," and sometimes it is negative, and after it you find a noun, and the meaning is: "I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe." The address is directed to the believers, because they are the ones who benefit from warning and from good tidings: what they are warned of, they do not do; what they are given good tidings of, they do.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 7, verse 189:

And the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul, and made from it its mate, that he might find rest in her. Then, when he covered her, she bore a light burden and walked about with it. But when it became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous (child), we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ (189).

As for His saying, Exalted is He: "created you from a single soul," what is meant is Adam. And the saying of the Truth, "and made from it its mate," what is meant is Eve (Hawwa'). We notice in the expression of this verse that the pronoun refers to the feminine.

﴿He it is who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate﴾, then He came with the masculine in His saying: ﴿that he might find rest in her﴾.

So the distinction of maleness from femaleness came at "that he might find rest." It is as if the speech about the soul is directed at the human species, which we call "the human being" (al-insan), and among it is maleness and among it is femaleness. For this reason, when He, glory be to Him, speaks of maleness as maleness and femaleness as femaleness, He uses either the masculine pronoun or the feminine pronoun. And His saying: ﴿that he might find rest in her﴾.

Because He wishes to make clear that the woman was made a rest (sakan) for the man. It is not said that she is a rest for him unless he is in motion; as if movement and toil in life belong to the man, and then he rests with the woman and finds peace in her through tenderness, compassion and gentleness. But if she is not a rest for him, he goes out of the house, for that is better for him. And the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿and made from it its mate﴾.

It reminds us of what we have known before, that Allah created Adam from clay and from dried clay, then our Lord breathed into him of the spirit. As for Eve, He mentions her in this matter and makes clear: "I made from it its mate." "From it" means that she is a part of him. It was said: she was created from a crooked rib. Whoever favors this opinion says to you: because Allah wishes to make the bond of rest an organic connection; the woman is a part of the man, and we know that one loves his son because he is a part of him. Accordingly, this statement came to establish affection. And there are those who say: Eve was created like Adam, so why was Adam mentioned and Eve not mentioned?

We say: Adam was given the form in the creation of man from clay, because Adam is the messenger and the one to whom prostration was made. And we know that the woman is always built upon concealment (sitr). An example of this: we find the farmer in Egypt does not say "my wife," but says "the household" (al-jama'a) or "the children" or says "my people" (ahli), and never mentions the name of the wife.

And the Truth says here: "and made from it." If she was created from the rib, then "min" (من) is partitive (tab'idiyya); and if she was created like Adam, then "min" is explicative (bayaniyya), meaning "from her kind," like our Lord's saying: ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them﴾ (Qur'an 62:2).

That is, the messenger is from our human kind, so that he may be a companion to the one who conveys from Allah, and the one who conveys from Allah is one of us, and we may be at ease with him. For this reason we said: Allah's choice of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from among mankind is a refutation of those who wanted the messenger to be of a kind other than human. The Truth said on their tongues: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (Qur'an 17:94).

The reply to them comes:

﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ (Qur'an 17:95).

Then, if the messenger were of the kind of angels, how would they see him in his true form? He would necessarily have to be created by Allah in the form of a human being.

He, glory be to Him, continues: ﴿Then, when he covered her, she bore a light burden﴾:

"Covered her" is a polite expression for the act of intercourse in the sexual function between husband and wife. The ghisha' (غشاء) is the covering, and Allah made intercourse for the sake of procreation, "to spread from the two of them many men and women."

The meaning here is that she carried the fetus for a period while she did not know she was pregnant, because the growth of the fetus is very slow; the mother does not feel it.

﴿and walked about with it, but when it became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous (child), we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

(Qur'an 7:189):

"And walked about with it" is meant to say that she goes about her life's movements standing and sitting until she becomes heavy and feels the pregnancy in its final months.

Here the husband knows that there is a pregnancy, and the two of them raise their hands in supplication to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the child be righteous in bodily formation and fit to uphold the values of the methodology.

﴿He it is who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find rest in her﴾ (Qur'an 7:189).

That is, maleness has become separated from femaleness, and the male comes to rest with the female.

Thus the matter concerning Adam was like this, and then the speech came to the offspring, especially since Eve used to bear a male and a female, and Adam, Eve and their children are the origin of human existence and the origin of procreation.
