The Qur'an may speak of subjects that appear distant, yet they contain values of a unique order, and we find the Truth speaking of one matter and then of another, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea; until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes to them a stormy wind and the waves come at them from every place, and they assume that they are encompassed by them﴾ (Qur'an 10:22).

He did not mention the travel of land here; rather He spoke of land and sea and then moved on to speak of the coming of death. Also consider the saying of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ (Qur'an 46:15).

Here the Truth enjoins man concerning his parents, the father and the mother, then He continues:

﴿His mother bore him in hardship and gave birth to him in hardship, and his bearing and weaning is thirty months﴾ (Qur'an 46:15).

The account of the man is not mentioned; rather all the particulars are for the mother.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 190:

And He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. But exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾

It is narrated that this verse was revealed concerning Qusayy, who was one of the forefathers of the Prophet (ﷺ). Qusayy asked Allah to grant him righteous offspring. When our Lord granted him righteous offspring, he named them with names of servitude, so he did not say "Abd Allah" or "Abd al-Rahman," but said: "Abd Manaf," "Abd al-Dar," "Abd al-Uzza." Thus he made partners with Allah in the naming. For this reason the Word of the Truth came: "they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them," to show us that a person, in his weakest states, that is, when he is weak in facing events, his Lord comes to his mind, because he loves to surrender himself to the One who gives him what he wants, and after he attains his request he forgets. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us concerning a harm that touched him.﴾ (Qur'an 10:12). The benefit of harm is that it makes us turn to our Lord. Therefore we find a person at his best in remembrance of Allah and glorification of Allah when he is in hardship and in illness. So if the sick person appreciated Allah's blessing upon him in his hardship and illness, I do not say that he would wish to prolong the duration of the illness and hardship. No, rather he should only refrain from complaining, turn to his Lord, and supplicate to Him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us this when he said: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my humiliation before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful. You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who frowns at me, or to an enemy whom You have given power over my affair? If there is no anger from You against me, I do not mind, but Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face by which the darknesses are illuminated and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, from Your descending wrath upon me or Your displeasure befalling me. To You is the reproach until You are pleased; there is no might nor power except through You." (1)

A sick person, at the moment he is in illness, must recognize the blessing within it. In every movement he makes, he remembers Allah, and as the energy of carnal impulses subsides within him, he fills with lofty positive qualities. Therefore we find that in the Hadith Qudsi our Lord, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. He said: O my Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? He said: Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me. He said: O my Lord, how could I feed You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? He said: Did you not know that My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him? Did you not know that if you had fed him, you would have found that with Me? O son of Adam, I asked you for drink and you did not give Me drink. He said: O my Lord, how could I give You drink, when You are the Lord of the worlds? He said: My servant so-and-so asked you for drink and you did not give him drink. Did you not know that if you had given him drink, you would have found that with Me?﴾ (2)

So what of the state of a sick person who feels that his Lord is with him, who is in illness with the Benefactor, and in health with the blessing?

﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. But exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

The meaning of this is that our Lord, blessed and exalted, declares Himself far above what the wrongdoers say and the gods they claim to associate with Him. For this reason the Most High says: ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ (7:191).

1 Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya li-Ibn Hisham.
2 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, in the chapter on the virtue of visiting the sick.

Does the tafsir text here include a verse "﴿وَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ لَهُمْ نَصْرًا...﴾" — yes, it does, so translation continues through it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 7, verse 191:

Do they associate with Allah those who create nothing, while they themselves are created by Allah? Those who associated idols with Allah did so through illusion, and they abandoned reason. It was obligatory for them to be rational, so that they would not take idols as gods.

﴿Do they associate with Him what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ For this reason there is another verse that exposes their claim, in which the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ (Qur'an 22:73).

We know that humans in laboratories have come to recognize their inability to create a single cell, which cannot be seen with the naked eye. For this reason Allah made clear that the matter is not one of creation alone. Rather, if a fly lands on a person's food and takes something on its wing or in its proboscis, no one can retrieve what was taken from it. The seeker and the sought are both weak.

Truth, as we know, is the first rank of the ranks of power. If the idols these people took as partners create nothing, by their own admission, then how do they worship them? They do not create anything, as is proven by the fact that they do not reproduce. Indeed, if the worshippers wish to increase the number of idols, they make an idol themselves. We note that Allah expressed this here with the phrase "Do they associate", in the form of wonder (ta'ajjub). Wonder arises from denying what the interrogation concerns, that is, a wonder that is disapproving in accordance with ordinary human nature, just as He says to us: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah?﴾ (Qur'an 2:28).

That is, tell us, by what means do you disbelieve in Allah and conceal His existence, with these clear and manifest signs? It is as though this is a strange matter that calls the people of truth to astonishment, wonder, and fierce denial. When the Truth speaks by denying something because it is a strange matter, He directs the speech sometimes to them and sometimes to others, like His saying here: ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾

The address is to the believers, because He wishes to give two images in the verse. The first image: to deny what these people did, and to increase the people who did not do it in confidence in themselves and joy in their faith positions, since they were not like these.

﴿Do they associate what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ In this noble verse there is a linguistic pause within the Arabic style itself, which may raise a difficulty for some, in His saying "ma lā yakhluqu shay'an" (what does not create anything). "Mā" means "that which does not create anything," and "yakhluqu" here is singular, yet Allah gave the singular here the action of the plural, saying: ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing?﴾

I say: whoever pauses at this and notices this point is a person superficial in Arabic culture, because he knows that "mā," "man," and "al-" are used for the singular and feminine, the dual and its feminine, and the masculine plural and feminine plural. You say: "The one I honored came to me," "The one [f.] I honored came to me," "The two I honored came to me," "The two [f.] I honored came to me," "Those I honored came to me," and "Those [f.] I honored came to me."

Likewise "mā." Therefore the Truth's saying "mā lā yakhluqu" is singular in appearance, but the wording applies to the singular and the plural. Hence in the second clause it observes the plural: "yakhluqu" is for the singular, and "hum yukhlaqūn" is for the plural, because His saying "mā" is suitable for all: for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine, and the feminine.

An example of this is the saying of the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they go out from your presence﴾ (Qur'an 47:16).

He, glorified is He, said here: "And among them are those who listen to you," and did not say "until when he goes out from your presence," but rather "until when they go out," that is, He brought the plural. So when you see this in "mā," "man," and "al-," know that these words are used equally for the singular, the feminine, the dual, the feminine dual, the masculine plural, and the feminine plural. ﴿Do they associate what creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾

Here in this verse there is another linguistic pause, in His saying "hum" (they), which is used only for a group of rational beings. How then is "hum" applied to idols, which are not rational? I say: when the Almighty knew that they believe that these idols harm and benefit, He spoke with them according to what they believe, in order to advance with them in rejecting every denial that deserves to be denied. The first stage: He made them know that the idols do not create. The second stage: He made them know that they themselves are created, and the idols cannot help them. So they are disabled from every side, since they do not create. This is the first incapacity. On the other hand, they are created, and this is another incapacity. But after this first incapacity and this second incapacity, are they able to help others? Behold, He, glorified is He, advances in dialogue with them to a further elevation, saying:

﴿And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves﴾ (Qur'an 7:192).

So none of the idols is able to help itself or guarantee help for anyone else.

Thus we find the dialogue ascending through four stages: first, "they create nothing"; second, "they are created"; third, "they cannot help you"; and fourth, "nor can they help themselves."

Then comes the fifth stage, in His saying, the Truth:

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is alike for you whether you call them or you remain silent.﴾ (7:193).

So these are five stages—therefore, I repeat them so that they settle in the mind. The first is that it is permissible that He does not create, and it is permissible that He is created; it is permissible that He is unable to give victory to another because He is weak, and He does not give victory to Himself because He is weaker; and yet, if you wish to guide them to something of this or to something of knowledge, they will not accept it from you.

In the Jahiliyyah, when a grave matter frightened them, they would call upon them, saying: "O Hubal! O Lat! O 'Uzza!" But if no calamity befell them, they would fall silent about calling upon the idols. Therefore, God says to them, through the revelation to His Messenger ﷺ:

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is alike for you whether you call them or you remain silent.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf): That is, if you call them to it, it is of no benefit in any matter, just as your silence is of no benefit.

We observe that the style here differs: "sawa'un 'alaykum a-da'awtumuhum" rather than "ad'awtumuhum am samatum." This is because the verb implies occurrence (hudūth), and we should know that they would only turn to their gods at great events. As for the rest of the time, they never spoke to them at all. Therefore "samitun" came as a nominal sentence, because it is a noun, and the noun implies permanence and continuity, whereas the verb implies occurrence and renewal.

The Truth here conveys to the polytheists: whether you call upon them or do not call upon them, alike it is for you—non-response is realized in them and proceeds from them, and the non-granting of victory to themselves and to others is realized from them.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) speaks on another matter:

﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful.﴾ (7:194)

The word "tadʿūn" (you invoke/call upon) has two meanings. The first is that you take them as gods and worship them. The second is that one says "tadʿūnahu," meaning you ask something of him. Both meanings occur in this verse: "Indeed, those whom you invoke (tadʿūna) besides Allah are servants like you (ʿibādun amthālukum), so call upon them..."

When a person hears the word "ʿibād" (servants), he understands it to be of the rational, living kind, so how can idols be "servants"? I say: here we take it according to the common usage of the word. But if we wish to verify the word and establish its morphology, the root is derived from submission and subjugation. Did not Moses say to Pharaoh:

﴿And this is a favor of which you remind me, that you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ (Surah al-Shuʿarāʾ, 26:22).

That is, you humiliated them. In the verse we are contemplating, the idols are "servants like them" in that they are subjected to humiliation, for when a flood comes or a wind blows, we find these idols fallen and their necks broken, and the polytheists hasten to bring someone to repair these gods! So you, O polytheists, since you are created by Allah, may possess a power and strength by which, if harm comes to you, you can repel the harm from yourselves; but the idols have not the least power if someone comes to smash them, break them, or mend them. Thus they are weaker than you. Accordingly, the phrase "servants like you" is a kind of escalation. And even granting that they are "servants like you," a living servant, when something comes to subdue him, may be able to defend himself to some extent, unless the thing is stronger than his capacity. So the meaning intended is that they are servants like you, that is, subjugated and subdued, and unable to repel anything from themselves. And if you consider this matter and take the meaning of "ʿibād" in its absolute sense, you know that a servant is everything subjected and subdued among the servants.

But there is one who is subdued and subjected in matters over which he has no choice, and another who is subdued and subjected in matters over which he also has choice. The difference between the two is that the disbeliever, in what he has choice over, either believes or does not believe and chooses disbelief; indeed, the believing person has the choice to obey or disobey. But there are other things that befall a person over which he has no choice: he may fall ill and cannot say, "No, I will not fall ill," or death may come to him and he cannot say, "I will not die." His wealth may perish or his house may burn, and he cannot repel the decree. All these are compelling matters in which a person is subdued and subjected, and the disbeliever and the believer are equal in these matters.

The believer is distinguished by following the method of Allah in what he has choice over, and this is the benefit of faith. Thereby the believer passes from the choice created in him by Allah to the will of Allah concerning him in the command, and he becomes equal with everything subjected to Allah. For this reason we say to those who disbelieve: you have disbelieved and refused, having been created with the choice to believe in Allah.

And Allah has made this clear to you in His saying:

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (18:29).

Since each of you, O disbelievers, is refusing and arrogant toward the command of Allah, then each of you has a training in rebellion. So why do you not say to the illness, "I will not submit to you"? None of the disbelievers can do that, for he disbelieves only in that for which he has a right granted by Allah in the realm of choice; but in other than that, all are subdued servants.

﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them, and let them respond to you﴾ (7:194).

The saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted: "So call upon them" means: ask of them to answer whatever request you make of them, and they will not respond to you, for they are utterly incapable. In this saying there is a kind of challenge: "let them respond to you," yet they will not respond, for they have no power to defy the command of our Lord and say, "We will give you what you ask," since their strength and nature cannot respond.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 195:

After the Truth (al-Haqq) had said of the idols that they are servants like you, He wished to lower them to a rank beneath humans, so He said:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear? Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.﴾

The Truth, blessed and exalted, is alerting every polytheist, as if He were saying to him: You have feet with which you walk, you have hands with which you may strike, you have ears with which you hear, and you have eyes with which you see. So do the idols have senses like these? No, they do not. The idols are therefore lower than you. How, then, do you make the lesser a god to the greater? This is indeed the essence of ruin.

His words "they walk with them," "they hear," and "they see" came about because the polytheists fashioned the statue with two legs, two ears and two eyes, and they would place a bead in the place of each eye to be like the pupil of the eye. When one of them looks at the statue, it seems to him that the statue is looking at him. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿They look at you, yet they do not see﴾ (part of verse 198, surah al-A'raf).

And in His words, may He be exalted:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ (part of verse 195, surah al-A'raf).

When the Truth presents such matters in the form of a question, He intends to establish the matters by the strongest path, because a question must have an answer. Speech from God, in the view of the disbeliever, may be taken as true or as false. The disbeliever's answer would certainly be that the idols cannot walk, touch, see or hear; therefore the Truth wished that the judgment not come from His side, but from the side of the polytheists, and in this there is their own acknowledgment. This is why the Truth says, addressing the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ (surah al-Inshirah).

Could He, glory be to Him, not have said: "We expanded your breast for you"? He could have. But He brings the question whose answer is: "Yes, You have expanded my breast." His words, may He be exalted:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾

alert to a comparison of the idols with humans. Humans have feet, hands, eyes and ears, and each of these limbs has a function it performs; thus it becomes certain to the polytheists that they are higher in rank than their idols.

How, then, is it permissible by the standard of reason for the higher in rank to be a servant of the lower in rank? That is a form of folly.

﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.﴾

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke this statement to refute their belief in these idols which they had taken as gods, and to make foolish their intellects concerning them. Thereby he declared enmity against them, both worshippers and worshipped, and it became an actual dispute. He challenged them to call upon their partners to plot against the Messenger of God with harm, hardship, or the prevention of the victory that had come to Islam, if you or they have any power to harm or benefit.

﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.﴾

He (ﷺ) challenges them to plot against him and their gods, and plotting (kayd) is a hidden, well-planned scheming. Look and see what will happen: no harm at all will reach the Messenger of God, by the permission of his Lord.

Therefore we find that the Truth, glory be to Him, has brought about for the Messenger of God certain things, by which He established certain things. They said: someone has bewitched the Prophet. Let us suppose that such sorcery did occur; how could the Prophet be bewitched? We say: and who said that he was bewitched? Our Lord informed him of the sorcerer, of the type of sorcery, and of where the object bearing the sorcery was placed, to show them that their scheming, even through their devils, is exposed before God.

﴿When those who disbelieved schemed against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you﴾ (part of verse 30, surah al-Anfal).

They had secretly planned the scheme against the Messenger of God, and they intended to strike him in a single blow so that his blood would be scattered among the tribes. Our Lord made clear: you plotted secretly, but your scheming will fail before your eyes. And to establish for them that by confrontation they would not be able to oppose his call, nor by human plotting could they strike his call, nor by the plotting of the jinn, who are more capable of action, could they confront his call. Since they had come to know that they would not prevail over the Messenger, and that their scheming, sorcery or plotting with their devils would not benefit them, then they must despair; therefore He challenged them and said:

﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.﴾ (part of verse 195, surah al-A'raf).

"Anzarahu" means "akhkharahu" (delayed him). The meaning here is: do not delay your scheming with your partners, but carry out the plot swiftly. The Truth commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to say this, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had taken refuge in a strong support; therefore the Messenger of God, by the command of the Truth, says:

﴿Indeed my protector is God, who revealed the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous﴾ (verse 196).

Since the Protector (al-Wali) is God, the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) does not care about them. "Wali" is one who stands closest to you (yalīk), and you do not make anyone your close associate (yalīk) except those nearest to your self and to your heart. And none becomes nearest to your self and your heart unless you perceive in him a benefit beyond your own benefit, a strength beyond your strength, and knowledge beyond your knowledge. The Messenger's saying, by the command of Allah the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿Indeed, my Protector is Allah﴾:

That is, He is my Helper against any scheme the camp of polytheism tries to devise or plot against me. Allah is the Wali (Protector) of the Messenger, meaning his Helper, and the one who is close to Him through the attributes of perfection and majesty that belong specially to Him, the Glorified and Exalted. When a believer has a trait of weakness, he goes to one who has a trait of strength. For this reason we said in the story of Musa (peace be upon him), when his people looked back and saw the people of Pharaoh, and said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾, meaning that Pharaoh's army will overtake them, because the sea was before them and the enemy behind them. They had no room in front for escape and no outlet except to stand firm before Pharaoh's army while they were without strength. Musa (peace be upon him) did not deny their statement; rather, he said to them, reassuring them:

﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (Qur'an 26:62)

At this point the matter passed beyond human means and ended at the mighty support to which the messengers resort. Nobody says this statement except one who is completely certain of Allah's support. I have previously related to you the story of the European woman who embraced Islam because she was reading the biography of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) as a hero among the heroes of the world, who effected the greatest revolution in the history of humanity. When she came across his life (peace and blessings be upon him), she read that his Companions used to guard him from his opponents and enemies, until one day they were surprised when the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to them: "Leave me. For Allah has revealed to me:

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ (Qur'an 5:67)

This incident gave this woman pause, and she said: "If this man wanted to lie to people, he would not have lied about himself. And he could not hand himself over to his enemies without guards unless he was certain that Allah had revealed this to him and that He is able to protect him; otherwise he would have thrown himself into a trial." This woman took the lesson of this incident as a point of insight. In a similar vein, the Blessed and Exalted Lord says on the tongue of His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him):

﴿Say: Call your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.﴾ (Qur'an 7:195)

It is as if he (peace and blessings be upon him) is summoning them to a challenge in battle, through cunning and plotting, and not to delay in doing so, while he is certain that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will support him.

﴿Indeed, my Protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He protects the righteous.﴾ (Qur'an 7:196)

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down the Clear Book to His Messenger to convey it to creation, and it is not possible that He would hand it over to an enemy who would prevent him from completing the communication from Allah. Allah sent down the Book to His Messenger to convey it to all people, and it is impossible that He would abandon it. ﴿Indeed, my Protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He protects the righteous.﴾

As for His saying ﴿and He protects the righteous﴾: that is, He does not make protection a privilege of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) alone; rather He says to each of his followers: Be righteous at any time, before any enemy, and you will find Allah protecting you with victory. And when Allah generalizes the ruling, He spreads faith-based tranquility in the hearts of the followers of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), and whoever bears anything of his call (peace and blessings be upon him) will have this support. Glory be to Him who made His Messenger the one who conveys the method from Him; He, Glorified, protects the righteous for the cultivation of the universe, because Allah has made man a vicegerent (khalifah) to set right the universe, and the first degree of reform is that the righteous remain upon their righteousness, or that they increase in righteousness if possible.

Then He, glory be to Him, says afterward:

﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ (7:197)

For one who cannot help you may well be stingy with his support, since his love for you may be mere show, or because he has no desire to keep for himself what he might use to help you. As for one who is unable to help you because he does not possess the means of victory, this shows the helplessness and deficiency of the one you have taken as a protector, and such was the condition of the polytheists. On the day of the Conquest (al-Fath), the Muslims came with hatchets and the idols were smashed, and not a single idol resisted. Rather, they all shattered entirely.

And the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear; and you see them looking at you, but they do not see.﴾

Naturally, if anyone were to call these idols to guidance, the idols would not be guided, because they are inanimate matter with which no call or understanding can be of any use. Although the idol has eyes, like those you see today in the temples of the Hindus or the Buddhists, where they place in the position of the pupil of the eye a colored bead resembling an eye, and the pupil is directed by its inclination, as if it were looking at you while it sees nothing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 7, verse 199:

The Blessed and Exalted Lord then says, addressing His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Take what is easy and forgiving, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.﴾

This is a verse in which the Mighty and Majestic Lord has gathered the noble qualities of character.

After the Blessed and Exalted Lord had informed His Messenger ﷺ that the polytheists may plot against him together with their devils and their idols, but they will not be able to do so, He then makes clear to him: I want you to take what is forgiving (al-'afw). This is an instruction for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and for whoever follows him. The word "al-'afw" is used on our tongues, yet we do not know that it has an original meaning in the language. If someone asks you, "Where did you get this thing from?", you say: "It came to me 'afwan," meaning without effort, without hardship, without seeking it out and without any scheming to acquire it.

It is also said: "This thing came to so-and-so 'afw al-khatir," meaning he did not think about it; rather it came to him easily. This is the meaning of al-'afw. Here the Truth commands His Messenger ﷺ to take al-'afw, that is, to take the easy, facile matter, in which there is no burden and no exertion, because by doing so you make people's affairs easy for them and do not complicate them. As for when things are burdened, that wearies people. Therefore the Truth commands His Messenger to say:

﴿Say: I do not ask of you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend.﴾ (Surah Sad).

His saying "and I am not of those who pretend" means that he ﷺ does not burden affairs such that life becomes difficult and there is no contention (ladd) among people, for what produces contention is burdening and coercing people. Dealings among them must be conducted without contention or burden. Therefore it is said: the believer is lenient when he sells, lenient when he buys, lenient when he demands his right, and lenient when his right is demanded from him; that is, in all his affairs he is lenient.

The command to take al-'afw has another meaning, which is that you pardon the one who wronged you, because that makes affairs easy.

Al-'afw also has a third meaning, which is the surplus, as in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted Lord before the zakat was prescribed:

﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus.﴾ (part of verse 219, Surah al-Baqarah).

Then the Truth afterwards specified zakat and its recipients. We note that the command to spend before zakat was prescribed and the spending after the command of zakat was revealed meet in ease, because the believer does not spend from what he needs, but rather from what exceeds his need.

The saying of Allah, glory be to Him, in the verse "Take al-'afw" contains the command "take" (khudh), and its counterpart is "give" (a'ti). You may give a person something and he will not accept it from you if he sees that what you give him is not in his interest. But when the Blessed and Exalted Lord says "take," this is a command whose benefit returns to you. If pardoning the one who wronged you appears to diminish you in some respect, know that you have taken al-'afw for yourself.

Know that the Blessed and Exalted Lord loves that His believing servant be gentle and soft with his brothers in faith. If a believing brother is hard upon him, let him be lenient with him. If a Muslim brother acts superior to you or displays arrogance, do not act superior to him or show arrogance, lest a battle arise between you; rather humble yourself, so that Allah increases you in elevation and honour.

It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, is affirming to you that when you give al-'afw you take good through it. I always give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: when you enter your home and find that your son has wronged his brother, your heart and your tenderness turn to the wronged one. We are the dependents of our Lord; if one person wrongs another, then by his wrongdoing the wrongdoer places Allah on the side of the wronged. Therefore the wrongdoer needs us to treat him well, since he was the cause of Allah's care for us. So we act toward him as Sayyidna Hasan al-Basri did when it was said to him: "So-and-so backbit you yesterday." Sayyidna Hasan al-Basri called his servant and said: "A tray of the first dates has come to us. Take it to so-and-so," and he named for the servant the person who had backbitten him. The servant was amazed: "How can you send dates to him when he has backbitten you?" He said: "Shall I not be good to the one whom Allah has placed beside me? Say to him: 'My master tells you: since you have backbitten him, he has given you his good deeds, and he has sent you his dates.'"

﴿Take what is easy and forgiving, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.﴾

The noble verse deals with the command to enjoin what is right:

Al-'urf is the conduct whose rightness sound minds recognize, to which souls are at peace, and which accords with the Law of Allah. It is called 'urf because everyone recognizes it (yata'arraf 'alayhi), and no one is ashamed of it. Therefore in various societies we hear of certain patterns of conduct: "This is what custom (al-'urf) has run with." What runs by custom among believing societies is considered one of the sources of the legal rulings. The best example of this is that we find a young man not ashamed to knock on a family's door to ask for their daughter's hand, because this is customary and there is no shame in it; whereas we find the Muslim society ashamed that there should exist among its members a person who commits adultery. The aim of adultery is enjoyment, and the aim of seeking a girl's hand is enjoyment too; but there is a great difference between an enjoyment that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, and an enjoyment that Allah, Exalted, has made lawful.

At the end of the verse Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And turn away from the ignorant.﴾

How is turning away from the ignorant to be understood? One errs who thinks that the ignorant one is the one who does not know, for the one who does not know is the unlettered (ummi). As for the ignorant (jahil), he is the one who knows a matter that contradicts reality. We note that problems do not come from the unlettered who do not know; the unlettered among them believes any matter you tell him about, and it is acceptable to his nature, because he possesses no alternative to it. But the ignorant is one who knows a matter contrary to reality and needs his knowledge of that matter to be changed; the second step is that you persuade him of the correct matter.

The Truth here clarifies: turn away from the ignorant one who holds a matter contrary to reality and fanatically clings to it. When you turn away from the ignorant, you must not argue with him (tumariyahu), that is, you must not dispute with him, because disputing with him will not lead to a beneficial result. Therefore I say to everyone who confronts the question of religiosity and has not read a single book about religion, yet has read hundreds of books on deviation from religion: just as you have read hundreds of books opposing religion, wisdom requires you to be just and fair, so read in the field of religiosity some of the books specific to it, as you have read in other fields. If you wish to investigate the question of religion in a logical way that corrects your creed, you must set aside all your prior convictions and your feelings. Study both matters apart from your bias, and then admit into your bias the matter with which you feel at ease; but do not keep in your heart a matter while opposing its content with the outward tongue. The Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body.﴾ (part of verse 4, Surah al-Ahzab).

You have one heart: either it is filled with faith and certainty, or with something else. The heart is a single space, so do not occupy it with falsehood while searching for the truth; rather expel falsehood from your heart first, and place both falsehood and truth outside it, and search with your intellect; then admit into your heart whatever is made easy for you to admit.

In explaining the meaning of this verse, which is the subject of our reflections, Ubayy reported to us, saying: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: "Take what is easy and forgiving, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "Allah commands you to pardon the one who wronged you, to give to the one who withheld from you, and to join the one who cut you off." (1)... Glorified is He, then, wanting to teach us a faith-based and humane principle; for you, as a Muslim, help one afflicted in his body, so what of one afflicted in his values? Does he not need your assistance?

(1) Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 200:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

"Nazgh" (نزغ) is equivalent to the word "nakhs" (نخس), meaning to take hold of something and place its tip into the body of one who is beside you or in front of you. It is clear from the meaning of "nakhs" that there is a distance between the one who pricks and the one who is pricked, and an instrument or means for the pricking.

In the act of pricking, neither the one who pricks nor the one who is pricked perceives the warmth of the other. As for the word "mass" (مس), the one who touches and the one touched each quickly feels the warmth of the other, but one of them does not perceive the softness of the other. As for "lams" (لمس), it involves perceiving both the softness and the warmth of the one who touches and the one touched. All battles of war revolve within this range. When the enemy is far away, his opponent needs to keep away from him so that he does not strike him with arrows or missiles, while he himself tries to strike his opponent with arrows or missiles. This is just as modern armies do when they send their aircraft to drop bombs on the enemy's forces. The strength of states is measured by their ability to strike hostile forces without those forces being able to respond, because they strike from afar in the age of long-range missiles. We find the indication in the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ (part of verse 60, Surah al-Anfal).

Our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), clarified the meaning of "power" in what 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir narrated from him, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say while on the minbar: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. Indeed, power is archery; indeed, power is archery." (1) Because archery enables your projectile to reach your enemy while you are far from him, so he cannot strike you with what he throws.

In the past, armies would advance, and the adversaries would hurl arrows and javelins upon them. When the armies drew closer to their enemies, each side would direct spears toward what is near the bodies of the other side. When the fury of the battle intensified, swords would clash. So all of these are pricking, touching, and contact.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed his Lord saying: "O Lord, what about anger?" — meaning, how is anger to be treated? — the word of the Truth descended:

﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

Someone may ask: Does Satan incite the Messenger? I say: The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, did not say "when Satan incites you," but said "and if he incites you," meaning if that should happen, and this wording implies doubt. Moreover, why would Allah deprive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the pleasure of confronting Satan? We know from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

("There is none of you but that a companion from the jinn has been assigned to him, and a companion from the angels." They said: "And you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "And me, except that Allah has helped me against him, so he has submitted, and he does not command me except to good.")(2)

Here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾.

Seeking refuge (al-isti'adhah) means seeking help, shelter, and protection, and you do not seek help, take refuge, or seek protection except from one who is stronger than the one who wishes to inflict harm upon you. It is well known that Satan has agility of movement, capacity for penetration, and many means of infiltration. Therefore, you should not seek refuge in one like him or one below him, but you seek refuge in the Creator of mankind, jinn, and all creatures, and He is able to nullify the effectiveness of Satan. He is Hearing and Knowing: hearing has its objects, and knowledge has its objects. When you summon the meaning of seeking refuge while you are filled with faith and turn to the One who created you and created that Satan, then Satan must flee from your path, because he knows that you are taking refuge in the Creator, the Mighty and Able, and he has no power over his Creator. He is Hearing of your saying "I seek refuge in Allah," and Knowing of what is in your soul of the meaning of this word.

And if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has spoken here about the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying ﴿And if he incites you﴾, meaning that Satan is far off and merely attempts incitement, then what of the community of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this regard? Here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when a passing thought from Satan touches them, remember [Allah], and at once they are seeing clearly.﴾ (201)

1 Narrated by Imam Muslim, Imam Ahmad, Ibn Majah and Abu Dawud.
2 Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, vol. 1, and Jami' al-Ahadith of al-Suyuti, vol. 5, p. 608.

Among the mercies of God Most High toward the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that He said, "When they are touched" (إذا مسّهم), and did not say "when it touches them" (لمسَهم). This is because they are among those who have taken God-consciousness (ittaqa), that is, they have placed between themselves and the attributes of the majesty of God a shield (wiqaya) that makes them stop at His limits. Therefore He says:

﴿Indeed, those who have God-consciousness, when a visitation from Satan touches them, remember [God], and at once they see clearly.﴾

The ṭā'if (visitation) is the phantom that roams around a person at night. Since Satan is not seen, we depict him as a phantom. When Satan roams about them with the touch of temptation, those who have God-consciousness remember the Creator of Satan and their own Creator, and they remember the way of God which collides with their desires, and they remember that the eye of God sees them and does not neglect them, and that the sacred prohibitions of God are clear and evident. Our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), says in the hadith narrated from him by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir:

(The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever guards against doubtful matters has cleared himself regarding his religion and his honour. Whoever falls into doubtful matters is like a shepherd who grazes around a protected pasture, about to fall into it. Indeed, every king has a protected pasture; indeed, the protected pasture of God on earth is His prohibitions. Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart.) (1)

And when the believers remember the punishment that follows from any shameful act that Satan makes attractive to them, then any veil is lifted from them and they see the straight path.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Faith, vol. 1, p. 185.

The Most High, blessed and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿And their brothers extend them in error, then they do not hold back.﴾ (7:202)

When we trace the word "yamuddunahum" in the Qur'an, we find it once as "yamuddunahum," and once as "yumiddukum," as in the saying of the Most High:

﴿And He will extend to you wealth and sons.﴾ (71:12)

We know that the devils will not leave the believers in their state; rather, they continue in an attempt at seduction. The devils try to seduce the obedient believers more than they try to seduce the disobedient sinners, because the sinner already aids the devil by following the desires of his own soul, and neither the sinner nor the devil falls short in this; rather, the sinner or the devil seeks to seduce the believers. And "aqsar" is from the root "qasara," meaning that one is capable of lengthening the distance but shortens it instead. Thus is the persistence of the devils in seducing the believers.

So the devil, as the Qur'an relates, acknowledges his position of pursuing the believers with whisperings and the adornment of sins:

﴿Surely I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path.﴾ (7:16)

And the devil knows that one who does not fear God has no need for adornment or seduction, because he is inclined and drawn to sins, God forbid; therefore the devil does not exert great effort in his seduction.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 7, verse 203:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not chosen one?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe."﴾ (203)

The Truth, blessed and exalted, had earlier used the word "āyāt" (signs). As we have explained, āyāt are either cosmic signs (āyāt kawniyyah), or the miracles (mu'jizāt) that attest to the truthfulness of the messengers, or the legal signs (āyāt al-aḥkām).

Here Almighty God uses the singular "āyah" (a sign), not the plural "āyāt." The cosmos before them is full of His signs, and the method revealed to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is clear. What they lack, in their view, is only the miraculous sign they demand. The Truth alerts them with His saying, blessed and exalted, in Surat al-Isrā':

﴿We have indeed displayed for mankind in this Qur'an every kind of parable, but most people refuse except disbelief. And they say, "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it in abundance, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring God and the angels as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you send down to us a book we can read." Say, "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (Surat al-Isrā', 89-93).

So the miracles they asked for are not brought by the Messenger from himself, and the verses through which the method is sent down are likewise not from himself, but are a revelation from the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.

They used to accuse him, peace and blessings be upon him, of fabricating the Qur'an. Therefore they asked him, peace and blessings be upon him, for a sensory miracle, forgetting what the verses of the noble Qur'an contain of a miracle: they could not produce even one verse like its verses. They said to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿Why have you not chosen one?﴾ So he was told: ﴿Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾

Here his Lord commands him to say: ﴿Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾

That is, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, is charged with conveying to them what the revelation brings, which the Trustworthy Spirit, Jibrīl, peace be upon him, carries, from the verses of the Qur'an bearing the divine method. This method in itself is a miracle of continuing bounty. Therefore He adds:

﴿These are insights from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.﴾ (Surat al-A'rāf).

In the Noble Qur'an are insights (baṣā'ir), guidance and mercy. The word baṣā'ir is the plural of baṣīrah, from al-ibṣār (seeing). When the heart is filled with the light of faithful certainty, its possessor lives in clarity and radiance, and the owner of this inner vision is called a person of baṣīrah. Sight (baṣar), however, is the function of the eye in sensory matters, but there are non-sensory matters that only insight (baṣīrah) discovers. Insight illuminates the heart with light so that it perceives those non-sensory matters, and the heart possesses insight only when it is charged with faithful certainty.

The Noble Qur'an is insights because it gives and bestows upon whoever believes in it and contemplates it insights, so that non-sensory matters are renewed and have become "made visible" (mubṣarah), as if he were able to see and witness them, as if they were the eye of certainty.

This glorious Qur'an is insights and guidance, that is, it indicates to man and guides him to the true method and to the straight path of God. It is also a mercy for whoever does not possess the illuminations of the heart that guide to faith and does not possess the strength to grasp the proof that leads to guidance. Thus it is a mercy for all people, guidance for those who seek proof, and insights for those who have firmly grasped the foundations of faith by witnessing.

As we said before: God has informed the believers of unseen matters, and among these unseen matters are that He has a Garden and that He has a Fire. The believers affirmed everything that reached them of the message from their Lord, and they knew that it was from God, and this knowledge became knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn) shared among them. When the Day of Resurrection comes and they see the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) laid over the back of Hell, corresponding to what they had affirmed, it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn). And if some of them enter the Fire, God forbid, as expiation for sins they committed, that is truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). I gave an example earlier, and to God belongs the highest example: geographers used to speak to us, when we were students, about the map of the United States, and they would say that its capital is "Washington," and its great port is called "New York," and in New York there are skyscrapers, massive buildings, where the height of a single one of these buildings exceeds a hundred floors, that is, more than two hundred meters. We believed our geography teacher. When some of us were given the opportunity to travel and saw Washington and New York from the aircraft, the seeing became the eye of certainty after it had been knowledge of certainty. And upon the landing of the aircraft at Washington airport, the seeing became the truth of certainty.

God Almighty has presented to us faith in some of the unseen in His saying:

﴿Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If you knew with certain knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ (Surat al-Takāthur, 1-7).

Here He mentioned "knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqīn), and as for "truth of certainty" (ḥaqq al-yaqīn), it came in His saying:

﴿As for one who is among those brought near, there will be rest and bounty and a Garden of pleasure. And as for one who is among the companions of the right, "Peace be upon you, from the companions of the right." And as for one who is among the deniers, the astray, there will be a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the truth of certainty.﴾ (Surat al-Wāqi'ah, 88-95).

The believers who affirm reports of the unseen are at different levels. There are those who affirm God's report about the unseen as the eye of certainty, and there are those who affirm God's word as the truth of certainty. For this reason we find Imam ʿAlī, may God honour his face, saying: "Were the veil lifted from me, I would not increase in certainty."

In the following dialogue that took place between the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the noble companion al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik, what reveals to us the essence of this kind of faith:

"Al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī reported that he passed by the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said to him: 'How did you wake up, O Ḥārith?' He said: 'I woke up a true believer.' He said: 'Consider what you say, for every thing has a reality. What is the reality of your faith?' He said: 'My soul has turned away from this world, so I stay awake through my nights and go thirsty through my days, and it is as if I see the Throne of my Lord laid bare, and as if I see the people of Paradise visiting one another in it, and as if I see the people of the Fire shrieking in it.' He said: 'O Ḥārith, you have known; then hold fast to it three times.'" (2)

This noble companion reached the point where everything the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said became truth of certainty for him, and he possessed the insight by which he saw all of that.

﴿When you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not chosen one?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe."﴾ (Surat al-A'rāf).

Thus we find the Noble Qur'an to be insights for those of lofty station and high rank, guidance for those who reason, and mercy for all.

(1) yataḍārraghūn: that is, they raise their voices in shrieking and wailing.
(2) Related by al-Ḥāfiẓ al-Ṭabarānī from al-Ḥārith ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī.

And God, blessed and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ (7:204)

Since the Lord, glory be to Him, has already made clear to you that this Qur'an is insights (basa'ir) from your Lord, and guidance and mercy, should it not deserve that you cherish it, O believer? Are you not drawn by these three aspects to give it your ear and not turn away from it?

So you must listen to the noble Qur'an in order to receive its three benefits: the insights, the guidance, and the mercy. It is worthy and deserving that its hearing be guarded when it is recited.

Note that God, exalted is He, said ﴿fastami'u lahu﴾ (listen to it) and did not say "isma'u" (hear). This is because istima' (listening) implies a deliberate effort to hear everything said around you, whereas sam' (hearing) means you hear everything said around you, and you may or may not pay attention to what you hear. And out of Muhammadan mercy, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade eavesdropping on the secrets of others to spy on them by searching for their faults, as related from our master Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not spy on one another, do not outbid one another, and be, servants of God, brothers." (1)

In this is a warning against these five matters, among which are prying and eavesdropping on people's secrets.

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

A person may remain silent and listen but without the intention of worship, and so he is deprived of the reward of listening. So listen and be silent with the intention of worship, for it is God who is speaking, and it is neither reasonable nor proper toward God that your Lord speaks and you turn away from His speech. Our master Ja'far al-Sadiq (2) has drawn our attention to this and alerted us to the good in it, where he says:

"I am amazed at one who fears and does not resort to His saying, blessed and exalted: 'Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs,' for I have heard that God follows it by saying: 'So they returned with favor from God and grace, no harm touched them.'

And I am amazed at one who is distressed and does not resort to His saying, blessed and exalted: 'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers,' for I have heard God follow it by saying: 'So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.'

And I am amazed at one who is plotted against and does not resort to His saying, blessed and exalted: 'And I entrust my affair to God. Indeed, God is Seeing of His servants,' for I have heard God follow it by saying: 'So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted.'

And I am amazed at one who seeks the world and does not resort to His saying: 'That which God willed; there is no power except by God,' for I have heard God follow it by saying: 'Perhaps my Lord will give me better than your garden.'"

When we listen to the recitation of the noble Qur'an with the intention of worship, that is the good manners with which we should receive the lessons that return benefit to us.

The scholars differed concerning silence during the hearing of the Qur'an: Is silence required whenever the Qur'an is recited, in any circumstance, or only when it is recited in prayer, or when it is recited in the Friday sermon?

They differed on this. Some said: the intended meaning here is silence for the Qur'an when it is recited in prayer, and the reason is that the early Muslims, whenever the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited in prayer, would repeat after him every sentence he recited. When he said "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim," they would say "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim," and when he said "al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-'alamin," they would say "al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-'alamin." So God, mighty and majestic, alerted them to leave the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to recite while they listen to him without repeating the recitation.

Others among the scholars said: silence for the Qur'an applies in prayer, and in the Friday or Eid sermon, because these contain verses of the Qur'an. But their inclusion of verses is less than what the preacher says. Some pointed out that silence for the sermon is established by the evidence of the saying of the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace:

("If you say to your companion on Friday while the imam is preaching, 'Be silent,' you have engaged in idle talk.") (3)

Thus, silence for the sermon is established by evidence from the Sunnah.

There is also a view that listening is required to the Qur'an in any situation in which it is recited, for in this is respect and reverence for the speech of God, mighty and majestic. This view is attributed to our imam, master, and lord, my lord "Abu Abdullah al-Husayn," who says:

"When the Qur'an is recited, whether you are in prayer, or in a sermon, or free, then be silent, for the True, glory be to Him, wished to distinguish the Qur'an from all speech, so He singled it out with things: when it is recited, you must be silent to it; and when the mushaf is touched, one must be in a state of ablution, so that people do not become bold and touch the mushaf like any other book. This cultivates reverence, so you do not hold the mushaf except while you are in ablution. Thus when we teach our children, we say to one of them: do not approach the mushaf except while you are in ablution; and reverence grows in the child's soul."

Also, in "writing," the True, blessed and exalted, willed for some of its words a special orthography distinct from the standard rules of spelling, so that the Qur'an has a special sanctity: it is a unique book, not like every book, and its speech is not like every speech.

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf). Some scholars said: what is required is not merely listening with the ears, but the intended listening here is that we respond to its demands. Do you not say to one another, when one of you prays for another, "May God hear your supplication"? You say it while knowing that God hears you, but you mean by it that God, glory be to Him, respond to this supplication. Thus listening to the Qur'an entails responding to what the Qur'an requires. Why? In order to attain mercy from the True, for He is the Merciful, the Compassionate. ﴿That you may receive mercy.﴾ We know that "la'alla" (perhaps) and "'asa" (perhaps/it may be) when said denote hope, while "layta" (would that) denotes wishing, which is impossible and not expected. We wish in order to show that this is something beloved to us, though we know it is impossible, as the aged poet said: "Would that youth would return one day, so I could tell it what old age has done." He knows with certainty that youth will not return, but his saying indicates that youth is a beloved period.

Like the saying of the poet: "Would that the stars would draw near to me so I could string them into a necklace of praise for you, for I am not content with what you have as words." The stars will not draw near.

Thus, whenever you hear "'asa" or "la'alla," it comes to your mind that this is a hope to happen; and if it is a hope from God, it is a hope from the Generous, which must have reality.

1 Related by Imam Muslim (Kitab al-Birr wa'l-Silah wa'l-Adab), vol. 16, p. 119.
2 Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq ibn Sayyidi Muhammad al-Baqir, ibn Sayyidi 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin ibn Sayyidina al-Husayn.
3 Related by Imam Malik in his Musnad, and by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, and by al-Bayhaqi, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, from Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 7, verse 205:

And the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless.(205)﴾

Remembrance (dhikr) is the passing of a thing through the mind. If it is in the heart, it is remembrance within the self (dhikr fi'l-nafs). If it is with the tongue but is not heard by others, and only you hear it, this is remembrance in secret (dhikr al-sirr). If it is spoken aloud, it is of two kinds: loudness that is accepted, and loudness that is not accepted. The unaccepted loudness is when the remembrance turns into disturbance, God forbid. For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent in it, but seek a way between that.﴾ (part of verse 110, surah al-Isra').

Perhaps our brethren the readers will pay attention to this verse, with an attention that makes them turn to carrying out God's command in this matter, so that they do not shout or raise their voices with it to the point of disturbance. For I say to each one of them: your Lord did not even ask you for loudness; He asked for less than loudness. I say this especially to those who spoil God's blessing upon His creation, who shout at night and deprive people of God's mercy at night, of which He said: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.(73)﴾ (surah al-Qasas).

So do not spoil the mercy of our Lord for people. The call to God is not shouting from the pulpits, unless you are making for yourselves a media publicity on the mosques of God and on the pulpits of God. This is something rejected and not accepted by the Shari'ah. ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear.﴾ The Truth, blessed and exalted, says once: ﴿O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.(41)﴾ (surah al-Ahzab). And once He says: ﴿And remember your Lord.﴾ The saying "remember God" carries the sense of the obligations, because God is the One worshipped, and the One worshipped is the One obeyed in commands and prohibitions. As for His saying "remember your Lord," it is a reminder to you of what He has bestowed upon you of favours: He created you, nurtured you, and gave you from the overflow of His blessings what cannot be counted or numbered. So remember your Lord; for if you do not love Him out of obligation, you have loved Him because He sustains you with blessings, and He, glory be to Him, bestows favour upon us and befriends us all with blessings.

Let me strike for you this example—and to God belongs the highest example, and He is exalted above comparison: you have children, and you give them pocket money. When you give them their money every month, you find them not eager to see you except once a month. But if you give them their pocket money daily, you turn around to find them around you. If you are sleeping, your son enters your bedroom, walks beside you, and clears his throat to say that he needs something in the room. So what about you, who with all your existence are a servant to the goodness of your Lord? And as long as you are a servant of goodness, remember the One who does good to you. Remember your Lord always. And remember Him in two states: first, humbly (tadarru'an), that is, in submission, for you may remember someone with arrogance; but the Creator, the Benefactor, it is incumbent upon you to remember Him in the humility of servitude before the station of Lordship. And remember your Lord "in fear" (khifatan), that is, fearful and humble; for whenever you humble yourself before Him, He honours you. For this reason we find servitude disliked among humans, which is enslavement, and people flee from one who enslaves them; for a human's servitude to his equal is great tyranny and grave injustice. It gives the servant's goodness to the master. But your servitude to God gives God's goodness to you. For this reason we find the Truth bestowing favour upon the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, when He says: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.(1)﴾ (surah al-Isra').

The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, attained a great rank through the event of the Night Journey, and speaking of it was in gratitude from God to His servant and messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The believing poet says: "It is enough honour for my self that I am a servant, who is honoured without appointments with his Lord, in His most mighty sanctuary; but I meet whenever and wherever I love."

And you, O believing servant, meet God whenever you wish. When you surrender your reins to faith, the reins are in your hand. It is enough that you intend prayer and say "God is greatest," and you are in His presence, glory be to Him, whether you are in the house, on the street, or in any place. In this is the utmost honour for you.

﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech﴾ (part of verse 205, surah al-A'raf). Here He did not say "Lord of the worlds," but "your Lord, O Muhammad." This is the summit of the gifts that came to people: this gift that came with Muhammad as messenger is a blessing and favour from God upon the believers in his message. After that, the gift that came to Muhammad is attributed to every Muslim. His saying, exalted be He, to His Messenger: "And remember your Lord within yourself," means that He, glory be to Him, did not confine the evidence of His care for you to what is seen outside and far from you only; for you may see nothing in the cosmos or hear nothing in the cosmos, because the cosmos is separate from you. Rather, look at your own self, and you will find all the signs reminding you of your Creator.

﴿And within yourselves. Will you not see?(21)﴾ (surah al-Dhariyat). Before our Lord made the evidence in the cosmos around you, He made the evidence for you also within yourself, because your self does not leave you, and you know best its faculties, its limbs, and its impulses. For this reason, supplication to God and fear of Him have a place here, because you can see the secret of His craftsmanship in you, and you will find many signs, signs greater than yourself. Therefore you shrink before the One who gave you all this, and you fear that you will not fulfil His right over you.

Let us return to the saying of God, exalted be He: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings.﴾ Remembrance (dhikr) is an event (hadath), and an event needs time and place. "Mornings" (al-ghuduww) and "evenings" (al-asal) are two times that encompass the day: al-ghuduww is the beginning of the day, and al-asal is from the afternoon to sunset, as we say "the sun of the late afternoon" (shams al-asil). This cosmic sign is repeated often in the Noble Qur'an. The Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.(41) And glorify Him morning and evening.(42)﴾ (surah al-Ahzab). And as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner.(8) That you may believe in God and His Messenger, and support him and honour him, and glorify Him morning and evening.(9)﴾ (surah al-Fath).

Here "al-asil" is shared (mushtarak), and the opposite of al-asil the Truth calls at times "bukrah" (morning), and at other times "al-ghuduww." He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. God guides to His light whom He wills. And God presents examples for people, and God is Knower of all things.(35) In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; wherein exalt Him in the mornings and the evenings.(36)﴾ (surah al-Nur).

When you read "in houses" you know that this is an event (hadath), because the phrase "in houses" is a prepositional phrase with the sense of a adverb of place (zarf), and if you trace what precedes it, you will find no thing it depends upon. The apparent meaning, then, is that what precedes it is ﴿light upon light﴾ ﴿in houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned﴾. So when you go to the mosque to meet God, that is light; and when you pray to Him, that is light; and you leave this light with a light that descends upon you in His house. All of this is light upon light. Whoever wishes to expose himself to the breaths of the light of God, mighty and majestic, let him frequently go to the houses of God, the mosques, in reverence for the light, because they are places of prayer. We know that prayer is the intimate communion between the servant and his Lord. And when a matter distressed the Messenger of God, he would stand to pray. And if you follow the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and pray two rakʿahs to God when a matter distresses you, and a question is difficult for you and beyond your means, then go to God, He will not bring you out except content. ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; wherein exalt Him in the mornings and the evenings.﴾

The mornings and the evenings, or the bukrah and the asil, as we have known, are the times of the beginning of the day and the beginning of the night. And why the times of the beginning of the day and the beginning of the night? Because these are the times in which remembrance is sought. Before you go out to work at the beginning of the day, you need a charge of resolve with which you face work for the needs of life; and at the end of the day you need to lean upon your Lord so that He removes from you the hardships of this day. So beware lest life distract you from the Giver of life. You may remember our Lord while you live with each work you perform and carry out, and meet each result of work with the words "Praise be to God" (al-hamdu lillah). And when you see any beauty from the Bestower, glory be to Him and exalted, you must say "What God wills" (ma sha'a Allah). And when you see anything that pleases you, say "Glory be to God" (subhan Allah). For this reason, when God called His believing creatures to prayer, He said: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.(9)﴾ (surah al-Jumu'ah).

This obligation concerns the obligatory Friday prayer as a congregational prayer, and congregation is required in it, and it is necessary that you be present in it as a gathering, because congregation is a condition for it, so it is not valid without congregation. We know that prayer is in fact remembrance of our Lord; so what comes after it?

﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of God, and remember God often that you may succeed.(10)﴾ (surah al-Jumu'ah).

That is, beware lest your dispersal in the land and your seeking of God's bounty, and taking the means of this world, distract you from your duty toward God. Rather, you must remember Him, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless.(205)﴾ (surah al-A'raf).

That is, do not be among the heedless of God's requirements within the limits God, mighty and majestic, has set; for heedlessness means the preoccupation of the heart with other than your Creator. If you keep your Creator in your mind always, you will not be heedless of His requirements in the mornings and the evenings and at all times, whether you are in the five prayers, or you are traveling the earth in any sense. Take as your model, O believer, the angels who glorify night and day without ceasing. If the angels, who have committed no sin and have none of the causes of sin, and who do not eat or reproduce, and have no appetite of the belly or appetite of the private parts (and all sins come from this direction), nevertheless you must take them as your model, for they are those who do not disobey God in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded. They do not disdain to worship Him; they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate. Therefore the Truth says after that:

﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.(206)﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 7, verse 206:

If we are all with our Lord, and in the presence of what He has granted us of creation and what He has sustained us with of bringing into being from non-existence, equally, then why did He single out these with nearness?

Beware lest you understand from "nearness" that it is nearness of place, for place is confined, and our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is not confined to a place. The nearness here is the nearness of grace, the nearness of mercy, the nearness of sovereignty, and the nearness of care. Or: every creation of Allah has been given causes and effects, but there is a creation of His who glorify Him in His very essence, and have no other work, and they are known as the exalted angels (al-mala'ika al-'alin), not the angels who manage affairs (al-mudabbirat amran) or the guardians (al-hafaza). This is why we said earlier: when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and Iblis refused, He said to him:

﴿Have you become arrogant, or have you been among the exalted?﴾ (part of verse 75, Surah Sad).

And "al-'alin" are those who were not included in the command to prostrate. They are angels who exist and have no work except glorifying the Exalted Essence, and they know nothing of creation or the world. They are other than the angels subjected to serve us. Those who are with our Lord are the angels "muhayyamun" (absorbed in awe), who know nothing but the Divine Essence and the glorification of the Essence, and their work is defined by Allah here: ﴿They do not disdain to worship Him, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾.

The scholars differed about how the angels prostrate: is it submission? Is it prayer? Is it the prostration we know? For us, prostration is the utmost of submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the time of prayer, because it is lowering the most noble thing in a human being, which is the face that the believer places on the ground in submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us that when we pass over a verse of prostration in the verses of the Book of Allah that contains such a thing, we must respond to it with a true response and prostrate for it, a prostration called the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawa), which occurs at its recitation or at hearing it from the reciter. The scholars have confined these to what you find in the Mushaf at each prostration, marking them with a sign and placing a small mark under the word at which we prostrate. When the scholars undertook to clarify the places where prostrations are required, they found that they begin with the prostration at the end of Surah "al-A'raf", which we are now reflecting upon, and end with the prostration in "al-'Alaq".

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾ (verse 1, Surah al-'Alaq).

Between them are prostrations, and some scholars counted two prostrations in Surah al-Hajj, while some ignored the second prostration in this surah. Whoever counts them as fifteen counts the second prostration of al-Hajj, which is disputed, along with the first prostration of al-Hajj, which is agreed upon. Some scholars said they are fourteen, because they did not count the second prostration of al-Hajj.

Suppose you wish to prostrate to Allah in gratitude at any time, and at any verse, then prostrate to Allah the prostration of thankfulness (sujud al-shukr). It is one prostration like the prostration of recitation, and it is recommended upon the renewal of a blessing, the lifting of a distress, or the removal of a calamity, and it is only performed outside the prayer.

Naturally, you begin the prostration with takbir and raising the hands, as if you were beginning the prayer. It would be proper to say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us what to say in the prostration of recitation. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came to him and said: "I saw last night, in what the sleeper sees, that I was praying at the root of a tree. I recited the prostration and prostrated, and the tree prostrated to my prostration, and I heard it say: 'O Allah, remove from me by it a burden, record for me by it a reward, and make it for me a treasure with You.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) recite the prostration and prostrate, and I heard him say in his prostration similar to what the man reported of the tree's words.(1)

(1) Narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi, who added: "And accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dawud, peace be upon him."
